model.description: Pharmaceuticals is a research-intensive industry focused on discovering, developing, and manufacturing medicines, vaccines, and consumer health products to treat and prevent diseases across therapeutic areas including oncology, immunology, and rare diseases.

domains.name: discovery
domains.description: Owns all data generated during drug discovery and target identification, including high-throughput screening (HTS) results, structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis, mechanism of action (MOA) studies, hit-to-lead progression, molecular targets, and early-stage compound optimization under GLP. Manages research data from electronic lab notebooks (ELN) in IDBS/Dotmatics, assay results, and compound libraries. Authoritative source for NCE (New Chemical Entity) and NBE (New Biological Entity) research data entering the development pipeline.
domains.references: ICH Q8 Pharmaceutical Development / GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

products.name: molecular_target
products.description: Master record for biological molecular targets identified during drug discovery, including proteins, enzymes, receptors, ion channels, and nucleic acids. Captures target class, gene name, UniProt/Ensembl identifiers, mechanism of action (MOA), therapeutic area relevance, target validation status, druggability assessment, and disease association. Authoritative SSOT for all target identification data entering the discovery pipeline from IDBS/Dotmatics ELN.

attributes.name: molecular_target_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the molecular target record in the discovery data product. Primary key for all downstream joins and lineage tracking.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer — Internal PK Convention

attributes.name: drug_substance_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_substance. Business justification: Target-based portfolio analysis: links validated biological target to marketed API for competitive intelligence, patent landscape assessment, MOA-based product clustering. Supports freedom-to-operate

attributes.name: gxp_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.gxp_obligation. Business justification: Target validation studies must comply with specific GxP obligations (GLP for preclinical, 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records). Obligation linkage ensures regulatory defensibility of validation data

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Molecular targets are patented inventions requiring patent protection tracking for freedom-to-operate analysis, portfolio management, and competitive intelligence in target selection decisions.

attributes.name: primary_patent_claim_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_claim. Business justification: Specific patent claims cover target modulation methods; claim-level tracking required for FTO clearance, licensing negotiations, and assessing blocking IP in target validation stage gates.

attributes.name: competitive_landscape_summary
attributes.description: Summary of known competitive programs targeting this molecular target, including approved drugs, clinical-stage compounds, and disclosed research programs from competitor organizations. Business-confidential intelligence used for portfolio strategy.
attributes.references: Internal Competitive Intelligence; FDA Orange Book; ClinicalTrials.gov

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this molecular target record was first created in the discovery data product. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Databricks Lakehouse Audit

attributes.name: discovery_program_code
attributes.description: Internal program or project code under which this target is being investigated. Links the target to the broader drug discovery program for portfolio management, resource allocation, and P&L tracking.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO (Controlling / Project System); Internal Portfolio Management

attributes.name: disease_association
attributes.description: Specific disease or condition(s) associated with this molecular target, as supported by published literature or internal research data. May reference ICD-10/ICD-11 disease codes or MeSH disease terms.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-11; MeSH Disease Ontology; Open Targets Platform; DisGeNET

attributes.name: druggability_assessment
attributes.description: Scientific assessment of the target's amenability to small molecule or biologic modulation based on structural, biochemical, and computational analyses. Key input to portfolio prioritization and NCE/NBE strategy decisions.
attributes.references: ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines; Hopkins & Groom Druggability Framework (Nature Reviews Drug Discovery)

attributes.name: eln_notebook_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier to the primary Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) experiment record in IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics that documents the original target identification and characterization data. Provides full scientific audit trail.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; GLP (21 CFR Part 58); 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records)

attributes.name: ensembl_gene_code
attributes.description: Ensembl stable gene identifier (e.g., ENSG00000146648) for the gene encoding the molecular target. Used for genomic cross-referencing, variant analysis, and bioinformatics pipelines.
attributes.references: Ensembl Genome Browser (EMBL-EBI); ICH E15 Pharmacogenomics Definitions

attributes.name: expression_tissue
attributes.description: Primary tissue(s) or cell type(s) where this molecular target is expressed at therapeutically relevant levels, as determined by transcriptomic or proteomic profiling (e.g., liver, lung epithelium, T-cells). Informs tissue selectivity and delivery strategy.
attributes.references: Human Protein Atlas; GTEx; FANTOM5; ICH S6 Preclinical Safety for Biologics

attributes.name: first_disclosed_date
attributes.description: Date on which this molecular target was first formally disclosed or documented in the internal ELN or target identification database. Establishes the scientific priority date for IP purposes.
attributes.references: USPTO Patent Priority Date Rules; EPC Article 54 (Novelty); IDBS/Dotmatics ELN

attributes.name: gene_name
attributes.description: Official HGNC (HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee) approved gene symbol encoding the molecular target (e.g., EGFR, TP53, BRCA1). Standard identifier used in regulatory submissions and scientific publications.
attributes.references: HGNC — HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee; FDA Pharmacogenomics Guidance

attributes.name: genetic_association_score
attributes.description: Quantitative score (0.0000–1.0000) representing the strength of genetic evidence linking this target to the associated disease, derived from GWAS, Mendelian randomization, or Open Targets Platform data. Higher scores indicate stronger genetic validation.
attributes.references: Open Targets Platform; GWAS Catalog (EMBL-EBI); ICH E15 Pharmacogenomics

attributes.name: indication_code
attributes.description: ICD-11 (International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision) code for the primary indication associated with this target. Enables standardized cross-referencing with regulatory submissions and clinical trial registries.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-11; FDA IND Application Requirements (21 CFR Part 312)

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent scientific or portfolio review of this target record. Ensures data currency and supports periodic target triage processes.
attributes.references: Internal Target Review SOP; GLP (21 CFR Part 58) Data Integrity Requirements

attributes.name: moa_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the molecular mechanism by which modulation of this target is expected to produce a therapeutic effect. Captures agonism, antagonism, inhibition, activation, or allosteric modulation details as documented in ELN.
attributes.references: ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Studies; FDA Pharmacology Review Guidance

attributes.name: moa_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the pharmacological mechanism of action for compounds acting on this target. Used to group targets by intervention strategy in SAR analysis and portfolio reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: agonist|antagonist|inhibitor|activator|allosteric_modulator|degrader|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology MOA Classification; ICH E8

attributes.name: modality
attributes.description: Preferred drug modality for targeting this molecular target based on its structural and biochemical properties. Determines the NCE (New Chemical Entity) or NBE (New Biological Entity) classification of resulting compounds. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologic|antibody|peptide|oligonucleotide|cell_therapy|gene_therapy|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA CDER/CBER Modality Classification; ICH Q6A/Q6B; EMA Biologics Guidelines

attributes.name: novelty_status
attributes.description: Classification of the target's novelty relative to the competitive landscape. Novel targets represent first-in-class opportunities; established targets have existing approved drugs; repurposed targets are being explored in new indications.
attributes.references: FDA Innovation and Drug Discovery Guidance; IP Strategy — Patent Filing (21 CFR Part 314)

attributes.name: organism
attributes.description: Biological organism in which the molecular target is expressed and studied. Typically Homo sapiens for human targets, but may include model organisms used in preclinical validation studies.
attributes.references: NCBI Taxonomy Database; ICH S5 Reproductive Toxicology; GLP Guidelines (21 CFR Part 58)

attributes.name: patent_landscape_summary
attributes.description: High-level summary of the patent landscape around this molecular target, including freedom-to-operate (FTO) considerations and known composition-of-matter or method-of-use patents. Supports IP strategy decisions.
attributes.references: USPTO; EPO; ICH Q11; 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA IP Certification)

attributes.name: pathway_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary biological signaling or metabolic pathway in which this target participates (e.g., PI3K/AKT/mTOR, RAS/MAPK, JAK/STAT). Supports pathway-based target clustering and polypharmacology analysis.
attributes.references: KEGG Pathway Database; Reactome Pathway Knowledgebase; WikiPathways

attributes.name: pdb_code
attributes.description: RCSB Protein Data Bank accession code for the primary 3D structure of this molecular target. Used by computational chemistry and structure-based drug design (SBDD) teams for molecular docking and virtual screening.
attributes.references: RCSB Protein Data Bank (PDB); wwPDB Guidelines

attributes.name: prioritization_tier
attributes.description: Portfolio prioritization tier assigned to this target by the Target Selection Committee, reflecting strategic importance, scientific confidence, and commercial potential. Tier 1 targets receive maximum resource allocation.
attributes.references: Internal Portfolio Review Process; ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Studies

attributes.name: protein_structure_available
attributes.description: Indicates whether a resolved 3D protein structure (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, or NMR) is available for this target in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) or internal structural biology repository. Directly impacts structure-based drug design (SBDD) feasibility.
attributes.references: RCSB Protein Data Bank (PDB); ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines

attributes.name: safety_concern_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of identified safety liabilities associated with modulation of this target (e.g., hERG channel activity, hepatotoxicity risk, immunosuppression). Populated only when safety_concern_flag is True.
attributes.references: ICH S7A/S7B; FDA Safety Pharmacology Guidance; EMA Preclinical Safety Guidelines

attributes.name: safety_concern_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether known safety liabilities or toxicological concerns have been identified for this target based on literature, genetic association studies, or internal preclinical data. Triggers mandatory safety review before progression.
attributes.references: ICH S7A/S7B Safety Pharmacology; FDA Preclinical Safety Evaluation Guidance; GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

attributes.name: selectivity_profile
attributes.description: Assessment of the target's selectivity relative to related family members or off-target proteins. Informs compound design strategy to minimize off-target toxicity and maximize therapeutic index.
attributes.references: ICH S7A Safety Pharmacology Studies; FDA Pharmacology/Toxicology Review Guidance

attributes.name: target_class
attributes.description: Pharmacological class of the molecular target based on its biochemical function and structural family. Drives druggability assessment strategy and compound screening cascade design. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GPCR|kinase|nuclear_receptor|ion_channel|protease|phosphatase|epigenetic_regulator|transcription_factor|transporter|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology Target Classification; ChEMBL Target Classification

attributes.name: target_code
attributes.description: Internally assigned alphanumeric business identifier for the molecular target, used as the externally-known unique code across systems (ELN, LIMS, CTMS). Distinct from the surrogate PK and from external database accession numbers.
attributes.references: Internal Master Data Management (MDM) Standard; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN

attributes.name: target_engagement_assay
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the primary biochemical or biophysical assay used to measure compound engagement with this target (e.g., HTRF binding assay, SPR, ITC, NanoBRET). Registered in LIMS (LabWare/SampleManager) and ELN.
attributes.references: LIMS — LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; GLP (21 CFR Part 58); IDBS/Dotmatics ELN

attributes.name: target_name
attributes.description: Human-readable scientific name of the molecular target (e.g., EGFR, BRAF, PD-L1, CDK4/6). Serves as the primary identity label used by research scientists and in ELN records within IDBS/Dotmatics.
attributes.references: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology; UniProt Protein Nomenclature Guidelines

attributes.name: target_owner
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the principal scientist or research team lead responsible for this molecular target within the discovery organization. Accountable for target validation decisions and data quality.
attributes.references: Internal HR / Organizational Data; GLP (21 CFR Part 58) Accountability Requirements

attributes.name: target_type
attributes.description: Biological molecule type of the target (e.g., protein, enzyme, receptor, ion channel, nucleic acid). Determines the modality of drug intervention and screening assay design. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: protein|enzyme|receptor|ion_channel|nucleic_acid|lipid|carbohydrate|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology; ChEMBL Target Type Ontology

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic area or disease domain for which this target is being investigated (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience, Cardiovascular). Aligns with the company's portfolio strategy and pipeline reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_disease|neuroscience|cardiovascular|infectious_disease|metabolic|respiratory|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WHO International Classification of Diseases (ICD-11); ATC Classification System; ICH E8

attributes.name: uniprot_accession
attributes.description: Universal Protein Resource (UniProt) accession number uniquely identifying the protein target in the global UniProtKB database. Enables cross-referencing with external biological databases and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: UniProt Knowledgebase (UniProtKB); ICH M4 CTD Guidelines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this molecular target record. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GDPR Article 5; Databricks Lakehouse Delta Lake

attributes.name: validation_completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which target validation studies were completed and the target was formally declared validated (in vitro or in vivo). Marks the transition from target identification to hit-to-lead progression stage.
attributes.references: ICH S7A/S7B; GLP (21 CFR Part 58); Internal Stage-Gate Process

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle stage of target validation, reflecting the level of scientific evidence supporting the target's role in disease. Drives go/no-go decisions for hit-to-lead progression. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: identified|hypothetical|validated_in_vitro|validated_in_vivo|clinically_validated|deprioritized — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH S7A/S7B Safety Pharmacology Guidelines; FDA Target Validation Guidance; IDBS/Dotmatics ELN Workflow

products.name: compound
products.description: Master record for all chemical and biological compounds in the discovery compound library, including NCEs (New Chemical Entities) and NBEs (New Biological Entities). Captures compound identity (IUPAC name, INN/USAN, registration number, CAS number), structural representation (molecular formula, molecular weight, SMILES, InChI), compound class (small molecule, biologic, peptide, ADC), source (synthesized, purchased, natural product), physicochemical properties (purity, physical state, storage conditions), and library membership. Authoritative SSOT for compound identity and structure across the discovery domain.

attributes.name: compound_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated surrogate key for each compound record in the discovery compound library. Primary key for the compound master data product.

attributes.name: drug_master_file_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.drug_master_file. Business justification: Compounds (APIs) are covered by DMFs for regulatory submissions; linkage supports IND/NDA filings, tracks manufacturing site authorization, and enables CMC strategy coordination between discovery and

attributes.name: drug_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_product. Business justification: Portfolio management necessity: links discovery compound directly to formulated product for development tracking, IP-to-product mapping, and commercial forecasting. Supports stage-gate decisions, pate

attributes.name: drug_substance_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_substance. Business justification: Regulatory CMC requirement: IND/NDA submissions must trace marketed API back to discovery compound for chemistry documentation. Critical for candidate nomination handoff, regulatory filing preparation

attributes.name: material_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: Compounds progressing to development/manufacturing are registered as materials in ERP for procurement, inventory management, batch tracking, and supply chain planning. Critical integration point betwe

attributes.name: part11_system_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.part11_system. Business justification: Compounds are registered and managed in Part 11-compliant systems (ELN, LIMS, registration databases). System assignment enables audit trail verification, electronic signature validation, and inspecti

attributes.name: patent_claim_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_claim. Business justification: Compounds must link to patent claims to track IP protection. This is essential for pharmaceutical asset valuation and freedom-to-operate analysis. No visible redundant columns to remove.

attributes.name: patent_family_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_family. Business justification: Compounds belong to patent families covering composition-of-matter globally; family-level tracking supports international IP strategy, prosecution coordination, and portfolio valuation for business de

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Compounds are patented chemical matter requiring direct patent linkage for IP lifecycle management, orange book listing preparation, patent term extension applications, and generic entry risk assessme

attributes.name: trademark_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.trademark. Business justification: Compounds (branded products) require trademark protection; linkage tracks brand strategy, supports naming decisions, coordinates trademark filing with development timelines, and protects commercial id

attributes.name: atc_code
attributes.description: WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code assigned to the compound based on its therapeutic use and pharmacological properties. Used for market access analysis, competitive benchmarking, and regulatory submissions. May be provisional at early discovery stage.

attributes.name: cas_number
attributes.description: Globally unique Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) registry number assigned by the American Chemical Society to uniquely identify the chemical substance. Used for regulatory submissions, procurement, and cross-system compound lookup.
attributes.references: CAS Registry, ICH Q6A, FDA Substance Registration System (SRS)

attributes.name: compound_class
attributes.description: Broad classification of the compound by molecular modality. Drives regulatory pathway selection (NDA vs BLA), manufacturing strategy (chemical synthesis vs biologics), and analytical method requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologic|peptide|adc|oligonucleotide|cell_therapy|rna_therapy|gene_therapy — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH Q6A (small molecules), ICH Q6B (biologics), FDA CDER/CBER classification

attributes.name: compound_name
attributes.description: Internal working name or code name assigned to the compound during discovery (e.g., project code name such as 'ABC-1234'). Used as the primary human-readable label in ELN, LIMS, and CTMS systems before an INN or USAN is assigned.

attributes.name: compound_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the compound within the discovery pipeline. 'Active' indicates the compound is under active research; 'promoted' indicates advancement to preclinical or clinical development; 'discontinued' indicates the compound has been deprioritized or terminated.
attributes.references: ICH Q8, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics, 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: controlled_substance_schedule
attributes.description: U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) controlled substance schedule classification for the compound (Schedule I–V or not controlled). Determines handling, storage, procurement, and regulatory reporting requirements under the Controlled Substances Act.
attributes.references: DEA Controlled Substances Act (21 USC 812), 21 CFR Part 1308, DEA

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System-generated timestamp recording when the compound record was first created in the data platform (Silver Layer). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q10, GDPR Article 5(2)

attributes.name: discovery_stage
attributes.description: Current stage of the compound within the drug discovery pipeline. Tracks progression from target identification through hit identification, hit-to-lead, lead optimization, and candidate selection before IND filing. Used for portfolio reporting and stage-gate decision making.
attributes.references: ICH Q8, ICH M3(R2), FDA IND Guidance 21 CFR Part 312, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: eln_reference_code
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this compound record to the originating experiment or notebook entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability from the compound master record back to the primary research data and synthesis records.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11, OECD GLP Principles, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: entity_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: New Chemical Entity / New Biological Entity (NCE/NBE) Type
attributes.description: Regulatory classification of the compound as a New Chemical Entity (NCE), New Biological Entity (NBE), biosimilar, fixed-dose combination, or prodrug. Determines regulatory exclusivity periods, patent strategy, and submission pathway under FDA, EMA, and ICH guidelines.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108, EMA Guideline on NCE/NBE, ICH Q8

attributes.name: glp_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the compound and its associated research data have been generated under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) conditions as required for regulatory submissions. GLP compliance is mandatory for safety pharmacology and toxicology studies supporting IND applications.
attributes.references: OECD Principles of GLP, 21 CFR Part 58, EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

attributes.name: hazard_classification
attributes.description: Globally Harmonized System (GHS) hazard classification for the compound covering health, physical, and environmental hazards (e.g., 'Acute Toxicity Cat. 2, Carcinogen Cat. 1A'). Required for Safety Data Sheet (SDS) preparation, occupational health risk assessment, and EHS compliance.
attributes.references: GHS (UN Purple Book), OSHA HazCom 2012, REACH Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, ICH Q3C

attributes.name: hba_count
attributes.description: Number of hydrogen bond acceptors (HBA) in the compound structure. Key Lipinski Rule of Five parameter (threshold: ≤ 10 HBAs) used in drug-likeness assessment and oral bioavailability prediction during hit-to-lead and lead optimization.
attributes.references: Lipinski Rule of Five, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines

attributes.name: hbd_count
attributes.description: Number of hydrogen bond donors (HBD) in the compound structure. Key Lipinski Rule of Five parameter (threshold: ≤ 5 HBDs) used in drug-likeness assessment and oral bioavailability prediction during hit-to-lead and lead optimization.
attributes.references: Lipinski Rule of Five, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines

attributes.name: inchi
attributes.description: IUPAC International Chemical Identifier (InChI) string providing a standardized, layered representation of the compound's chemical structure. Used for cross-system compound deduplication, registry lookups, and interoperability with external databases (PubChem, ChEMBL). Classified confidential as it encodes proprietary structural IP.
attributes.references: IUPAC InChI Trust, ICH Q6A, FDA SRS

attributes.name: inchi_key
attributes.description: Fixed-length 27-character hashed representation of the InChI string (InChIKey). Used as a compact, searchable identifier for compound lookup in external databases (PubChem, ChEMBL, CAS SciFinder) and for deduplication across compound registries.
attributes.references: IUPAC InChI Trust, FDA SRS, PubChem

attributes.name: inn
attributes.description: World Health Organization (WHO)-assigned International Nonproprietary Name (INN) for the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Used in regulatory submissions (NDA, BLA, MAA) and scientific communications. May be null for early-stage compounds not yet assigned an INN.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme, ICH Q6A, 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: iupac_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) Name
attributes.description: Systematic chemical name of the compound following International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) nomenclature rules. Provides an unambiguous, internationally recognized chemical identity for regulatory submissions and scientific publications.
attributes.references: IUPAC 2013 Recommendations, ICH Q6A, FDA SRS

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date
attributes.description: Date on which the compound record was last reviewed by a qualified scientist or data steward for accuracy, completeness, and continued relevance in the discovery portfolio. Supports data governance and periodic compound library curation activities.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q10, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: library_membership
attributes.description: Designation of the compound library or collection to which this compound belongs within the corporate compound library management system. Drives screening campaign design, compound availability, and resource allocation in HTS and fragment-based drug discovery programs.
attributes.references: ISPE GAMP 5, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics, LIMS - LabWare / SampleManager

attributes.name: logp
attributes.description: Logarithm of the octanol-water partition coefficient (LogP), a measure of the compound's lipophilicity. Critical SAR and ADME parameter used to predict membrane permeability, oral bioavailability, and CNS penetration. Lipinski Rule of Five threshold: LogP ≤ 5.
attributes.references: Lipinski Rule of Five, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: mechanism_of_action
attributes.description: Described mechanism of action (MOA) of the compound — the biochemical interaction through which the compound produces its pharmacological effect (e.g., 'selective inhibitor of EGFR tyrosine kinase'). Critical for target validation, patent claims, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E8, FDA Pharmacology Review Guidance, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: molecular_formula
attributes.description: Empirical molecular formula of the compound expressed using Hill notation (e.g., C21H30N2O5). Represents the elemental composition and is used in regulatory submissions, analytical method development, and structural verification.
attributes.references: IUPAC Hill System, ICH Q6A, FDA SRS

attributes.name: molecular_weight
attributes.description: Average molecular weight of the compound expressed in grams per mole (g/mol). Critical physicochemical property used in SAR analysis, ADME profiling, formulation development, and Lipinski Rule of Five drug-likeness assessment.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A, Lipinski Rule of Five, IUPAC

attributes.name: physical_state
attributes.description: Physical state of the compound at standard conditions (solid, liquid, gas, semi-solid). Determines handling procedures, formulation approach, and storage requirements. Captured in the ELN and LIMS at time of compound registration.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A, GMP 21 CFR Part 211, LIMS - LabWare / SampleManager

attributes.name: primary_target
attributes.description: Primary biological molecular target of the compound (e.g., gene name, protein name, receptor, enzyme — such as 'EGFR', 'PD-1', 'BCL-2'). Used in target identification, SAR analysis, and cross-compound target coverage analysis within the discovery portfolio.
attributes.references: ICH E8, ChEMBL Target Nomenclature, UniProt, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: purity_percent
attributes.description: Measured chemical purity of the compound expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00%). Determined by analytical methods such as HPLC or NMR. Critical quality attribute (CQA) for assay reliability, GLP compliance, and advancement decisions in hit-to-lead progression.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A, GLP (OECD Principles), 21 CFR Part 58, LIMS - LabWare / SampleManager

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the compound was formally registered in the corporate compound registry (IDBS/Dotmatics). Marks the official entry of the compound into the discovery compound library and initiates the compound lifecycle tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11, OECD GLP Principles, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: registration_number
attributes.description: Internally assigned unique registration number for the compound within the corporate compound registry (e.g., IDBS/Dotmatics compound registration system). Serves as the primary business identifier used across discovery, CMC, and regulatory workflows.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A, 21 CFR Part 312, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: rotatable_bond_count
attributes.description: Number of rotatable bonds in the compound structure. Veber rule parameter (threshold: ≤ 10) used alongside TPSA to predict oral bioavailability and molecular flexibility in SAR and lead optimization analyses.
attributes.references: Veber Rules, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines

attributes.name: smiles
attributes.business_glossary_term: Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) Notation
attributes.description: Canonical SMILES (Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System) string representing the two-dimensional chemical structure of the compound. Used in cheminformatics, HTS data analysis, SAR modeling, and AI/ML-based drug discovery workflows. Classified confidential as it encodes proprietary structural IP.
attributes.references: Daylight SMILES Specification, ICH Q6A, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: solubility_aqueous_um
attributes.description: Measured or predicted aqueous solubility of the compound expressed in micromolar (µM). Key ADME physicochemical property used in SAR analysis, formulation feasibility assessment, and drug-likeness profiling (Lipinski, Veber rules).
attributes.references: ICH Q6A, Lipinski Rule of Five, ADME Guidelines, LIMS

attributes.name: source_type
attributes.description: Origin classification of the compound indicating how it was obtained. Synthesized compounds are produced in-house; purchased compounds are acquired from external vendors or CROs; natural products are derived from biological sources. Impacts IP strategy and CMC documentation.
attributes.references: ICH Q11, FDA CMC Guidance, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: storage_condition
attributes.description: Recommended storage conditions for the compound (e.g., '-20°C, under nitrogen, protected from light, desiccated'). Ensures compound stability and integrity in the compound library. Derived from stability data and referenced in CoA and compound library management SOPs.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A (Stability Testing), ICH Q6A, GMP 21 CFR Part 211.68, LIMS

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic area or disease indication for which the compound is being developed (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience, Cardiovascular). Aligns with the ATC classification system and drives portfolio prioritization and resource allocation decisions.
attributes.references: WHO ATC Classification, ICH E8, FDA Therapeutic Area Guidance

attributes.name: tpsa_angstrom2
attributes.description: Topological Polar Surface Area (TPSA) of the compound expressed in square angstroms (Å²). Used to predict intestinal absorption, blood-brain barrier penetration, and oral bioavailability. Veber rule threshold: TPSA ≤ 140 Å² for oral drugs.
attributes.references: Veber Rules, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System-generated timestamp recording when the compound record was last modified in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and enables change detection for downstream data consumers and AI/ML pipelines.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q10, GDPR Article 5(2)

attributes.name: usan
attributes.description: United States Adopted Name (USAN) assigned by the USAN Council for the compound. Used in US regulatory submissions (NDA/BLA) and US commercial labeling. May differ slightly from INN.

attributes.name: vendor_catalog_number
attributes.description: Vendor-assigned catalog or product number for purchased compounds. Used for reorder, procurement traceability, and cross-referencing with vendor CoA and SDS documentation. Applicable only when source_type is 'purchased'.
attributes.references: ICH Q10, SAP S/4HANA MM Module, GMP 21 CFR Part 211

attributes.name: vendor_name
attributes.description: Name of the external vendor, CRO, or supplier from whom the compound was purchased or sourced, if applicable. Relevant for purchased compounds and natural product extracts. Used for procurement traceability, vendor qualification, and supply chain management.
attributes.references: ICH Q10, GMP 21 CFR Part 211, SAP S/4HANA MM Module

products.name: assay
products.description: Master record for biological and biochemical assays used in drug discovery screening and profiling. Captures assay name, assay type (biochemical, cell-based, phenotypic, ADME, toxicity), assay format (HTS, dose-response, selectivity), target association, assay technology platform (HTRF, AlphaScreen, SPR, NMR), assay validation status, GLP compliance flag, detection method, assay protocol reference, throughput capacity, and responsible scientist. Sourced from IDBS/Dotmatics ELN.

attributes.name: assay_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the assay master record in the discovery domain. Primary key for the assay data product. Role classification: MASTER_RESOURCE.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN internal object model

attributes.name: gxp_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.gxp_obligation. Business justification: Assays used for regulatory submissions must comply with specific GxP obligations (GLP validation, data integrity, method validation). Obligation mapping drives validation requirements, inspection prep

attributes.name: molecular_target_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: Assays are designed to screen against specific molecular targets. The assay table currently has target_name and target_class as denormalized STRING attributes. Adding molecular_target_id FK allows joi

attributes.name: responsible_scientist_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: GxP compliance and regulatory inspections require traceable accountability for assay validation and execution. Responsible scientist must link to qualified employee record for training verification, e

attributes.name: assay_code
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique code assigned to the assay within the ELN or LIMS (e.g., ASY-HTS0042). Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used for cross-system referencing between IDBS/Dotmatics, LabWare LIMS, and SAP QM.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; LabWare LIMS; ICH Q2(R1)

attributes.name: assay_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the assay as registered in the ELN (e.g., 'EGFR Kinase Inhibition HTRF Assay'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used in scientific reports, regulatory submissions, and compound screening dashboards.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; ICH M10 (Bioanalytical Method Validation)

attributes.name: assay_type
attributes.description: Primary scientific classification of the assay based on its biological or chemical mode of measurement. Serves as the CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Drives downstream SAR analysis workflows and compound triage decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: biochemical|cell_based|phenotypic|ADME|toxicity|binding|functional — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH S7A/S7B (Safety Pharmacology); FDA Guidance on Drug Interaction Studies; IDBS Dotmatics assay taxonomy

attributes.name: automation_compatible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the assay has been adapted and validated for automated liquid handling platforms (e.g., Hamilton, Tecan, Beckman Coulter). Determines eligibility for inclusion in HTS screening campaigns and impacts throughput capacity planning.
attributes.references: ISPE GAMP 5; ANSI/SLAS Microplate Standards; IDBS E-WorkBook automation integration

attributes.name: cell_line
attributes.description: Name of the cell line used in cell-based assays (e.g., HEK293, HeLa, Jurkat, A549, MCF-7). Null for biochemical or cell-free assays. Required for assay reproducibility and cross-site comparability. Cell line authentication records are maintained in the ELN.
attributes.references: ATCC cell line standards; ISPE GAMP 5; ICH Q5D (Cell Substrates); LabWare LIMS biological material registry

attributes.name: coefficient_of_variation_pct
attributes.description: Percentage coefficient of variation (%CV) of the assay signal across replicate measurements, representing assay precision and reproducibility. Typically required to be ≤ 15% for HTS assays and ≤ 20% for bioanalytical assays per ICH Q2(R1). Stored from the assay validation run.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

attributes.name: concentration_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for compound concentrations used in the assay (e.g., nM, µM, mM). Standardizes concentration reporting across compound screening results and SAR analysis. Required for dose-response curve fitting and IC50/EC50 calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: nM|uM|mM|mg_mL|ug_mL|ng_mL|pM — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1); IUPAC nomenclature; LabWare LIMS unit registry

attributes.name: cost_per_well_usd
attributes.description: Estimated reagent and consumable cost per assay well in US dollars. Used for screening campaign cost modeling, budget planning, and make-vs-buy decisions for outsourcing to CROs. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA MM procurement data and lab supply records.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO (Cost Center Accounting); ICH Q10; ISPE Cost of Goods guidance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the assay master record was first created in the ELN or data platform. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH Q10; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

attributes.name: cro_vendor_name
attributes.description: Name of the external Contract Research Organization (CRO) executing this assay when outsourced_to_cro is true. Null for in-house assays. Used for vendor performance tracking, contract management, and regulatory audit trail documentation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA MM (Vendor Master); ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: detection_method
attributes.description: Physical or chemical detection principle used to measure the assay signal (e.g., fluorescence, luminescence, radioactivity, mass spectrometry). Distinct from technology_platform — platform is the instrument system, detection_method is the underlying measurement principle. Used for assay validation documentation and GLP compliance records. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fluorescence|luminescence|absorbance|radioactivity|mass_spectrometry|NMR|SPR|calorimetry — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance

attributes.name: eln_notebook_reference
attributes.description: Identifier of the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) experiment or notebook entry in IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics where the assay development and validation data are recorded. Provides direct traceability from the data product to the source scientific record.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP)

attributes.name: first_used_date
attributes.description: Date when the assay was first deployed for compound screening or profiling activities. Marks the operational start of the assay lifecycle. Used for assay age tracking, periodic revalidation scheduling, and portfolio lifecycle management.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook audit trail

attributes.name: format
attributes.description: Operational format describing how the assay is run in the screening workflow (e.g., High-Throughput Screening (HTS) primary screen, dose-response, selectivity panel). Determines throughput capacity planning and compound consumption requirements.
attributes.references: ISPE GAMP 5; IDBS E-WorkBook assay format taxonomy; ICH Q2(R1)

attributes.name: glp_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the assay is conducted under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations as required for regulatory submissions (IND/NDA/BLA). GLP-compliant assays require full audit trails, validated equipment, and certified personnel. Critical for preclinical safety study data submitted to FDA/EMA.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); OECD Principles of GLP; EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

attributes.name: hit_threshold_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the hit_threshold_value (e.g., percent inhibition, nM IC50). Ensures unambiguous interpretation of the hit-calling criterion across different assay types and readout formats.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH Q2(R1); IUPAC nomenclature

attributes.name: hit_threshold_value
attributes.description: Numerical threshold used to classify a compound as a 'hit' in primary screening (e.g., ≥ 50% inhibition at 10 µM). Defined during assay validation and used by automated hit-calling algorithms in the HTS data analysis pipeline. Critical for hit-to-lead progression decisions.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics hit-calling configuration; ICH Q2(R1); FDA HTS Guidance

attributes.name: incubation_time_hours
attributes.description: Standard incubation duration in hours for the assay reaction or cell treatment step. Critical for assay reproducibility and scheduling of automated liquid handling workflows. Stored from the validated assay protocol.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook protocol parameters; ISPE GAMP 5

attributes.name: last_validated_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent formal validation or requalification of the assay per ICH Q2(R1) or fit-for-purpose qualification criteria. Used to trigger periodic revalidation workflows and to assess whether assay data is current for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1); 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

attributes.name: lims_assay_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Assay ID
attributes.description: Cross-reference identifier for this assay in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) — LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager. Enables bidirectional traceability between the discovery data product and the LIMS assay execution records.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10

attributes.name: multiplexed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the assay measures multiple analytes or endpoints simultaneously in a single well or reaction (multiplexed assay). Multiplexed assays increase data density per compound and reduce reagent consumption. Relevant for assay cost modeling and data analysis pipeline configuration.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook multiplex assay configuration; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: outsourced_to_cro
attributes.business_glossary_term: Outsourced to Contract Research Organization (CRO) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this assay is currently outsourced to an external Contract Research Organization (CRO) for execution. When true, the cro_vendor_name field captures the CRO identity. Impacts data governance, IP ownership, and regulatory audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Oversight of Clinical Investigations (adapted for preclinical CRO oversight)

attributes.name: owning_department
attributes.description: Name of the research department or functional group that owns and maintains the assay (e.g., 'HTS Group', 'In Vitro Pharmacology', 'ADME Sciences', 'Toxicology'). Used for resource allocation, cost center attribution, and assay portfolio governance.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO (Cost Center Management); IDBS E-WorkBook organizational hierarchy

attributes.name: plate_format
attributes.description: Microplate format used in the assay (e.g., 96-well, 384-well, 1536-well). Determines reagent volumes, automation compatibility, and throughput capacity. Critical for liquid handling robot programming and compound dispensing protocols.
attributes.references: ANSI/SLAS Microplate Standards; ISPE GAMP 5; LabWare LIMS plate management

attributes.name: protocol_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier or URL reference to the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) or assay protocol document stored in the ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics) or document management system (Veeva Vault QualityDocs). Ensures traceability from assay execution to the governing protocol version.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); Veeva Vault QualityDocs; ISPE GAMP 5; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System

attributes.name: protocol_version
attributes.description: Version number of the assay protocol document in effect at the time of assay execution (e.g., v1.0, v2.3). Required for GLP audit trails and regulatory submission traceability. Distinct from protocol_reference which is the document identifier.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); ICH Q10; Veeva Vault QualityDocs version control

attributes.name: readout_type
attributes.description: Primary quantitative output metric reported by the assay (e.g., IC50, EC50, Ki, Kd, percent inhibition, percent activation). Determines how compound activity data is interpreted in SAR analysis and hit-to-lead progression decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IC50|EC50|Ki|Kd|percent_inhibition|percent_activation|ratio|count|viability_pct — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IUPAC pharmacology nomenclature; ChEMBL data standards; ICH M10

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether assay results generated using this assay are eligible for inclusion in regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA). Eligibility requires full validation per ICH Q2(R1) and GLP compliance where applicable. Governs data governance workflows for regulatory data packages.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312 (IND); 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); ICH Q2(R1); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date when the assay was formally retired and removed from active use. Null for active assays. Retirement is triggered by target deprioritization, supersession by a superior assay, or platform decommissioning. Required for data governance and historical data archival.
attributes.references: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); IDBS E-WorkBook lifecycle management

attributes.name: signal_window
attributes.description: Ratio of the maximum signal (positive control) to the minimum signal (negative control), quantifying the dynamic range of the assay. A signal window ≥ 2 is typically required for HTS qualification. Used in assay validation reports and Z-factor calculations.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1); Zhang JH et al. (1999) SLAS Discovery — Z-factor definition; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance

attributes.name: species_origin
attributes.description: Biological species from which the assay target, cells, or biological material is derived (e.g., human, mouse, rat, recombinant). Critical for translational relevance assessment and cross-species selectivity profiling. Impacts regulatory acceptability of preclinical data for IND submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: human|mouse|rat|rabbit|dog|monkey|in_vitro_recombinant — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH S5(R3) Reproductive Toxicology; ICH S7A/S7B; FDA IND Guidance

attributes.name: technology_platform
attributes.description: Detection technology or instrument platform used to execute the assay (e.g., HTRF, AlphaScreen, Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR), NMR, FRET, TR-FRET, Luminescence, Flow Cytometry). Critical for assay reproducibility assessment and equipment scheduling. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HTRF|AlphaScreen|SPR|NMR|FRET|TR-FRET|luminescence|flow_cytometry|mass_spectrometry|fluorescence_polarization — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISPE GAMP 5; ICH Q2(R1); LabWare LIMS instrument registry

attributes.name: temperature_celsius
attributes.description: Standard incubation or reaction temperature in degrees Celsius for the assay. Critical for assay reproducibility across sites and instruments. Deviations from this value are flagged as out-of-specification (OOS) events in the LIMS.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1); 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); LabWare LIMS environmental monitoring

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Disease or therapeutic area that the assay supports (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience, Cardiovascular). Links assay activity to the business portfolio and pipeline planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_diseases|neuroscience|cardiovascular|infectious_diseases|metabolic — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WHO ICD-11; ATC classification; ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies

attributes.name: throughput_capacity
attributes.description: Maximum number of compounds or samples that can be processed per day using this assay under standard HTS conditions. Serves as the MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used for compound library screening campaign planning and resource scheduling in the discovery lab.
attributes.references: ISPE GAMP 5; IDBS E-WorkBook capacity planning module

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the assay with respect to its scientific and regulatory validation. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. 'validated' indicates full ICH Q2(R1) compliance; 'qualified' indicates fit-for-purpose qualification; 'development' indicates the assay is still being optimized. Governs whether assay results can be used in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

attributes.name: z_prime_factor
attributes.description: Statistical measure of assay quality (Z') calculated from positive and negative control variability. Values ≥ 0.5 indicate an excellent assay suitable for HTS. Stored as the validated Z' from the assay qualification run. Used to gate assay deployment for compound screening campaigns.
attributes.references: Zhang JH et al. (1999) A Simple Statistical Parameter for Use in Evaluation and Validation of High Throughput Screening Assays; ICH Q2(R1)

products.name: hts_campaign
products.description: Master record for High-Throughput Screening (HTS) campaigns executed against compound libraries. Captures campaign name, target or assay being screened, compound library used, screening format (primary, confirmatory, counter-screen), campaign status, start and end dates, number of compounds screened, hit rate, assay window (Z-prime factor), screening technology platform, CRO involvement flag, and campaign owner. Central operational entity for HTS execution tracking.

attributes.name: hts_campaign_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the HTS campaign record in the discovery data product. Primary key for all downstream joins and lineage tracking.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics internal entity model; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System

attributes.name: assay_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.assay. Business justification: HTS campaigns execute screening using specific assays. The campaign currently has assay_format, assay_technology, target_name, target_class as denormalized attributes. Adding assay_id FK establishes t

attributes.name: compound_library_id
attributes.description: Reference to the compound library screened in this campaign, linking to the compound library master record that defines the collection of molecules tested (e.g., diversity set, focused kinase library, natural product library).
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics compound registry; LIMS - LabWare SampleManager

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: HTS campaigns are major cost events requiring cost center allocation for financial tracking, budget management, and project costing. Enables campaign cost analysis, resource planning, and financial re

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: HTS campaigns are cost-tracked R&D projects requiring internal order assignment for budget control, variance analysis, and cost-per-screen metrics essential to pharmaceutical screening operations and

attributes.name: invention_disclosure_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.invention_disclosure. Business justification: HTS campaigns identify novel hits requiring invention disclosure; direct linkage ensures IP capture from screening, tracks disclosure-to-filing pipeline, and supports patent prosecution strategy for s

attributes.name: owner_employee_id
attributes.description: FK to workforce.employee

attributes.name: primary_hts_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the scientist or principal investigator responsible for the HTS campaign. Accountable for campaign design, execution quality, and data integrity. Maps to the employee/researcher master record.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics user management; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q10

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: HTS campaigns operate under compliance programs governing data integrity, GLP compliance, and electronic records management. Program assignment determines audit scope, inspection readiness requirement

attributes.name: project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent drug discovery project under which this HTS campaign is executed. Links the campaign to the broader target identification and hit-to-lead program for portfolio tracking.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics project hierarchy; ICH Q10

attributes.name: actual_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the HTS campaign screening execution was completed. Used to calculate campaign duration, throughput metrics, and to trigger downstream hit confirmation workflows.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: actual_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the HTS campaign screening execution actually commenced. Compared against planned_start_date to measure schedule variance and operational efficiency.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: assay_format
attributes.description: Scientific format of the assay used in the campaign, indicating whether the screen measures biochemical activity (purified protein), cellular response, whole-organism phenotype, direct binding (biophysical), or fragment-based interactions. Critical for interpreting hit quality and SAR analysis.
attributes.references: NIH NCATS HTS Assay Guidance; ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines

attributes.name: assay_technology
attributes.description: Specific detection technology or instrumentation platform used in the assay (e.g., HTRF, AlphaScreen, FRET, TR-FRET, FP, luminescence, absorbance, imaging). Determines data interpretation rules and quality thresholds. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HTRF|AlphaScreen|FRET|TR-FRET|FP|luminescence|absorbance|imaging|SPR|ITC — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SLAS (Society for Laboratory Automation and Screening) Technology Standards; ISPE GAMP 5

attributes.name: campaign_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the HTS campaign, assigned by the ELN or LIMS system (e.g., HTS-EGFR-2024). Used for cross-system referencing in Dotmatics, LabWare, and project management tools.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics campaign numbering convention; LIMS - LabWare SampleManager

attributes.name: campaign_description
attributes.description: Free-text scientific description of the HTS campaign objectives, biological rationale, assay design, and any special conditions or deviations from standard protocols. Provides context for data interpretation and scientific review.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: campaign_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the HTS campaign, typically including the target name and campaign purpose (e.g., 'EGFR Kinase Primary Screen Q1 2024'). Used in reports, dashboards, and scientific communications.

attributes.name: campaign_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the HTS campaign, tracking progression from planning through execution to completion or cancellation. Drives operational dashboards and resource allocation decisions.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics workflow states; ICH Q10

attributes.name: coefficient_of_variation_percent
attributes.description: Percentage coefficient of variation of the neutral control wells across all campaign plates, measuring intra- and inter-plate reproducibility. Acceptable CV% thresholds are defined per assay type and are a key quality acceptance criterion.
attributes.references: SLAS Assay Quality Standards; ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures

attributes.name: compounds_screened_count
attributes.description: Total number of unique compounds tested in this HTS campaign. Key operational metric for campaign scope, resource planning, and hit rate denominator calculation.
attributes.references: SLAS HTS Metrics Guidelines; ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the HTS campaign record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GLP data integrity regulations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GLP 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q10

attributes.name: cro_involved
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Contract Research Organization (CRO) was engaged to execute or support this HTS campaign. Drives vendor management, data transfer agreement requirements, and IP ownership tracking.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; GDPR Article 28 (data processor agreements)

attributes.name: cro_name
attributes.description: Name of the CRO engaged for this HTS campaign, when cro_involved is True. Used for vendor performance tracking, contract management, and regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Overall data quality assessment for the HTS campaign based on Z' factor, CV%, plate failure rate, and control performance. Determines whether campaign data is accepted for hit identification and downstream SAR analysis.
attributes.references: SLAS Assay Quality Standards; ICH Q2(R1); GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: eln_notebook_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this HTS campaign to the corresponding experiment record in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability to raw experimental data, protocols, and scientist sign-off records.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: failed_plate_count
attributes.description: Number of assay plates that failed quality control criteria and were excluded from hit identification analysis. High failed plate counts may trigger campaign re-screening decisions.
attributes.references: SLAS Assay Quality Standards; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q10

attributes.name: glp_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether this HTS campaign was conducted under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations. GLP compliance is required for studies intended to support regulatory submissions (IND/NDA). Non-GLP campaigns are exploratory research.
attributes.references: GLP - 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; FDA GLP Regulations

attributes.name: hit_count
attributes.description: Number of compounds that met or exceeded the hit threshold criteria in this campaign. Used to calculate hit rate and to scope confirmatory screening workload.
attributes.references: SLAS HTS Metrics Guidelines; ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines

attributes.name: hit_rate_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of screened compounds that qualified as hits (hit_count / compounds_screened_count × 100). Key campaign quality metric used to assess assay selectivity, library quality, and target druggability. Stored as a raw business measurement, not a derived KPI.
attributes.references: SLAS HTS Metrics Guidelines; NIH NCATS HTS Best Practices

attributes.name: hit_threshold_percent
attributes.description: Percentage inhibition or activation threshold used to define a 'hit' in this campaign (e.g., ≥50% inhibition at screening concentration). Determines the stringency of hit identification and directly impacts hit count and hit rate.
attributes.references: SLAS HTS Best Practices; NIH NCATS Hit Criteria Guidelines

attributes.name: lims_batch_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Batch ID
attributes.description: Batch or run identifier assigned by the LIMS (LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager) for the sample processing associated with this HTS campaign. Enables traceability of compound samples, plate preparation, and analytical results.
attributes.references: LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; 21 CFR Part 11; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: planned_start_date
attributes.description: Scheduled start date for the HTS campaign as defined in the project plan. Used for resource scheduling, capacity planning, and tracking schedule adherence.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics project planning; ICH Q10

attributes.name: plate_count
attributes.description: Total number of assay plates processed during the campaign. Used for capacity planning, reagent consumption tracking, and quality control review scope.

attributes.name: plate_format
attributes.description: Microplate format used in the HTS campaign, defining the number of wells per plate. Determines throughput capacity, liquid handling requirements, and data volume per plate.

attributes.name: positive_control_compound
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the reference compound used as the positive control in the assay (known active compound). Defines the 100% inhibition/activation benchmark for data normalization and Z' factor calculation.
attributes.references: SLAS HTS Best Practices; GLP (Good Laboratory Practice) 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: screen_type
attributes.description: Classification of the screening campaign by its scientific purpose in the HTS funnel. Primary screens test the full compound library; confirmatory screens re-test hits; counter-screens eliminate false positives; dose-response screens establish potency; selectivity screens assess off-target activity.
attributes.references: ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines; NIH NCATS HTS Best Practices

attributes.name: screening_concentration_um
attributes.description: Single-point screening concentration in micromolar (µM) at which compounds are tested in the primary screen. Defines the activity threshold context for hit identification and is a critical parameter for hit rate comparability across campaigns.
attributes.references: SLAS HTS Best Practices; NIH NCATS Assay Guidance

attributes.name: signal_to_background_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of the positive control signal to the background (negative control) signal, measuring the dynamic range of the assay. A higher S/B ratio indicates a more robust assay window. Complementary to Z' factor for assay quality assessment.
attributes.references: SLAS Assay Quality Standards; NIH NCATS HTS Assay Guidance

attributes.name: target_class
attributes.description: Pharmacological class of the molecular target being screened. Used for portfolio analysis, technology platform selection, and benchmarking hit rates across target families. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: kinase|GPCR|protease|ion_channel|nuclear_receptor|epigenetic|PPI|phosphatase|transporter|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ChEMBL target classification; ATC classification; ISPE Drug Discovery Guidelines

attributes.name: target_name
attributes.description: Name of the biological target (protein, enzyme, receptor, pathway node) being screened against in this campaign (e.g., EGFR, BRAF V600E, TNF-alpha). Central scientific identifier linking the campaign to the drug discovery target portfolio.
attributes.references: UniProt protein nomenclature; HGNC gene nomenclature; ICH M7

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Disease or therapeutic area that the HTS campaign is intended to address (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience). Aligns the campaign to the company's R&D portfolio strategy and pipeline reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_disease|neuroscience|cardiovascular|infectious_disease|metabolic|respiratory — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WHO ICD-11 disease classification; ATC classification; ICH E8

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the HTS campaign record. Required for data lineage tracking, change control auditing, and Silver layer incremental processing in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GLP 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q10

attributes.name: z_prime_factor
attributes.description: Statistical measure of assay quality (Z' factor) calculated from positive and negative control signals, ranging from 0 to 1. A Z' ≥ 0.5 indicates an acceptable HTS assay window. Critical quality gate for campaign data acceptance per SLAS and NIH NCATS standards.
attributes.references: Zhang JH et al. (1999) J Biomol Screen; SLAS Assay Quality Standards; NIH NCATS

products.name: screening_result
products.description: Transactional record capturing individual compound screening results from HTS campaigns, dose-response assays, and selectivity panels. Captures compound, assay, and campaign references, plate/well position, raw signal, percent inhibition/activation, potency values (IC50/EC50/Ki), Hill slope, curve fit quality (R-squared), result classification (active, inactive, inconclusive, toxic, hit, confirmed hit, false positive), selectivity score, replicate number, run date, and data quality flags. Includes hit-to-lead eligibility determination. Distinct from in_vitro_study: screening_result covers primary and confirmatory screening at scale; in_vitro_study covers deeper mechanistic follow-up on selected compounds.

attributes.name: screening_result_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each individual screening result record in the HTS or dose-response assay campaign. Primary key for the screening_result data product in the discovery domain.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; ICH M10 Bioanalytical Method Validation

attributes.name: assay_id
attributes.description: Reference to the assay definition used to generate this screening result, including assay type, target, and protocol version.
attributes.references: LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; GLP (Good Laboratory Practice) 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the scientist or analyst responsible for executing or approving this assay run. Required for GLP audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature compliance.
attributes.references: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: hts_campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the High-Throughput Screening (HTS) campaign or screening project under which this result was generated. Enables grouping of results by campaign for SAR analysis.

attributes.name: molecular_target_id
attributes.description: Reference to the biological molecular target (e.g., protein, enzyme, receptor) against which the compound was screened. Central to target identification and MOA studies.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH S9 Nonclinical Evaluation for Anticancer Pharmaceuticals

attributes.name: primary_screening_compound_id
attributes.description: Reference to the compound (NCE or NBE) that was screened in this assay run. Links to the compound master record in the compound library.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH Q6A Specifications for New Drug Substances

attributes.name: coefficient_of_variation_pct
attributes.description: Coefficient of variation (CV%) for replicate measurements of this compound in the assay run. Measures intra-assay reproducibility; high CV% triggers data quality review.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: compound_concentration_um
attributes.description: Concentration of the compound tested in the assay well, expressed in micromolar (µM). Critical for dose-response curve fitting and potency determination.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1); GLP 21 CFR Part 58; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this screening result record was first created in the system. Required for GLP audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: curve_fit_r_squared
attributes.description: Coefficient of determination (R²) from the dose-response curve fitting model. Values close to 1.0 indicate a high-quality fit. Used as a data quality gate for potency value acceptance.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Data quality status assigned to this screening result based on automated QC rules and manual review. 'flagged' indicates a potential issue requiring review; 'rejected' excludes the result from downstream analysis.
attributes.references: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; ICH Q2(R1)

attributes.name: ec50_nm
attributes.description: Half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) derived from dose-response curve fitting, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Key potency metric for agonist/activator compounds.
attributes.references: ICH S9; ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: eln_notebook_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this screening result to the corresponding experiment entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability to the original experimental record.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GLP 21 CFR Part 58; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: hill_slope
attributes.description: Hill slope (cooperativity coefficient) from the four-parameter logistic (4PL) dose-response curve fit. Values near 1 indicate simple binding; values significantly different from 1 may indicate cooperativity, aggregation, or assay artifacts.
attributes.references: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: ic50_nm
attributes.description: Half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) derived from dose-response curve fitting, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Key potency metric for inhibitory compounds in SAR analysis and hit-to-lead progression.
attributes.references: ICH S9; ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: instrument_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the laboratory instrument (e.g., plate reader, liquid handler, mass spectrometer) used to generate the raw signal. Supports instrument qualification tracking and systematic error investigation per GLP.
attributes.references: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; ISPE GAMP 5

attributes.name: is_hit_to_lead_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this compound result meets the predefined criteria for progression into the hit-to-lead (H2L) phase, based on potency, selectivity, and data quality thresholds.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH Q6A; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: ki_nm
attributes.description: Inhibition constant (Ki) representing the binding affinity of the compound to the target, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Derived from competitive binding or enzyme kinetics assays. Used in mechanistic SAR studies.
attributes.references: ICH S9; ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: lims_result_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier from the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) for this screening result record. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational LIMS source system.
attributes.references: LIMS - LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; 21 CFR Part 11; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: max_response_percent
attributes.description: Maximum observed response (top asymptote) from the dose-response curve, expressed as a percentage of control. Indicates the efficacy ceiling of the compound at the target.

attributes.name: min_response_percent
attributes.description: Minimum observed response (bottom asymptote) from the dose-response curve, expressed as a percentage of control. Used to assess baseline signal and curve quality.

attributes.name: pan_assay_interference_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the compound has been identified as a Pan-Assay Interference Compound (PAINS) — a compound that produces artifactual activity signals across multiple assays due to non-specific mechanisms. PAINS compounds are deprioritized in hit-to-lead.
