attributes.description: Current stage of the drug discovery workflow. Progresses from target identification through candidate nomination, representing the standard industry gate-based progression model. Used for portfolio stage-gate reporting and resource planning.
attributes.references: ICH Q8(R2) Pharmaceutical Development; ISPE Drug Discovery guidelines

attributes.name: portfolio_decision
attributes.description: Most recent portfolio governance committee decision for the project. Recorded at each stage-gate review and drives resource reallocation and pipeline reporting.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; ISPE Drug Discovery; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: portfolio_decision_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent portfolio governance committee decision. Used for audit trail and decision history tracking in conjunction with portfolio_decision.

attributes.name: project_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric project identifier assigned by the portfolio governance office (e.g., DISC-20240001). Used as the business key across IDBS/Dotmatics ELN, SAP project structures, and regulatory submissions. Aligns with the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER canonical category.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; IDBS E-WorkBook naming conventions

attributes.name: project_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the drug discovery project (e.g., 'KRAS G12C Inhibitor Program'). Classified confidential as it may reveal pipeline strategy prior to public disclosure. Aligns with the IDENTITY_LABEL canonical category.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; SOX Section 302 (pipeline disclosure controls)

attributes.name: project_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the discovery project as managed in the portfolio governance system. Drives portfolio dashboards and resource allocation decisions. Aligns with the LIFECYCLE_STATUS canonical category.
attributes.references: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; FDA IND regulations 21 CFR 312

attributes.name: project_type
attributes.description: Classification of the discovery project by the nature of the entity being developed. NCE (New Chemical Entity) and NBE (New Biological Entity) drive distinct regulatory and IP strategies. Aligns with CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE canonical category.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA; EMA CHMP; ICH Q11; 21 CFR 314 (NDA) and 21 CFR 601 (BLA)

attributes.name: projected_candidate_nomination_date
attributes.description: Target date by which a development candidate is expected to be nominated and handed off to preclinical development. Key milestone for pipeline planning, IND filing timelines, and portfolio forecasting.
attributes.references: ICH Q8(R2); FDA IND 21 CFR 312; ISPE Drug Discovery guidelines

attributes.name: sap_wbs_element
attributes.description: SAP Project System WBS element code that maps this discovery project to the financial controlling structure in SAP S/4HANA. Enables cost allocation, budget tracking, and financial reporting at the project level.
attributes.references: SAP PS (Project System) module; SAP CO; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: sponsor
attributes.description: Senior executive or therapeutic area head who sponsors and champions the project at the portfolio governance level. Distinct from the project leader who manages day-to-day execution.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Official date on which the discovery project was formally initiated and approved by portfolio governance. Used for project duration calculations, milestone tracking, and portfolio timeline reporting.

attributes.name: strategic_priority_tier
attributes.description: Portfolio governance classification indicating the strategic importance of the project (Tier 1 = highest priority, Tier 3 = exploratory). Drives resource allocation, budget prioritization, and executive reporting. Classified confidential as it reflects pipeline strategy.
attributes.references: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: target_organism
attributes.description: Primary biological system or organism used in discovery assays and preclinical models. Relevant for GLP study design, species selection justification in IND applications, and ADME/PK modeling.
attributes.references: ICH S5(R3); ICH S6(R1); 21 CFR 58 (GLP); OECD GLP Principles

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Documented reason for project termination or discontinuation (e.g., safety signal, lack of efficacy, strategic reprioritization, IP conflict). Nullable for active projects. Critical for lessons-learned analysis and portfolio retrospectives. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: safety_signal|lack_of_efficacy|strategic_reprioritization|ip_conflict|resource_constraints|competitive_landscape|regulatory_concern — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH Q10; FDA IND 21 CFR 312.38 (IND withdrawal); EMA scientific advice

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Broad disease area or medical specialty the project targets (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Used for portfolio segmentation, budget allocation, and strategic alignment reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_diseases|cardiovascular|neuroscience|infectious_disease|metabolic|respiratory — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WHO ATC Classification; EMA Therapeutic Area guidelines

products.name: target_validation_study
products.description: Transactional record for studies conducted to validate a molecular target's role in disease and its suitability for drug intervention. Captures target identifier, validation method (genetic knockdown/knockout, overexpression, chemical probe, patient genetics), model system used (cell line, animal model, patient-derived), validation evidence level (strong, moderate, weak), disease linkage evidence, publication references, study outcome, validation scientist, and study completion date. Supports go/no-go decisions on target investment.

attributes.name: target_validation_study_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the target validation study record in the discovery domain. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: compound_id
attributes.description: Internal compound identifier for the chemical probe used in the validation study (where validation_method = chemical_probe). Links to the compound library registry in Dotmatics.
attributes.references: Chemical Probes Portal; SGC Probe Standards; Dotmatics Compound Registry

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Target validation studies are discrete cost centers requiring internal order assignment for R&D cost allocation, therapeutic area P&L reporting, and target prioritization decisions based on validation

attributes.name: molecular_target_id
attributes.description: Reference to the molecular target (gene, protein, pathway node) being validated in this study. Links to the master target registry.
attributes.references: UniProt; ChEMBL Target Schema; IDBS Dotmatics

attributes.name: project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.discovery_project. Business justification: Target validation studies are conducted within discovery projects to validate a molecular target's role in disease and its druggability. The study table currently has program_code as a denormalized ST

attributes.name: target_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the principal scientist responsible for conducting and interpreting the target validation study. Links to the HR/personnel master data.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP Personnel); ICH E6(R2); Internal HR System

attributes.name: target_study_director_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the GLP Study Director accountable for the overall scientific conduct and regulatory compliance of the study, as required under 21 CFR Part 58.33.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58.33; OECD GLP Principles Section 1.2; GLP Regulations

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the therapeutic area master record under which this target validation study is funded and governed, enabling portfolio-level investment tracking.
attributes.references: Internal Therapeutic Area Taxonomy; ATC Classification

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Target validation often involves CRO vendors for specialized model systems, disease models, or validation assays. Vendor qualification, quality oversight, GLP compliance, and regulatory submission req

attributes.name: biomarker_hypothesis
attributes.description: Proposed patient selection or pharmacodynamic biomarker hypothesis arising from the validation study, informing future clinical trial design and companion diagnostic strategy.
attributes.references: FDA Biomarker Qualification Program; EMA Biomarker Guidance; ICH E16

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: SAP cost center code to which the study expenses are allocated, enabling financial tracking of discovery investment by organizational unit.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO Module; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this target validation study record was first created in the data platform, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: decision_date
attributes.description: Date on which the go/no-go investment decision was formally recorded by the portfolio governance committee.
attributes.references: Internal R&D Stage-Gate Process; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: disease_area
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic area or disease indication for which the target is being validated (e.g., oncology, immunology, rare disease, neurology). Aligns with the company's therapeutic area taxonomy.
attributes.references: MeSH Disease Classification; ICD-11; ATC Classification

attributes.name: disease_indication
attributes.description: Specific disease or condition for which the target's role is being validated (e.g., non-small cell lung cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, Gaucher disease). More granular than disease_area.

attributes.name: disease_linkage_evidence
attributes.description: Summary of the genetic, epidemiological, or clinical evidence linking the target to the disease (e.g., GWAS associations, somatic mutation frequency, patient cohort data, biomarker correlations).

attributes.name: druggability_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of the target's amenability to small molecule, biologic, or other modality intervention based on structural, biochemical, and computational analysis.
attributes.references: ChEMBL Druggability Pipeline; Hopkins & Groom Druggability Framework; EMA Scientific Advice

attributes.name: eln_notebook_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this study record to the corresponding experiment entries in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics), ensuring data traceability.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; IDBS E-WorkBook; Dotmatics ELN; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles

attributes.name: endpoint_result_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the primary endpoint result value (e.g., %, nM, fold-change, mm³). Ensures dimensional correctness for cross-study comparisons.
attributes.references: SI Units; ICH E8(R1); LIMS LabWare / SampleManager

attributes.name: endpoint_result_value
attributes.description: Quantitative result value for the primary study endpoint (e.g., 85.3 for 85.3% knockdown efficiency). Paired with endpoint_result_unit for dimensional context.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ALCOA+ Data Integrity; LIMS LabWare / SampleManager

attributes.name: glp_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the study was conducted in compliance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations (21 CFR Part 58 / OECD GLP Principles), relevant for regulatory submission support.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; GLP (Good Laboratory Practice)

attributes.name: go_no_go_decision
attributes.description: Portfolio governance decision on whether to proceed with further investment in this target based on the validation study outcome. Drives hit-to-lead progression.
attributes.references: Internal R&D Stage-Gate Process; ICH Q8(R2) QbD Principles

attributes.name: moa_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the proposed mechanism of action (MOA) by which modulating the target is expected to produce a therapeutic effect in the disease indication.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; FDA Pharmacology Review Guidance; EMA Scientific Guidelines

attributes.name: model_system_name
attributes.description: Specific name or designation of the biological model system used (e.g., HeLa, MCF-7, C57BL/6 mouse, HCT116 xenograft). Provides experimental reproducibility context.
attributes.references: ATCC Cell Line Registry; ILAR Nomenclature; GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

attributes.name: model_system_type
attributes.description: Category of biological model system used in the validation study (e.g., cell line, animal model, patient-derived xenograft, organoid). Determines translational relevance of the findings.
attributes.references: ICH S5(R3); GLP (21 CFR Part 58); OECD GLP Principles

attributes.name: patent_relevance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the target validation findings have been flagged as potentially patentable or relevant to existing IP filings, triggering IP team review.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 101-103; EPC Article 52-57; Internal IP Policy

attributes.name: primary_endpoint
attributes.description: The principal measurable endpoint used to assess target validation success (e.g., target knockdown efficiency ≥80%, tumour volume reduction, cytokine suppression level).
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); FDA Endpoint Guidance; EMA Scientific Guidelines

attributes.name: publication_references
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of PubMed IDs, DOIs, or internal report identifiers for published or internal literature supporting the target validation findings (e.g., PMID:12345678, DOI:10.1016/...).

attributes.name: selectivity_profile
attributes.description: Description of the target's selectivity relative to related family members or off-target proteins, informing safety and specificity risk assessment during early discovery.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; ChEMBL; KINOMEscan; Eurofins SafetyScreen

attributes.name: species
attributes.description: Biological species used in the model system for the validation study. Critical for translational relevance assessment and regulatory species concordance requirements.
attributes.references: ICH S5(R3); ICH S6(R1); ILAR Nomenclature; OECD GLP

attributes.name: study_completion_date
attributes.description: The date on which all experimental work and data analysis for the target validation study were completed and the final study report was issued.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; IDBS E-WorkBook

attributes.name: study_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the target validation study, assigned at study initiation (e.g., TVS-EGFR-2024). Used for cross-system referencing in IDBS/Dotmatics ELN and CTMS.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics Study Registration; ICH M10

attributes.name: study_outcome
attributes.description: Overall scientific conclusion of the target validation study, indicating whether the target has been confirmed as suitable for drug intervention in the specified disease context.
attributes.references: OpenTargets; ICH E8(R1); Internal R&D Decision Framework

attributes.name: study_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which experimental work for the target validation study formally commenced, as recorded in the ELN.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; IDBS E-WorkBook

attributes.name: study_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the target validation study, tracking progression from planning through completion or termination.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics Study Lifecycle; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: study_title
attributes.description: Descriptive title of the target validation study, summarising the target, disease context, and primary validation approach (e.g., 'KRAS G12C Genetic Knockdown in NSCLC Cell Lines').
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: target_class
attributes.description: Pharmacological class of the molecular target, used to guide druggability assessment and modality selection. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: kinase|GPCR|nuclear_receptor|ion_channel|protease|epigenetic|transcription_factor|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ChEMBL Target Classification; IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this target validation study record was most recently modified, supporting change tracking and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: validation_evidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the strength of evidence supporting the target's role in disease, based on reproducibility, model translatability, and mechanistic clarity. Drives go/no-go investment decisions.

attributes.name: validation_method
attributes.description: Primary experimental method used to validate the target's role in disease biology. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: genetic_knockdown|genetic_knockout|overexpression|chemical_probe|patient_genetics|CRISPR_editing|RNAi|antisense_oligonucleotide — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH S7A; GLP (21 CFR Part 58); ISPE GAMP 5

products.name: in_vitro_study
products.description: Transactional record for in vitro mechanistic and safety studies conducted on selected compounds post-screening, including mechanism of action confirmation, pathway modulation, cell viability, and early cytotoxicity assessments. Captures study type, biological system (cell line, primary cells, organoids), compound and concentration range, endpoint measured, result values, cytotoxicity flag, protocol reference, GLP compliance flag, study date, and responsible scientist. Distinct from screening_result: in_vitro_study covers hypothesis-driven follow-up studies on prioritized compounds rather than high-throughput screening at scale.

attributes.name: in_vitro_study_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each in vitro mechanistic or safety study record in the discovery domain. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN

attributes.name: assay_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.assay. Business justification: In vitro mechanistic and safety studies use specific assays to measure compound activity. The study table currently has assay_format and assay_technology as denormalized STRING attributes. Adding assa

attributes.name: compound_id
attributes.description: Reference to the compound (NCE or NBE) under investigation in this study, as registered in the compound library. Links to the compound master record for structure, molecular weight, and registration data.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH Q6A; ICH Q6B

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the scientist responsible for designing and executing this in vitro study. Used for accountability, GLP audit trail, and scientific ownership tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); 21 CFR Part 11; OECD Principles of GLP

attributes.name: gxp_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.gxp_obligation. Business justification: In vitro studies used for regulatory submissions must comply with GLP obligations. Obligation assignment determines validation requirements, data integrity controls, and inspection readiness for study

attributes.name: molecular_target_id
attributes.description: Reference to the biological molecular target (protein, receptor, enzyme, pathway node) that this study is designed to interrogate. Links to the target identification master record.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH S7A; UniProt / ChEMBL target ontology

attributes.name: project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the drug discovery project under which this in vitro study is conducted. Enables aggregation of study results at the programme level for hit-to-lead and lead optimisation decisions.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; SAP S/4HANA PS module; ICH M3(R2)

attributes.name: protocol_id
attributes.description: Reference to the approved study protocol document governing this in vitro study. Ensures traceability to the authorised experimental procedure and version.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); OECD Principles of GLP; MasterControl / TrackWise QMS

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: In vitro studies (safety pharmacology, genotoxicity, receptor binding) are submitted in Module 4 of eCTD. Real regulatory requirement: nonclinical study reports with full traceability to submissions f

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: In vitro studies commonly outsourced to CRO vendors. Procurement manages vendor qualification, quality agreements, GLP compliance verification, data integrity oversight, and regulatory submission requ

attributes.name: assay_z_prime_factor
attributes.description: Z'-factor statistical metric quantifying assay quality and separation between positive and negative controls (range 0–1; values ≥0.5 indicate an excellent assay). Required for HTS and in vitro assay quality acceptance.
attributes.references: Zhang et al. 1999 (J Biomol Screen); ICH S7A; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: biological_system_type
attributes.description: Category of the biological system used in the study. Determines the physiological relevance, regulatory acceptance, and interpretation framework for the results.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; ICH S2(R1); OECD Test Guidelines 471-490; EMA Guideline on non-clinical safety studies

attributes.name: cell_line_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cell Line or Biological System Name
attributes.description: Specific name or designation of the cell line, primary cell type, organoid model, or other biological system used (e.g., HeLa, HepG2, Caco-2, iPSC-derived hepatocytes). Essential for scientific reproducibility and cross-study comparability.
attributes.references: ATCC / ECACC cell line standards; ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines

attributes.name: cell_line_passage_number
attributes.description: Number of times the cell line has been subcultured since its original isolation or receipt. High passage numbers can affect cell behaviour and result validity; tracked for quality and reproducibility.
attributes.references: ATCC / ECACC guidelines; ICH S7A; GLP OECD Principles

attributes.name: compound_batch_number
attributes.description: Specific batch or lot identifier of the compound used in this study. Critical for reproducibility, traceability, and investigation of batch-to-batch variability in results.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); ICH Q7; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: concentration_max_nm
attributes.description: Highest concentration of the compound tested in this study, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Defines the upper bound of the concentration-response range; used to assess ceiling effects and cytotoxicity thresholds.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; ICH M10; OECD Test Guidelines; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: concentration_min_nm
attributes.description: Lowest concentration of the compound tested in this study, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Defines the lower bound of the concentration-response range used for dose-response modelling.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; ICH M10; OECD Test Guidelines; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: concentration_point_count
attributes.description: Number of distinct concentration levels tested in the dose-response series. Indicates the resolution of the concentration-response curve and the robustness of derived potency estimates.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this in vitro study record was first created in the system. Part of the GLP-required audit trail for electronic records per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); OECD Principles of GLP

attributes.name: cytotoxicity_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether cytotoxic effects were observed at the tested concentration range. A True value signals that the primary endpoint result may be confounded by non-specific cell death and requires scientific interpretation caution.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; ICH S2(R1); OECD Test Guideline 129; EMA Non-clinical Safety Guidelines

attributes.name: cytotoxicity_threshold_nm
attributes.description: Concentration in nanomolar at which cytotoxic effects were first observed (CC50 or NOEC for cytotoxicity). Used to define the safe concentration window for interpreting mechanistic results.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; OECD Test Guideline 129; ICH S2(R1)

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Scientific data quality assessment status for this study result. Flagged or rejected results are excluded from SAR analysis and compound progression decisions pending investigation.
attributes.references: GLP OECD Principles; MasterControl / TrackWise QMS; ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: eln_notebook_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this study record to the corresponding experiment entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides the authoritative source of raw data and experimental narrative.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN

attributes.name: endpoint_type
attributes.description: Type of pharmacological or toxicological endpoint measured in this study (e.g., IC50 for inhibitory concentration, EC50 for effective concentration, Ki for inhibition constant, CC50 for cytotoxic concentration). Governs result interpretation and SAR analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ic50|ec50|ki|cc50|emax|hill_slope|percent_inhibition|ld50|td50|pec50 — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH S7A; ICH M10; IUPHAR Pharmacology Guidelines; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: glp_compliant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this in vitro study was conducted in full compliance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations. GLP-compliant studies are required for regulatory submissions supporting IND/NDA/BLA applications.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); OECD Principles of GLP; FDA GLP Regulations; EMA GLP Guidelines

attributes.name: incubation_temperature_c
attributes.description: Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the compound was incubated with the biological system. Deviations from protocol-specified temperature can invalidate results.
attributes.references: GLP OECD Principles; ICH S7A; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: incubation_time_hours
attributes.description: Duration of compound incubation with the biological system prior to endpoint measurement, expressed in hours. Affects the pharmacological and toxicological outcome; standardised per protocol.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: lims_sample_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Sample ID
attributes.description: Sample identifier assigned by the LIMS (LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager) for the compound sample used in this study. Enables traceability from study result back to sample preparation, storage, and chain of custody.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: moa_confirmed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this study confirmed the hypothesised mechanism of action (MOA) for the compound at the tested target. A True value supports progression to the next stage of hit-to-lead development.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: positive_control_result
attributes.description: Measured result value for the positive control compound included in this study run. Used to validate assay performance and confirm that the assay window is within acceptable limits.
attributes.references: GLP OECD Principles; ICH S7A; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: replicate_count
attributes.description: Number of independent experimental replicates performed for this study. Higher replicate counts increase statistical confidence; minimum thresholds are defined in the study protocol.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; GLP OECD Principles; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: result_confidence_interval
attributes.description: 95% confidence interval for the primary result value, expressed as a string range (e.g., '0.032-0.061 µM'). Quantifies statistical uncertainty around the point estimate for SAR and progression decisions.
attributes.references: ICH M10; ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: result_qualifier
attributes.description: Relational qualifier for the result value indicating whether the measurement is exact, a lower bound, or an upper bound (e.g., '>' for greater than, '<' for less than). Used when the true value falls outside the assay detection range.
attributes.references: ICH M10; CDISC SEND; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: result_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the primary result value (e.g., nM, µM, %, fold-change). Required for correct scientific interpretation and cross-study comparability.
attributes.references: ICH M10; SI Units (BIPM); LabWare LIMS; IDBS E-WorkBook

attributes.name: result_value
attributes.description: Numeric value of the primary pharmacological or toxicological endpoint measured in this study (e.g., IC50 = 0.045 µM). The principal quantitative outcome used for SAR analysis and compound progression decisions.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; ICH M10; LabWare LIMS; IDBS E-WorkBook

attributes.name: selectivity_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of the cytotoxicity threshold (CC50) to the primary pharmacological potency endpoint (IC50/EC50). A higher ratio indicates greater selectivity for the intended target over non-specific cytotoxic effects. Key SAR metric for compound progression.
attributes.references: ICH S7A; SAR analysis best practices; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

attributes.name: study_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the in vitro study experiment was physically conducted. Distinct from the record creation timestamp; used for scientific timeline tracking and GLP audit trail.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); OECD Principles of GLP; ICH M10

attributes.name: study_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique study identifier assigned by the ELN (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics) or LIMS at study initiation. Used for cross-system traceability and regulatory reference. Format: IVS-<ProjectCode>-<SequenceNumber>.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; LabWare LIMS; ICH M10; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP)

attributes.name: study_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the in vitro study. Controls workflow progression from planning through execution to data review and archival.
attributes.references: MasterControl / TrackWise QMS; IDBS E-WorkBook; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: study_title
attributes.description: Descriptive title of the in vitro study summarising the scientific objective, biological system, and compound under investigation. Used for search, reporting, and scientific communication.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; ICH S7A; GLP OECD Principles

attributes.name: study_type
attributes.description: Classification of the scientific purpose of the in vitro study. Drives protocol selection, endpoint interpretation, and regulatory categorisation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mechanism_of_action|pathway_modulation|cell_viability|cytotoxicity|receptor_binding|enzyme_inhibition|genotoxicity|permeability|metabolic_stability — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH S7A; ICH S7B; ICH S2(R1); OECD Test Guidelines; 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this in vitro study record. Required for audit trail integrity under 21 CFR Part 11 and GLP regulations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); OECD Principles of GLP

attributes.name: vehicle_concentration_pct
attributes.description: Final concentration of the vehicle/solvent in the assay expressed as a percentage. Concentrations above accepted thresholds (e.g., >0.1% DMSO) can cause non-specific cytotoxicity or assay interference.
attributes.references: GLP OECD Principles; ICH S7A; LabWare LIMS

attributes.name: vehicle_solvent
attributes.description: Solvent or vehicle used to dissolve and dilute the compound for testing (e.g., DMSO, PBS, ethanol). Solvent effects can confound results; tracked for quality control and reproducibility.
attributes.references: GLP OECD Principles; ICH S7A; LabWare LIMS

products.name: in_vivo_study
products.description: Transactional record for in vivo animal studies conducted during discovery to assess compound efficacy, PK/PD relationships, and early tolerability. Captures study type (efficacy, PK, PD, tolerability), animal species and strain, study design (dose, route, frequency, duration), compound identifier, dose levels, PK parameters (Cmax, AUC, t1/2, Vd, CL), efficacy endpoints, tolerability observations, study status, GLP compliance flag, IACUC protocol number, study director, and study completion date.

attributes.name: in_vivo_study_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the in vivo animal study record within the discovery domain lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58 (Good Laboratory Practice for Nonclinical Laboratory Studies)

attributes.name: compound_id
attributes.description: Reference to the compound (New Chemical Entity or New Biological Entity) under investigation in this study, as registered in the compound library or ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics). Links to the authoritative compound master record.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q6A; ICH S7A

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: In vivo studies are major cost drivers requiring cost center allocation for animal care, facility costs, and study execution. Critical for pharmacology budget management, project costing, and financia

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: In vivo studies are high-cost activities requiring dedicated internal order tracking for budget management, CRO invoice reconciliation, program cost analysis, and candidate selection economics in phar

attributes.name: molecular_target_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: In vivo studies test compounds against specific molecular targets to assess target engagement and efficacy in animal models. Adding molecular_target_id FK establishes the link to the target master rec

attributes.name: project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.discovery_project. Business justification: In vivo animal studies are conducted within discovery projects to assess compound efficacy and PK. Currently in_vivo_study only links to compound but lacks project context. Adding discovery_project_id

attributes.name: regulatory_inspection_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_inspection. Business justification: GLP-compliant in vivo studies are subject to regulatory inspections (FDA, EMA). Inspection linkage enables tracking of study-specific observations, Form 483 responses, and CAPA requirements for precli

attributes.name: study_director_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: GLP compliance mandates study director accountability with traceable qualifications. FDA inspections verify study director training, experience, and authority. FK to employee enables verification of G

attributes.name: animal_count
attributes.description: Total number of animals used across all dose groups in the study. Required for IACUC protocol compliance, 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) reporting, and statistical power justification.
attributes.references: PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; IACUC regulations; 21 CFR Part 58.90

attributes.name: animal_sex
attributes.description: Sex of the animals used in the study (male, female, or both sexes). Relevant for sex-specific PK/PD differences, hormonal effects, and regulatory requirements for balanced study design.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58.90; ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines

attributes.name: animal_species
attributes.description: Species of animal used in the in vivo study (e.g., mouse, rat, dog, non-human primate). Determines applicable regulatory guidelines, PK/PD scaling factors, and IACUC protocol requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mouse|rat|rabbit|dog|monkey|minipig|hamster|guinea_pig — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines; IACUC regulations (PHS Policy)

attributes.name: animal_strain
attributes.description: Specific strain or substrain of the animal species used (e.g., C57BL/6 mouse, Sprague-Dawley rat, Beagle dog). Strain selection impacts pharmacological response, metabolic profile, and cross-study comparability.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58.90; OECD GLP Principles; ICH S7A

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which the in vivo study was completed (last animal procedure, sample collection, or terminal endpoint). Null if the study is still in progress or was terminated early. Used for study report timelines and regulatory submission planning.

attributes.name: compound_batch_number
attributes.description: Specific batch or lot number of the test article (compound) used in this study, as recorded in the LIMS or compound management system. Critical for traceability, reproducibility, and GLP compliance — links to Certificate of Analysis (CoA) for purity and characterization data.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58.105; OECD GLP Principles Section 8; ICH Q6A

attributes.name: compound_identifier
attributes.description: Internal compound registration number or code (e.g., NCE/NBE identifier from the compound library) as assigned in the ELN or compound management system. Denormalized here for operational traceability without requiring a join. Classified confidential due to IP sensitivity.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q6A; GDPR Article 25 (data minimisation)

attributes.name: conducting_facility
attributes.description: Name of the facility (internal research site or external CRO/CMO) where the in vivo study was physically conducted. Relevant for multi-site studies, CRO oversight, and GLP facility qualification tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58.3; OECD GLP Principles; PIC/S GLP

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this in vivo study record was first created in the system (ISO 8601 format with timezone offset). Audit trail field required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance and data lineage tracking in the lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; OECD GLP Principles; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

attributes.name: cro_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the study was outsourced to a Contract Research Organization (CRO) rather than conducted in-house. Drives CRO oversight workflows, contract management linkage, and sponsor responsibility documentation under GLP.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58.10; OECD GLP Principles; ICH M3(R2)

attributes.name: dose_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency of compound administration during the study (e.g., single dose, once daily, twice daily). Defines the dosing regimen and is critical for PK/PD modeling and exposure calculations.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: dose_levels
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of dose levels tested in the study (e.g., '1, 3, 10, 30' in the unit specified by dose_unit). Captures the full dose range including vehicle/control group. Stored as a structured string for multi-dose studies; individual dose group records are managed in the study design detail.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: dose_route
attributes.description: Route of compound administration to the animals (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous). Directly impacts bioavailability, PK profile, and translational relevance to the intended clinical route. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intraperitoneal|intramuscular|inhalation|topical|intranasal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines; 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: dose_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for dose levels administered in the study (e.g., mg/kg, µg/kg). Standardized unit required for cross-study comparability, allometric scaling, and regulatory submission.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines

attributes.name: efficacy_endpoint
attributes.description: Description of the primary efficacy endpoint measured in the study (e.g., tumor volume reduction, blood glucose normalization, survival rate, biomarker inhibition percentage). Defines the scientific success criterion for the study and links to the compound's mechanism of action (MOA).
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; FDA Guidance: Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials

attributes.name: efficacy_result_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the primary efficacy outcome observed in the study (e.g., '60% tumor growth inhibition at 10 mg/kg QD', 'statistically significant reduction in target biomarker at all dose levels'). Supports portfolio review and go/no-go decision-making.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58.185

attributes.name: eln_notebook_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this study record to the corresponding experiment or notebook entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability to raw experimental data, protocols, and observations recorded at the bench.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles

attributes.name: glp_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the study was conducted in full compliance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations (21 CFR Part 58 / OECD GLP Principles). GLP-compliant studies are required for regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA). Non-GLP studies are exploratory/screening studies.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ICH M3(R2); EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

attributes.name: iacuc_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the IACUC protocol was formally approved, authorizing the commencement of animal studies. Study start_date must not precede this date. Critical for GLP compliance and regulatory audit readiness.
attributes.references: PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; Animal Welfare Act (9 CFR); 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: iacuc_protocol_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) Protocol Number
attributes.description: Unique protocol number assigned by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) approving the animal use in this study. Mandatory for all in vivo studies conducted in the US under the Animal Welfare Act and PHS Policy. Required for regulatory submissions and audit.
attributes.references: PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; Animal Welfare Act (9 CFR); 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: lims_study_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Study Reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this study record to the corresponding study or sample set in the LIMS (LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager). Enables traceability of sample management, analytical results, and chain of custody for study samples.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: noael_mg_kg
attributes.description: No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) determined from the study, expressed in mg/kg. The highest dose at which no statistically or biologically significant adverse effects were observed. Critical for safety margin calculations, human dose prediction, and IND-enabling study packages.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; FDA Guidance: Estimating the Maximum Safe Starting Dose; 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: pk_auc_ng_ml_h
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pharmacokinetics (PK) Area Under the Curve AUC (ng·mL⁻¹·h)
attributes.description: Area Under the plasma concentration-time Curve (AUC) representing total systemic exposure to the compound, expressed in ng·mL⁻¹·h. Fundamental PK parameter for bioavailability assessment, dose proportionality analysis, and PK/PD modeling.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Bioavailability and Bioequivalence Studies; ICH S7A

attributes.name: pk_bioavailability_pct
attributes.description: Absolute oral bioavailability (%F) of the compound expressed as a percentage, calculated as the ratio of AUC after oral administration to AUC after intravenous administration. Critical for oral drug candidate selection and dose prediction.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Bioavailability and Bioequivalence Studies

attributes.name: pk_clearance_ml_min_kg
attributes.description: Systemic clearance (CL) of the compound normalized to body weight (mL/min/kg). Represents the volume of plasma cleared of the compound per unit time. Key parameter for predicting human PK and first-in-human dose selection.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Pharmacokinetics; ICH S7A

attributes.name: pk_cmax_ng_ml
attributes.description: Maximum observed plasma concentration (Cmax) of the compound following administration, expressed in nanograms per milliliter (ng/mL). Key PK parameter for exposure assessment, dose-response modeling, and allometric scaling to human dose prediction.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function; ICH S7A

attributes.name: pk_half_life_h
attributes.description: Terminal elimination half-life (t½) of the compound in hours, representing the time required for plasma concentration to decrease by 50%. Used for dosing frequency determination, accumulation prediction, and species-to-human PK translation.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Pharmacokinetics; ICH S7A

attributes.name: pk_vd_l_kg
attributes.description: Apparent volume of distribution (Vd) of the compound normalized to body weight (L/kg). Indicates the extent of tissue distribution versus plasma binding. Critical for PK/PD modeling and human dose prediction via allometric scaling.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Pharmacokinetics; ICH S7A

attributes.name: principal_investigator
attributes.description: Full name of the Principal Investigator (PI) responsible for the scientific design and execution of the study. May differ from the Study Director in multi-site or CRO-conducted studies. Classified confidential as an internal personnel reference.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP (for reference alignment)

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the in vivo study was initiated (first animal dosing or first experimental procedure). The principal real-world event date for this study record. Used for timeline tracking, regulatory reporting, and study portfolio management.

attributes.name: study_duration_days
attributes.description: Total planned duration of the in vivo study in calendar days from first dose to last observation/sample collection. Used for study planning, resource allocation, and regulatory classification (e.g., single-dose vs. repeat-dose toxicology).
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: study_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique study identifier assigned by the research organization or LIMS (e.g., IDBS/Dotmatics ELN). Used for cross-referencing in regulatory submissions, study reports, and IACUC protocols. Follows the site-specific numbering convention.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58.185; OECD GLP Principles; ICH S7A/S7B

attributes.name: study_phase
attributes.description: Drug discovery pipeline phase during which this in vivo study was conducted. Indicates the maturity of the compound under investigation and the decision gate this study supports (e.g., hit-to-lead progression, candidate selection).
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance for Industry: Drug Interaction Studies

attributes.name: study_report_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the final GLP or non-GLP study report generated upon study completion. Used for cross-referencing in regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, eCTD), dossier compilation, and audit trail. Null until the study report is issued.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58.185; OECD GLP Principles Section 9; ICH M4S (eCTD Module 4)

attributes.name: study_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the in vivo study. Drives workflow routing, data lock decisions, and reporting eligibility. 'Terminated' indicates early discontinuation with a documented reason; 'cancelled' indicates the study was never initiated.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ICH M3(R2)

attributes.name: study_title
attributes.description: Descriptive title of the in vivo study as recorded in the electronic lab notebook (ELN) or LIMS. Provides a human-readable summary of the study objective, compound, and species (e.g., 'Single-dose PK study of Compound XYZ-001 in Sprague-Dawley rats').

attributes.name: study_type
attributes.description: Classification of the primary scientific objective of the in vivo study. Drives downstream data capture requirements and regulatory reporting pathways. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: efficacy|pharmacokinetics|pharmacodynamics|tolerability|safety|pk_pd|dose_range_finding|moa — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH S7A; ICH S7B; ICH M3(R2); 21 CFR Part 58

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which the study was prematurely terminated, if applicable. Distinct from completion_date (planned end). Populated only when study_status is 'terminated'. Requires a corresponding termination_reason.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ICH M3(R2)

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Documented reason for early termination of the study (e.g., unexpected toxicity, compound supply failure, scientific decision to deprioritize). Required when termination_date is populated. Supports portfolio decision audit trail.

attributes.name: tolerability_finding
attributes.description: Summary of tolerability observations recorded during the study, including body weight changes, clinical signs, and any adverse findings at tested dose levels. Informs the therapeutic index assessment and maximum tolerated dose (MTD) determination for candidate progression.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58; OECD Test Guidelines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this in vivo study record (ISO 8601 format with timezone offset). Required for change tracking, audit compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks lakehouse.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; OECD GLP Principles; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

products.name: candidate_nomination
products.description: Transactional record capturing the formal nomination of a development candidate (DC) compound for progression from discovery into preclinical development. Captures nominated compound identifier, lead series identifier, discovery project identifier, nomination date, therapeutic area, target, proposed indication, key efficacy data summary, key safety data summary, ADME/PK profile summary, IP status, CMC feasibility assessment, nomination decision (approved, deferred, rejected), decision committee, and handoff date to preclinical team. Critical milestone event linking discovery to clinical development pipeline.

attributes.name: candidate_nomination_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the development candidate (DC) nomination record. Primary key for this transactional milestone event in the discovery-to-preclinical pipeline.

attributes.name: compound_id
attributes.description: Reference to the nominated compound record in the compound library or ELN (IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics). Links the nomination to the specific chemical or biological entity being advanced.

attributes.name: hts_campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the High-Throughput Screening (HTS) campaign in LIMS (LabWare or SampleManager) from which the hit compound was originally identified prior to lead optimization. Provides full traceability from HTS hit to development candidate.
attributes.references: GLP (21 CFR Part 58); LIMS SOP; ICH M4S

attributes.name: inspection_readiness_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.inspection_readiness. Business justification: Candidate nominations trigger inspection readiness assessments for discovery sites/functions before IND filing. Readiness linkage drives mock inspections, gap remediation, and CAPA completion tracking

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Candidate nomination packages require cost tracking for the nomination process itself (committee meetings, documentation preparation, regulatory strategy) via internal orders for stage-gate cost analy

attributes.name: lead_series_id
attributes.description: Reference to the lead chemical series from which the nominated development candidate was optimized. Supports Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) traceability and series-level portfolio analysis.

attributes.name: manufacturing_plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.plant. Business justification: Candidate nominations assess manufacturing feasibility at specific plants for CMC planning, capacity assessment, and tech transfer readiness. Links discovery candidates to manufacturing infrastructure

attributes.name: medicinal_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: R&D productivity tracking: links nominated development candidates to approved products for attrition analysis, success rate metrics, regulatory milestone tracking. Critical for stage-gate retrospectiv

attributes.name: method_validation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.method_validation. Business justification: Candidate nomination triggers validation of analytical methods (potency, purity, identity) for the nominated compound. Method validation is a regulatory requirement for IND filing and ensures data qua

attributes.name: nominated_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Regulatory audit trails for IND submissions require traceable accountability for candidate nomination decisions. Links nominator to qualified employee record for verification of scientific authority,

attributes.name: patent_family_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_family. Business justification: Nominated candidates require robust patent protection assessment for IND readiness; patent family linkage supports IP due diligence, regulatory exclusivity strategy, and go/no-go decisions at nominati

attributes.name: preclinical_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IND-enabling preclinical development plan created upon approved nomination. Links the nomination milestone to the downstream preclinical program and study schedule.
attributes.references: ICH M3(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.23; FDA Guidance on IND-Enabling Studies

attributes.name: project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent drug discovery project under which this candidate was identified and optimized. Links the nomination to the originating research program in the discovery portfolio.
attributes.references: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312; Internal R&D Portfolio Governance SOP

attributes.name: specification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.specification. Business justification: Candidate nomination establishes initial drug substance specifications (purity, potency, impurity limits) that are documented in quality systems and included in IND submissions. Specifications referen

attributes.name: stability_study_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.stability_study. Business justification: Candidate nomination triggers formal stability studies (ICH Q1A) as part of the IND-enabling package. Stability protocols reference the nomination to track regulatory commitments and support shelf-lif

attributes.name: adme_pk_summary
attributes.business_glossary_term: Absorption Distribution Metabolism Excretion / Pharmacokinetics (ADME/PK) Profile Summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the compound's Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion (ADME) and Pharmacokinetics (PK) profile, including key parameters such as oral bioavailability, half-life, clearance, and metabolic stability. Critical for dose prediction and formulation strategy.
attributes.references: ICH M4S; ICH M3(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.23(a)(8); FDA Guidance on Drug Metabolism

attributes.name: cmc_feasibility_assessment
attributes.business_glossary_term: Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) Feasibility Assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of the Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) feasibility for the nominated compound, evaluating synthetic accessibility, scalability, and formulation developability. Informs manufacturing strategy and go/no-go decision.
attributes.references: ICH M4Q (CMC); ICH Q8/Q9/Q10; 21 CFR Parts 210/211; ISPE GAMP Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the candidate nomination record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: decision_date
attributes.description: Date on which the nomination committee rendered its formal decision (approved, deferred, or rejected) on the development candidate nomination. May differ from nomination_date if committee review takes multiple sessions.
attributes.references: ICH M4; Internal Stage-Gate Governance SOP

attributes.name: deferral_reason
attributes.description: Documented rationale for deferral or rejection of the development candidate nomination, capturing the scientific, safety, CMC, IP, or strategic basis for the committee's decision. Required for governance records and future re-nomination consideration.
attributes.references: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312; Internal Stage-Gate Governance SOP

attributes.name: efficacy_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of key in vitro and in vivo efficacy data supporting the nomination, including primary pharmacology results from High-Throughput Screening (HTS) and lead optimization assays. Sourced from LIMS and ELN records.
attributes.references: ICH M4S (Pharmacology); 21 CFR Part 312.23(a)(8)(i); GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

attributes.name: eln_notebook_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking to the primary Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) experiment or project record in IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics that contains the supporting scientific data for this nomination. Ensures data provenance and GLP traceability.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GLP (21 CFR Part 58); OECD GLP Principles; ISPE GAMP 5

attributes.name: estimated_ind_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Investigational New Drug (IND) Filing Date
attributes.description: Projected target date for filing the Investigational New Drug (IND) application with the FDA (or equivalent CTA with EMA/MHRA) based on the approved nomination and preclinical development plan. Key pipeline milestone for portfolio planning.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.23; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) 536/2014; ICH M3(R2)

attributes.name: first_in_class
attributes.description: Indicates whether the nominated development candidate represents a first-in-class mechanism of action with no approved drugs acting on the same molecular target. Informs competitive positioning, IP strategy, and regulatory designation eligibility.
attributes.references: FDA CDER Novel Drug Approvals; ICH M4; Internal IP Strategy SOP

attributes.name: glp_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the key safety and pharmacology studies supporting this nomination were conducted in compliance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations. GLP compliance is required for IND-enabling studies submitted to regulatory authorities.
attributes.references: GLP (21 CFR Part 58); OECD GLP Principles; EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

attributes.name: handoff_date
attributes.description: Date on which the nominated development candidate was formally handed off to the preclinical development team. Marks the transition from discovery to preclinical and initiates IND-enabling studies planning.
attributes.references: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312.23; Internal Pipeline Transition SOP

attributes.name: ip_status
attributes.description: Current status of intellectual property protection for the nominated development candidate, including patent filing status and Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) assessment outcome. Confidential business data critical for portfolio valuation and licensing strategy.
attributes.references: USPTO; EPO; ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 314.53; Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)

attributes.name: moa_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the compound's Mechanism of Action (MOA) — how it interacts with the molecular target to produce the desired pharmacological effect. Sourced from ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics) and used in IND applications and regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: modality
attributes.description: The drug modality class of the nominated development candidate, distinguishing New Chemical Entities (NCE) from New Biological Entities (NBE) and advanced therapy types. Determines regulatory pathway (NDA vs BLA) and CMC strategy.
attributes.references: FDA CDER/CBER Classification; ICH M4Q; 21 CFR Parts 210/211/312

attributes.name: molecular_target
attributes.description: The biological macromolecule (protein, receptor, enzyme, nucleic acid) that the nominated compound is designed to modulate. Central to target identification and Mechanism of Action (MOA) characterization (e.g., EGFR, PD-1, BRAF, JAK1).
attributes.references: ICH M4S; ChEMBL Target Nomenclature; UniProt

attributes.name: nce_nbe_classification
attributes.business_glossary_term: New Chemical Entity / New Biological Entity (NCE/NBE) Classification
attributes.description: Classification of the nominated compound as a New Chemical Entity (NCE) — a small molecule not previously approved — or a New Biological Entity (NBE) — a biologic not previously approved. Determines regulatory exclusivity, data protection, and CMC requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108 (NCE Exclusivity); 42 USC 262 (Biologics); FDA CDER/CBER Classification

attributes.name: nomination_committee
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the governance committee responsible for reviewing and rendering the nomination decision (e.g., Drug Discovery Committee, Portfolio Review Board, R&D Leadership Team). Supports governance traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; Internal R&D Governance Charter

attributes.name: nomination_date
attributes.description: The formal calendar date on which the development candidate was officially nominated for progression from discovery into preclinical development. This is the principal business event date for this milestone record.
attributes.references: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312.23; Internal Stage-Gate Milestone SOP

attributes.name: nomination_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the development candidate nomination (e.g., DC-ONCO-2024-0042). Used in cross-functional communications, regulatory filings, and portfolio tracking systems such as IDBS/Dotmatics ELN.
attributes.references: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312.23; Internal Compound Numbering SOP

attributes.name: nomination_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the development candidate nomination decision made by the nomination committee. Drives pipeline progression and resource allocation decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: approved|deferred|rejected|pending_review|withdrawn — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]
attributes.references: ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 312; Internal Stage-Gate Governance SOP

attributes.name: orphan_drug_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the nominated development candidate is potentially eligible for Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) based on the proposed indication affecting fewer than 200,000 patients in the US (or equivalent EU criteria). Triggers early regulatory strategy planning.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 316 (Orphan Drug Regulations); EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; FDA OOPD

attributes.name: portfolio_priority
attributes.description: Strategic priority classification assigned to the nominated development candidate by the R&D portfolio governance committee, reflecting unmet medical need, competitive landscape, commercial potential, and scientific confidence. Drives resource allocation.
attributes.references: Internal R&D Portfolio Governance SOP; ICH M4

attributes.name: proposed_indication
attributes.description: The specific disease or clinical condition for which the development candidate is proposed to be developed (e.g., Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer, Rheumatoid Arthritis, Sickle Cell Disease). Informs IND strategy and regulatory pathway selection.

attributes.name: regulatory_pathway
attributes.description: Anticipated regulatory approval pathway for the development candidate based on the proposed indication and unmet medical need (e.g., Standard, Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy Designation, Accelerated Approval). Drives regulatory strategy and timeline planning.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312; FDA FDASIA Section 902; FDA Guidance on Breakthrough Therapy; EMA PRIME Scheme

attributes.name: safety_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of early safety and tolerability findings from in vitro toxicology screens, genotoxicity assays, and any preliminary in vivo safety studies conducted under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP). Informs risk assessment for IND-enabling studies.
attributes.references: ICH M4S (Toxicology); ICH S7A/S7B; 21 CFR Part 312.23(a)(8)(ii); GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

attributes.name: selectivity_profile
attributes.description: Summary of the compound's selectivity against the primary target versus off-target proteins or receptors, derived from selectivity panel screening (e.g., kinase panel, GPCR panel). Informs safety risk and differentiation strategy.
attributes.references: ICH M4S; SAR Analysis SOP; EMA Guideline on Non-Clinical Safety Studies

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this candidate nomination record originated or was primarily authored (e.g., IDBS E-WorkBook, Dotmatics, LIMS). Supports data lineage and Silver layer provenance tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ISPE GAMP 5; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: target_patient_population
attributes.description: Description of the intended patient population for the proposed indication, including relevant biomarker stratification, disease stage, or demographic characteristics (e.g., adult patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC, pediatric patients with SMA). Informs clinical trial design.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Enrichment Strategies; EMA Guideline on Stratified Medicine

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The disease or medical specialty area that the nominated development candidate is intended to address (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neuroscience). Drives portfolio segmentation and resource allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_disease|cardiovascular|neuroscience|infectious_disease — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WHO ATC Classification; ICH E8; Internal Therapeutic Area Taxonomy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the candidate nomination record. Required for change tracking, audit compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data pipeline processing.

products.name: computational_model
products.description: Master record for computational and in silico models supporting drug discovery decisions. Covers QSAR, molecular docking, virtual screening, pharmacophore models, PK/PD models, ADMET prediction, and AI/ML property prediction. Captures model name, type, target or property predicted, algorithm, training dataset, performance metrics (AUC, RMSE, enrichment factor), PK/PD parameters (Emax, EC50, Hill coefficient, compartment structure) where applicable, validation status, software platform, model owner, and deployment status. Supports computational chemistry, pharmacometrics, and AI-driven compound design.
products.reference: QSAR / In Silico Modeling / Computational Chemistry

attributes.name: computational_model_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the computational or in silico model record within the drug discovery data product. Primary key for the computational_model entity.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer — Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: model_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: CSV (Computer System Validation) and regulatory submissions require traceable model ownership to qualified employees. Model validation, change control, and periodic review processes depend on linking

attributes.name: molecular_target_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: Computational models (QSAR, pharmacophore, docking, PK/PD) are built for specific molecular targets. The model table currently has target_name as a denormalized STRING attribute. Adding molecular_targ

attributes.name: project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.discovery_project. Business justification: Computational models are developed within discovery projects to support drug discovery decisions. The model table currently has discovery_programme_code as a denormalized STRING attribute. Adding disc

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Computational models (PBPK, QSP, QSAR) increasingly submitted to support dosing rationale and safety assessments. Real regulatory trend: FDA/EMA encourage model-informed drug development (MIDD). Model

attributes.name: algorithm
attributes.description: The computational or machine learning algorithm used to build the model (e.g., 'Random Forest', 'Support Vector Machine', 'Deep Neural Network', 'Glide SP docking', 'Gaussian Process Regression'). Essential for reproducibility and scientific peer review.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation; FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology; ICH Q8

attributes.name: applicability_domain_description
attributes.description: Narrative or technical description of the chemical space within which the model is considered reliable (e.g., 'MW 150–600 Da, logP -2 to 5, Tanimoto similarity ≥0.4 to training set'). Mandatory for OECD-compliant QSAR models; guides scientists on when predictions are trustworthy.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 3); FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology

attributes.name: auc_roc
attributes.description: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve performance metric for classification models (range 0.0–1.0). Primary discriminatory performance indicator for virtual screening and ADMET classification models.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 4); FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology

attributes.name: compartment_structure
attributes.description: Pharmacokinetic compartment structure of the model (e.g., one_compartment, two_compartment, physiologically_based). Applicable to PK/PD and ADME prediction models. Null or not_applicable for QSAR and docking models.
attributes.references: FDA Population PK Guidance; ICH E4; Rowland & Tozer 'Clinical Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics'

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the computational model record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); ISO 9001 (Quality Management)

attributes.name: cross_validation_folds
attributes.description: Number of folds used in k-fold cross-validation during model training and internal validation (e.g., 5, 10). Null if cross-validation was not used. Supports reproducibility and scientific peer review.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 4); FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology

attributes.name: deployment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the model was first deployed to a production or internal scientific environment for active use in compound design or screening decisions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ISPE GAMP 5; Internal Model Governance Policy

attributes.name: deployment_status
attributes.description: Operational deployment state of the model within the computational chemistry or pharmacometrics platform. Distinguishes models available for active compound scoring from those under development or retired.
attributes.references: ISPE GAMP 5; 21 CFR Part 11; Internal Model Governance Policy

attributes.name: ec50
attributes.description: Concentration producing 50% of the maximum pharmacodynamic effect (EC50) in the PK/PD model, expressed in molar or mass concentration units. Key parameter for dose selection and therapeutic window assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E4; FDA Exposure-Response Guidance; Holford & Sheiner (1981) Clin Pharmacokinet

attributes.name: eln_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this model to the corresponding experiment or notebook entry in the ELN system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability from the model record back to the primary scientific data and experimental context.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation

attributes.name: emax
attributes.description: Maximum pharmacodynamic effect (Emax) parameter from a PK/PD model, expressed in the units of the pharmacodynamic endpoint. Applicable only to PK/PD and pharmacometric models; null for QSAR or docking models.
attributes.references: ICH E4 (Dose-Response Information); FDA Exposure-Response Guidance; Holford & Sheiner (1981) Clin Pharmacokinet

attributes.name: enrichment_factor
attributes.description: Enrichment factor at a defined percentage of the ranked library (e.g., EF1% or EF5%) for virtual screening models. Measures the model's ability to prioritise active compounds over inactives. Critical for HTS triage decisions.
attributes.references: OECD QSAR Toolbox; Jain & Nicholls (2008) J Comput Aided Mol Des; ICH Q8

attributes.name: hill_coefficient
attributes.description: Hill coefficient (n or γ) describing the steepness of the concentration-effect relationship in the Emax model. Values >1 indicate cooperative binding; values <1 indicate negative cooperativity. Applicable to PK/PD models only.
attributes.references: ICH E4; FDA Exposure-Response Guidance; Hill (1910) J Physiol

attributes.name: is_glp_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the model and its supporting data were generated under GLP (Good Laboratory Practice) conditions. GLP-compliant models may be used to support regulatory submissions including IND and NDA/BLA filings.
attributes.references: OECD Principles of GLP (ENV/MC/CHEM(98)17); 21 CFR Part 58; FDA GLP Regulations

attributes.name: model_code
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique business identifier for the model (e.g., CM-QSAR0042). Used in scientific publications, ELN references, and cross-system traceability within IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN Naming Convention; ICH Q8 (Pharmaceutical Development)

attributes.name: model_description
attributes.description: Free-text scientific description of the model's purpose, scope, key assumptions, and intended use cases within the drug discovery workflow. Provides context for scientists and regulatory reviewers.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 1); ICH Q8; FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology

attributes.name: model_name
attributes.description: Descriptive human-readable name of the computational model (e.g., 'EGFR Kinase QSAR Model v2', 'ADMET Solubility Predictor'). Used as the primary display label in scientific dashboards and model registries.

attributes.name: model_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the computational model. Controls whether the model may be used for active compound design decisions. Validated and deployed models are authoritative for NCE/NBE progression decisions.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation; FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: model_type
