attributes.description: Classification of the computational model by its scientific methodology. Drives downstream routing to appropriate validation workflows and performance benchmarks. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: QSAR|molecular_docking|virtual_screening|pharmacophore|PKPD|ADMET|AI_ML_property|scaffold_hopping|free_energy_perturbation|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH Q8; OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (2004); FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Semantic version number of the model (e.g., 1.0, 2.3.1). Enables tracking of model evolution, retraining cycles, and reproducibility of predictions across drug discovery campaigns.

attributes.name: molecular_descriptor_set
attributes.description: Name or description of the molecular descriptor set or fingerprint type used as model input features (e.g., 'ECFP4 Morgan fingerprints', 'RDKit 2D descriptors', 'MACCS keys', '3D pharmacophore features'). Required for OECD QSAR Principle 2 (unambiguous algorithm definition).
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 2); RDKit Documentation; Daylight Chemical Information Systems

attributes.name: owning_team
attributes.description: Name of the scientific team or department responsible for the model (e.g., 'Computational Chemistry', 'Pharmacometrics', 'AI Drug Design'). Supports organisational accountability and model governance reporting.

attributes.name: predicted_property
attributes.description: The specific biological, physicochemical, or pharmacokinetic property or endpoint the model predicts (e.g., 'pIC50 vs EGFR', 'aqueous solubility (logS)', 'human hepatic clearance', 'hERG inhibition'). Central to model cataloguing and scientific search.
attributes.references: ICH Q8; OECD QSAR Toolbox; FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology

attributes.name: publication_reference
attributes.description: DOI, PubMed ID, or internal report number of the scientific publication or technical report describing the model methodology and validation. Supports IP management, scientific credibility, and regulatory submission traceability.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation; ICH Q8; Internal IP Management Policy

attributes.name: r_squared
attributes.description: R-squared (coefficient of determination) for regression models, measuring the proportion of variance in the predicted property explained by the model. Reported on the external test set per OECD guidelines.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 4); FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the model was retired or superseded and is no longer authoritative for compound design decisions. Null if the model is still active. Supports lifecycle governance and audit trail.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ISPE GAMP 5; Internal Model Governance Policy

attributes.name: rmse
attributes.description: Root Mean Square Error of prediction on the test set for regression models. Primary accuracy metric for QSAR regression and PK/PD parameter prediction models. Units match the predicted property.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 4); ICH Q8

attributes.name: software_platform
attributes.description: Name and version of the computational software or platform used to build and run the model (e.g., 'Schrödinger Suite 2023-3', 'RDKit 2023.09', 'MOE 2022.02', 'KNIME 4.7', 'Python 3.10 / scikit-learn 1.3'). Required for CSV (Computer System Validation) and reproducibility.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ISPE GAMP 5 (Computer System Validation); ICH Q8

attributes.name: test_set_size
attributes.description: Number of compounds or data points in the external test/validation dataset used to assess model generalisability. Distinct from training set; required for OECD-compliant QSAR validation.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 4); FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Therapeutic area or disease indication for which the model was developed (e.g., 'Oncology', 'Immunology', 'Rare Diseases', 'Neuroscience'). Enables portfolio-level analytics and resource allocation across drug discovery programmes.
attributes.references: WHO ATC Classification; ICH E8 (General Considerations for Clinical Studies)

attributes.name: training_dataset_name
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the dataset used to train the model (e.g., 'ChEMBL34_EGFR_IC50', 'Internal_HTS_2022_Q3'). Supports data lineage, model reproducibility, and regulatory traceability per OECD QSAR principles.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 2); FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology

attributes.name: training_set_size
attributes.description: Number of compounds or data points in the training dataset. Key model quality indicator; small training sets flag potential overfitting risk during scientific review.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 2); ICH Q8

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the computational model record. Required for change tracking, audit trail, and data synchronisation with source ELN and model registry systems.

attributes.name: validation_method
attributes.description: Statistical or experimental method used to validate the model's predictive performance (e.g., cross_validation, external_test_set, prospective validation). Determines regulatory acceptability of the model for decision-making.
attributes.references: OECD Principles for QSAR Model Validation (Principle 4); FDA Guidance on Computational Toxicology; ICH Q8

products.name: compound_supply_agreement
products.description: This association product represents the supply contract between a discovery compound and a procurement vendor. It captures vendor-specific sourcing terms, pricing, quality specifications, and procurement logistics that exist only in the context of this compound-vendor relationship. Each record links one compound to one vendor with commercial and quality attributes negotiated for that specific supply arrangement.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical operations, a single compound can be sourced from multiple vendors to ensure supply security, optimize costs, and maintain regulatory redundancy (multi-sourcing strategy). Conversely, each vendor supplies multiple compounds across the discovery library. The business actively manages these supply relationships as distinct agreements, each with vendor-specific pricing, lead times, purity specifications, catalog numbers, and preferred vendor designations that cannot be stored on either the compound or vendor entity alone.

attributes.name: compound_supply_agreement_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated surrogate key for each compound-vendor supply agreement record

attributes.name: compound_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the compound being sourced from this vendor

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the vendor supplying this compound

attributes.name: agreement_effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the supply agreement for this compound-vendor combination became effective

attributes.name: agreement_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date when the supply agreement for this compound-vendor combination expires and requires renewal or renegotiation

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this compound-vendor supply agreement. Active: approved for procurement. Inactive: temporarily suspended. Pending: under negotiation. Expired: past expiry date. Terminated: permanently ended.

attributes.name: catalog_number
attributes.description: Vendor-specific catalog number or SKU for this compound in the vendor's product catalog. Used for purchase order line item specification.

attributes.name: coa_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Certificate of Analysis (CoA) must be provided by the vendor with each shipment of this compound. CoA requirements vary by compound criticality and vendor qualification status.

attributes.name: last_purchase_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent purchase order placed for this compound from this vendor. Used to track active supply relationships and vendor performance history.

attributes.name: last_quality_issue_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent quality issue reported for this compound from this vendor

attributes.name: lead_time_days
attributes.description: Number of business days from purchase order placement to delivery for this compound from this vendor. Lead time varies by vendor based on synthesis complexity, inventory availability, and shipping logistics.

attributes.name: minimum_order_quantity
attributes.description: Minimum quantity (in grams, milligrams, or units) that must be ordered from this vendor for this compound. MOQ varies by vendor based on synthesis batch economics.

attributes.name: minimum_order_quantity_uom
attributes.business_glossary_term: Minimum Order Quantity Unit of Measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the minimum order quantity (gram, milligram, kilogram, vial, unit)

attributes.name: preferred_vendor_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this vendor is designated as the preferred supplier for this specific compound based on quality, price, reliability, and strategic relationship. A compound may have multiple approved vendors but only one preferred vendor.

attributes.name: price_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the unit price (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP)

attributes.name: purity_specification
attributes.description: Contractually agreed minimum purity specification for this compound from this vendor (e.g., ≥95%, ≥98%, ≥99.5%). Purity requirements may vary by vendor capability and intended use.

attributes.name: quality_issue_count
attributes.description: Number of quality issues (out-of-specification results, failed CoA, contamination) reported for this compound from this vendor. Used for vendor performance tracking and sourcing decisions.

attributes.name: unit_price
attributes.description: Negotiated price per unit (gram, milligram, or vial) for this compound from this vendor. Price varies by vendor based on volume commitments, purity specifications, and contract terms.

products.name: compound_exposure
products.description: This association product represents the treatment exposure event between a discovery compound and a clinical trial patient. It captures the investigational use of a compound in a patient, including dosing regimen, treatment duration, clinical response, and discontinuation details. Each record links one compound to one patient in the context of a specific treatment episode within a clinical trial. This is the authoritative source for compound-patient exposure history across the discovery-to-clinical continuum.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical development, one compound is tested in many patients across multiple trials and trial phases, and one patient may receive multiple investigational compounds either sequentially (across different trials) or simultaneously (in combination therapy trials). The business actively manages compound-patient exposure records as operational entities with treatment-specific data including dosing regimen, treatment duration, clinical response, and discontinuation reasons. This is a recognized business concept called 'compound exposure' or 'treatment exposure' that is critical for pharmacovigilance, efficacy analysis, and regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: compound_exposure_id
attributes.description: Primary key for compound_exposure

attributes.name: compound_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the discovery compound that was administered to the patient. Identifies the specific investigational compound (NCE/NBE) used in this treatment exposure.

attributes.name: investigational_product_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific investigational product formulation administered (links to clinical.investigational_product). Captures the drug product form, not just the compound.

attributes.name: patient_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the patient who received the compound. Identifies the clinical trial participant or patient in the treatment exposure record.

attributes.name: trial_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the clinical trial protocol under which this compound exposure occurred. Links to clinical.trial for trial-level context.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this exposure record was created. Audit metadata for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: discontinuation_reason
attributes.description: Primary reason why the patient discontinued treatment with this compound. Critical for safety analysis, efficacy assessment, and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: dose_level
attributes.description: Dose level or dosing regimen administered to the patient (e.g., '100mg QD', '5mg/kg Q2W'). Captures the specific dosing schedule for this compound-patient exposure.

attributes.name: enrollment_date
attributes.description: Date when the patient was enrolled into the treatment arm and began receiving the investigational compound. Critical for exposure duration calculation and safety reporting windows.

attributes.name: exposure_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this compound exposure record (active, completed, discontinued, withdrawn). Tracks whether the patient is currently receiving treatment.

attributes.name: response_category
attributes.description: Overall clinical response of the patient to the compound treatment, typically using standardized response criteria (e.g., RECIST for oncology). Captures efficacy outcome for this exposure.

attributes.name: treatment_arm
attributes.description: Clinical trial treatment arm to which the patient was randomized or assigned (active, placebo, comparator, combination). Determines which compound or regimen the patient received.

attributes.name: treatment_duration_days
attributes.description: Total duration of compound exposure expressed in days. Used for exposure-response analysis, safety signal detection, and pharmacovigilance reporting.

attributes.name: treatment_end_date
attributes.description: Actual date of last dose administration of the compound to the patient. Used for exposure duration calculation and follow-up period determination.

attributes.name: treatment_start_date
attributes.description: Actual date of first dose administration of the compound to the patient. Used for exposure window calculation and temporal safety analysis.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this exposure record was last updated. Audit metadata for change tracking.

domains.name: clinical
domains.description: Manages end-to-end clinical trial design, execution, and data management across all phases (I-IV). Covers investigational sites, principal investigators, trial protocols, case report forms (CRF), electronic data capture (EDC) from Medidata Rave, CTMS records from Oracle/Siebel, eTMF in Veeva Vault, and GCP-compliant execution. Includes patient enrollment, randomization, blinding, and intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis. Authoritative source for clinical efficacy and safety endpoints including ORR, PFS, OS, and QoL metrics. Supports IND/NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
domains.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP / 21 CFR Part 312 / EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

products.name: trial
products.description: Master record for each clinical trial (study) conducted by Pharmaceuticals, covering all phases (I–IV). Captures investigational product, therapeutic area, phase, study design (randomized, blinded, open-label), primary and secondary endpoints (ORR, PFS, OS, QoL), IND/CTA reference numbers, EudraCT/NCT identifiers, sponsor, CRO partner, planned vs. actual start/end dates, GCP compliance status, regulatory submission references (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA), overall trial lifecycle state, and key operational milestones (FPFV, LPLV, database lock, CSR completion, interim analysis dates) with planned vs. actual tracking and variance commentary. Authoritative SSOT for all trial-level metadata and timeline milestones consumed by regulatory submissions and eTMF in Veeva Vault.

attributes.name: actual_enrollment

attributes.name: actual_primary_completion_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Actual Primary Completion Date (Last Patient Last Visit)

attributes.name: actual_start_date

attributes.name: analysis_population

attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 5.2; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle; EMA Reflection Paper on Missing Data

attributes.name: blinding_type
attributes.description: Level of blinding applied to the trial to minimize bias. Double-blind is the gold standard for Phase 3 confirmatory trials. Open-label is common in oncology and rare disease studies. Impacts GCP compliance requirements and unblinding procedures.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.7; 21 CFR 312.23

attributes.name: candidate_nomination_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.candidate_nomination. Business justification: Candidate nomination is the formal discovery-to-clinical handoff event. IND preparation, transition meetings, and regulatory strategy require linking trials to their originating nomination decision. E

attributes.name: control_type
attributes.description: Type of control arm used in the trial. Placebo-controlled is standard for regulatory approval; active comparator is required when placebo is unethical. Historical control is used in rare disease single-arm studies.
attributes.references: ICH E10 Choice of Control Group; 21 CFR 314.126; EMA Guideline on Choice of Non-Inferiority Margin

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the trial master record was first created in the clinical data lakehouse Silver layer. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for audit trail and data lineage purposes. Populated automatically on insert.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); ICH E6(R2) Audit Trail; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

attributes.name: cro_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary Contract Research Organization (CRO) engaged to conduct or support trial operations. Captured from SAP vendor master and CTMS. Sponsors may delegate GCP responsibilities to CROs per ICH E6(R2) Section 5.2.

attributes.name: csr_completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Clinical Study Report (CSR) was finalized and approved per ICH E3 guidelines. The CSR is a mandatory component of NDA/BLA/MAA regulatory submissions. Tracked in Veeva Vault eTMF.
attributes.references: ICH E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports; 21 CFR 314.50; EMA Module 5 CTD

attributes.name: cta_reference
attributes.description: Regulatory authority-assigned Clinical Trial Authorisation reference number for trials conducted in EU/EEA, UK (MHRA), or other ex-US jurisdictions. Supports multi-regional trial tracking.
attributes.references: EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; MHRA Clinical Trials Regulations; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: database_lock_date
attributes.description: Date on which the clinical trial database was locked in Medidata Rave EDC following data cleaning, query resolution, and medical review sign-off. Marks the point after which no further data changes are permitted without formal unblinding procedures. Critical milestone for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: eclinical_system_study_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Data Capture (EDC) System Study Identifier
attributes.description: Study identifier assigned in Medidata Rave EDC system. Used to cross-reference clinical data collected in Rave with CTMS records and the trial master record. Enables data lineage tracing from source EDC to the Silver layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; Medidata Rave Study Configuration

attributes.name: etmf_vault_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) Vault Document ID
attributes.description: Veeva Vault eTMF study-level document identifier linking this trial master record to the corresponding eTMF study folder. Enables direct navigation to trial documentation for regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 8 (Essential Documents); TMF Reference Model; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: eudract_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: European Union Drug Regulating Authorities Clinical Trials (EudraCT) Number
attributes.description: Unique identifier assigned by the European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT / CTIS) for trials conducted in the European Economic Area. Required for EMA regulatory submissions and MAA dossiers.
attributes.references: EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; EMA EudraCT/CTIS

attributes.name: gcp_compliance_status
attributes.description: Current GCP compliance status of the trial based on internal quality oversight, audit findings, and regulatory inspection outcomes. Critical findings may trigger clinical holds. Tracked in MasterControl/TrackWise QMS and Veeva Vault.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Inspections; PIC/S GCP Guide

attributes.name: ind_number
attributes.description: FDA-assigned IND application number under which this trial is conducted. Links the trial to the regulatory submission record. Required for all Phase I–III trials in the US. May reference multiple INDs for combination studies.

attributes.name: indication
attributes.description: Specific disease or medical condition being studied (e.g., 'Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer', 'Rheumatoid Arthritis'). Mapped to MedDRA preferred terms and ICD-10 codes for regulatory submissions and pharmacovigilance cross-referencing.

attributes.name: interim_analysis_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the pre-specified interim efficacy or futility analysis reviewed by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB). Relevant for adaptive trials and trials with early stopping rules. Defined in the Statistical Analysis Plan.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; DSMB Charter

attributes.name: irb_approval_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Ethics Committee Approval Status
attributes.description: Status of IRB/Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) approval for the trial protocol. Mandatory before any patient enrollment. Tracked per jurisdiction. Suspension triggers immediate halt of enrollment per GCP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 3 (IRB/IEC); 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 4

attributes.name: is_adaptive_design
attributes.description: Indicates whether the trial employs a pre-specified adaptive design allowing modifications to the trial or statistical procedures based on interim data analysis. Requires additional FDA/EMA guidance compliance per ICH E20.
attributes.references: ICH E20 Adaptive Designs; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs (2019); EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: is_pediatric_study
attributes.description: Indicates whether the trial includes a pediatric population (patients under 18 years). Triggers Pediatric Study Plan (PIP/PSP) requirements under FDA PREA and EMA Paediatric Regulation. Impacts regulatory strategy and labeling.
attributes.references: FDA PREA (Pediatric Research Equity Act); EMA Paediatric Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006; ICH E11(R1)

attributes.name: nct_number
attributes.description: Unique public registry identifier assigned by ClinicalTrials.gov (U.S. National Library of Medicine). Mandatory for trials subject to FDAAA 801 registration requirements. Used in regulatory submissions and public disclosure.
attributes.references: FDAAA 801; 42 CFR Part 11; ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration and Results System

attributes.name: phase
attributes.description: Regulatory development phase of the clinical trial per ICH and FDA/EMA classification. Phase 1/2 and 2/3 denote seamless adaptive designs. attributes.name: planned_enrollment
attributes.description: Target number of patients to be enrolled in the trial as specified in the approved protocol and IND/CTA. Basis for site activation planning, supply chain forecasting, and budget allocation in SAP.

attributes.name: planned_primary_completion_date

attributes.name: planned_start_date

attributes.name: primary_endpoint

Defined in the protocol and statistical analysis plan. Drives regulatory approval decisions.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E8(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Endpoints

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_type

IND for US investigational studies; NDA/BLA for US marketing applications; MAA for EU; CTA for clinical trial authorisation. Links to the regulatory.submission domain. attributes.name: secondary_endpoints

attributes.name: short_title

attributes.name: sponsor_protocol_number

attributes.name: study_design_type
attributes.description: Fundamental design classification of the clinical trial. Determines statistical analysis plan requirements, randomization procedures, and regulatory acceptability. attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the clinical trial. Drives operational workflows, regulatory reporting obligations, and eTMF archival triggers. 'on_hold' indicates a clinical hold per 21 CFR 312.42. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this master record.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 312.42 (Clinical Hold); ICH E6(R2); ClinicalTrials.gov status definitions

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

Linked to the parent trial and managed in Veeva Vault eTMF. Each amendment creates a new versioned protocol record with change justification.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.rsi. Business justification: Protocols reference current Reference Safety Information (IB/RSI) for SUSAR determination during trial conduct. Investigators assess expectedness against RSI version effective at AE onset; link requir

attributes.name: trial_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent clinical trial to which this protocol version belongs. Links the protocol to the overarching study record in the CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: allocation_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of subjects assigned to each treatment arm (e.g., 1:1, 2:1, 1:1:1). Directly impacts sample size calculations and statistical power. Documented in the randomization section of the protocol.

attributes.name: amendment_number
attributes.description: Sequential integer counter for protocol amendments. Zero (0) indicates the original protocol; each subsequent amendment increments by one. Supports amendment history tracking and regulatory submission traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; FDA Guidance on Protocol Amendments; 21 CFR 312.30

attributes.name: amendment_rationale
attributes.description: Documented justification for protocol changes introduced in this amendment version. Required by regulatory agencies to assess the impact of changes on subject safety, data integrity, and study validity. Null for original protocol (amendment_number = 0).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; 21 CFR 312.30; EMA Guideline on Protocol Amendments

attributes.name: amendment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the amendment's regulatory significance. 'Substantial' amendments require prior regulatory authority approval; 'non_substantial' require notification only; 'administrative' are minor corrections. Determines regulatory submission pathway.
attributes.references: EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014; EMA Guideline on Substantial Modifications; 21 CFR 312.30

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the sponsor's internal governance (e.g., Clinical Development Committee) formally approved this protocol version for implementation. Distinct from IRB/IEC approval; triggers eTMF filing in Veeva Vault.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.11; Veeva Vault eTMF; SOPs

attributes.name: blinding_method
attributes.description: Level of masking applied to the trial to prevent bias. Double-blind masks both subject and investigator; open-label has no masking. Critical for GCP compliance and regulatory acceptance of efficacy data.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.7; ICH E9(R1); 21 CFR 312

attributes.name: clinicaltrials_gov_number
attributes.description: National Clinical Trial (NCT) identifier assigned by ClinicalTrials.gov upon trial registration. Mandatory for FDA-regulated trials under FDAAA 801 and required for publication in peer-reviewed journals per ICMJE policy.
attributes.references: FDAAA 801; ICMJE Clinical Trial Registration Policy; WHO ICTRP

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this protocol record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity standards.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: design_type
attributes.description: Structural design of the clinical trial. Determines how treatment arms are organized and how subjects are allocated. Informs statistical analysis plan and regulatory review strategy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: parallel|crossover|factorial|single_arm|basket|umbrella|platform — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: dosing_regimen
attributes.description: Description of the investigational product dose, route of administration, frequency, and duration for each treatment arm (e.g., Drug X 200mg IV Q3W for 12 cycles). Directly linked to CMC and IND/NDA/BLA submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.6; ICH M4E (CTD Module 5); 21 CFR 312.23

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this protocol version is operationally effective at investigational sites. For amendments, this is the date sites must implement the changes. Drives site notification and training requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; 21 CFR 312.30; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

attributes.name: eudract_number
attributes.description: European Union Drug Regulating Authorities Clinical Trials (EudraCT) registration number assigned by EMA for clinical trials conducted in the EU/EEA. Required for MAA submissions and EU Clinical Trial Regulation compliance.
attributes.references: EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014; EMA EudraCT Database; EMA GCP Guideline

attributes.name: exclusion_criteria
attributes.description: Conditions or characteristics that disqualify a subject from enrollment (e.g., prior therapy, comorbidities, contraindications). Complements inclusion criteria to define the eligible study population.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.5; 21 CFR 312.23; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

attributes.name: exploratory_objectives
attributes.description: Hypothesis-generating objectives not powering the study, such as biomarker analyses, translational research endpoints, or health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) assessments. Supports future study design and RWE generation.

attributes.name: gcp_compliance_attestation
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this protocol version has been formally attested as compliant with ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice guidelines. Required for regulatory submissions and audit readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR 312; EMA GCP Guideline; PIC/S GCP Guide

attributes.name: inclusion_criteria
attributes.description: Eligibility criteria that subjects must meet to be enrolled in the trial (e.g., age range, diagnosis, performance status, biomarker positivity). Defines the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) population. Stored as structured free text per protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.5; 21 CFR 312.23; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

attributes.name: ind_number
attributes.description: FDA-assigned Investigational New Drug (IND) application number under which this protocol is filed. Links the protocol to the regulatory submission record. Required for US clinical trial conduct under 21 CFR Part 312.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 312.23; FDA IND Application; eCTD Module 5

attributes.name: indication
attributes.description: Specific disease or medical condition being studied in the trial (e.g., Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer, Rheumatoid Arthritis). Mapped to ICD-10 or MedDRA coding for regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: irb_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) granted approval for this protocol version. Milestone date for site activation and GCP compliance documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 3.1; 21 CFR 56.109; EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: irb_approval_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) Approval Reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the IRB/IEC approval for this protocol version. Required for GCP compliance and site activation. Tracked in Veeva Vault eTMF under the Trial Master File structure.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 3; 21 CFR 56; EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: phase
attributes.description: Regulatory development phase of the clinical trial as defined by ICH and FDA guidelines. Determines the study objectives, patient population size, and regulatory pathway (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA).
attributes.value_regex: Phase I|Phase I/II|Phase II|Phase II/III|Phase III|Phase IV
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); 21 CFR 312.21; FDA Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: planned_sample_size
attributes.description: Total number of subjects planned for enrollment as determined by the sample size justification in the protocol. Based on statistical power calculations for the primary endpoint. Drives site activation and enrollment planning.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.5; ICH E6(R2) Section 6.9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: primary_endpoint
attributes.description: The principal clinical outcome measure used to evaluate the primary objective (e.g., Overall Survival (OS), Progression-Free Survival (PFS), Objective Response Rate (ORR)). Drives sample size calculation and statistical analysis plan.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

attributes.name: primary_objective
attributes.description: The principal scientific and clinical objective of the trial as stated in the protocol. Defines the primary endpoint and the key question the study is designed to answer (e.g., demonstrate superiority in Overall Survival).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.2; ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles

attributes.name: protocol_number
attributes.description: Sponsor-assigned unique protocol identifier used across all regulatory submissions, eTMF filings, and CTMS records. Externally known identifier referenced in IND/NDA/BLA/MAA dossiers.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; 21 CFR 312.23; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: protocol_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of this protocol version. 'draft' indicates work-in-progress; 'under_review' indicates IRB/IEC or sponsor review; 'approved' indicates fully authorized for use; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer amendment; 'retired' indicates withdrawn.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault QualityDocs Lifecycle States

attributes.name: randomization_scheme
attributes.description: Method used to randomly allocate subjects to treatment arms. Stratified randomization accounts for prognostic factors; adaptive randomization adjusts allocation ratios based on accumulating data. Documented in the protocol and statistical analysis plan.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) Section 6.7; FDA Guidance on Randomization

attributes.name: sample_size_justification
attributes.description: Narrative description of the statistical assumptions and power calculations supporting the planned sample size, including assumed effect size, alpha level, power, and dropout rate. Required by ICH E9(R1) and regulatory agencies.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.5; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

attributes.name: sap_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier or version reference for the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) associated with this protocol version. The SAP details the pre-specified statistical methods for analyzing primary and secondary endpoints per ICH E9(R1).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) Section 6.9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: secondary_objectives
attributes.description: Supporting scientific objectives of the trial beyond the primary endpoint. May include secondary efficacy endpoints (PFS, ORR, QoL), safety objectives, and PK/PD assessments. Stored as free text per protocol document.

attributes.name: short_title
attributes.description: Abbreviated or lay-language title of the protocol used in operational communications, CTMS displays, and site-facing materials. Distinct from the full regulatory title.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: stratification_factors
attributes.description: Clinical or demographic variables used to stratify randomization to ensure balanced treatment arms (e.g., disease stage, ECOG performance status, geographic region, biomarker status). Stored as free text per protocol specification.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Stratified Randomization

attributes.name: study_type
attributes.description: Broad classification of the study design indicating whether the trial involves an active intervention, passive observation, or special access program. Aligns with ClinicalTrials.gov and EudraCT registration categories.
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration; EudraCT

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Disease or medical specialty area targeted by the investigational product (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Used for portfolio planning, regulatory strategy alignment, and commercial analytics.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Full official title of the clinical trial protocol as it appears on the protocol document and regulatory submissions. Typically includes the investigational product name, indication, and study design descriptor.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this protocol record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity. Enables change detection in the Silver Layer lakehouse pipeline.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault eTMF where the authoritative protocol document is stored. Enables direct traceability from the data product record to the source document in the electronic Trial Master File.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; Veeva Vault eTMF; TMF Reference Model

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version identifier for this protocol document (e.g., 1.0, 2.0, 2.1). Each approved amendment increments the version. Used to distinguish original protocol from subsequent amendments.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; Veeva Vault eTMF Document Versioning

attributes.name: visit_schedule_summary
attributes.description: High-level description of the Schedule of Assessments (SoA) including number of study visits, key assessment windows, and follow-up duration. Detailed SoA is maintained in the protocol appendix and Medidata Rave EDC configuration.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.4; Medidata Rave EDC; CTMS Visit Schedule

products.name: investigational_site
products.description: Master record for each clinical investigational site (hospital, clinic, research center) participating in one or more trials. Captures site name, address, country, site number, IRB/IEC of record, site activation milestones (feasibility, selection, SIV, FPFV target), site closure date, enrollment capacity, GCP inspection history, site status (selected, activated, enrolling, on-hold, closed), regulatory authority jurisdiction, and CRA assignment for site initiation and ongoing oversight. Serves as the geographic and operational anchor for site-level enrollment, monitoring, and IMP accountability activities.
products.reference: Site Master File (ICH E6 GCP / CTMS)

attributes.name: investigational_site_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the investigational site record in the clinical data lakehouse. Primary key for this master record.

attributes.name: country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Sites are physically located in countries. Essential for regulatory authority jurisdiction determination, IRB/IEC requirements, site selection strategy, country-level enrollment tracking, and GCP comp

attributes.name: distribution_network_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.distribution_network. Business justification: Sites receive IMP through specific distribution nodes (depots/warehouses); GDP compliance requires documented supply chain routing. Clinical supply management uses this for shipment planning, temperat

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) assigned as the primary monitor for this site. The CRA is responsible for site initiation, ongoing monitoring visits, and GCP compliance oversight.

attributes.name: health_authority_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: Sites must comply with jurisdiction-specific regulations and inspection requirements. Site qualification, GCP inspection readiness, and regulatory compliance tracking require knowing which health auth

attributes.name: inspection_readiness_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.inspection_readiness. Business justification: Sites undergo inspection readiness assessments before regulatory inspections. Site qualification and monitoring includes tracking readiness status, gap remediation, and mock inspection results. Essent

attributes.name: masterdata_address_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.address. Business justification: Sites have standardized physical addresses. Required for site management, investigational product shipments, monitoring visit planning, regulatory documentation (site lists in submissions), and geoloc

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Sites participate in compliance programs (GCP training, data integrity, inspection readiness). Site qualification and monitoring includes compliance program enrollment and performance tracking. Essent

attributes.name: site_internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Sites incur costs tracked via internal orders for site activation, monitoring, patient recruitment, and investigator fees. Essential for trial budget management, site payment processing, and cost-per-

attributes.name: site_legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Sites are owned/operated by legal entities (hospitals, research institutions, private practices). Required for clinical trial agreements (CTAs), payment processing, insurance/liability coverage, and r

attributes.name: site_management_vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Many trial sites are managed by Site Management Organizations (SMOs) who are contracted vendors. Business process: vendor qualification for site services, payment processing, contract management, and

attributes.name: territory_msl_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.msl_profile. Business justification: MSLs are assigned to geographic territories covering investigational sites for site engagement, investigator support, medical information delivery, and IIT identification. Territory-based MSL assignme

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: Date on which the site close-out visit was completed and the site was formally closed. All essential documents must be archived in eTMF (Veeva Vault) by this date.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the investigational site record was first created in the clinical data lakehouse. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity standards.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: enrolled_subject_count
attributes.description: Actual number of subjects who have been randomized and enrolled at this site to date. Compared against enrollment_target to assess site performance and trigger enrollment support actions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC; CTMS Oracle/Siebel

attributes.name: enrollment_target
attributes.description: Planned number of subjects to be enrolled at this site as agreed between the sponsor and principal investigator. Used for enrollment forecasting, site performance benchmarking, and IMP supply planning.

attributes.name: etmf_site_folder_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) Site Folder ID
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the site-level folder in the Veeva Vault eTMF system. Links the site master record to its essential document archive for GCP inspection readiness and regulatory submission support.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 312.62

attributes.name: feasibility_date
attributes.description: Date on which the site feasibility assessment was completed, confirming the site's capability, patient population, and infrastructure to conduct the trial. First milestone in the site activation timeline tracked in CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; CTMS Oracle/Siebel Site Milestone

attributes.name: fpfv_actual_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: First Patient First Visit (FPFV) Actual Date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the first patient first visit (FPFV) occurred at this site. Compared against fpfv_target_date to measure site activation performance and enrollment timeline adherence.

attributes.name: fpfv_target_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: First Patient First Visit (FPFV) Target Date
attributes.description: Planned date for the first patient first visit (FPFV) at this site, representing the target enrollment start. Used for enrollment forecasting and site performance tracking against the clinical development timeline.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CTMS Oracle/Siebel Enrollment Milestone

attributes.name: gcp_inspection_status
attributes.description: Current GCP inspection status of the investigational site by a regulatory authority (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA). Critical for site risk assessment, regulatory submission support, and pre-approval inspection (PAI) readiness.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.68; EMA GCP Inspection Procedure; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19.3; PIC/S

attributes.name: investigational_site_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the investigational site within the clinical program. Drives CRA monitoring schedules, IMP shipment eligibility, and enrollment reporting. Values: selected (identified for participation), activated (SIV complete, ready to enroll), enrolling (actively screening/randomizing subjects), on_hold (enrollment paused), closed (no further activity), terminated (early discontinuation).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.62; CTMS Oracle/Siebel

attributes.name: irb_iec_approval_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current IRB/IEC approval for the trial protocol at this site expires. Triggers renewal workflow; enrollment must be suspended if approval lapses without renewal.

attributes.name: irb_iec_approval_number
attributes.description: Official approval reference number issued by the IRB/IEC for the clinical trial protocol at this site. Mandatory for site activation and must be filed in the eTMF (Veeva Vault) prior to first patient first visit (FPFV).

attributes.name: irb_iec_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Name
attributes.description: Name of the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) of record responsible for ethical oversight of clinical trial activities at this site. Required for GCP compliance and eTMF documentation in Veeva Vault.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 3; 21 CFR Part 56; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: is_gcp_trained
attributes.business_glossary_term: Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Training Confirmed Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether all required site staff have completed GCP training as documented in the eTMF (Veeva Vault) prior to site activation. Mandatory pre-condition for site initiation per ICH E6(R2).

attributes.name: is_lead_site
attributes.description: Indicates whether this site is designated as the lead or coordinating site for a multi-center trial. Lead sites often host the coordinating investigator and serve as the primary regulatory contact.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: last_gcp_inspection_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Last Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Inspection Date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent GCP inspection conducted at this site by a regulatory authority. Used to assess inspection recency and site compliance history for NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.68; ICH E6(R2); EMA GCP Inspection Procedure

attributes.name: lplv_actual_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Last Patient Last Visit (LPLV) Actual Date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the last patient last visit (LPLV) occurred at this site, marking the end of active patient participation. Triggers site close-out visit scheduling and IMP reconciliation.

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Primary regulatory authority with jurisdiction over the investigational site's clinical trial activities. Determines applicable GCP guidelines, inspection readiness requirements, and submission standards (IND/NDA/BLA/MAA). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|OTHER — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Parts 312, 314; EMA Regulation (EU) No 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: screen_failure_count
attributes.description: Number of subjects who were screened but failed to meet eligibility criteria at this site. Used to calculate screen failure rate and assess protocol feasibility and patient population fit.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC; CTMS Oracle/Siebel

attributes.name: selection_date
attributes.description: Date on which the sponsor formally selected the site for participation in the clinical trial, following feasibility review. Marks transition to site status 'selected' in CTMS.

attributes.name: site_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investigational site by institutional category, used for site selection strategy, feasibility analysis, and enrollment benchmarking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: academic_medical_center|community_hospital|private_clinic|research_center|cro_managed|veterans_affairs|pediatric_center — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CTMS Oracle/Siebel Site Classification

attributes.name: siv_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Site Initiation Visit (SIV) was conducted by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA). Confirms site readiness, staff training, and IMP accountability procedures. Required before first patient enrollment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.19.2; 21 CFR Part 312.62; CTMS Oracle/Siebel

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the investigational site (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London). Used for accurate timestamp alignment of EDC data from Medidata Rave, adverse event reporting timelines, and CRA scheduling.
attributes.references: IANA Time Zone Database; ICH E2B(R3) ICSR Reporting

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the investigational site record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data pipeline processing.

products.name: principal_investigator
products.description: Master record for each Principal Investigator (PI) and sub-investigator responsible for conducting a clinical trial at a site. Captures investigator name, medical license number, specialty, GCP training certification date, CV reference, financial disclosure status, delegation log reference, and regulatory authority registration. Distinct from the HCP domain (which covers commercial HCP engagement) — this entity is specifically scoped to GCP-regulated trial conduct roles.

attributes.name: principal_investigator_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the principal investigator or sub-investigator master record in the clinical domain. Serves as the primary key for this entity across all downstream clinical data products.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice (GCP); 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: ctms_investigator_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Investigator ID
attributes.description: Source system identifier for this investigator as recorded in Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS. Used for cross-system reconciliation and lineage tracing back to the operational CTMS record.
attributes.references: Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: hcp_master_id
attributes.description: FK to hcp.hcp_master.hcp_master_id — Principal investigators are HCPs — linking PI records to HCP master enables unified view of an HCPs relationship with the company across clinical, commercial, and medical affairs activities.

attributes.name: license_country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: PIs hold medical licenses in specific countries. Required for regulatory compliance verification, license validation against country-specific medical boards, Form FDA 1572 validation, and investigator

attributes.name: medical_kol_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.medical_kol_profile. Business justification: Principal investigators are frequently KOLs tracked in medical affairs for advisory boards, publication authorship, congress speaking, and strategic engagement. Same individual has dual roles requirin

attributes.name: reporter_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.reporter. Business justification: Principal Investigators are primary reporters of trial SAEs/SUSARs to sponsors. Linking PI identity to PV reporter records enables causality assessment tracking, follow-up correspondence, and regulato

attributes.name: country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the investigator primarily practices and conducts clinical trial activities. Determines applicable regulatory framework (FDA, EMA, PMDA, NMPA, etc.).
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ICH E6(R2); EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) 536/2014

attributes.name: cv_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or URL pointing to the investigator's current curriculum vitae stored in Veeva Vault eTMF. The CV is a mandatory eTMF document (TMF Reference Model artifact 01.01) required for regulatory submissions and site qualification.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 8.2.10; TMF Reference Model v3.0 (DIA); Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: delegation_log_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier pointing to the investigator's delegation of authority log stored in Veeva Vault eTMF or site trial master file. The delegation log documents which trial tasks have been assigned to sub-investigators and site staff, as required by GCP.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.5, 8.3.22; TMF Reference Model v3.0; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: email
attributes.description: Primary professional email address of the investigator used for trial-related communications, protocol amendments, and safety notifications. Distinct from personal email; should be institutional or practice-based.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 4; HIPAA Privacy Rule

attributes.name: fda_debarment_check_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investigator was last verified against the FDA Debarment List and the Office of Inspector General (OIG) exclusion database. Mandatory pre-engagement check and periodic re-verification per sponsor SOPs.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.70; FDA Debarment List; OIG Exclusion Database; FDCA Section 306

attributes.name: financial_disclosure_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investigator's financial disclosure form (FDA Form 3454 or 3455) was most recently submitted or updated. Required for NDA/BLA submissions to FDA.

attributes.name: financial_disclosure_status
attributes.description: Status of the investigator's financial disclosure form (FDA Form 3454/3455) as required under 21 CFR Part 54. Indicates whether the investigator has disclosed financial interests that could affect trial integrity. 'Disclosed' means the form has been submitted and reviewed.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 54 (Financial Disclosure by Clinical Investigators); FDA Guidance on Financial Disclosure

attributes.name: first_name
attributes.description: Legal given name of the principal investigator or sub-investigator as it appears on their medical license and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: form_1572_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investigator signed FDA Form 1572 (Statement of Investigator) for the most recent trial engagement. Form 1572 is a legal commitment by the investigator to comply with FDA regulations and GCP. Required for all IND-regulated trials in the US.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.53(c); FDA Form 1572; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: gcp_training_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Training Certification Date
attributes.description: Date on which the investigator most recently completed GCP training as required by ICH E6(R2). Mandatory for trial participation; triggers re-training alerts when approaching the validity window (typically 2-3 years).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.3; 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

attributes.name: gcp_training_expiry_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Training Expiry Date
attributes.description: Date on which the current GCP training certification expires. Investigators with expired GCP training must not conduct trial activities. Drives compliance monitoring and site qualification workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.3; FDA GCP Guidance; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

attributes.name: gcp_training_provider
attributes.description: Name of the organization or platform that delivered the GCP training (e.g., CITI Program, TransCelerate, sponsor-internal training). Supports audit trail for regulatory inspections.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA GCP Guidance; MHRA GCP Inspection findings

attributes.name: institutional_affiliation
attributes.description: Name of the hospital, academic medical center, research institution, or private practice with which the investigator is primarily affiliated (e.g., Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, Mayo Clinic). Used for site qualification and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; FDA Form 1572

attributes.name: investigator_role
attributes.description: GCP-defined role of the individual at the investigational site: Principal Investigator (PI) who bears overall responsibility, Sub-Investigator (sub-I) who assists under PI supervision, or Coordinating Investigator who coordinates multi-site activities.

attributes.name: investigator_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the investigator record. 'Active' indicates the investigator is qualified and currently engaged in trial conduct. 'Disqualified' reflects FDA or regulatory authority debarment or disqualification actions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.70 (Disqualification of Clinical Investigators); FDA Debarment List

attributes.name: irb_registration_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Ethics Committee Registration Number
attributes.description: Registration number of the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) with which the investigator's site is registered. Required for FDA-regulated trials under 21 CFR Part 56 and ICH E6(R2).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 56 (Institutional Review Boards); ICH E6(R2) Section 3; OHRP IRB Registration

attributes.name: is_debarred
attributes.description: Indicates whether the investigator is currently listed on the FDA Debarment List or OIG exclusion database. A value of True immediately disqualifies the investigator from participating in any FDA-regulated clinical trial.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.70; FDCA Section 306; OIG Exclusion Database

attributes.name: last_name
attributes.description: Legal family name of the principal investigator or sub-investigator as it appears on their medical license and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: license_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investigator's medical license expires. Triggers re-qualification workflows to ensure continued GCP-compliant trial conduct. Null if the license has no expiry.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; GCP compliance monitoring

attributes.name: license_issuing_authority
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory or professional body that issued the medical license (e.g., California Medical Board, General Medical Council UK, Ordre des Médecins France). Required for cross-border trial conduct verification.

attributes.name: medical_license_number
attributes.description: State or national medical license number issued by the relevant licensing authority. Required for regulatory submissions and site qualification. Uniquely identifies the investigator's right to practice medicine.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.53(c); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.1; State Medical Board regulations

attributes.name: medical_specialty
attributes.description: Primary board-certified or recognized medical specialty of the investigator (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Cardiology, Neurology). Used to match investigator expertise to trial therapeutic area and protocol requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS); UEMS (European Union of Medical Specialists)

attributes.name: middle_name
attributes.description: Middle name or initial of the investigator as recorded on official credentials. Used for disambiguation when first and last names are not unique.

attributes.name: npi_number
attributes.description: 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) assigned by CMS to US-based healthcare providers. Used for US-specific investigator identification, cross-referencing with HCP databases, and commercial engagement separation.
attributes.references: HIPAA Administrative Simplification (45 CFR Part 162); CMS NPI Registry; NPPES

attributes.name: orcid_identifier
attributes.description: Persistent digital identifier (ORCID iD) assigned to the investigator by the ORCID registry. Used to uniquely identify researchers across publications, grant applications, and clinical trial registries (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov).
attributes.references: ORCID Standard; ICH E6(R2); ClinicalTrials.gov registration requirements

attributes.name: phone
attributes.description: Primary professional phone number for the investigator, used for urgent safety communications, protocol queries, and site monitoring contact. Includes country code for international trials.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 4; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: prior_trial_count
attributes.description: Total number of GCP-regulated clinical trials in which the investigator has previously served as PI or sub-investigator. Key feasibility metric used by sponsors and CROs during site selection.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); TransCelerate Investigator Registry; FDA Guidance on Site Selection

attributes.name: professional_title
attributes.description: Highest relevant professional or academic degree held by the investigator (e.g., MD, PhD, PharmD). Used in regulatory submissions and delegation logs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MD|DO|PhD|MD-PhD|PharmD|MBBS|MBChB|DVM|Other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.53

attributes.name: qualification_verified_date
attributes.description: Date on which the sponsor or CRO last verified the investigator's qualifications, credentials, and GCP training as part of the site qualification or re-qualification process. Supports audit trail for regulatory inspections.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; 21 CFR Part 312.53; FDA Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) readiness

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the principal investigator master record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and GCP-compliant record management per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH E6(R2) Section 8; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the principal investigator master record was most recently modified. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+ data integrity principles

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_registration_number
attributes.description: Identifier assigned by a national regulatory authority for the investigator's registration to conduct clinical trials (e.g., FDA investigator registration number, EudraCT investigator ID, MHRA registration). Required for IND/NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.53; EudraCT; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) 536/2014; MHRA

attributes.name: sub_specialty
attributes.description: Secondary or sub-specialty area of clinical expertise (e.g., Hematologic Oncology, Pediatric Immunology). Provides finer-grained matching for complex or rare disease trials.

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_expertise
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic area(s) in which the investigator has documented clinical trial experience (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neurology). Used for protocol-to-investigator matching and feasibility assessments.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; TransCelerate Investigator Registry; FDA Guidance on Investigator Qualifications

attributes.name: years_of_clinical_trial_experience
attributes.description: Number of years the investigator has been conducting GCP-regulated clinical trials. Used during site feasibility assessments to evaluate investigator experience relative to protocol complexity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; FDA Guidance on Investigator Qualifications; TransCelerate Site and Investigator Quality Tolerance Limits

products.name: clinical_enrollment
products.description: Transactional record capturing each subject's complete enrollment and randomization journey within a clinical trial. Tracks screening number, subject number, enrollment date, informed consent confirmation, eligibility assessment (inclusion/exclusion criteria verification), screen failure reason, randomization date, randomization code, treatment arm assignment, stratification factors, blinding status, allocation ratio, block size reference, unblinding event details (if applicable), and enrollment/randomization status (screened, screen-failed, enrolled, randomized, withdrawn, completed). Supports ITT, modified ITT, and per-protocol population definitions. Authoritative SSOT for all subject-level randomization data including scheme parameters and individual assignments. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM (Randomization and Trial Supply Management) and Oracle CTMS.
products.reference: Subject Enrollment Record (Medidata Rave EDC / ICH E9)

attributes.name: clinical_enrollment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each subject enrollment and randomization record within a clinical trial. Primary key for the enrollment data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: investigational_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.investigational_product. Business justification: Enrolled subjects are assigned to specific investigational product kits at randomization. While enrollment has treatment_arm_code, linking to investigational_product provides the actual IMP kit assign

attributes.name: investigational_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site where the subject was screened and enrolled. Corresponds to the site record in Oracle CTMS / Medidata Rave.

attributes.name: medicinal_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Tracks which medicinal product each subject received. Required for product-specific safety reporting (ICH E2A), efficacy analysis by product, and regulatory queries about subject exposure in multi-pro

attributes.name: patient_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical trial subject (patient) record. Links to the subject master record sourced from Medidata Rave EDC.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); HIPAA 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: protocol_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific protocol version under which the subject was enrolled. A trial may have multiple protocol amendments; this captures the version active at enrollment.

attributes.name: randomization_schedule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the randomization scheme (schedule) used for this subject's assignment. A trial may use multiple schemes (e.g., by phase, cohort, or amendment). Links to the randomization scheme master record in Medidata Rave RTSM.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: trial_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent clinical trial under which this subject was screened and enrolled. Links to the trial master record in Oracle CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

attributes.name: allocation_ratio
attributes.description: The ratio of subjects allocated to each treatment arm as defined in the randomization scheme (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1:1:1'). Determines the probability of assignment to each arm. Sourced from the RTSM randomization schedule.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 2.3; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: blinding_status
attributes.description: Indicates the current blinding state of the subject's treatment assignment. 'blinded' = treatment assignment concealed; 'open_label' = treatment known from outset; 'unblinded' = previously blinded assignment has been revealed. Critical for data integrity and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Blinding

attributes.name: block_size
attributes.description: The number of subjects per randomization block used in the blocked randomization scheme. Confidential as knowledge of block size could compromise blinding. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM randomization parameters.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 2.3; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; FDA Guidance on Randomization

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject completed all protocol-required study procedures and follow-up visits. Populated only when enrollment_status = completed. Used for study close-out and final analysis datasets.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC CDASH Standard; ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this enrollment record was first created in the source system (Medidata Rave RTSM or Oracle CTMS). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2) GCP guidelines.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

attributes.name: ctms_subject_key
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Subject Key
attributes.description: The natural/business key for this subject enrollment record as assigned by Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS. Used for cross-system reconciliation between CTMS and Medidata Rave EDC. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

attributes.name: data_lock_flag
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the subject's enrollment and randomization data has been locked for analysis (database lock). True = data locked and frozen for statistical analysis; False = data still open for query resolution or updates. Critical for regulatory submission readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data; CDISC Standards

attributes.name: eligibility_confirmed
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the subject has been confirmed as meeting all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria as defined in the trial protocol. True = eligible; False = not eligible or assessment pending. Drives enrollment decision in RTSM.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria

attributes.name: enrollment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject was formally enrolled into the clinical trial following eligibility confirmation. Represents the principal business event timestamp for the enrollment transaction. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC CDASH Standard

attributes.name: enrollment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the subject within the enrollment and randomization workflow. Drives Intent-to-Treat (ITT), modified ITT, and Per-Protocol (PP) population definitions. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM and Oracle CTMS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screened|screen_failed|enrolled|randomized|withdrawn|completed|discontinued — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: informed_consent_confirmed
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether a valid, signed Informed Consent Form (ICF) has been confirmed for this subject prior to any study procedures. True = ICF confirmed; False = ICF not confirmed or pending. Mandatory GCP compliance check.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50.25; EMA Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

attributes.name: informed_consent_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject signed the Informed Consent Form (ICF), confirming voluntary participation in the trial. Must precede any study-specific procedures per GCP requirements. Critical for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50; EMA Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Article 29; GDPR Article 7

attributes.name: itt_population_flag
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population. True = subject is part of the ITT population (all randomized subjects regardless of protocol adherence). Drives primary efficacy analysis per ICH E9.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 5.2; ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands; 21 CFR Part 314; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

attributes.name: mitt_population_flag
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the modified Intent-to-Treat (mITT) analysis population. Criteria for mITT inclusion are protocol-defined (e.g., received at least one dose). Supports secondary efficacy analyses.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 5.2; ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on ITT Principle; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: pp_population_flag
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the Per-Protocol (PP) analysis population. True = subject completed the trial per protocol without major deviations. Used for sensitivity analyses in NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Section 5.2; ICH E9(R1); 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Statistical Principles

attributes.name: randomization_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code assigned by the RTSM system at the point of randomization, linking the subject to their treatment arm assignment within the randomization schedule. Confidential during blinded phase; revealed only upon unblinding. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: randomization_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject was randomized and assigned to a treatment arm via the RTSM system. May differ from enrollment_date in trials with a run-in period. Null for screen-failed or non-randomized subjects.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: rave_subject_key
attributes.description: The natural/business key for this subject enrollment record as assigned by Medidata Rave EDC/RTSM. Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracing back to the authoritative EDC source system.
