attributes.references: ICH E2A; Medidata Rave EDC; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: ae_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable identifier for the adverse event as assigned in the EDC system (Medidata Rave). Used for cross-referencing in CRFs, safety narratives, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Medidata Rave EDC; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: ae_reporting_category
attributes.description: Regulatory reporting classification of the adverse event: AE (non-serious), SAE (Serious Adverse Event), SUSAR (Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction), or AESI (Adverse Event of Special Interest). Drives reporting timelines and workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: ae_severity
attributes.description: Descriptive severity classification of the adverse event as recorded in the CRF. Corresponds to CTCAE grade but expressed as a categorical label for reporting and filtering.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; NCI CTCAE v5.0; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: ae_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the adverse event, indicating whether it is still ongoing, has resolved, resolved with residual effects, or resulted in death.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Medidata Rave EDC; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: ae_term_verbatim
attributes.description: The exact verbatim term as reported by the investigator or subject in the CRF prior to MedDRA coding. Preserved for audit and coding reconciliation purposes.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; MedDRA; Medidata Rave EDC; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: aesi_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Adverse Event of Special Interest (AESI) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event has been designated as an Adverse Event of Special Interest (AESI) per the trial protocol or regulatory guidance, requiring enhanced monitoring and reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA Guidance on AESI; EMA Guideline on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: argus_case_reference
attributes.description: The case identifier assigned in the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system when this trial AE is escalated to an ICSR. Enables traceability between the trial-level AE record and the PV safety database.
attributes.references: Argus Safety / Oracle AERS; ICH E2B(R3); FDA MedWatch

attributes.name: causality_assessment
attributes.description: Investigator's assessment of the causal relationship between the adverse event and the investigational medicinal product (IMP). Used in safety reporting and benefit-risk evaluation.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: concomitant_medication
attributes.description: Name or description of any concomitant medication administered to treat or manage the adverse event. Free-text field as captured in the CRF.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Medidata Rave EDC; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the adverse event record was first created in the EDC or source system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: ctcae_grade
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade
attributes.description: Severity grade of the adverse event per NCI CTCAE grading scale (1=Mild, 2=Moderate, 3=Severe, 4=Life-threatening, 5=Death). Mandatory for oncology trials and widely used across therapeutic areas.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E2A; FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: dechallenge_result
attributes.description: Result of withdrawing or reducing the investigational product dose in response to the adverse event. Positive dechallenge (AE improved on withdrawal) supports causal relationship.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria

attributes.name: ha_report_due_date
attributes.description: The regulatory deadline by which the SAE or SUSAR must be reported to the relevant health authority (e.g., FDA 7-day or 15-day, EMA 7-day or 15-day). Calculated from sponsor_aware_date.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on SUSAR Reporting

attributes.name: ha_reported_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the SAE or SUSAR was submitted to the health authority. Used to assess compliance with regulatory reporting timelines.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on SUSAR Reporting; FDA

attributes.name: initial_report_date
attributes.description: The date on which the adverse event was first reported by the investigator or site to the sponsor. Day 0 for regulatory reporting clock calculations (7-day/15-day timelines).
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: is_serious
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event meets the regulatory definition of a Serious Adverse Event (SAE) per ICH E2A criteria (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, or other medically important condition).
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: is_susar
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this adverse event has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), triggering expedited 7-day or 15-day regulatory reporting obligations to health authorities.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on SUSAR Reporting; Directive 2001/20/EC

attributes.name: is_unexpected
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event is unexpected — i.e., not listed in the current Investigator's Brochure (IB) or Reference Safety Information (RSI). A serious, unexpected, related AE constitutes a SUSAR requiring expedited reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on SUSAR Reporting

attributes.name: led_to_discontinuation
attributes.business_glossary_term: AE Led to Study Discontinuation Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event led to the subject's permanent discontinuation from the clinical trial. Critical for ITT and safety analysis populations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 312; Medidata Rave EDC

attributes.name: meddra_preferred_term
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term
attributes.description: The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) assigned to the adverse event following medical coding. Standard term used in regulatory submissions and safety databases.
attributes.references: MedDRA v26+; ICH M1; ICH E2A; FDA; EMA

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
attributes.description: The 8-digit numeric MedDRA code corresponding to the assigned Preferred Term. Used for programmatic safety analysis and ICSR generation in Argus Safety.
attributes.references: MedDRA v26+; ICH M1; Argus Safety / Oracle AERS

attributes.name: meddra_system_organ_class
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC)
attributes.description: The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) associated with the coded adverse event preferred term. Used for safety signal detection and aggregate reporting.
attributes.references: MedDRA v26+; ICH M1; ICH E2A; FDA; EMA

attributes.name: medical_review_status
attributes.description: Current status of the medical monitor's review of the adverse event record. Tracks the safety review workflow from initial entry through medical sign-off.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC; Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: medical_reviewer
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the sponsor medical monitor or physician who reviewed and assessed the adverse event record.

attributes.name: narrative
attributes.description: Free-text medical narrative describing the adverse event, its clinical course, management, and outcome. Used in ICSR submissions and clinical study reports (CSR).
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety / Oracle AERS; FDA MedWatch

attributes.name: onset_date
attributes.description: The date on which the adverse event first began or was first observed by the subject or investigator. Principal real-world event date for the AE lifecycle.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Medidata Rave EDC; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: outcome
attributes.description: The final or current clinical outcome of the adverse event as assessed by the investigator. Used in ICSR generation and aggregate safety reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Argus Safety / Oracle AERS; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA

attributes.name: rave_subject_key
attributes.description: The subject key as assigned in Medidata Rave EDC, used to cross-reference the adverse event record back to the source EDC system for data reconciliation and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: Medidata Rave EDC; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: rechallenge_result
attributes.description: Result of re-administering the investigational product after the adverse event resolved, to assess causality. Positive rechallenge strengthens causal relationship.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the adverse event resolved or returned to baseline. Null if the event is ongoing at the time of data cut.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Medidata Rave EDC; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: sae_criteria
attributes.description: The specific ICH E2A seriousness criterion or criteria met by this SAE (e.g., Death, Life-threatening, Hospitalization required, Persistent disability, Congenital anomaly, Medically significant). Multiple criteria may apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Death|Life-threatening|Hospitalization required|Persistent disability|Congenital anomaly|Medically significant|Other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: sponsor_aware_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor first became aware of the serious adverse event. Starts the regulatory reporting clock for SAE/SUSAR expedited reporting to health authorities.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on Safety Reporting; 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: treatment_given
attributes.business_glossary_term: Concomitant Treatment Given for AE Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether concomitant medication or other treatment was administered to manage or treat the adverse event.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Medidata Rave EDC; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the adverse event record was most recently modified in the source system or Silver Layer. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

products.name: trial_consent
products.description: Transactional record capturing each informed consent event for a trial subject, including consent form version, consent date, re-consent date (if protocol amended), subject signature confirmation, legally authorized representative details (if applicable), consent withdrawal date, and IRB/IEC approval reference for the consent version used. Ensures GCP-compliant documentation of subject autonomy and regulatory traceability.
products.reference: Informed Consent Form (ICH E6 GCP / 21 CFR 50)

attributes.name: trial_consent_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each informed consent event record in the clinical trial. Primary key for the trial_consent data product.

attributes.name: clinical_enrollment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.enrollment. Business justification: Informed consent is obtained during the enrollment process. Linking trial_consent to enrollment provides the complete enrollment context and enables verification that consent was obtained before enrol

attributes.name: crf_form_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.crf_form. Business justification: Informed consent may be captured via CRF form (consent CRF) in the EDC system, especially for electronic consent (eConsent) workflows. Linking trial_consent to crf_form enables traceability to the dat

attributes.name: investigational_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site where the consent event occurred. Links to the site master record in the CTMS.

attributes.name: investigator_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Principal Investigator (PI) or sub-investigator who conducted the informed consent discussion and signed the consent form. Links to the investigator master record in the CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 312.62

attributes.name: patient_id
attributes.description: Reference to the trial subject (patient) who provided informed consent. Links to the subject master record in the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 50; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: privacy_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.privacy_obligation. Business justification: Informed consent fulfills specific privacy obligations under GDPR (lawful basis for processing), HIPAA (authorization), and local regulations. Links consent management to regulatory privacy compliance

attributes.name: protocol_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.protocol. Business justification: Informed consent forms are version-controlled per protocol version. The trial_consent table has protocol_version as a string, but linking to protocol table provides the authoritative protocol version

attributes.name: trial_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical trial for which this consent was obtained. Links to the trial master record in the CTMS.

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.visit. Business justification: Informed consent is typically obtained at the screening visit. Linking trial_consent to visit provides the visit context and enables verification that consent was obtained before any protocol-specific

attributes.name: witness_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: When consent witness is an internal employee (e.g., study coordinator), regulatory requirements mandate documented identity and qualification. Replaces text field 'witness_name' with FK for GxP tracea

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes or comments related to the consent event, such as special circumstances, deviations from standard consent procedures, or clarifications noted by the investigator or study coordinator.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 312.62

attributes.name: consent_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject (or LAR) signed and dated the informed consent form, confirming voluntary agreement to participate in the trial. This is the principal business event date for the consent transaction.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.8; 21 CFR Part 50.27(a); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: consent_form_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the Informed Consent Form (ICF) used for this consent event, as approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC). Critical for regulatory traceability when protocol amendments trigger re-consent.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.2; 21 CFR Part 50.27; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent

attributes.name: consent_language
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 country subtag) of the language in which the ICF was presented and signed by the subject, ensuring the subject received information in their native language per GCP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.6; 21 CFR Part 50.25; ISO 639-1

attributes.name: consent_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this consent event, used for regulatory traceability and audit purposes. Typically generated by the CTMS or EDC system (e.g., Medidata Rave or Oracle Clinical).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50.25

attributes.name: consent_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the consent record. 'Active' indicates valid consent in force; 'withdrawn' indicates subject has revoked consent; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer consent version; 'pending' indicates awaiting subject signature; 'expired' indicates consent period has lapsed.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 7; 21 CFR Part 50

attributes.name: consent_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time at which the consent was electronically captured or recorded in the EDC/CTMS system (e.g., Medidata Rave), supporting 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA Electronic Records Guidance

attributes.name: consent_type
attributes.description: Classification of the consent event: initial consent at enrollment, re-consent triggered by protocol amendment, assent from a minor subject, consent by a Legally Authorized Representative (LAR), or withdrawal of consent.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50.25; GDPR Article 7

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this consent record was first created in the system (EDC or CTMS). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity standards.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles

attributes.name: econsent_platform
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the eConsent platform used to capture electronic consent (e.g., Medidata Rave eConsent, Veeva Vault). Populated only when electronic_consent is True.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Use of Electronic Informed Consent (2016)

attributes.name: electronic_consent
attributes.description: Indicates whether the consent was obtained via an electronic consent (eConsent) platform rather than a traditional paper-based process. Relevant for 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Use of Electronic Informed Consent (2016); ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: etmf_document_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) Document ID
attributes.description: Document identifier in the Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) system (e.g., Veeva Vault) for the scanned or electronically captured consent form. Enables direct linkage between the consent record and the regulatory-compliant document archive.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 8; DIA eTMF Reference Model; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: investigator_signed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Principal Investigator (PI) or delegated sub-investigator has signed the informed consent form, confirming the consent discussion was conducted per GCP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.8; 21 CFR Part 50.27(a)

attributes.name: irb_iec_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the IRB or IEC approved the ICF version referenced in this consent event. Consent must not be obtained prior to this date to maintain GCP compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 3.1.2; 21 CFR Part 56.109; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: irb_iec_approval_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Approval Number
attributes.description: Reference number of the IRB or IEC approval that authorized the specific ICF version used in this consent event. Ensures GCP-compliant traceability between the consent form version and its ethics committee approval.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 3.1; 21 CFR Part 56; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: itt_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject is included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population. Subjects who consented and received at least one dose of investigational product are typically included in the ITT population.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

attributes.name: lar_name
attributes.description: Full legal name of the Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) who provided consent on behalf of the subject. Populated only when lar_required is True.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.12; 21 CFR Part 50.3(l); GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: lar_relationship
attributes.description: Relationship of the Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) to the trial subject (e.g., parent, legal guardian, spouse). Required when lar_required is True to establish legal authority to consent.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.12; 21 CFR Part 50.3(l)

attributes.name: lar_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) was required to provide consent on behalf of the subject, applicable for minors, cognitively impaired subjects, or other legally incapacitated individuals.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.12; 21 CFR Part 50.3(l); GDPR Article 8

attributes.name: lar_signed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) has signed and dated the informed consent form. Applicable only when lar_required is True.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.12; 21 CFR Part 50.27(b)

attributes.name: optional_consent_biobank
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject provided optional consent for long-term storage and future use of biological samples in a biobank. This is a separate optional consent element from the main trial consent.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 9; 21 CFR Part 50.25(b); ISBER Best Practices

attributes.name: optional_consent_genetic
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject provided optional consent for genetic or genomic research using their biological samples. Separate from the main trial consent and biobank consent.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 9; 21 CFR Part 50.25(b); GINA (Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act)

attributes.name: reconsent_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject provided re-consent following a protocol amendment or updated ICF version. Null if no re-consent has been required for this subject.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.2; 21 CFR Part 50.25; FDA Guidance on Protocol Amendments

attributes.name: reconsent_reason
attributes.description: Reason that triggered the re-consent requirement, such as a protocol amendment, new safety information identified during the trial, or a regulatory authority request. Null if no re-consent was required.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.2; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent

attributes.name: source_document_location
attributes.description: Location reference for the original signed consent form source document, such as the eTMF folder path in Veeva Vault or physical file location at the investigational site. Supports GCP source data verification (SDV) and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.9; 21 CFR Part 312.62; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: subject_signed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject has personally signed and dated the informed consent form. False if consent was provided solely by a Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) without subject co-signature.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.8; 21 CFR Part 50.27(a)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this consent record in the system. Supports audit trail requirements and data integrity monitoring per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18; ALCOA+ Data Integrity Principles

attributes.name: withdrawal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subject formally withdrew consent to participate in the trial. Null if consent has not been withdrawn. Triggers subject discontinuation workflow in the CTMS.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.8; 21 CFR Part 50.25(a)(8); GDPR Article 7(3)

attributes.name: withdrawal_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded reason provided by the subject or investigator for withdrawal of consent. Captured for regulatory reporting and subject safety follow-up purposes.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.8; 21 CFR Part 312.62

attributes.name: witness_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether an impartial witness was required to be present during the consent process, applicable when the subject or LAR is unable to read or when a short-form consent is used.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.9; 21 CFR Part 50.27(b)(2)

products.name: investigational_product
products.description: Master record for each investigational medicinal product (IMP) and comparator used in clinical trials, including drug substance name (INN/USAN), formulation, dosage form, strength, route of administration, manufacturer, batch/lot number, expiry date, storage conditions (cold-chain requirements), blinding configuration (matching placebo details), IND/IMPD reference, dispensation tracking (quantity dispensed, return, destruction), and accountability log reference. Distinct from the commercial product catalog (owned by the product domain) — this entity is scoped to GCP-regulated IMP accountability, trial supply management, and regulatory compliance per ICH E6 R2 section 8.

attributes.name: investigational_product_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each investigational medicinal product (IMP) or comparator record in the clinical trial supply master. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Guideline; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: access_strategy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.access_strategy. Business justification: Access strategies are product-specific, targeting market access for each investigational product/indication combination. Each strategy plans pricing, reimbursement pathway, and HTA approach for a spec

attributes.name: brand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: Investigational products become commercial brands post-approval. Links IND/NDA submissions to commercial portfolio for lifecycle management, supply chain transition planning, and regulatory-commercial

attributes.name: coa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.coa. Business justification: Each IMP batch shipped to sites must have a Certificate of Analysis documenting compliance with specifications per GMP/GCP requirements. Essential for site accountability and regulatory inspection rea

attributes.name: compound_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.compound. Business justification: IND filings, CMC documentation, and pharmacovigilance require traceability from clinical investigational products back to discovery compound registration records. Essential for regulatory submissions

attributes.name: content_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.medical_content. Business justification: Medical content (scientific platforms, detail aids, MLR-approved materials) references specific investigational products for MSL engagement and medical education. Content approval requires product-spe

attributes.name: dmf_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.dmf. Business justification: Manufacturing processes, specifications, and control strategies for investigational products are documented in Drug Master Files. CMC regulatory strategy requires linking IMP to the supporting DMF for

attributes.name: drug_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_product. Business justification: Investigational products ARE drug products in clinical testing. Critical for IMP accountability, regulatory traceability (21 CFR 312), linking clinical batches to commercial formulations, and CMC-clin

attributes.name: formulation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.formulation. Business justification: IMP batch records must trace to specific formulations for comparability protocols, bridging studies, and regulatory compliance (ICH Q5E). Essential when formulation changes occur during development or

attributes.name: imp_cogs_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cogs_entry. Business justification: IMP consumption drives COGS for clinical supply manufacturing. Standard pharma cost accounting requires linking clinical supply batches to manufacturing costs for R&D capitalization decisions and tria

attributes.name: inspection_readiness_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.inspection_readiness. Business justification: Investigational products are scope of GMP/GCP inspection readiness programs. IMP accountability, storage conditions, and batch documentation are key inspection focus areas. Links product management to

attributes.name: investigational_site_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.investigational_site. Business justification: Investigational medicinal product inventory is managed at the site level. Each IMP batch/kit is shipped to and stored at a specific site. Linking investigational_product to investigational_site enable

attributes.name: manufacturing_batch_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.batch_record. Business justification: Investigational products used in clinical trials must link to manufacturing batch records for traceability, GMP compliance, and clinical supply chain management. This is critical for regulatory submis

attributes.name: manufacturing_plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.plant. Business justification: IMP is manufactured at specific GMP-certified plants. Required for batch genealogy, GMP traceability, regulatory submissions (manufacturing site identification in CTD Module 3), supply chain planning,

attributes.name: material_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: Investigational products are materials in the master data system. Links clinical trial drug supply to manufacturing/procurement master data. Essential for supply chain planning, batch traceability, re

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Investigational products (formulations, delivery mechanisms, manufacturing processes) are patented assets. Linking supports IP protection tracking, orange book/purple book listings, patent term extens

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.supply_plan. Business justification: Clinical supply planning aligns IMP production schedules with trial enrollment rates, site activation dates, and dosing regimens. Direct operational dependency for ensuring adequate IMP availability w

attributes.name: procurement_purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: Clinical supply procurement tracks which PO supplied each IMP batch/kit to trial sites. Essential for supply chain accountability, batch reconciliation audits, financial reconciliation, and tracing su

attributes.name: protocol_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.protocol. Business justification: Investigational medicinal products are specified in the protocol, including formulation, dosing regimen, and administration schedule. Linking IMP to protocol enables verification that the correct prod

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.pv_product. Business justification: Investigational products must map to authorized PV products for listedness determination (expected vs unexpected AE classification), SUSAR assessment, and RSI reference. Critical for regulatory expect

attributes.name: quality_batch_disposition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.batch_disposition. Business justification: Every IMP batch requires QA disposition approval before shipment to clinical sites per GMP Annex 13. Tracks release decision, quarantine status, and QP certification for clinical supply chain.

attributes.name: randomization_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.randomization_schedule. attributes.name: lab_name
attributes.description: Name of the central or local laboratory that performed the laboratory analysis (e.g., 'Covance Central Laboratory', 'Q2 Solutions', 'Local Site Lab'). Used for lab-level data quality monitoring, audit trail, and regulatory submission documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312.53; CDISC SDTM LB domain

attributes.name: lab_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the laboratory result was generated by a central laboratory (contracted central lab with standardized methods across all sites) or a local laboratory (site-specific lab). Central lab results are preferred for primary efficacy and safety endpoints due to standardization.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM LB domain

attributes.name: loinc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC) Code
attributes.description: Standardized LOINC code identifying the laboratory test or observation. Enables cross-study, cross-site, and cross-system harmonization of lab test definitions. Required for regulatory submissions and interoperability with central lab data transfers.
attributes.references: LOINC v2.77 (Regenstrief Institute); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog; CDISC CDASH/SDTM LB domain

attributes.name: method_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the analytical method or assay used by the laboratory to generate the result (e.g., spectrophotometry, flow cytometry, PCR, ELISA). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBMETHOD. Important for result comparability and method validation documentation.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBMETHOD); ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance

attributes.name: normal_flag
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the result is within, below, or above the laboratory's normal reference range. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBNRIND. Values: normal, low, high, critically_low, critically_high. Used in safety data listings and shift tables for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBNRIND); ICH E3; CTCAE v5.0; FDA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: out_of_range_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the result value falls outside the laboratory's defined reference range (either below lower limit or above upper limit). Distinct from clinical significance — a result can be out of range but not clinically significant. Used for automated data quality checks and safety signal detection.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain; ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: panic_value_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the result meets the laboratory's criteria for a panic (critical) value requiring immediate notification to the investigator or site. Supports GCP-compliant safety monitoring and timely SAE/AE reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312.32; CTCAE v5.0; CAP (College of American Pathologists) guidelines

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this laboratory result is associated with a protocol deviation (e.g., specimen collected outside the protocol-defined time window, incorrect specimen type collected). Used for ITT/PP population analysis and regulatory submission deviation summaries.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations

attributes.name: query_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether an open data query (discrepancy) exists for this laboratory result record in Medidata Rave EDC. Used by data managers to track unresolved data issues requiring site clarification before database lock.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Medidata Rave query management

attributes.name: rave_record_reference
attributes.description: Source system record identifier from Medidata Rave EDC for this laboratory result entry. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail back to the originating EDC system.

attributes.name: reference_range_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the laboratory's normal reference range for this test, applicable to the subject's demographic group (age, sex). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTNRHI. Used for normal/abnormal flagging and shift table generation.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTNRHI); ICH E3; CTCAE v5.0

attributes.name: reference_range_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the laboratory's normal reference range for this test, applicable to the subject's demographic group (age, sex). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTNRLO. Used for normal/abnormal flagging and shift table generation.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTNRLO); ICH E3; CTCAE v5.0

attributes.name: reported_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the laboratory result was officially reported and transmitted by the laboratory to the sponsor or EDC system. Used for turnaround time monitoring, GCP compliance (timely reporting of critical values), and data transfer reconciliation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; CAP turnaround time standards

attributes.name: result_status
attributes.description: Current status of the laboratory result record reflecting its lifecycle in the EDC and central lab workflow. Values: preliminary (initial result), final (verified and released), corrected (amended after initial release), cancelled (result voided), pending (awaiting analysis). Corresponds to HL7 observation status.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain; HL7 FHIR Observation.status; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: result_unit_standard
attributes.description: Standardized unit of measure for the laboratory result after conversion to a common unit for cross-site and cross-study comparability. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTRESU. Enables pooled analyses and regulatory submission datasets.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTRESU); UCUM; ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: result_value
attributes.description: The reported result value for the laboratory test as a string to accommodate both numeric and character results (e.g., '5.4', '>100', 'POSITIVE', 'NEGATIVE', 'TRACE'). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBORRES. Stored as STRING to preserve original reported value including qualifiers.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBORRES); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: result_value_numeric
attributes.description: Numeric representation of the laboratory result value after standardization and unit conversion. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTRESN. Used for quantitative statistical analyses, shift tables, and outlier detection. Null for non-numeric results.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTRESN); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: study_day
attributes.description: Relative study day of specimen collection calculated from the subject's first dose date (Day 1). Negative values indicate pre-dose assessments. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBDY. Used for time-course analyses, PK/PD modeling, and protocol compliance assessment.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBDY); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: test_category
attributes.description: Broad classification of the laboratory test panel or category (e.g., hematology, chemistry, urinalysis, coagulation). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBCAT variable. Used for grouping and filtering in safety data review and regulatory submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hematology|chemistry|urinalysis|coagulation|immunology|microbiology|pharmacokinetics|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBCAT); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: test_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the laboratory test performed (e.g., Hemoglobin, Serum Creatinine, ALT, White Blood Cell Count). Sourced from the central lab data transfer file and mapped to the CRF lab panel definition in Medidata Rave.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBTEST); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

attributes.name: test_subcategory
attributes.description: More granular sub-classification of the laboratory test within its category (e.g., liver function tests within chemistry, CBC within hematology). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSCAT variable.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSCAT); ICH E3

attributes.name: toxicity_grade
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Toxicity Grade
attributes.description: Toxicity grade assigned to the laboratory abnormality per the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading scale (Grade 1=Mild, Grade 2=Moderate, Grade 3=Severe, Grade 4=Life-threatening, Grade 5=Death). Used for safety signal detection, dose modification decisions, and regulatory safety reporting.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E3; FDA Safety Reporting Guidance; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: verified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the laboratory result was verified (source data verified, SDV) by the clinical monitor or data manager in Medidata Rave. Required for GCP audit trail and trial master file completeness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18.3; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring

products.name: trial_milestone
products.description: Transactional record tracking key operational milestones for each clinical trial, including FPFV (First Patient First Visit), LPLV (Last Patient Last Visit), database lock date, CSR completion date, regulatory submission date, and interim analysis dates. Captures planned vs. actual dates, milestone status, responsible function, and variance commentary. Supports portfolio-level trial timeline management and regulatory commitment tracking.

attributes.name: trial_milestone_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each trial milestone record in the clinical trial management system. Primary key for the trial_milestone data product.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Milestones are often country-specific (country-level regulatory submissions, country site activations, country database locks). Required for country-level trial planning, regulatory timeline tracking,

attributes.name: ctms_milestone_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Milestone ID
attributes.description: The native milestone identifier from the source Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS system. Preserved for traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational CTMS source of record.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: investigational_site_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.investigational_site. Business justification: Many trial milestones are site-specific, including FPFV (First Patient First Visit) per site, LPLV (Last Patient Last Visit) per site, and site activation/closure dates. Linking trial_milestone to inv

attributes.name: milestone_payment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.milestone_payment. Business justification: Clinical milestones (FPFV, LPLV, database lock, CSR completion) trigger contractual payments to CROs, sites, or licensing partners. Direct business process linking clinical achievement to financial ob

attributes.name: production_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.production_order. Business justification: Clinical milestones (FPFV, enrollment targets, database lock) trigger and constrain clinical supply production orders. Essential for supply forecasting, campaign planning, manufacturing slot allocatio

attributes.name: protocol_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.protocol. Business justification: Trial milestones are defined in the protocol and tracked per protocol version. Protocol amendments may change milestone definitions or timelines. Linking trial_milestone to protocol enables tracking w

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Clinical milestones (database lock, CSR completion, final study report) are prerequisites for regulatory submissions. Regulatory operations teams track submission readiness and PDUFA timelines based o

attributes.name: responsible_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Trial milestones require named accountable owners for project management and regulatory commitment tracking. Current text field 'responsible_owner' should be normalized to employee FK for workforce pl

attributes.name: trial_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent clinical trial to which this milestone belongs. Links the milestone record to the trial protocol and study-level metadata.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS Trial entity

attributes.name: actual_date
attributes.description: The confirmed date on which the milestone was achieved. Populated only upon milestone completion. Used to calculate variance against planned_date and to update regulatory commitment trackers.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the milestone completion or date change was formally approved. Supports electronic audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP inspection readiness.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); EMA GCP Inspections

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual who formally approved the milestone completion or date change. Supports GCP audit trail requirements and electronic signature compliance under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GCP guidelines

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: General free-text comments or notes associated with this milestone record, capturing additional context not covered by structured fields. Used by clinical operations teams for internal communication and audit trail documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS notes field

attributes.name: completion_evidence_type
attributes.description: Type of documentation used to confirm milestone completion (e.g., signed memo, system-generated log from Medidata Rave, regulatory authority letter, DSMB report). Required for GCP inspection readiness and audit trail completeness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GCP Inspections

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this milestone record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under GCP and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

attributes.name: database_lock_type
attributes.description: Specifies the type of database lock associated with this milestone, where applicable: interim (for interim analysis), final (for primary analysis), or partial (for a subset of sites or data). Populated only for database lock milestones. Supports data management planning.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave EDC database lock procedures; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: etmf_document_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) Document Reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this milestone to the corresponding evidence document stored in Veeva Vault eTMF (e.g., milestone completion evidence, signed confirmation letter). Supports GCP audit trail and inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; Veeva Vault eTMF; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EMA eTMF guidance

attributes.name: forecast_date
attributes.description: The current best estimate of when the milestone will be achieved, updated dynamically as the trial progresses. Distinct from planned_date (baseline) and actual_date (confirmed completion). Supports rolling forecast and portfolio timeline management.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; Kinaxis RapidResponse planning conventions

attributes.name: health_authority
attributes.description: The regulatory health authority to which this milestone is committed or reported (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA). Relevant when is_regulatory_commitment is True. Supports multi-regional regulatory commitment tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation; PMDA; MHRA; NMPA

attributes.name: ind_number
attributes.description: The FDA-assigned Investigational New Drug (IND) application number associated with the clinical trial. Required for regulatory commitment tracking and FDA correspondence. Nullable for non-US trials.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; IND application requirements

attributes.name: interim_analysis_number
attributes.description: Sequential number identifying which interim analysis this milestone represents (e.g., 1 for IA1, 2 for IA2). Populated only when is_interim_analysis is True. Supports tracking of multiple pre-specified interim analyses within a single trial.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; DSMB charter

attributes.name: is_critical_path
attributes.description: Indicates whether this milestone lies on the critical path of the clinical trial project plan. Critical path milestones directly impact the overall trial completion date and receive elevated monitoring priority in portfolio management.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ISPE GAMP 5; Oracle Siebel CTMS project planning

attributes.name: is_interim_analysis
attributes.description: Indicates whether this milestone represents an interim analysis event (e.g., a pre-specified interim efficacy or futility analysis). When True, additional blinding and DSMB (Data Safety Monitoring Board) governance controls apply.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; DSMB charter requirements

attributes.name: is_regulatory_commitment
attributes.description: Indicates whether this milestone represents a formal commitment made to a health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA) as part of an approval condition, post-approval commitment, or REMS requirement. When True, triggers mandatory regulatory commitment tracking workflows.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Post-Authorisation Commitments; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: milestone_category
attributes.description: Indicates whether the milestone is a planned internal target, a contractual obligation (e.g., with a CRO/CMO), a regulatory commitment (e.g., FDA/EMA post-approval commitment), or an internal management checkpoint. Drives escalation and governance workflows.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Post-Authorisation Commitments; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: milestone_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the milestone type within the organization's CTMS (e.g., FPFV, LPLV, DBL, CSR, IND_SUB). Used for cross-trial portfolio reporting and regulatory commitment tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: milestone_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the clinical trial milestone (e.g., 'First Patient First Visit', 'Last Patient Last Visit', 'Database Lock', 'Clinical Study Report Completion', 'Regulatory Submission'). Human-readable label used in portfolio dashboards and regulatory commitment trackers.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

attributes.name: milestone_sequence
attributes.description: Integer defining the chronological order of this milestone within the trial's project plan. Used to enforce milestone sequencing logic, detect out-of-order completions, and render Gantt-style timeline visualizations.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); project management best practices

attributes.name: milestone_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the milestone in its lifecycle. 'at_risk' indicates the milestone is projected to miss its planned date. 'delayed' indicates the actual date has passed the planned date without completion. Used for portfolio-level trial timeline management and escalation triggers.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: milestone_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the milestone by functional area: enrollment (patient-facing), data_management (EDC/database activities), analysis (statistical/interim), regulatory (submission-related), safety (DSMB/safety review), or operational (site/logistics). Supports portfolio-level filtering and reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS milestone category taxonomy

attributes.name: notification_sent
attributes.description: Indicates whether stakeholder notifications (e.g., to regulatory affairs, clinical operations leadership, CRO partners) have been dispatched upon milestone completion or delay detection. Supports automated workflow orchestration.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS workflow management

attributes.name: planned_date
attributes.description: The originally baselined target date for achieving this milestone, as defined in the clinical trial protocol or project plan. Used as the reference point for variance calculation and regulatory commitment tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: predecessor_milestone_code
attributes.description: The milestone_code of the immediately preceding milestone that must be completed before this milestone can begin. Enables dependency-aware critical path analysis and automated scheduling in the CTMS.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2); project management standards

attributes.name: region
attributes.description: Geographic region associated with this milestone for regional portfolio reporting and regulatory tracking. Used when a milestone applies to a specific region rather than a single country or globally.
attributes.value_regex: North America|Europe|Asia Pacific|Latin America|Middle East Africa|Global
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA; EMA; PMDA; NMPA regional regulatory frameworks

attributes.name: responsible_function
attributes.description: The organizational function or department accountable for achieving this milestone (e.g., Clinical Operations, Data Management, Biostatistics, Regulatory Affairs). Used for workload planning and accountability tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clinical_operations|data_management|biostatistics|regulatory_affairs|medical_affairs|pharmacovigilance|cro|cmdo|quality — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; GCP guidelines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this milestone record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements under GCP and 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks lakehouse.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

attributes.name: variance_commentary
attributes.description: Free-text narrative explaining the reason for any deviation between planned and actual/forecast milestone dates. Captures context not covered by variance_reason_code, including mitigation actions taken. Required for regulatory commitment reporting to FDA/EMA.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) No 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: variance_days
attributes.description: Signed integer representing the difference in calendar days between the actual (or forecast) date and the planned date. Positive values indicate delay; negative values indicate early completion. Stored as a business field to support regulatory commitment reporting without requiring runtime calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Post-Authorisation Commitments

attributes.name: variance_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code categorizing the root cause of any milestone variance. Used for portfolio-level trend analysis and process improvement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: site_activation_delay|enrollment_shortfall|protocol_amendment|regulatory_hold|safety_event|data_quality|resource_constraint|vendor_delay|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ISPE GAMP 5

products.name: biospecimen
products.description: Transactional record for each biological specimen (tissue biopsy, blood draw, urine, CSF) collected from a trial subject at protocol-defined timepoints. Captures specimen type, collection date, collection visit, tube/container type, volume/quantity, processing method, storage temperature, biobank location, shipment tracking to central lab, LOINC/SNOMED coding, chain-of-custody audit trail, and associated assay results reference. Critical for oncology trials requiring RECIST tumor assessments, pharmacogenomic stratification, companion diagnostic validation, and translational research endpoints. Sourced from LIMS integration with Medidata Rave EDC.

attributes.name: collection_date
attributes.description: The date on which the biospecimen was collected from the trial subject. Critical for protocol compliance and time-to-event analysis.

attributes.name: collection_method

attributes.name: collection_timestamp

attributes.name: collection_visit_name

attributes.name: consent_genetic_testing_flag

attributes.name: container_type
attributes.description: The type of tube or container used for specimen collection, such as EDTA tube, serum separator tube, cryovial. Critical for ensuring proper specimen handling and assay validity.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this biospecimen record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: deviation_description

attributes.name: fasting_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subject was fasting at the time of specimen collection. Critical for certain laboratory tests such as glucose and lipid panels.

attributes.name: loinc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC) Code
attributes.description: The standardized LOINC code representing the specimen type and associated test. Enables interoperability with laboratory information systems and regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: processing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the specimen was processed in the laboratory. Used to track time from collection to processing for quality control.

attributes.name: processing_method
attributes.description: The method used to process the specimen after collection, such as centrifugation, aliquoting, or fixation. Ensures traceability of specimen handling procedures.

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the specimen collection deviated from the protocol-defined procedures. True if a deviation occurred, False otherwise.

attributes.name: received_date
attributes.description: The date on which the specimen was received at the central laboratory or biobank. Used to verify shipment integrity and processing timelines.

attributes.name: shipment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the specimen was shipped to the central laboratory or biobank. Used to track transit time and ensure cold chain compliance.

attributes.name: shipment_tracking_number
attributes.description: The tracking number assigned to the shipment when the specimen was sent to a central laboratory or biobank. Supports chain-of-custody documentation.

attributes.name: snomed_code
attributes.description: The standardized SNOMED CT code representing the specimen type or anatomical source. Supports clinical terminology standardization and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: specimen_number
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the biospecimen, typically a barcode or alphanumeric code assigned at collection. Used for chain-of-custody tracking and laboratory processing.

attributes.name: specimen_quality
attributes.description: Assessment of the specimen quality upon receipt or processing. Identifies any conditions that may affect assay results or specimen usability.

attributes.name: specimen_status
attributes.description: The current lifecycle status of the biospecimen, indicating its stage in the collection, processing, storage, and analysis workflow. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: collected|processed|stored|shipped|received|analyzed|depleted|discarded — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: specimen_subtype
attributes.description: Further classification or detail of the specimen type, such as specific tissue origin or blood component. Provides granular categorization for specialized assays.

attributes.name: specimen_type
attributes.description: Classification of the biological specimen collected. Defines the nature of the sample for processing and analysis requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: blood|serum|plasma|urine|tissue|csf|saliva|bone_marrow|tumor_biopsy — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: LOINC, SNOMED CT, CDISC SDTM LB Domain

attributes.name: storage_temperature
attributes.description: The temperature condition under which the specimen is stored, such as room temperature, refrigerated (2-8°C), frozen at -20°C, frozen at -80°C, or in liquid nitrogen. Critical for specimen stability and assay integrity.

attributes.name: study_day
attributes.description: The day relative to the reference date (typically first dose or randomization) on which the specimen was collected. Negative values indicate pre-treatment, positive values indicate post-treatment.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this biospecimen record was last modified in the system. Supports audit trail and change tracking for regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: volume_collected
attributes.description: The quantity of specimen collected, measured in the unit specified in volume_unit. Used to determine sufficiency for planned assays.

attributes.name: parent_biospecimen_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on biospecimen (parent_biospecimen_id)

Tracks resolution status of prior visit findings. Core operational record for GCP oversight per ICH E6 R2 section 5.18 and supports risk-based monitoring (RBM) strategies.

attributes.name: employee_id

attributes.name: monitoring_accounts_payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: CRA monitoring visits generate travel, accommodation, and expense AP entries. Essential for trial budget management, CRO invoice reconciliation, and monitoring cost tracking per site and protocol.

attributes.name: principal_investigator_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.principal_investigator. Business justification: Monitoring visits include meetings with the principal investigator to review site performance and compliance. Linking monitoring_visit to principal_investigator enables tracking which PI was met with

attributes.name: protocol_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to clinical.protocol. Business justification: Monitoring visits verify site compliance with the specific protocol version in effect at the time of the visit. Protocol amendments may change monitoring requirements. Linking monitoring_visit to prot

attributes.name: trial_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical trial under which this monitoring visit was conducted.

attributes.name: actual_visit_date
attributes.description: The date on which the monitoring visit actually occurred. Primary business event timestamp for the monitoring activity.

attributes.name: ae_reporting_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether adverse event (AE) and serious adverse event (SAE) reporting was reviewed for completeness, accuracy, and timeliness during the monitoring visit. AE reporting is a critical safety requirement.

attributes.name: capa_items_raised
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Items Raised
attributes.description: Number of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) items initiated as a result of findings from this monitoring visit. CAPA items track remediation activities required to address identified deficiencies.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Additional free-text comments, observations, or contextual information about the monitoring visit that do not fit into structured fields. May include site feedback, logistical notes, or follow-up action items.

attributes.name: cra_name
attributes.description: Full name of the Clinical Research Associate who performed the monitoring visit. Captured for audit trail and accountability purposes.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp indicating when this monitoring visit record was first created in the data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: critical_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of critical findings identified during the monitoring visit. Critical findings represent major deviations from GCP, protocol, or regulatory requirements that pose significant risk to subject safety, data integrity, or trial validity.

attributes.name: etmf_document_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) Document Identifier (ID)
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the monitoring visit report and related documents in the electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) system, typically Veeva Vault eTMF.

attributes.name: findings_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of key findings, observations, and issues identified during the monitoring visit. Provides context for the quantitative finding counts and highlights areas requiring attention.

attributes.name: follow_up_letter_date
attributes.description: Date on which the formal monitoring visit follow-up letter was issued to the investigational site. The follow-up letter documents findings, required actions, and timelines for resolution.

attributes.name: gcp_compliance_status
attributes.description: Overall assessment of the investigational sites compliance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards based on observations during the monitoring visit. GCP compliance is mandatory for regulatory acceptance of trial data.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) - Good Clinical Practice Guidelines

attributes.name: informed_consent_verified_count
attributes.description: Number of informed consent forms reviewed and verified for completeness, signatures, and regulatory compliance during the visit.

attributes.name: investigator_meeting_held
attributes.description: Indicates whether a face-to-face meeting was conducted with the principal investigator during the monitoring visit to discuss trial progress, findings, and site performance.

attributes.name: ip_accountability_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether investigational product (IP) accountability records were reviewed and verified during the visit. IP accountability ensures proper receipt, storage, dispensing, and return/destruction of study drug.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.14 - Investigational Product Accountability

attributes.name: major_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of major findings identified during the monitoring visit. Major findings represent significant deviations that require corrective action but do not immediately threaten subject safety or data integrity.

attributes.name: minor_findings_count
attributes.description: Number of minor findings or observations identified during the monitoring visit. Minor findings represent low-impact deviations or areas for improvement that do not significantly affect trial conduct.

attributes.name: monitoring_report_date
attributes.description: Date on which the formal monitoring visit report was completed and submitted. The monitoring report is a GCP-required document that summarizes visit activities, findings, and recommendations.

attributes.name: monitoring_report_reference
attributes.description: Document reference or identifier for the formal monitoring visit report stored in the Trial Master File (TMF) or electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) system.

attributes.name: prior_capa_resolved_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Prior Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Resolved Count
attributes.description: Number of CAPA items from previous monitoring visits that were verified as resolved during this visit. Tracks effectiveness of corrective actions and continuous improvement.

attributes.name: protocol_deviations_identified
attributes.description: Number of protocol deviations identified during the monitoring visit. Protocol deviations represent departures from the approved study protocol that may affect subject safety, data integrity, or trial outcomes.

attributes.name: regulatory_binder_reviewed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the site regulatory binder (containing essential documents such as IRB approvals, investigator CVs, licenses, and training records) was reviewed for completeness and currency during the visit.

attributes.name: risk_score_change
attributes.description: Direction of change in the site risk score compared to the previous assessment. Indicates whether site performance and compliance are improving, deteriorating, or stable.

attributes.name: scheduled_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the monitoring visit as defined in the monitoring plan or risk-based monitoring (RBM) strategy.

attributes.name: sdv_completion_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of case report form (CRF) data points verified against source documents during this monitoring visit. SDV is a core GCP requirement to ensure data accuracy and integrity.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.4(e) - Source Data Verification

attributes.name: site_risk_score
attributes.description: Updated risk score for the investigational site following the monitoring visit. Risk scores inform risk-based monitoring (RBM) strategies and determine frequency and intensity of future monitoring activities.

attributes.name: subjects_reviewed_count
attributes.description: Number of enrolled subjects whose records were reviewed during this monitoring visit for protocol compliance, data quality, and safety assessment.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp indicating when this monitoring visit record was last modified in the data platform. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: visit_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the monitoring visit concluded at the investigational site.

attributes.name: visit_mode
attributes.description: Method by which the monitoring visit was conducted. On-site visits involve physical presence at the investigational site, remote visits use electronic systems and telecommunications, and hybrid visits combine both approaches.

attributes.name: visit_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the monitoring visit commenced at the investigational site.

attributes.name: followup_monitoring_visit_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on monitoring_visit (followup_monitoring_visit_id)

attributes.name: block_size

attributes.name: codes_remaining

attributes.description: Free-text comments or notes regarding the randomization schedule configuration, validation, or operational considerations.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: deactivation_date

attributes.name: etmf_document_reference

attributes.description: Reference to the randomization schedule document stored in the eTMF system (e.g., Veeva Vault eTMF).

attributes.name: iwrs_configuration_reference

attributes.description: Configuration identifier or reference code in the IWRS/IRT system for this randomization schedule.

attributes.name: iwrs_system_name

attributes.description: Name of the IWRS or IRT system used to manage randomization and treatment allocation (e.g., Medidata Rave RTSM, Oracle InForm IWRS).

attributes.name: randomization_list_location

attributes.name: randomization_type

attributes.name: treatment_arm_count

attributes.name: unblinding_procedure
