products.name: imp_administration
products.description: This association product represents the administration event between investigational_product and visit. It captures each instance of IMP dispensation to a trial subject during a clinical visit, documenting regulatory-required accountability data per ICH E6 R2 and 21 CFR Part 312. Each record links one investigational product (specific batch/lot) to one patient visit with administration-specific attributes including timestamp, dose, route, and deviation tracking that exist only in the context of this administration event.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trials, investigational medicinal product (IMP) administration is a core regulatory-mandated business process. A single IMP batch can be administered across multiple patient visits (different subjects, different timepoints), and a single patient visit can involve administration of multiple IMPs (combination therapies, dose escalation, or comparator plus active treatment). Each administration event is a distinct regulatory record with its own timestamp, dose, route, lot traceability, and deviation tracking per ICH E6 R2 and 21 CFR Part 312.

attributes.name: imp_administration_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each IMP administration event record

attributes.name: administered_by_investigator_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigator or qualified designee who administered or supervised the IMP administration

attributes.name: investigational_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the specific investigational medicinal product (IMP) batch administered at this visit

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the patient visit during which this IMP administration occurred

attributes.name: accountability_log_entry
attributes.description: Reference to the corresponding entry in the IMP accountability log maintained at the investigational site

attributes.name: administration_deviation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a protocol deviation occurred during this IMP administration (wrong dose, wrong time, wrong route, etc.)

attributes.name: administration_status
attributes.description: Status of this administration event: administered (full dose given), partially_administered, not_administered (subject refused or clinically contraindicated), returned (subject returned unused IMP), destroyed (IMP disposed per protocol)

attributes.name: administration_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the investigational product was administered to the subject, as recorded in source documents and EDC

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this IMP administration record was first created in the EDC system

attributes.name: deviation_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the protocol deviation related to this IMP administration, if deviation_flag is true

attributes.name: dose_administered
attributes.description: Quantity of IMP administered to the subject at this visit, expressed in the dose unit

attributes.name: dose_number
attributes.description: The sequential dose number administered to the subject at this visit, as recorded in the EDC (Medidata Rave). Null for non-dosing visits. Supports cumulative exposure and dose-response analysis. [Moved from visit: The dose_number attribute in visit represents the sequential dose count for the subject, which is actually a property of the administration event (the relationship between IMP and visit), not an intrinsic property of the visit itself. Multiple IMPs could be administered at a single visit, each with its own dose sequence.]
attributes.references: CDISC CDASH EX Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: dose_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the administered dose (mg, mL, tablets, capsules, units, mcg, g)

attributes.name: kit_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the IMP dispensation kit from which this dose was taken, linking to the randomization and supply chain

attributes.name: lot_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer batch or lot number of the specific IMP unit administered, required for drug accountability and traceability

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Route by which the IMP was administered (oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical, etc.) per protocol specifications

attributes.name: study_drug_administered_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the investigational medicinal product (IMP) or study drug was administered to the subject at this visit (True) or not (False). Supports exposure analysis and Intent-to-Treat (ITT) population derivation. [Moved from visit: This boolean flag in visit is a summary indicator that becomes redundant once the detailed imp_administration association exists. The flag can be derived by checking if any imp_administration records exist for the visit. The detailed administration records in the association provide the complete regulatory-required documentation.]
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC CDASH EX Domain; ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this IMP administration record, supporting audit trail requirements

products.name: site_imp_accountability
products.description: This association product represents the accountability relationship between investigational sites and inventory lots of Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP). It captures the regulatory-mandated tracking of IMP receipt, dispensation, return, and storage at each clinical site. Each record links one investigational site to one inventory lot with attributes that exist only in the context of this site-specific lot accountability. Required under ICH GCP E6 and GDP regulations for clinical trial material traceability.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trials, investigational sites receive multiple IMP lots over the trial duration due to resupply cycles, different batch releases, and enrollment progression. Each IMP lot is distributed to multiple sites based on enrollment forecasts and geographic distribution. Site-level IMP accountability is a regulatory-mandated business process under ICH GCP E6 and GDP, where Clinical Research Associates actively create, monitor, and reconcile site-lot accountability records during monitoring visits.

attributes.name: quarantine_quantity

attributes.name: received_quantity

attributes.name: returned_quantity

attributes.name: shipment_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the IMP shipment that delivered this lot to the site, linking to depot shipment records and temperature monitoring data

attributes.name: storage_location
attributes.description: Site-specific storage location identifier where this IMP lot is held (e.g., pharmacy refrigerator ID, secure cabinet number), documented during site initiation and verified during monitoring visits

attributes.name: temperature_excursion_flag

products.name: site_affiliation
products.description: This association product represents the affiliation relationship between investigational sites and healthcare professionals. It captures the operational reality that HCPs hold privileges, credentials, and roles at multiple clinical sites, and sites maintain rosters of affiliated physicians for trial enrollment capacity planning. Each record links one investigational site to one HCP with attributes that govern the HCP's ability to serve as investigator, enroll patients, and perform protocol procedures at that specific site.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trials, investigational sites maintain rosters of multiple affiliated physicians with varying roles (Principal Investigator, Sub-Investigator, site staff), and healthcare professionals hold privileges and credentials at multiple sites simultaneously. Site feasibility assessments require understanding which HCPs can enroll patients at which sites, and HCPs leverage multi-site affiliations for patient referral networks. This is an operational relationship actively managed through credentialing workflows, delegation of authority documentation, and site activation processes.

attributes.name: site_affiliation_id

attributes.name: affiliation_start_date

attributes.name: affiliation_type

attributes.name: credentialing_status
attributes.description: Current status of the HCP's credentialing process at this investigational site. Must be 'Credentialed' before HCP can perform protocol procedures or enroll subjects. Tracked per site per HCP.

attributes.name: department_name

attributes.name: enrollment_authority_flag

products.name: trial_investigator
products.description: This association product represents the investigator assignment relationship between clinical trials and healthcare professionals. It captures the operational assignment of HCPs to trials in investigator roles (Principal Investigator, Sub-Investigator, Study Coordinator), including GCP training compliance, financial disclosure status, site-specific responsibilities, delegation of authority, and enrollment accountability. Each record links one trial to one HCP with role-specific attributes that exist only in the context of this investigator assignment. Authoritative SSOT for investigator rosters required for regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA) and eTMF documentation in Veeva Vault.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trial operations, a single trial requires multiple investigators across sites (Principal Investigators, Sub-Investigators, Study Coordinators), and a single HCP routinely serves as investigator on multiple concurrent trials. The investigator assignment is an operational business entity actively managed by clinical operations teams: assignments are created during site activation, updated as roles/responsibilities change, and tracked throughout the trial lifecycle. The relationship carries substantial operational data (role, GCP training status, financial disclosures, delegation logs, enrollment counts) that belongs to neither the trial nor the HCP alone, but to the specific assignment.

attributes.name: trial_investigator_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each trial-investigator assignment record. Primary key for the association.

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the healthcare professional serving as investigator on this trial

attributes.name: trial_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the clinical trial for which this HCP serves as investigator

attributes.name: assignment_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this HCP's investigator assignment on this trial ended (site closure, investigator departure, trial completion). Null for active assignments. Used for historical investigator portfolio tracking and conflict-of-interest screening.

attributes.name: assignment_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this HCP was assigned to this trial as an investigator. Typically corresponds to site activation date or investigator onboarding completion. Used for investigator tenure tracking and workload analysis.

attributes.name: cv_on_file_date
attributes.description: Date when the investigator's current CV was received and filed in the eTMF for this trial. Required regulatory document per ICH-GCP. Must be updated if investigator credentials change during trial.

attributes.name: delegation_log_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or document ID for the Delegation of Authority Log entry that authorizes this investigator to perform specific trial activities. Required per ICH-GCP for all trial staff. Links to eTMF document management system (Veeva Vault).

attributes.name: enrollment_responsibility
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this investigator has patient enrollment responsibilities for this trial. Principal Investigators typically have enrollment responsibility; some Sub-Investigators and Coordinators may not. Drives enrollment tracking and site performance metrics.

attributes.name: financial_disclosure_status
attributes.description: Status of FDA Form 3454 (Financial Disclosure) submission and review for this investigator on this trial. Required for all covered clinical studies per 21 CFR Part 54. Conflict Identified triggers sponsor review and potential investigator exclusion from trial.

attributes.name: financial_disclosure_submission_date
attributes.description: Date when the investigator submitted financial disclosure documentation for this trial. Required for regulatory submission timelines.

attributes.name: gcp_training_date
attributes.description: Date when this HCP completed Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training specific to this trial or valid for this trial period. Required before investigator can perform any trial-related activities per ICH-GCP. Must be renewed periodically (typically every 2-3 years).

attributes.name: gcp_training_expiration_date
attributes.description: Expiration date of the GCP training certification for this investigator on this trial. Triggers re-training workflows and compliance alerts in CTMS.

attributes.name: investigator_role
attributes.description: Role classification for this HCP on this specific trial. Principal Investigator (PI) has ultimate responsibility for trial conduct at the site; Sub-Investigators and Coordinators have delegated responsibilities. Drives regulatory reporting requirements and delegation log structure.

attributes.name: investigator_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this investigator assignment on this trial. Active indicates the HCP is currently authorized to perform trial activities. Suspended/Terminated indicates removal from the trial team. Drives access control in EDC systems (Medidata Rave) and eTMF permissions.

attributes.name: irb_approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) approved this investigator to conduct this trial at this site. Required before any trial activities can begin.

attributes.name: medical_license_verified_date
attributes.description: Date when the sponsor or CRO verified the investigator's medical license status for this trial. Required before site activation. Typically re-verified annually during trial conduct.

attributes.name: patients_enrolled_count
attributes.description: Count of patients enrolled by this investigator on this trial. Used for site performance tracking, investigator workload analysis, and enrollment forecasting. Updated as patients are consented and randomized.

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_count
attributes.description: Count of protocol deviations attributed to this investigator on this trial. Used for quality oversight, investigator performance monitoring, and risk-based monitoring (RBM) triggers.

attributes.name: site_assignment
attributes.description: Site identifier or site name where this investigator is assigned for this trial. Links to the clinical site/investigator site record. An HCP may serve as investigator at multiple sites for the same trial (multi-site PI scenarios).

products.name: site_protocol_activation
products.description: This association product represents the activation and operational lifecycle of a specific protocol version at a specific investigational site. It captures the regulatory, training, enrollment, and compliance milestones that exist only when a protocol is activated at a site. Each record links one investigational site to one protocol version with attributes tracking activation dates, site-specific enrollment targets, training completion, protocol deviations, and closure dates that belong to neither the site nor the protocol alone but to their operational relationship.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trial operations, investigational sites participate in multiple clinical trials (each with its own protocol), and each protocol is activated at multiple investigational sites globally. Site Protocol Activation is a recognized operational entity in CTMS systems, tracking the regulatory, training, enrollment, and compliance lifecycle of each protocol version at each site. This relationship carries substantial operational data (activation dates, site-specific enrollment targets, training completion, deviation counts, closure dates) that belongs to neither the site nor the protocol alone.

attributes.name: site_protocol_activation_id

attributes.name: investigational_site_id

attributes.name: protocol_id

attributes.name: deviation_count

attributes.name: enrollment_target
attributes.description: Planned number of subjects to be enrolled at this site under this specific protocol version. May differ from the site's overall enrollment target if multiple protocols or protocol amendments are active. Corresponds to site_enrollment_target_per_protocol from detection data.

attributes.name: site_protocol_activation_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of this protocol version at this site. Tracks lifecycle from activation through closure. Corresponds to site_protocol_version_status from detection data. Distinct from the site's overall status and the protocol's overall status.

attributes.name: training_completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which all required site staff completed protocol-specific training for this protocol version at this site. Required before site can begin enrolling subjects. Corresponds to site_protocol_training_date from detection data.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

products.name: clinical_advisory_board_membership

It captures the formal appointment of a PI to serve on a specific advisory board, including their role, term dates, participation metrics, compensation, and conflict of interest disclosures required for regulatory compliance and transparency reporting. Each record links one principal investigator to one medical advisory board with attributes that exist only in the context of this membership relationship.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical medical affairs operations, principal investigators serve on multiple advisory boards across different therapeutic areas, compounds, and strategic topics, while each advisory board has multiple PI members with diverse expertise. The business actively manages these memberships as formal appointments with specific roles (Chair, Member, Observer), term dates, attendance tracking, FMV-compliant honoraria, and conflict of interest disclosures required for regulatory transparency reporting (Sunshine Act, EFPIA). This is an operational relationship that Medical Affairs creates, monitors, and reports on as a distinct business process.

products.name: imp_accountability
products.description: This association product represents the accountability record between clinical trials and inventory lots of investigational medicinal products (IMPs). It captures the dispensation, return, and destruction of specific drug product lots used in clinical trials, ensuring full traceability and regulatory compliance per GCP and 21 CFR Part 312. Each record links one trial to one inventory lot with quantities, dates, and accountability status that exist only in the context of this trial-lot relationship. This is the authoritative SSOT for IMP accountability reconciliation required for regulatory inspections and CSR appendices.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical operations, trials consume multiple inventory lots over their lifecycle due to resupply needs, dose escalation cohorts, and multi-site distribution, while individual lots (especially in Phase I or multi-indication studies) are allocated across multiple concurrent trials. IMP accountability is a regulated operational process where clinical teams actively create, monitor, and reconcile dispensation records for each trial-lot combination, tracking quantities dispensed, returned, and destroyed per GCP requirements.

attributes.name: imp_accountability_id

attributes.name: inventory_lot_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the specific inventory lot (batch) of investigational medicinal product dispensed to this trial

attributes.name: accountability_status

attributes.name: destruction_quantity

attributes.name: discrepancy_reason

attributes.name: dispensed_date

attributes.name: dispensed_quantity
attributes.description: Total quantity of this lot dispensed to patients at the site for this trial. Used for accountability reconciliation: dispensed + returned + destroyed must equal shipped quantity.

attributes.name: reconciliation_date
attributes.description: Date on which this trial-lot accountability record was formally reconciled and closed by the clinical monitor or site coordinator. Required for database lock and CSR completion.

attributes.name: remaining_quantity

attributes.name: return_quantity

attributes.name: shipped_quantity

attributes.name: temperature_monitoring_compliant

products.name: trial_vendor_engagement

This is the authoritative SSOT for vendor-trial service agreements consumed by procurement, clinical operations, and trial management systems.. The business actively manages these vendor-trial engagements as distinct operational entities with contractual terms, service scopes, performance metrics, and deliverables tracked per engagement.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the clinical trial that requires vendor services

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the vendor providing services or materials to the trial

attributes.name: actual_deliverable_date
attributes.description: Actual date when the primary deliverable was received from the vendor. Used to calculate delivery variance and assess on-time performance.

attributes.name: contract_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the contract value (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency trial budget consolidation.

attributes.name: contract_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the legal contract or purchase order governing this vendor engagement. Links to contract management system (e.g., Ariba, SAP SRM) for full contract terms, amendments, and payment tracking.

attributes.name: contract_value
attributes.description: Total contracted monetary value for the vendor services in the trial currency. Used for budget tracking, accruals, and vendor spend analysis. May be fixed-price or estimated value for time-and-materials contracts.

attributes.name: deliverable_due_date
attributes.description: Date when the primary deliverable from the vendor is due (e.g., CSR for medical writing vendor, database lock for data management vendor, final lab report for central lab). Used for milestone tracking and performance monitoring.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual date when the vendor engagement concluded and services were completed. Null for ongoing engagements. Used for vendor lifecycle tracking and historical analysis.

attributes.name: engagement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the vendor engagement. Planned: contract negotiation in progress. Active: services being delivered. On Hold: temporarily suspended. Completed: services successfully delivered. Terminated: contract ended prematurely.

attributes.name: performance_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of vendor performance on this specific trial engagement. Evaluated based on deliverable quality, timeline adherence, communication, issue resolution, and GCP compliance. Feeds into vendor scorecarding and future vendor selection decisions.

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: Email address of the vendor primary contact for operational communication regarding this trial engagement.

attributes.name: primary_contact_name
attributes.description: Full name of the vendor representative serving as the primary point of contact for this trial engagement. Typically the project manager, account manager, or study director assigned by the vendor.

attributes.name: scope_of_work
attributes.description: Detailed description of the specific services, deliverables, and responsibilities assigned to the vendor for this trial. May reference contract exhibits, SOWs, or protocol sections. Critical for defining vendor accountability and managing scope changes.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Classification of the service or material provided by the vendor for this trial. Determines operational workflows, deliverable expectations, and performance metrics. Examples: CRO Full Service (end-to-end trial management), Central Laboratory (sample analysis), IMP Manufacturing (investigational medicinal product production), SMO (site management organization for patient recruitment).

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date when the vendor engagement became effective and services commenced. Used to track vendor tenure on trial and calculate performance metrics over the engagement period.

domains.name: regulatory
domains.description: Manages all regulatory submissions, approvals, and compliance management including IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, and eCTD dossiers. Tracks interactions with FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, and NMPA health authorities. Manages regulatory milestones, pre-approval inspections (PAI), REMS programs, post-approval commitments, drug master files (DMF), label management, and regulatory correspondence. Integrates with Veeva Vault RIM and RIMS for submission tracking and lifecycle management.
domains.references: 21 CFR Part 314 / EMA Regulatory Framework / ICH M4 eCTD

products.name: submission
products.description: Master record and single source of truth for all regulatory submissions (filing events) to health authorities including original applications, supplements, amendments, responses to information requests, and annual reports. Each submission represents a discrete eCTD sequence filed under a parent application. Tracks submission type, sequence number, dossier format (eCTD), submission date, target agency, eCTD lifecycle operation (new, replace, append, delete), submission medium, validation status, regulatory pathway, priority designation, and current lifecycle status. Includes document-level composition tracking with CTD module/section assignment (Modules 1-5), individual document metadata (title, type, version, author, status, file format, checksum), version control, and dossier completeness assessment aligned with ICH M4 (CTD structure) and M8 (eCTD technical specification). SSOT for regulatory submission identity, lifecycle, sequence tracking, dossier content, and document inventory in Veeva Vault RIM.

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each regulatory submission record in the Pharmaceuticals data lakehouse. Primary key for the submission data product.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent regulatory application (e.g., NDA, BLA, MAA, IND) under which this submission sequence is filed. Each submission belongs to exactly one parent application.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Submissions require a regulatory affairs lead for preparation, gateway submission, and health authority interaction tracking. Critical for workload management, regulatory inspection readiness (who pre

attributes.name: actual_decision_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the health authority issued its formal regulatory decision (approval, complete response, refusal, withdrawal). Used to measure review cycle time against PDUFA/EMA target dates and track regulatory performance.

attributes.name: agency_tracking_number
attributes.description: Official tracking or docket number assigned by the health authority upon receipt of the submission (e.g., FDA STN number, EMA procedure number). Used for all official correspondence and status inquiries with the regulatory agency.
attributes.references: FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway; EMA eSubmission Gateway; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: cover_letter_title
attributes.description: Title or subject line of the cover letter accompanying this submission, summarizing the purpose and scope of the filing. Provides a human-readable description of the submission intent for regulatory affairs tracking and correspondence management.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.50(a); EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this submission record was first created in the data lakehouse, conforming to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail, data lineage, and regulatory record-keeping requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GDPR Article 5(2); ISO 8601

attributes.name: ctd_modules_included
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ICH CTD modules included in this submission (e.g., '1,2,3,4,5' for a full NDA; '1,2' for an administrative amendment). Modules: 1=Administrative/Regional; 2=Summaries; 3=Quality (CMC); 4=Nonclinical; 5=Clinical. Supports dossier completeness assessment.
attributes.references: ICH M4 Common Technical Document (CTD); ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification

attributes.name: document_count
attributes.description: Total number of individual documents included in this submission sequence. Used for dossier completeness assessment, submission quality metrics, and workload estimation for health authority reviewers.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification; Veeva Vault RIM Document Management

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: Pharmaceutical dosage form of the drug product covered by this submission (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, lyophilized powder for solution, transdermal patch). Captured per ICH M4 CTD Module 1 product information.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD Module 1; FDA 21 CFR Part 314.50; EMA Guideline on Pharmaceutical Development (ICH Q8)

attributes.name: dossier_format
attributes.description: Technical format of the regulatory dossier submitted to the health authority. eCTD (Electronic Common Technical Document) is the current standard; NeeS (Non-eCTD Electronic Submission) and paper are legacy formats. Determines validation and processing requirements.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification; FDA 21 CFR Part 314.50; EMA eCTD Guidance

attributes.name: ectd_operation
attributes.description: eCTD lifecycle operation code indicating how this submission sequence modifies the dossier content relative to the prior sequence. New = first submission of a document; Replace = supersedes a prior document; Append = adds to existing content; Delete = removes prior content. Conforms to ICH M8 eCTD specification.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification v4.0; FDA eCTD Guidance for Industry; EMA eCTD Guidance

attributes.name: fee_usd
attributes.description: Regulatory user fee paid to the health authority for processing this submission, denominated in US Dollars. For FDA submissions, this is the PDUFA application fee. Tracked for financial planning, budget management, and fee waiver/exemption monitoring.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA VI User Fee Schedule; 21 CFR Part 314.50; FDA FDASIA 2012

attributes.name: fee_waiver_granted
attributes.description: Indicates whether a regulatory user fee waiver or exemption has been granted for this submission (e.g., orphan drug fee waiver, small business waiver, public health waiver). True = fee waiver approved by the health authority.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA VI; 21 CFR Part 314.50; FDA Orphan Drug Act (21 CFR Part 316)

attributes.name: indication
attributes.description: Clinical indication or disease/condition for which marketing authorization or investigational use is being sought in this submission. Defines the scope of the regulatory review and the approved label if authorization is granted.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD Module 1.3.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 314.50(c); EMA Guideline on Summary of Product Characteristics

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the submission within the regulatory review lifecycle. Draft = being prepared; Submitted = transmitted to agency; Under Review = agency actively reviewing; Approved = marketing authorization granted; Complete Response = FDA issued CRL requiring additional data; Refused = EMA/MHRA refusal; Withdrawn = applicant withdrew; On Hold = review paused. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.110 (Complete Response Letter); EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: medium
attributes.description: Physical or electronic channel used to transmit the submission to the health authority. Electronic Gateway (e.g., FDA ESG, EMA eSubmission Gateway) is the standard; physical media (CD/DVD/USB) and portal submissions are also tracked.
attributes.references: FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG); EMA eSubmission Gateway; ICH M8

attributes.name: pai_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) of manufacturing facilities is required as part of the review of this submission. PAIs verify GMP compliance and data integrity of manufacturing processes prior to approval. True = PAI required.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Parts 210, 211; FDA PAI Compliance Program 7346.832; EMA GMP Inspection Procedures; PIC/S

attributes.name: priority_designation
attributes.description: Special regulatory designation granted to the submission or parent application that confers expedited review or development benefits. Includes FDA Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, Priority Review, Accelerated Approval, Orphan Drug designation. Multiple designations may apply; primary designation recorded here.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 316 (Orphan Drug); FDA FDASIA 2012 Section 902; EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000 (Orphan Medicinal Products)

attributes.name: receipt_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the health authority officially acknowledged receipt of the submission. Triggers the start of the regulatory review clock and PDUFA/EMA review timeline. May differ from submission_date due to gateway processing.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.101; FDA PDUFA VI; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 6

attributes.name: regulatory_pathway
attributes.description: Regulatory review pathway designation assigned to this submission, determining review timelines and procedural requirements. Examples include FDA Standard, Priority Review, Accelerated Approval, Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track; EMA Conditional Marketing Authorisation, Rolling Review. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.80; FDA FDASIA 2012; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 14; ICH E8

attributes.name: rems_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program is required or proposed as part of this submission. REMS programs are FDA-mandated risk management strategies for drugs with serious safety concerns. True = REMS required/proposed.
attributes.references: FDA FDAAA 2007 Section 505-1; 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDA REMS Guidance

attributes.name: review_division
attributes.description: Name of the health authority review division or committee responsible for evaluating this submission (e.g., FDA CDER Office of Oncology Products, EMA Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP), PMDA Office of New Drug I). Determines reviewer assignment and procedural rules.
attributes.references: FDA CDER Manual of Policies and Procedures; EMA CHMP Rules of Procedure; PMDA Organizational Structure

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Route by which the drug product is administered to patients as specified in this submission (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical, inhalation). Captured per ICH M4 CTD Module 1 product information.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD Module 1; FDA 21 CFR Part 314.50; EMA Guideline on Summary of Product Characteristics

attributes.name: sequence_number
attributes.description: Four-digit zero-padded eCTD sequence number uniquely identifying this submission within the parent application lifecycle (e.g., 0000 for initial submission, 0001 for first amendment). Conforms to ICH M8 eCTD technical specification.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification; FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eCTD Guidance

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the submission was formally transmitted to the health authority. This is the principal business event date used for regulatory timeline calculations, PDUFA date computation, and compliance tracking.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA VI; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; 21 CFR Part 314.101; ICH M8

attributes.name: submission_number
attributes.description: Human-readable external submission reference number assigned by the health authority or internal tracking system (e.g., NDA 123456/S-001, EMA/H/C/000123/0001). Used for correspondence and regulatory tracking.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.50; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: submission_type
attributes.description: Classification of the submission event within the regulatory application lifecycle. Original = initial filing; Supplement = post-approval change; Amendment = pre-approval change; Annual Report = periodic safety/status update; Response = reply to agency information request; Withdrawal = voluntary withdrawal of application. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: original|supplement|amendment|annual_report|response|withdrawal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.70; ICH M4 CTD; EMA Variation Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008

attributes.name: subtype
attributes.description: Further classification of the submission type providing regulatory granularity (e.g., Prior Approval Supplement, Changes Being Effected Supplement, Type IA Variation, Type IB Variation, Type II Variation). Jurisdiction-specific categorization used for review timeline determination. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Variation Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008; ICH M4

attributes.name: target_action_date
attributes.description: Regulatory target date by which the health authority is committed to completing its review and issuing a decision. For FDA submissions, this is the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) goal date. For EMA, this is the Day 210 opinion date. Critical milestone for commercial planning.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA VI; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; 21 CFR Part 314.100

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Clinical therapeutic area or disease category addressed by the drug product in this submission (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neurology). Used for portfolio analytics, resource planning, and regulatory strategy alignment.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD; ATC Classification System (WHO); FDA CDER Therapeutic Area Taxonomy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this submission record was last modified in the data lakehouse, conforming to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data integrity verification under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GDPR Article 5(2); ISO 8601

attributes.name: validation_error_count
attributes.description: Number of technical validation errors identified during eCTD dossier validation. Zero indicates a clean submission. Used to assess submission quality and track remediation effort prior to resubmission.
attributes.references: FDA eCTD Validation Criteria; EMA eCTD Validation Criteria v6.0; ICH M8

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Technical validation status of the eCTD dossier as assessed by the health authority's automated validation tools (e.g., FDA Validation Criteria, EMA eCTD Validation Criteria). Passed = all technical criteria met; Failed = validation errors requiring correction; Waived = validation requirement formally waived.
attributes.references: FDA eCTD Validation Criteria; EMA eCTD Validation Criteria v6.0; ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification

attributes.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
attributes.description: Unique document identifier assigned by Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management) system for this submission record. Enables direct cross-reference and deep-link navigation to the source system of record for submission lifecycle management.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures)

products.name: health_authority
products.description: Reference master for all global health authority agencies with which the company interacts, including FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, NMPA, WHO, and national competent authorities. Captures agency name, acronym, jurisdiction, country/region, agency type, contact details, submission portal URL, accepted dossier formats, and applicable regulatory frameworks. Enables consistent agency identification across all regulatory activities.

attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each health authority agency record in the regulatory master reference. Primary key for the health_authority data product.

attributes.name: accepted_dossier_formats
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of submission dossier formats accepted by the health authority (e.g., 'eCTD', 'NeeS', 'paper', 'eCTD v4.0'). Drives submission preparation and formatting decisions in Veeva Vault RIM and RIMS.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Guideline; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA eCTD Specification

attributes.name: acronym
attributes.description: Commonly used abbreviation or acronym for the health authority (e.g., 'FDA', 'EMA', 'PMDA', 'MHRA', 'NMPA', 'WHO'). Used in regulatory correspondence, submission tracking, and reporting.
attributes.references: ICH M4 eCTD Guideline; WHO Prequalification Programme

attributes.name: agency_name
attributes.description: Official full legal name of the health authority agency (e.g., 'U.S. Food and Drug Administration', 'European Medicines Agency'). Used as the primary identity label for the agency across all regulatory activities.
attributes.references: ICH M4 eCTD Guideline; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: agency_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the health authority record. 'active' indicates the agency is currently operational and accepting submissions; 'inactive' indicates it is no longer operational; 'merged' indicates it has been absorbed into another agency; 'dissolved' indicates it has been formally disbanded; 'under_review' indicates the record is pending validation.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; Internal Regulatory Master Data Governance

attributes.name: agency_type
attributes.description: Classification of the health authority by its organizational scope and mandate. Distinguishes between national competent authorities (e.g., FDA, MHRA), supranational agencies (e.g., EMA), international organizations (e.g., WHO), regional authorities, and advisory bodies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: national_competent_authority|supranational_agency|international_organization|regional_authority|advisory_body — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]
attributes.references: ICH Governance; WHO Prequalification Programme; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: agency_website_url
attributes.description: Official public website URL of the health authority (e.g., https://www.fda.gov, https://www.ema.europa.eu). Used for reference, guidance document retrieval, and regulatory intelligence.
attributes.references: FDA; EMA; MHRA; PMDA; NMPA Official Websites

attributes.name: bla_accepted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority accepts Biologics License Application (BLA) submissions or their local equivalent for marketing authorization of biological products, vaccines, and biosimilars.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 601 (FDA BLA); EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH Q5 Biologics Guidelines

attributes.name: breakthrough_designation_program
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority offers a breakthrough therapy designation or equivalent expedited development program (e.g., FDA Breakthrough Therapy, EMA PRIME scheme, MHRA Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway). Drives early engagement strategy.
attributes.references: FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation (21 CFR Part 312.82); EMA PRIME Guideline; MHRA ILAP

attributes.name: dmf_accepted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority accepts Drug Master File (DMF) submissions for confidential disclosure of manufacturing, processing, packaging, and storage information for drug substances and excipients.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.420 (DMF); EMA Active Substance Master File (ASMF) Guideline; ICH Q7

attributes.name: ectd_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority mandates submission in Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) format as per ICH M8 guideline. Drives submission formatting and Veeva Vault RIM configuration.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Guideline; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA eCTD Specification v3.2.2

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this health authority record is considered valid and active for use in regulatory submissions and compliance activities. Supports temporal validity management in the regulatory master data.
attributes.references: Internal Master Data Governance; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: external_agency_code
attributes.description: Official external identifier assigned to the health authority by an industry body or cross-reference system (e.g., DUNS number, ISO organization code, or identifier from a regulatory intelligence database). Supports cross-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: ISO 6523 Organization Identifier; DUNS; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: gmp_inspection_authority
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority has the mandate and capability to conduct Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) inspections of pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities. Drives inspection readiness and compliance programs.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Parts 210/211 (FDA cGMP); EMA GMP Guidelines; PIC/S PE 009; ICH Q7

attributes.name: ich_member
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority is a full member or observer of the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH). ICH membership signals alignment with harmonized technical guidelines for drug registration.
attributes.references: ICH Governance; ICH Members and Observers List

attributes.name: icsr_reporting_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) Reporting Required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority requires Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) submissions for pharmacovigilance and adverse event reporting. Drives Argus Safety / Oracle AERS configuration for expedited and periodic safety reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) ICSR Guideline; FDA 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010; PMDA PV Regulations

attributes.name: ind_accepted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority accepts Investigational New Drug (IND) applications or their local equivalent for clinical trial authorization. Drives IND filing strategy for global clinical development programs.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312 (FDA IND); ICH E6 GCP; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation EU 536/2014

attributes.name: jurisdiction_type
attributes.description: Scope of regulatory jurisdiction exercised by the health authority — federal (e.g., FDA within the US), national (e.g., MHRA for UK), regional (e.g., state-level agencies), supranational (e.g., EMA for EU member states), or international (e.g., WHO).
attributes.references: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; 21 CFR Parts 210/211

attributes.name: language_of_submission
attributes.description: Official language(s) required for regulatory submissions to this health authority (e.g., 'English' for FDA/EMA/MHRA, 'Japanese' for PMDA, 'Chinese (Simplified)' for NMPA). Drives translation and localization planning for global submissions.
attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD Guideline; PMDA Submission Requirements; NMPA Technical Guidelines

attributes.name: local_representative_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority requires a local regulatory representative, marketing authorization holder, or in-country agent to be designated for submissions and post-approval activities. Critical for market access planning in jurisdictions like Japan (PMDA) and China (NMPA).
attributes.references: PMDA Pharmaceutical Affairs Act; NMPA Drug Registration Regulations; EMA Directive 2001/83/EC Article 8

attributes.name: mailing_address
attributes.description: Full official mailing address of the health authority's headquarters or primary regulatory affairs office. Used for formal paper submissions and official correspondence.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: mutual_recognition_agreements
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRA) or equivalence arrangements the health authority has with other regulatory bodies (e.g., 'FDA-EMA MRA', 'PIC/S Member'). Impacts GMP inspection reliance and submission strategy.
attributes.references: FDA-EMA MRA (2017); PIC/S Mutual Recognition; ICH Q10

attributes.name: nda_accepted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority accepts New Drug Application (NDA) submissions or their local equivalent (e.g., MAA for EMA, J-NDA for PMDA) for marketing authorization of small molecule drugs.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314 (FDA NDA); EMA Directive 2001/83/EC; ICH M4 CTD

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional regulatory context, special requirements, recent guidance updates, or operational notes specific to this health authority. Maintained by the Regulatory Affairs team.
attributes.references: Internal Regulatory Affairs SOP; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: orphan_drug_program
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority operates an orphan drug designation program providing incentives (e.g., market exclusivity, fee waivers, protocol assistance) for rare disease treatments. Relevant for oncology and rare disease therapeutic areas.
attributes.references: FDA Orphan Drug Act (21 CFR Part 316); EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; PMDA Orphan Drug Designation

attributes.name: pai_conducted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority conducts Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI) of manufacturing facilities as part of the marketing authorization review process. Drives inspection readiness planning.
attributes.references: FDA PAI Program (21 CFR Parts 210/211); EMA GMP Inspection Programme; PIC/S Guidelines

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: Official primary contact email address for regulatory correspondence with the health authority. Used for submission inquiries, meeting requests, and formal communications.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6 GCP

attributes.name: primary_contact_phone
attributes.description: Official primary telephone number for the health authority's regulatory affairs contact office. Includes country dialing code.

attributes.name: priority_review_duration_days
attributes.description: Expedited or priority review clock duration in calendar days for applications granted priority review designation at this health authority (e.g., 180 days for FDA Priority Review, 150 days for EMA accelerated assessment). Supports regulatory strategy for breakthrough therapies.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA VI Priority Review Goals; EMA Accelerated Assessment Guideline; MHRA Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway

attributes.name: psur_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority requires Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSUR) or Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRER) as part of post-marketing pharmacovigilance obligations. Aligns with ICH E2C(R2) guideline.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) PBRER/PSUR Guideline; EMA Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010; FDA PADER Requirements

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this health authority master record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this health authority master record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data currency validation under 21 CFR Part 11.

attributes.name: region

attributes.references: ICH M4 eCTD Guideline; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: Primary regulatory framework or legislation governing the health authority's operations (e.g., '21 CFR Parts 210/211/312/314' for FDA, 'Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation 726/2004' for EMA, 'Pharmaceutical Affairs Act' for PMDA). Critical for compliance mapping.

attributes.name: standard_review_duration_days
attributes.description: Standard regulatory review clock duration in calendar days for a standard marketing authorization application at this health authority (e.g., 365 days for FDA standard NDA review, 210 days for EMA centralized procedure). Used for regulatory timeline planning.

attributes.name: regulatory_action_date

attributes.name: regulatory_action_type

attributes.name: regulatory_procedure_type

attributes.name: related_sequence_number

attributes.name: review_clock_start_date

attributes.name: sequence_number

attributes.name: submission_status

attributes.name: submission_timestamp

attributes.name: submission_unit_count

attributes.name: supplement_category

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.name: conditions

attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.520; EMA Regulation (EC) No 507/2006 Article 4; REMS guidance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this approval record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data governance and 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.

attributes.name: ectd_sequence_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Sequence Number
attributes.description: The eCTD sequence number of the submission that resulted in this approval. Enables traceability from the approval back to the specific eCTD dossier version reviewed by the health authority.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Specification; FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eCTD Guidance

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the approval becomes legally binding and the product may be marketed. May differ from approval_date in cases where a transition period is granted.

attributes.name: exclusivity_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the regulatory exclusivity period for this approval expires, after which generic or biosimilar applications may be approved. Critical for commercial lifecycle and IP strategy planning.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Hatch-Waxman Act; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 14

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the marketing authorization expires and must be renewed. Applicable in jurisdictions requiring periodic renewal (e.g., EMA 5-year renewal cycle). Null for indefinite approvals such as FDA standard approvals.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 14; MHRA Human Medicines Regulations 2012

attributes.name: has_rems
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program is required as a condition of this approval. True if REMS is mandated by FDA; False otherwise.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDA REMS Guidance; FDAAA 2007

attributes.name: inn_name
attributes.description: The WHO-assigned International Nonproprietary Name (INN) of the active substance in the approved drug product. Provides a globally recognized, non-proprietary identifier for the active ingredient.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; ICH Q6A; 21 CFR Part 299

attributes.name: label_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the approved product label (prescribing information / Summary of Product Characteristics) at the time of approval. Used to track label revisions and ensure current label compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201.57; EMA Guideline on Summary of Product Characteristics; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: letter_date
attributes.description: Date of the official approval letter issued by the health authority. May differ from the approval_date in cases where the letter is issued after the formal approval decision.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.105; FDA Approval Letter Templates; EMA Decision Date

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional regulatory notes, special circumstances, or contextual information related to this approval that is not captured in structured fields. Used by regulatory affairs teams for internal documentation.

attributes.name: orphan_drug_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the approved drug product holds orphan drug designation for the approved indication. Orphan designation confers market exclusivity and regulatory incentives for rare disease treatments.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 316; EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; Orphan Drug Act

attributes.name: pai_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) of manufacturing facilities was required and conducted as part of the approval process. True if PAI was mandated; False otherwise.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314; FDA PAI Guidance; PIC/S PE 009

attributes.name: pediatric_indication
attributes.description: Indicates whether the approval includes a pediatric indication or pediatric labeling. Relevant for tracking compliance with Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) and Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314; PREA; BPCA; ICH E11; EMA Paediatric Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006

attributes.name: post_approval_commitment_count
attributes.description: Number of post-approval commitments (PACs) or post-marketing requirements (PMRs) imposed by the health authority as conditions of this approval. Drives tracking of outstanding regulatory obligations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Post-Authorisation Measures; FDAAA 2007

attributes.name: regulatory_exclusivity_type
attributes.description: Type of regulatory exclusivity granted with this approval. NCE (New Chemical Entity) exclusivity, orphan exclusivity, pediatric exclusivity, or data/market exclusivity. Determines the period during which generic or biosimilar competition is blocked.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Hatch-Waxman Act; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 14; Orphan Drug Act

attributes.name: regulatory_region
attributes.description: Regulatory region or jurisdiction grouping for the approval. Used for regional reporting and portfolio management (US=FDA, EU=EMA, JP=PMDA, CN=NMPA, UK=MHRA, CA=Health Canada, AU=TGA, ROW=Rest of World). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: US|EU|JP|CN|UK|CA|AU|ROW — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH M4; FDA 21 CFR; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: review_division
attributes.description: The specific review division or committee within the health authority responsible for evaluating and granting this approval (e.g., FDA CDER Division of Oncology Products, EMA CHMP, PMDA Review Division).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314; FDA CDER Organization; EMA CHMP Rules of Procedure

attributes.name: submission_type
attributes.description: Type of regulatory submission that led to this approval. NDA (New Drug Application), BLA (Biologics License Application), MAA (Marketing Authorization Application), ANDA (Abbreviated NDA), sNDA/sBLA/sMAA (supplemental submissions). products.name: ha_interaction

Consolidates both meeting-based and written communications into a single chronological record per application. For written correspondence, summarizes the subject matter. Business-confidential as it contains regulatory strategy information.

Four-digit zero-padded number per ICH M8 eCTD specification. Null if the interaction is not associated with a formal eCTD submission.

Enables granular tracking of agency relationships and division-specific regulatory strategies.

attributes.name: interaction_date

Serves as the BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP (date precision) for this transaction. For written correspondence, this is the document date on the letter or communication.

attributes.name: interaction_format

attributes.name: inn

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: pai_flag

attributes.name: priority_flag

attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.110; FDA PDUFA Performance Goals; ICH E2A Safety Reporting

attributes.name: received_date
attributes.description: Date the inbound correspondence was officially received from the health authority. For outbound correspondence, this field is null. Used as the baseline for calculating response due dates and compliance with agency deadlines.

attributes.name: rems_flag

attributes.name: response_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the company submitted its formal response to the health authority correspondence. Compared against response_due_date to assess compliance with agency deadlines and PDUFA timelines.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.110; FDA PDUFA Performance Goals; EMA Procedural Timelines

attributes.name: response_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the company must respond to an inbound agency correspondence (e.g., information request, deficiency letter). Calculated based on agency-specified timelines or regulatory requirements. Critical for compliance monitoring and escalation workflows.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.110; FDA PDUFA Performance Goals; EMA Procedural Timelines; ICH E6 GCP

attributes.name: response_extension_requested
attributes.description: Indicates whether the company has formally requested an extension to the response deadline from the health authority. True = extension requested; False = no extension requested. Supports compliance tracking and agency negotiation records.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.110; FDA MAPP 6020.1; EMA Procedural Guidance on Extensions

attributes.name: responsible_person
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the regulatory affairs professional responsible for managing and responding to this correspondence. Serves as the primary point of contact for the correspondence lifecycle within the organization.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Procedural Guidance; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: sent_date
attributes.description: Date the outbound correspondence was officially transmitted to the health authority. For inbound correspondence, this field is null. Captured for audit trail and submission timeline tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314; FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway; EMA eSubmission Portal

attributes.name: subject
attributes.description: Brief subject line or title of the correspondence describing the primary topic or matter addressed (e.g., 'Response to Information Request on Clinical Study XYZ', 'Complete Response to NDA 123456'). Used for search and categorization in Veeva Vault RIM.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 314; ICH M4 eCTD

attributes.name: subject_matter_category
attributes.description: High-level categorization of the subject matter area addressed in the correspondence, aligned with eCTD module structure. attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Therapeutic area classification of the drug product associated with this correspondence (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neurology). Enables portfolio-level analytics on regulatory correspondence by disease area.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this regulatory correspondence record. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance, and incremental data loading in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10

attributes.name: vault_document_reference
attributes.description: Document reference identifier in Veeva Vault RIM or eTMF for the correspondence document. Enables direct retrieval of the source document from the document management system for audit and review purposes.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault RIM; FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eSubmission Standards

Captures DMF number, DMF type (Type I-V), holder name, subject of DMF, filing date, last annual update date, authorization letters issued, and associated products referencing the DMF. Supports CMC regulatory strategy and third-party supplier qualification. Aligns with 21 CFR 314.420 and EMA DMF guidelines.

attributes.name: drug_substance_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: Drug Master Files are filed with specific health authorities (FDA, EMA, etc.). Currently dmf has only an incoming FK from dossier_document, making it nearly siloed. Adding health_authority_id links DM

attributes.name: holder_legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: DMF holders are legal entities that own drug master files. Regulatory compliance requires tracking the legal entity for authorization letters, annual updates, and cross-referencing in NDAs/ANDAs. Hold

attributes.name: holder_vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: DMFs are filed by API/excipient manufacturers who are procurement vendors. Pharma companies link DMF holders to vendor master for GMP qualification status, audit scheduling, supply chain risk assessme

attributes.name: manufacturing_site_country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: DMF manufacturing site jurisdiction determines applicable GMP standards, inspection authority, and regulatory pathway. Critical for CMC assessment and supply chain risk management. Manufacturing_site_

attributes.name: amendment_count
attributes.description: Total number of amendments submitted to the health authority for this DMF since the original filing date. Reflects the change history and regulatory maintenance activity for the DMF.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: associated_product_names
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Associated Product Names
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of internal drug product names or development codes that reference this DMF in their NDA, BLA, or MAA submissions. Provides a quick cross-reference for CMC regulatory strategy without requiring a full join to the submission registry.

attributes.name: authorization_letter_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Authorization Letter Date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent Letter of Authorization (LoA) was issued by the DMF holder to the referencing applicant. Null if no authorization letter has been issued.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420(d); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: authorization_letter_issued
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Authorization Letter Issued
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DMF holder has issued a Letter of Authorization (LoA) to the referencing applicant, granting the health authority permission to review the confidential DMF contents in support of an NDA, BLA, or ANDA submission.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420(d); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: cmc_section
attributes.description: Identifies the specific Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) section of the eCTD/CTD dossier (Module 3) to which this DMF contributes. Used to map DMF content to the corresponding CTD section in NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
attributes.references: ICH M4Q (CTD Module 3); ICH Q11; 21 CFR 314.420

attributes.name: confidentiality_commitment
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DMF holder has provided a formal confidentiality commitment to the referencing company, ensuring that proprietary manufacturing information disclosed in the DMF will not be shared beyond the regulatory review context.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry; GDPR Article 28

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this DMF record was first created in the regulatory data product. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH Q10

attributes.name: deficiency_letter_received
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Deficiency Letter Received
attributes.description: Indicates whether the health authority has issued a deficiency letter (also known as a Complete Response Letter or information request) identifying gaps or issues in the DMF that must be addressed before the referencing application can be approved.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry; EMA DMF Guidelines

attributes.name: deficiency_response_due_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Deficiency Response Due Date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the DMF holder must respond to a deficiency letter issued by the health authority. Null if no deficiency letter has been received. Critical for regulatory timeline management.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: dmf_number
attributes.description: Official DMF number assigned by the health authority (e.g., FDA) upon receipt of the filing. Serves as the externally-known unique identifier for the DMF across regulatory submissions and CMC dossiers.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance; EMA DMF Guidelines

attributes.name: dmf_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the DMF with the health authority. Active indicates the DMF is in good standing and available for reference; withdrawn indicates the holder has withdrawn the filing; closed indicates the authority has closed the file.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry; EMA DMF Guidelines

attributes.name: dmf_type
attributes.description: Classification of the DMF per FDA categorization: Type I (Manufacturing Site, Facilities, Operating Procedures, and Personnel), Type II (Drug Substance, Drug Substance Intermediate, and Material Used in Their Preparation, or Drug Product), Type III (Packaging Material), Type IV (Excipient, Colorant, Flavor, Essence, or Material Used in Their Preparation), Type V (FDA-Accepted Reference Information).
attributes.value_regex: Type I|Type II|Type III|Type IV|Type V
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: ectd_sequence_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Sequence Number
attributes.description: Four-digit eCTD sequence number of the most recent submission lifecycle for this DMF. Used to track the current version of the eCTD dossier in the health authority's document management system.
attributes.references: ICH M8 (eCTD); FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the DMF was originally submitted and received by the health authority. Establishes the official filing date of record for regulatory and IP purposes.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: gmp_certificate_expiry_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Certificate Expiry Date
attributes.description: Expiry date of the current GMP certificate associated with the manufacturing site in the DMF. Used to trigger renewal activities and assess supplier qualification status.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Parts 210-211; EMA GMP Guidelines; PIC/S; cGMP

attributes.name: gmp_certificate_number
attributes.description: Certificate number of the current Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certificate issued by a competent authority for the manufacturing site referenced in the DMF. Supports supplier qualification and PAI readiness.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Parts 210-211; EMA GMP Guidelines; PIC/S; cGMP

attributes.name: internal_owner
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the internal regulatory affairs professional responsible for managing this DMF relationship, tracking updates, and coordinating authorization letters with the DMF holder.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10

attributes.name: last_amendment_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Last Amendment Date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent amendment submitted to the health authority for this DMF. Used to assess currency of the DMF content and identify DMFs requiring review.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: last_annual_update_date

attributes.description: Date of the most recent annual update submitted to the health authority to confirm the DMF remains current and accurate. FDA requires annual updates under 21 CFR 314.420(c). Failure to update may result in DMF inactivation.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420(c); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: manufacturing_site_name
attributes.description: Name of the manufacturing facility covered by or associated with the DMF. For Type I DMFs, this is the primary subject. For Type II DMFs, this identifies where the API or drug substance is manufactured. Confidential as it reveals supply chain details.

attributes.name: next_annual_update_due_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Next Annual Update Due Date
attributes.description: Calculated due date for the next mandatory annual update submission to the health authority. Used for proactive compliance tracking and regulatory calendar management.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420(c); FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: pai_status
attributes.description: Current status of the Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) for the manufacturing site or process covered by this DMF. PAI is conducted by FDA or other health authorities prior to approval of an NDA/BLA referencing this DMF. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: not_initiated|scheduled|completed|passed|failed|pending_response — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Parts 210-211; FDA PAI Guidance; EMA GMP Inspection Procedures

attributes.name: referencing_application_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drug Master File (DMF) Referencing Application Count
attributes.description: Number of regulatory applications (NDA, BLA, ANDA, MAA) that currently reference this DMF. Indicates the strategic importance of the DMF to the product portfolio and the breadth of supplier dependency.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: strategic_importance
attributes.description: Internal classification of the strategic importance of this DMF to the company's product portfolio and supply chain. Critical indicates sole-source supplier for a marketed product; high indicates key supplier for pipeline assets; medium/low for non-critical materials.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; FDA Supply Chain Guidance; Internal CMC Regulatory Strategy

attributes.name: subject
attributes.description: Detailed description of the subject matter covered by the DMF, such as the specific API, excipient, packaging component, or manufacturing site. Aligns with the 'Subject of DMF' field in FDA eCTD submissions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA eCTD Guidance; ICH M4 (CTD)

attributes.name: submission_format
attributes.description: Format in which the DMF was submitted to the health authority: eCTD (Electronic Common Technical Document), paper, or NeeS (Non-eCTD Electronic Submission). FDA mandates eCTD for most submissions since 2017.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.420; FDA eCTD Guidance; ICH M8 (eCTD)

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Official title or subject description of the DMF as submitted to the health authority, describing the substance, material, site, or process covered by the filing.

attributes.name: withdrawal_date

products.name: label
products.description: Single source of truth for approved product labeling (prescribing information, package insert, patient information leaflet, SmPC) and complete change history across all markets and languages. Tracks current label version, effective date, approval date, market/country, language, label type, content sections, and lifecycle status. Maintains full amendment history including change reason (safety update, new indication, dosage modification, black box warning), change type (agency-initiated, company-initiated), regulatory basis, affected sections, submission reference, and implementation status across markets. SSOT for both current approved labeling and all historical label changes — no separate label change product exists. Integrates with Veeva Vault PromoMats and RIM.

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory submission (NDA, BLA, MAA, or supplement) under which this label version was approved or submitted.

attributes.name: affected_sections
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of label sections modified in this version (e.g., 'Warnings and Precautions, Adverse Reactions, Dosage and Administration'). Enables targeted review of changes and supports regulatory correspondence tracking.

attributes.name: black_box_warning
attributes.description: Indicates whether this label version contains an FDA Boxed Warning (Black Box Warning) — the most serious warning required by the FDA for drugs with significant risk of serious or life-threatening adverse effects. True = boxed warning present; False = no boxed warning.

attributes.name: effective_date

attributes.name: indications

attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201.57(a)(1); EMA SmPC Section 4.1; ICH M4; FDA Labeling Guidance

attributes.name: inn
