True = current approved version; False = historical/superseded version. Enables efficient querying of the current label without date-range filtering.

attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201; EMA Guideline on SmPC; ICH M4; FDA Labeling Guidance

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: IETF BCP 47 / ISO 639 language code for the language of this label version (e.g., en, fr, de, ja, zh-CN). Supports multi-language label management across global markets.
attributes.references: ISO 639; IETF BCP 47; EMA SmPC Guideline; ICH M4

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current state of the label version within its regulatory lifecycle. Draft: in preparation; Under Review: submitted to health authority or under internal review; Approved: currently approved and in force; Superseded: replaced by a newer version; Withdrawn: removed from market; Archived: historical record retained for compliance.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Post-Authorisation Procedures; ICH Q10

attributes.name: market_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the market/country for which this label version is approved and applicable (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU, JPN, CHN). Enables market-specific label tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ICH M4; FDA 21 CFR Part 201; EMA SmPC Guideline

attributes.name: marketing_authorization_number
attributes.description: The marketing authorization (MA) or product license number assigned by the health authority for the approved drug product in the relevant market (e.g., NDA 123456 for FDA, EU/1/24/1234 for EMA centralized procedure). Links the label to the formal marketing authorization.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.105; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; MHRA Human Medicines Regulations 2012; PMDA Pharmaceutical Affairs Law

attributes.name: ndc_code
attributes.description: FDA-assigned National Drug Code (NDC) for the drug product associated with this label. The NDC is a unique 10-digit, 3-segment number identifying the labeler, product, and trade package size. Applicable for US market labels only.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 207; FDA NDC Directory; FDA Labeling Guidance

attributes.name: product_name
attributes.description: Brand/trade name of the drug product as it appears on this label version. Captured directly on the label record to preserve the exact name at the time of approval, which may differ from the current master product name.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201.10; EMA SmPC Section 1; ICH M4; WHO INN Programme

attributes.name: regulatory_basis
attributes.description: The regulatory or scientific basis justifying this label version change (e.g., 'Post-market safety study PMSS-2024-001', 'PSUR cycle 5 findings', 'FDA safety communication dated 2024-03-15', 'Pediatric study per PREA'). Provides the evidentiary foundation for the label amendment.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Variation Regulation; FDA PREA; ICH E2C(R2) PSUR Guideline

attributes.name: rems_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program is required for this drug product as referenced in this label version. True = REMS required; False = no REMS requirement.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDA REMS Guidance; FDAAA Section 505-1

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Approved route of administration as stated on this label (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, topical, inhalation). Reflects the regulatory-approved administration pathway for the drug product.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201.56; EMA SmPC Section 4.2; ICH M4; FDA Route of Administration Terminology

attributes.name: spl_document_reference
attributes.description: FDA-assigned UUID for the Structured Product Labeling (SPL) document submitted to the FDA DailyMed system. Unique identifier for the SPL XML document in the FDA labeling repository. Applicable for US market labels only.
attributes.references: FDA SPL Implementation Guide; 21 CFR Part 201; FDA DailyMed; HL7 SPL Standard

attributes.name: strength
attributes.description: Strength of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) as stated on this label (e.g., 10 mg, 500 mg/5 mL, 100 mg/mL). Captures the exact strength designation from the approved label text.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201.56; EMA SmPC Section 3; ICH M4; USP

attributes.name: superseded_date
attributes.description: Date on which this label version was superseded by a newer approved version. Null for the currently active label. Enables full historical label version tracking and compliance audit trails.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Post-Authorisation Procedures; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic area or disease area for which the drug product is approved as reflected in this label (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neurology). Supports portfolio-level label analytics and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ICH M4; EMA SmPC Section 4.1; FDA Labeling Guidance; WHO ATC Classification

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this label record in the regulatory data system. Supports change detection, incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer, and audit trail compliance per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10; Veeva Vault RIM Audit Trail; Databricks Delta Lake

attributes.name: vault_document_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault PromoMats or RIM for the full label content document. Enables direct retrieval of the complete label text, formatted PDF, and XML source from the document management system.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; Veeva Vault PromoMats; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records)

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for this label document (e.g., 1.0, 2.1, 3.0). Incremented with each approved amendment. Enables full version history tracking across the label lifecycle.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Guideline on Summary of Product Characteristics

products.name: label_change
products.description: Tracks all label changes and labeling amendments including the reason for change, change type (safety update, new indication, dosage modification, black box warning addition), regulatory basis, submission reference, effective date, and implementation status across markets. Captures the specific sections modified, change description, and whether the change was agency-initiated or company-initiated. Critical for pharmacovigilance-driven label updates and post-approval lifecycle management.

attributes.name: label_change_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each label change record in the regulatory labeling lifecycle management system.

attributes.name: brand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: Label changes impact promotional claims and sales messaging. Commercial must update materials and train field force when brand labels change to maintain compliance.

attributes.name: content_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.medical_content. Business justification: Label changes trigger updates to medical content to maintain regulatory compliance and accurate scientific messaging. When labels are updated (safety changes, indication expansions), all medical conte

attributes.name: coverage_decision_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.coverage_decision. Business justification: Safety-driven label changes (black box warnings, contraindications, REMS additions) trigger mandatory payer coverage policy reviews and updates to prior authorization criteria, directly impacting form

attributes.name: label_document_label_id
attributes.description: Document management system identifier (e.g., Veeva Vault document ID) for the approved label document associated with this change, enabling direct retrieval of the label text from the document management system.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA eDRLS

attributes.name: label_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.label. Business justification: Label changes modify specific label versions. Currently label_change links to product and submission but not to the actual label record being changed. Adding label_id establishes which label version i

attributes.name: medicinal_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the drug product (finished dosage form) for which the label change applies.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201; EMA Guideline on Summary of Product Characteristics

attributes.name: product_recall_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.product_recall. Business justification: Safety-driven label changes often originate from recall investigations, post-market surveillance, or adverse event patterns. Linking label changes to recalls enables root cause analysis and regulatory

attributes.name: promo_material_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.promo_material. Business justification: Label changes mandate promotional material updates. MLR teams must identify and revise affected materials when labels change to maintain fair balance and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: quality_capa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.quality_capa. Business justification: Safety-driven label changes often originate from quality issues (deviations, complaints, stability failures) requiring CAPAs. Links pharmacovigilance-driven labeling to root cause corrective actions—c

attributes.name: regulatory_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Label changes require a regulatory owner for change control execution, health authority correspondence, and implementation tracking. Essential for labeling change management, regulatory project tracki

attributes.name: safety_signal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pharmacovigilance safety case or signal that initiated a safety-driven label update, such as a new warning, contraindication, or black box warning addition.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module IX; Argus Safety

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory submission (e.g., NDA supplement, BLA supplement, MAA variation) that triggered or documents this label change.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Variation Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the health authority formally approved the label change. Null for company-initiated CBE changes that do not require prior approval.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Variation Regulation; FDA Approval Letter

attributes.name: atc_code
attributes.description: WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for the drug product, used for standardized cross-market reporting and regulatory analytics.
attributes.references: WHO ATC Classification System; EMA Product Information

attributes.name: change_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the specific modifications made to the product label, including the nature of the change, the scientific or safety rationale, and the specific text added, removed, or modified.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Variation Regulation; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: change_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the label change, used for cross-referencing with regulatory submissions, health authority correspondence, and internal change control systems. Format: LC-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 314.70

attributes.name: change_rationale
attributes.description: Scientific, clinical, or regulatory rationale supporting the label change, including references to clinical study data, pharmacovigilance signals, or health authority directives that justify the modification.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA GVP Module IX

attributes.name: change_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the label change record, tracking progression from initial drafting through regulatory approval to market implementation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_approval|submitted|approved|implemented|superseded|withdrawn — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Variation Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: change_type
attributes.description: Classification of the nature of the label change, indicating the primary reason or category of modification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: safety_update|new_indication|dosage_modification|black_box_warning|contraindication|drug_interaction|precaution|patient_information|administrative — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201; FDA Labeling Guidance; EMA Guideline on Summary of Product Characteristics

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, internal commentary, or contextual information related to the label change that does not fit into structured fields, such as negotiation history with health authorities or implementation challenges.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH Q10; SOPs

attributes.name: correspondence_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier for the health authority correspondence (e.g., FDA Complete Response Letter, EMA Day 120 List of Questions) that directed or acknowledged this label change.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.110; EMA Variation Regulation; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this label change record was first created in the system, providing the audit trail entry point for the change lifecycle.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: ectd_sequence_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Sequence Number
attributes.description: The eCTD sequence number associated with the regulatory submission containing this label change, enabling traceability to the electronic dossier submitted to the health authority.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Specification; FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eCTD Guidance

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the updated label becomes legally effective and must be used in commercial distribution. May differ from approval date based on implementation timelines.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201; FDA Labeling Guidance; EMA SmPC Guideline; GDP

attributes.name: health_authority
attributes.description: The regulatory health authority that approved, mandated, or received notification of this label change. Determines the applicable regulatory framework and submission requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|ANVISA|TGA|Health_Canada — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; MHRA; PMDA; NMPA

attributes.name: health_authority_reference
attributes.description: The reference number or tracking number assigned by the health authority (e.g., FDA NDA/BLA supplement number, EMA procedure number) for the submission associated with this label change.
attributes.references: FDA CDER; EMA EPAR; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: implementation_deadline
attributes.description: The regulatory or company-mandated deadline by which the updated label must be physically implemented on all marketed product packaging and distributed to the supply chain.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201; FDA Labeling Guidance; EMA SmPC Guideline; GDP

attributes.name: implementation_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the physical label implementation across manufacturing and supply chain, tracking whether the updated label has been applied to product packaging and distributed.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 211; cGMP; GDP; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: initiator_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the label change was initiated by the company (e.g., based on new clinical data or pharmacovigilance signal) or mandated by a health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA directive or post-approval commitment).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.70; FDA Labeling Guidance; EMA GVP Module IX; ICH E2D

attributes.name: inn
attributes.description: The WHO International Nonproprietary Name (INN) of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) for which the label is being changed, enabling cross-product and cross-market label tracking.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; ICH Q6A; EMA Product Information

attributes.name: is_black_box_warning
attributes.description: Indicates whether this label change includes the addition, modification, or removal of a black box warning (boxed warning), which is the FDA's most serious warning for drug safety risks.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201.57(c)(1); FDA Boxed Warning Guidance

attributes.name: is_pv_driven
attributes.description: Indicates whether this label change was driven by a pharmacovigilance signal, safety review, or post-market surveillance finding, as opposed to a new clinical indication or administrative update.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module IX; 21 CFR Part 314.81; Argus Safety

attributes.name: is_rems_related
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Related Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this label change is associated with a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program requirement, such as a new REMS, REMS modification, or REMS-driven labeling update.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDA REMS Guidance; FDAAA Section 505-1

attributes.name: market_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the market in which this label change applies. Enables multi-market label lifecycle tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; ICH Q10; EMA Variation Regulation

attributes.name: prior_label_version
attributes.description: Version number of the product label that was in effect immediately before this change, enabling traceability of label evolution and comparison of changes.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10

attributes.name: regulatory_basis
attributes.description: The regulatory pathway, regulation, or guidance document that provides the legal or scientific basis for the label change (e.g., 21 CFR 314.70(c), EMA Article 61(3), ICH E2D post-marketing safety data management).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.70; EMA Variation Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008; ICH E2D; ICH E2C

attributes.name: review_completed_date
attributes.description: The date on which the internal cross-functional review of the label change was completed, including sign-off from Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, and Legal.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 314; Veeva Vault RIM; SOPs

attributes.name: sections_modified
attributes.description: Comma-delimited list of label sections that were modified in this change (e.g., 'Warnings and Precautions, Dosage and Administration, Adverse Reactions'). Aligned with the Physician Labeling Rule (PLR) section structure for US labels and SmPC sections for EU labels.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 201.56; FDA Physician Labeling Rule (PLR); EMA SmPC Guideline

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The therapeutic area or disease category associated with the product label change (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular), used for portfolio-level reporting and regulatory analytics.
attributes.references: ATC Classification; WHO INN; ICH E1-E6

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this label change record, supporting audit trail requirements and change history tracking under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: urgency_level
attributes.description: Classification of the urgency with which the label change must be processed and implemented, based on the severity of the safety signal or regulatory requirement. Urgent and immediate changes may require expedited health authority notification.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; FDA Safety Labeling Changes Guidance; EMA GVP Module IX

products.name: rems
products.description: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program master record for products requiring FDA-mandated risk management programs. Captures REMS program name, associated NDA/BLA, REMS elements (medication guide, communication plan, ETASU), program approval date, assessment schedule, enrollment requirements, certified pharmacy/prescriber requirements, and program status. Tracks REMS modifications and assessment submission history. Specific to FDA-regulated products under 21 CFR 314.520.
products.reference: REMS / Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy / 21 CFR 314.520

attributes.name: rems_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) ID
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the REMS program master record in the Pharmaceuticals data lakehouse.

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.application. Business justification: REMS programs are mandated for specific regulatory applications (NDA/BLA). Currently rems is siloed with no FK relationships. Adding application_id links REMS to the regulatory application that requir

attributes.name: approval_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.approval. Business justification: REMS programs are mandated at the time of approval and are tied to the specific approval record. This FK links REMS to the approval that imposed the requirement. The approval_date and initial_approval

attributes.name: atc_classification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: REMS programs are therapeutic class-specific risk mitigation strategies. ATC classification enables shared REMS analysis, class-wide safety signal detection, and FDA assessment reporting. Atc_code is

attributes.name: brand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: REMS programs restrict distribution/prescribing for specific brands. Commercial operations (sampling, speaker programs, detailing) must comply with brand-specific REMS requirements.

attributes.name: clinical_supply_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.clinical_supply_order. Business justification: REMS programs with restricted distribution (ETASU) require tracking every dispensed unit through certified channels. Clinical supply orders for REMS products must be linked for FDA assessment reportin

attributes.name: copay_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.copay_program. Business justification: REMS programs may restrict copay assistance (e.g., certified prescribers only). Programs must exclude REMS-restricted scenarios to maintain controlled distribution compliance.

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: REMS programs require ongoing operational costs (program administration, assessments, reporting, modifications) tracked via internal orders for budget management and cost allocation to the approved pr

attributes.name: internal_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: REMS programs require an internal program owner for assessment coordination, modification management, and FDA correspondence. Critical for REMS compliance tracking, program oversight, and regulatory a

attributes.name: market_payer_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.payer_contract. Business justification: REMS programs impose distribution restrictions that affect payer contracting terms; contracts specify specialty pharmacy networks, certified prescriber requirements, and patient enrollment logistics.

attributes.name: med_education_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.med_education_program. Business justification: REMS programs require healthcare provider education and certification, delivered through medical education programs. REMS with ETASU elements require certified prescriber training; Medical Affairs dev

attributes.name: patient_access_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.patient_access_program. Business justification: Patient access programs must integrate REMS enrollment requirements; hub services coordinate REMS patient registration, prescriber certification verification, and pharmacy network compliance alongside

attributes.name: patient_support_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.patient_support_program. Business justification: REMS programs may require patient enrollment, monitoring, or restricted distribution. PSPs must integrate REMS compliance (e.g., patient registries, prescriber certification) into program design.

attributes.name: rmp_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.rmp. Business justification: REMS programs implement risk minimization measures defined in the RMP. Real business process: RMP identifies important risks → REMS operationalizes mitigation strategies (ETASU, communication plans).

attributes.name: sample_management_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.sample_management. Business justification: REMS programs may restrict sampling to certified prescribers or require patient enrollment. Sample distribution must comply with REMS requirements for controlled access.

attributes.name: assessment_schedule
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Assessment Schedule
attributes.description: FDA-mandated schedule for submitting REMS assessments (e.g., '18 months, 3 years, and 7 years after approval', or 'annually'). Defines the cadence of program effectiveness reporting obligations.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this REMS program master record was first created in the data lakehouse. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: Pharmaceutical dosage form of the drug product covered by the REMS (e.g., oral capsule, injectable solution, transdermal patch). Relevant to dispensing and administration risk controls.

attributes.name: ecm_submission_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Submission Reference
attributes.description: eCTD sequence number or submission reference in Veeva Vault RIM corresponding to the most recent REMS submission or modification filed with FDA. Enables traceability to the regulatory dossier.
attributes.references: eCTD Guidance; FDA ESG; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: etasu_elements
attributes.business_glossary_term: Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU) Description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the specific ETASU elements required under this REMS program (e.g., certified prescriber requirement, certified pharmacy requirement, patient enrollment registry, laboratory monitoring, patient agreement form). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: certified_prescriber|certified_pharmacy|patient_registry|lab_monitoring|patient_agreement|safe_use_condition — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: fda_contact_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Food and Drug Administration (FDA) REMS Contact Name
attributes.description: Name of the FDA project manager or reviewer assigned to this REMS program. Used for official regulatory correspondence and health authority interactions.

attributes.name: goal_statement
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Goal Statement
attributes.description: Official FDA-approved goal statement for the REMS program describing the specific safety outcome the program is designed to achieve (e.g., 'Mitigate the risk of fetal exposure to isotretinoin').

attributes.name: has_communication_plan
attributes.description: Indicates whether the REMS program includes a Communication Plan element targeting healthcare professionals (HCPs) about serious risks associated with the drug.

attributes.name: has_etasu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU) Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the REMS program includes Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU), which are the most restrictive REMS requirements such as certified prescriber/pharmacy networks, patient registries, or laboratory testing requirements.

attributes.name: has_medication_guide
attributes.description: Indicates whether the REMS program includes a Medication Guide as a required REMS element to be dispensed to patients at each prescription fill.

attributes.name: inn_name
attributes.description: WHO-assigned International Nonproprietary Name (INN) of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) subject to the REMS program (e.g., isotretinoin, clozapine, thalidomide).

attributes.name: last_assessment_outcome
attributes.business_glossary_term: Last Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Assessment Outcome
attributes.description: FDA's determination following review of the most recently submitted REMS assessment report. Indicates whether the program is meeting its goals or requires modification.

attributes.name: last_assessment_submission_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Last Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Assessment Submission Date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent REMS assessment report was submitted to FDA via eCTD. Used to verify compliance with the assessment schedule.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.520(c); eCTD Guidance; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: last_modification_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Last Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Modification Date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent FDA-approved modification to the REMS program. Used to track program currency and trigger downstream label and communication updates.

attributes.name: last_modification_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Last Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Modification Type
attributes.description: Classification of the most recent REMS modification as major (substantive change to ETASU or goals), minor (non-substantive change), or administrative (formatting/contact updates).

attributes.name: modification_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Modification Count
attributes.description: Total number of FDA-approved modifications made to the REMS program since initial approval. Tracks program evolution and regulatory change history.

attributes.name: next_assessment_due_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Next Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Assessment Due Date
attributes.description: Date by which the next REMS assessment report must be submitted to FDA per the approved assessment schedule. Critical for regulatory compliance tracking.

attributes.name: program_administrator
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program Administrator
attributes.description: Name of the organization or vendor contracted to administer the REMS program operations (e.g., patient enrollment, prescriber certification, pharmacy certification, call center). May be an internal team or a third-party REMS administrator.

attributes.name: program_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program Name
attributes.description: Official FDA-approved name of the REMS program as registered in Veeva Vault RIM and the FDA REMS database (e.g., 'iPLEDGE REMS', 'TIRF REMS ACCESS').

attributes.name: program_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program Status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the REMS program. 'active' indicates the program is fully operational; 'under_review' indicates FDA is evaluating a modification; 'pending_approval' indicates initial REMS awaiting FDA approval.

attributes.name: program_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program Version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the current approved REMS program document, incremented with each FDA-approved modification (e.g., v1.0, v2.3). Aligns with eCTD submission versioning in Veeva Vault RIM.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.520; eCTD Guidance; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: rems_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program Number
attributes.description: FDA-assigned unique program identifier for the REMS, used for official correspondence and regulatory submissions. Serves as the externally-known business identifier.

attributes.name: requires_certified_pharmacy
attributes.description: Indicates whether pharmacies must be certified or enrolled in the REMS program before they are authorized to dispense the drug. Restricts dispensing to a controlled pharmacy network.

attributes.name: requires_certified_prescriber
attributes.description: Indicates whether prescribers must be certified or enrolled in the REMS program before they are authorized to prescribe the drug. A key ETASU element for high-risk products.

attributes.name: requires_lab_monitoring
attributes.description: Indicates whether the REMS program mandates specific laboratory tests (e.g., pregnancy tests, liver function tests, blood counts) as a condition of prescribing or dispensing the drug.

attributes.name: requires_patient_enrollment
attributes.description: Indicates whether patients must be enrolled in the REMS program (e.g., patient registry or patient agreement) before receiving the drug. Enables tracking of patient exposure and outcomes.

attributes.name: risk_description
attributes.description: Summary description of the serious risk(s) that necessitate the REMS program (e.g., teratogenicity, QT prolongation, severe hepatotoxicity, opioid addiction and overdose). Derived from the FDA-approved REMS document.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.520; FDA REMS Approval Letter; ICH E2A

attributes.name: route_of_administration

attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; EMA EPAR; ICH E10

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the regulatory strategy record was first created in the source system (Veeva Vault RIM). Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault RIM; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: development_phase
attributes.description: Current clinical development phase of the drug program at the time this regulatory strategy is authored. Determines the regulatory interactions and submission milestones applicable. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: preclinical|phase_1|phase_2|phase_3|phase_3b|pre_submission|post_approval — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: ectd_module_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Module Reference
attributes.description: Reference to the eCTD module and section where the regulatory strategy documentation is filed within the submission dossier (e.g., Module 1.2 - Product Overview). Aligns strategy to the ICH eCTD structure.
attributes.references: ICH M4 eCTD; FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eCTD Guidance

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this version of the regulatory strategy is considered active and binding for the development program. Marks the start of the strategy's applicability period.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this version of the regulatory strategy is superseded or retired. Null for currently active strategies. Supports version lifecycle management in Veeva Vault RIM.

attributes.name: fast_track_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether FDA Fast Track Designation is being pursued or has been granted for this program. Fast Track facilitates development and expedites review of drugs treating serious conditions with unmet medical need.

attributes.name: global_filing_sequence
attributes.description: Ordered sequence of regulatory agency submissions planned globally, describing the order in which dossiers will be filed across jurisdictions (e.g., FDA first, then EMA, then PMDA). Supports launch sequencing and resource planning.
attributes.references: ICH M4; ICH E5; FDA; EMA; PMDA; MHRA; NMPA

attributes.name: inn_name
attributes.description: The International Nonproprietary Name (INN) of the active pharmaceutical ingredient as designated by the WHO. Used as the globally recognized non-proprietary identifier for the drug substance in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; ICH Q6A; 21 CFR Part 299

attributes.name: key_regulatory_risks
attributes.description: Narrative description of the principal regulatory risks identified for this program, including data gaps, safety signals, manufacturing concerns, or precedent-setting issues that could delay or prevent approval.
attributes.references: ICH Q9 (Quality Risk Management); FDA Risk Management Guidance; EMA Risk Management Plan

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the regulatory strategy record was most recently updated in the source system. Tracks document revision history for compliance and version control purposes.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault RIM; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: orphan_drug_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) is being pursued or has been granted by FDA or EMA. ODD provides market exclusivity, fee waivers, and tax credits for drugs targeting rare diseases.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 316; EMA Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; Orphan Drug Act

attributes.name: prime_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether EMA PRIority MEdicines (PRIME) designation is being pursued or has been granted. PRIME provides enhanced EMA support for medicines that offer a major therapeutic advantage over existing treatments.
attributes.references: EMA PRIME Scheme; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: priority_markets
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes representing the priority markets targeted for initial regulatory submissions (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU, JPN). Drives global filing sequence planning.
attributes.references: ICH M4; FDA; EMA; PMDA; MHRA; NMPA

attributes.name: regulatory_pathway_type
attributes.description: The planned regulatory approval pathway for the drug program (e.g., NDA 505(b)(1), NDA 505(b)(2), BLA, MAA, Abbreviated NDA, 510(k)). Determines the submission type and data package requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NDA_505b1|NDA_505b2|ANDA|BLA|MAA|NDS|JNDA|sNDA|sBLA|sMAA — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314; 21 CFR Part 601; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH M4

attributes.name: rems_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program is anticipated or required by FDA as part of the approval conditions for this drug. REMS programs manage known or potential serious risks.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDA FDAAA Section 505-1; REMS Guidance

attributes.name: sakigake_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether PMDA Sakigake designation is being pursued for this program in Japan. Sakigake provides priority review and early consultation for innovative drugs addressing serious diseases.
attributes.references: PMDA Sakigake Designation Programme; Japanese Pharmaceutical Affairs Law

attributes.name: strategic_rationale
attributes.description: Narrative explanation of the strategic reasoning behind the chosen regulatory pathway, filing sequence, and expedited program designations. Documents the decision-making basis for regulatory governance review.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH E8; FDA Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: strategy_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier for the regulatory strategy document as assigned in Veeva Vault RIM. Used for cross-functional referencing and regulatory correspondence tracking.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH M4 eCTD

attributes.name: strategy_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the regulatory strategy document within Veeva Vault RIM. Drives workflow routing and version control. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|under_review|approved|active|superseded|retired — promote to reference product if additional statuses are needed]

attributes.name: submission_type
attributes.description: Primary submission type targeted by this regulatory strategy (e.g., IND, NDA, BLA, MAA). Defines the regulatory dossier format and applicable agency requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IND|NDA|BLA|MAA|sNDA|sBLA|sMAA|ANDA|DMF|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312; 21 CFR Part 314; 21 CFR Part 601; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH M4 eCTD

attributes.name: target_approval_date
attributes.description: Anticipated date of regulatory approval from the lead agency based on standard or priority review timelines. Drives commercial launch planning and supply chain readiness.
attributes.references: FDA PDUFA; EMA Centralised Procedure Timeline; PMDA Review Timeline

attributes.name: target_indication
attributes.description: The disease or medical condition for which regulatory approval is being sought. Defines the scope of the regulatory strategy and aligns with the Target Product Profile (TPP).
attributes.references: ICH E8; FDA Guidance for Industry; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

attributes.name: target_submission_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the primary regulatory submission (e.g., NDA, BLA, MAA) to the lead agency. Used for milestone tracking and commercial launch timeline planning.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; ICH M4; FDA PDUFA

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Broad therapeutic area classification for the drug program (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Used for portfolio-level regulatory planning and resource allocation.
attributes.references: ATC Classification; WHO INN; ICH E8

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Descriptive title of the regulatory strategy document, typically including the compound name, indication, and target market. Human-readable label used in Veeva Vault RIM and regulatory governance meetings.

attributes.name: tpp_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the Target Product Profile (TPP) describing the desired label claims, patient population, dosing regimen, safety profile, and differentiation from existing therapies. Anchors the regulatory strategy to commercial objectives.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Target Product Profile; ICH E8; EMA Guideline on TPP

attributes.name: vault_document_reference
attributes.description: The unique document identifier assigned by Veeva Vault RIM to the regulatory strategy document. Enables direct cross-reference and deep-linking to the source document in the regulatory information management system.

attributes.name: version

attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH M4

products.name: dossier_document

Captures document title, CTD section code, document type, version, author, creation date, approval date, document status, file format, file size, checksum, and Veeva Vault document ID. Supports dossier compilation, completeness review, and submission readiness assessment. Aligns with ICH CTD structure (M4) and eCTD technical specification (M8).

attributes.name: dmf_id

attributes.name: internal_order_id

attributes.name: inventory_lot_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.master_batch_record. Business justification: CMC dossier documents (Module 3.2.P.3) reference specific MBRs as source documentation. Essential for eCTD compilation, ensuring traceability between regulatory submissions and approved manufacturing

attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD Structure; Veeva Vault RIM; SAP S/4HANA MM Module

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.method_validation. Business justification: CTD Module 3 (Quality) dossier documents reference analytical method validation reports. Essential for regulatory submission assembly—every analytical method in CMC sections must have validated method

attributes.name: psur_id

attributes.name: related_document_dossier_document_id

attributes.name: rmp_id

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent regulatory submission (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, etc.) to which this document belongs. Links the document to its submission context.

attributes.name: approval_date

attributes.name: checksum_algorithm
attributes.description: The hashing algorithm used to generate the document checksum (e.g., MD5, SHA-256). Required to correctly validate file integrity during eCTD processing.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this dossier document record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5; Veeva Vault RIM Audit Trail

attributes.name: ctd_module

attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD Structure; ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification

attributes.name: ctd_section_code

attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD Structure; ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification

attributes.name: document_number

attributes.name: document_status

attributes.references: ICH M4 CTD Structure; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: document_type
attributes.description: Classification of the document by its regulatory content type (e.g., Clinical Study Report, Investigator Brochure, Stability Report, Labeling, Module 2 Summary, Nonclinical Study Report). attributes.name: expiry_date

attributes.name: file_format
attributes.description: File format of the document (e.g., PDF, XML, SAS dataset, DOCX). PDF is the primary format for eCTD submissions; XML is used for structured data files and backbone.
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide; EMA eCTD Guidance

attributes.name: file_name
attributes.description: The actual file name of the document as stored in the eCTD dossier directory structure, including extension. Must comply with eCTD file naming conventions (lowercase, no spaces, max 64 characters).
attributes.references: ICH M8 eCTD Technical Specification; FDA eCTD Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: file_size_bytes
attributes.description: Size of the document file in bytes. Used for dossier volume management, submission package size validation, and health authority file size compliance checks.

attributes.name: health_authority

attributes.name: review_due_date

products.name: application_indication
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory approval pursuit between a regulatory application and a therapeutic indication. It captures the approval status, designation flags, exclusivity dates, and label claims that exist only in the context of a specific application seeking approval for a specific indication. Each record links one application to one indication with jurisdiction-specific approval data, supporting regulatory tracking of multi-indication applications and multi-jurisdiction indication pursuits.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical regulatory operations, a single regulatory application (NDA, BLA, MAA) can seek approval for multiple therapeutic indications, either in the original submission or via supplemental applications (sNDAs). Conversely, a single indication can be pursued across multiple applications in different jurisdictions (US NDA, EU MAA, Japan PMDA) or via different regulatory pathways. Regulatory affairs teams actively manage application-indication pairs, tracking approval status, designation flags, exclusivity dates, and label claims that are specific to each application-indication-jurisdiction combination.

attributes.name: application_indication_id
attributes.description: Primary key for the application_indication association

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the regulatory application (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, ANDA) that is seeking approval for this indication

attributes.name: indication_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the therapeutic indication being pursued in this application

attributes.name: accelerated_approval_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this product-indication received accelerated approval based on surrogate or intermediate clinical endpoints, with requirement for post-marketing confirmatory trials. True indicates accelerated approval pathway used; False indicates standard approval. [Moved from product_indication: Accelerated approval is granted per application-indication pair. The same indication may receive accelerated approval in one application but standard approval in another.]
attributes.references: FDA Accelerated Approval, 21 CFR 314 Subpart H, 21 CFR 601 Subpart E

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the health authority granted marketing authorization for this indication via this application. Null if not yet approved.

attributes.name: approval_jurisdiction
attributes.description: The regulatory jurisdiction or health authority that granted approval for this application-indication combination (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA).

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current regulatory approval status of this specific application for this specific indication. Tracks the lifecycle state of the application-indication pursuit.

attributes.name: breakthrough_designation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this application received breakthrough therapy designation for this specific indication from the FDA.

attributes.name: conditional_approval_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this product-indication received conditional marketing authorization (EMA pathway) based on less comprehensive data than normally required, with obligations to provide additional data post-approval. True indicates conditional approval; False indicates standard authorization. [Moved from product_indication: Conditional approval (EMA) is granted per application-indication pair. This is application-specific regulatory status.]
attributes.references: EMA Conditional Marketing Authorization, Regulation (EC) No 507/2006

attributes.name: exclusivity_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which regulatory market exclusivity protections expire for this application-indication combination. Exclusivity is granted per application-indication pair.

attributes.name: fast_track_designation_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this product-indication combination has received FDA Fast Track designation to facilitate development and expedite review of drugs treating serious conditions and filling unmet medical needs. True indicates fast track designation granted; False indicates not designated. [Moved from product_indication: Fast track designation is granted per application-indication pair by the FDA. This is application-specific, not indication-specific.]
attributes.references: FDA Fast Track Designation, 21 CFR 312 Subpart E

attributes.name: indication_added_date
attributes.description: Date on which this indication was first added to this application (original submission or supplemental application date).

attributes.name: label_claim_text
attributes.description: The exact verbatim text from the approved product label describing the indication as approved by the health authority for this specific application. Varies by application and jurisdiction.

attributes.name: orphan_designation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this application received orphan drug designation for this specific indication from the health authority.

attributes.name: priority_review_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this product-indication application received priority review status, reducing FDA review time from standard 10 months to 6 months for drugs that offer significant improvements in safety or effectiveness. True indicates priority review granted; False indicates standard review. [Moved from product_indication: Priority review is granted per application submission, not per indication alone. This flag varies by application-indication combination.]
attributes.references: FDA Priority Review, PDUFA Performance Goals

attributes.name: submission_sequence_number
attributes.description: The eCTD sequence number or supplemental application number for the submission that added or modified this indication within the application lifecycle.

products.name: application_site_authorization
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory authorization relationship between a regulatory application and a manufacturing site. It captures the site-specific role in the application (API manufacturer, drug product manufacturer, fill-finish, packaging, testing laboratory), the manufacturing step performed at each site, the regulatory approval status of that specific site for that specific application, qualification dates, and capacity allocation. Each record links one application to one manufacturing site with attributes that exist only in the context of this regulatory authorization relationship.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical regulatory operations, a single regulatory application (NDA, BLA, MAA) routinely lists multiple manufacturing sites performing different roles in the supply chain (API synthesis at one site, drug product formulation at another, fill-finish at a third, packaging at a fourth, and testing laboratories). Conversely, a manufacturing site typically supports multiple regulatory applications across different drug products. The business actively manages these authorizations as distinct regulatory compliance artifacts, tracking site-specific approval statuses, qualification dates, manufacturing step assignments, and capacity allocations for each application-site pairing.

attributes.description: The regulatory approval status of this specific site for this specific application. A site may be approved for one application but pending for another. Tracks health authority acceptance of the site for manufacturing/testing this drug product.

attributes.name: capacity_allocation
attributes.description: The percentage or amount of site capacity allocated to this specific application. Enables capacity planning and tracking when a site supports multiple applications. May be expressed as percentage of total site capacity or absolute units.

attributes.name: exclusion_date
attributes.description: The date on which this manufacturing site was removed from the regulatory application (e.g., due to site closure, transfer to another CMO, or regulatory non-compliance). Enables tracking of site change history.

attributes.name: gmp_inspection_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a health authority GMP inspection of this site is required as part of the approval process for this application. Inspection requirements vary by application type, site history, and regulatory pathway.

attributes.name: inclusion_date
attributes.description: The date on which this manufacturing site was included in the regulatory application dossier. Tracks when the site was added to the application (original submission or subsequent variation).

attributes.name: last_inspection_date_for_application
attributes.description: The date of the most recent health authority inspection of this site specifically in the context of this application. Different from the site's general last inspection date, as inspections may be application-triggered.

attributes.name: manufacturing_step
attributes.description: The specific manufacturing step or process stage assigned to this site for this application (e.g., API synthesis, formulation, sterile filling, lyophilization, primary packaging). Enables tracking of the manufacturing chain across multiple sites.

attributes.name: primary_site_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the primary manufacturing site for this application for this manufacturing step. An application may have multiple sites for the same step (backup capacity), but typically designates one as primary.

attributes.name: qualification_date
attributes.description: The date on which this site was qualified by the health authority for manufacturing or testing activities related to this specific application. Qualification is site-and-application-specific.

attributes.name: site_master_file_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the Site Master File (SMF) or Drug Master File (DMF) submitted to the health authority for this site in support of this application. SMF references are application-specific.
attributes.references: FDA DMF, EMA Site Master File

attributes.name: site_role
attributes.description: The specific manufacturing or testing role that this site performs for this application. A site may have different roles for different applications.

products.name: service_engagement
products.description: This association product represents the Contract between application and vendor. It captures the engagement of external vendors (CROs, CMOs, regulatory consultants) to support specific regulatory applications with defined services, timelines, and deliverables. Each record links one application to one vendor with attributes that exist only in the context of this service engagement relationship.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical regulatory operations, a single regulatory application (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA) routinely engages multiple external vendors simultaneously: CROs conduct clinical trials, CMOs manufacture drug substance and drug product, regulatory consultants provide strategic guidance, and medical writing firms prepare dossier modules. Conversely, each vendor (especially CROs and CMOs) supports multiple applications across the company's portfolio. The business actively manages these engagements as distinct operational entities, tracking service type, contract value, deliverable status, and engagement timelines for each application-vendor pair.

attributes.name: service_engagement_id
attributes.description: Primary key for the regulatory_service_engagement association

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the regulatory application being supported by this vendor engagement

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the vendor providing services for this regulatory application

attributes.name: contract_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the contract value (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Specifies the currency in which the vendor is compensated for this engagement.

attributes.name: contract_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the contract or purchase order governing this vendor engagement for this application. Links to procurement contract management system.

attributes.name: contract_value
attributes.description: Total monetary value of the contract or purchase order for this vendor engagement on this application. Represents the financial commitment for this specific application-vendor service relationship.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this engagement record was created in the system.

attributes.name: deliverable_status
attributes.description: Current status of the deliverables expected from this vendor for this application. Tracks progress of vendor obligations and service completion.

attributes.name: engagement_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the vendor engagement for this application concluded or is scheduled to conclude. May be actual completion date or planned end date for ongoing engagements.

attributes.name: engagement_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the vendor engagement for this application officially commenced. Marks the beginning of service delivery under the contract.

attributes.name: engagement_status
attributes.description: Overall lifecycle status of this vendor engagement for this application. Indicates whether the engagement is currently active, has concluded, or has been suspended/terminated.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this engagement record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: primary_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary contact person at the vendor organization responsible for delivering services for this specific application engagement.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Classification of the service provided by the vendor for this application. Defines the scope of work (e.g., CRO conducting clinical trials, CMO manufacturing drug substance, regulatory consultant providing strategy).

products.name: payer_coverage
products.description: This association product represents the coverage contract between a regulatory approval and a payer account. It captures the specific terms under which a payer agrees to cover an approved drug product, including formulary placement, utilization management requirements, and contract economics. Each record links one approval to one payer account with attributes that exist only in the context of this payer-specific coverage relationship.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical market access operations, a single regulatory approval (e.g., an oncology drug approved by FDA) is independently negotiated with dozens or hundreds of payer organizations (Medicare, UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Anthem, etc.), each resulting in distinct coverage terms including formulary tier placement, prior authorization requirements, rebate agreements, and utilization management policies. Conversely, a single payer account covers hundreds of approved drug products across multiple therapeutic areas, each with payer-specific coverage terms. The business actively manages these payer coverage agreements as operational entities with lifecycle tracking, contract renewal cycles, and performance monitoring.

attributes.name: payer_coverage_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this payer coverage agreement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: approval_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the regulatory approval record for the drug product covered under this payer agreement

attributes.name: negotiation_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the market access account manager or payer relations director responsible for negotiating and maintaining this specific payer coverage agreement.

attributes.name: payer_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the payer account that provides coverage under this agreement

attributes.name: contract_type
attributes.description: Type of commercial arrangement governing this specific payer-product coverage relationship. Reflects the negotiation structure for this combination.

attributes.name: contract_value
attributes.description: Estimated annual contract value or rebate commitment associated with this payer coverage agreement for this specific approved product. Commercially sensitive relationship-specific data.

attributes.name: coverage_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the coverage agreement between this payer and this approved product. Tracks whether coverage is currently in effect.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this payer's coverage for this approved product became or will become effective. Marks the start of the coverage relationship.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this payer's coverage agreement for this approved product expires and must be renegotiated. Null if evergreen or indefinite.

attributes.name: formulary_tier
attributes.description: The specific formulary tier assigned by this payer for this approved drug product. Determines patient cost-sharing and access. Varies by payer for the same approval.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) committee review by this payer for this approved product. Tracks formulary decision cycle history.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next P&T committee review of this product by this payer. Enables proactive market access planning.

attributes.name: prior_authorization_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this specific payer requires prior authorization for coverage of this specific approved product. Utilization management requirement that varies by payer-product combination.

attributes.name: quantity_limit
attributes.description: Payer-imposed quantity limits for this approved product (e.g., '30 tablets per 30 days'). Utilization management control specific to this payer-product relationship.

attributes.name: rebate_percentage
attributes.description: Negotiated rebate percentage that the manufacturer provides to this payer for this approved product. Commercially sensitive and varies by payer-product negotiation.

attributes.name: step_therapy_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this payer requires step therapy (fail-first protocols) for this specific approved product. Utilization management policy that varies by payer-product combination.

domains.name: manufacturing
domains.description: Manages production of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP) including API production, formulation, fill-finish, and packaging under cGMP. Covers manufacturing execution system (MES) data, batch records, critical process parameters (CPP), critical quality attributes (CQA), equipment scheduling, and production schedules. Includes CMO and CDMO oversight. Integrates with SAP PP/QM and MES systems. Supports QbD principles and PAT implementation per 21 CFR Parts 210/211.
domains.references: 21 CFR Parts 210/211 / ICH Q7 / ICH Q10 / ISPE GAMP 5

attributes.description: Date and time when the production order record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data governance and compliance.

attributes.name: expiry_date

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user
attributes.description: User ID of the person who last modified the production order record. Required for audit trail and accountability per 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the production order record was last updated. Audit trail field for tracking changes to order details, status transitions, or confirmations.

attributes.name: order_number

attributes.name: pat_enabled_flag

attributes.name: planned_quantity

attributes.name: priority

attributes.name: qbd_flag

attributes.name: reconciliation_status

attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 211.188 Batch Production and Control Records; ICH Q7 Section 6.7 - Material Reconciliation

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_flag

Requires enhanced documentation and retention per regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314 - Applications for FDA Approval to Market a New Drug; ICH M4 Common Technical Document

attributes.name: retest_date
attributes.description: Date by which Drug Substance (DS) or Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) must be retested to confirm continued compliance with specifications. Applicable primarily to bulk API and intermediates stored before further processing.

attributes.name: rework_flag

attributes.description: Indicates whether the production order is a validation batch used for process qualification, process performance qualification (PPQ), or continued process verification. Validation batches require enhanced documentation and are used to demonstrate process capability and reproducibility.

attributes.name: yield_percentage

products.name: batch_record

Serves as the primary cGMP compliance document and SSOT for batch lifecycle from production through disposition. Sourced from MES and SAP PP/QM.
