attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: ICSRs reference patents when adverse events relate to patented formulations, manufacturing processes, or delivery systems. Critical for causality assessment, regulatory submissions, and understanding

attributes.name: patient_id
attributes.description: FK to patient.patient.patient_id — Safety-to-patient linkage enables longitudinal safety analysis — ICSRs must link to patient records for duplicate detection, medical history context, and regulatory case processing (ICH E2B R3).

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.pv_product. Business justification: ICSR reports adverse events for a specific product under PV surveillance. The pv_product_id FK links to the authoritative PV product master. Remove suspect_product_name as it normalizes to pv_product.

attributes.name: regulatory_inspection_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_inspection. Business justification: Individual case reports are cited in inspection observations for reporting delays, coding errors, or causality assessment deficiencies. Inspection findings reference specific cases for deficiency docu

attributes.name: reporter_country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Reporter country determines regulatory reporting obligations, timelines (15-day vs 90-day rules), and format requirements (E2B versions). Critical for pharmacovigilance compliance and case routing to

attributes.name: reporter_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.reporter. Business justification: Every ICSR has a reporter who submitted it. This is a critical missing link. The reporter_id FK allows joining to get reporter qualification, type, and contact details. Remove primary_reporter_type as

attributes.name: rsi_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.rsi. Business justification: ICSR listedness assessment references RSI to determine if the adverse event is listed in the reference safety information. Add rsi_id FK (nullable - populated during listedness assessment). This links

attributes.name: ae_onset_date
attributes.description: Date of onset of the adverse event/reaction as reported by the reporter. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) E.i.4. Used for time-to-onset analysis, dechallenge/rechallenge assessment, and signal detection.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) E.i.4; ICH E2A; GVP Module VI

attributes.name: ae_outcome
attributes.description: Outcome of the adverse event at the time of reporting. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) E.i.7. Fatal outcome triggers mandatory expedited reporting and mortality signal analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) E.i.7; ICH E2A; GVP Module VI B.3

attributes.name: case_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text medical narrative summarizing the adverse event, patient history, suspect drug details, clinical course, and outcome. Authored by the medical reviewer. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) H.1. Classified confidential as it may contain de-identified but sensitive clinical information.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) H.1; GVP Module VI B.6; 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: case_nullification_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this case version represents a nullification (retraction) of a previously submitted ICSR. True = nullification report submitted to health authorities. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.11.1.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.11.1; EMA EudraVigilance Technical Specification

attributes.name: case_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the ICSR within the pharmacovigilance case management system (Argus Safety). Drives SLA monitoring for 7-day and 15-day regulatory reporting deadlines. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new|in_triage|in_processing|pending_review|closed|archived|nullified — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: case_version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version counter for the ICSR record. Version 1 = initial report; subsequent integers represent follow-up reports with new or amended information. Nullification reports are tracked via case_nullification_flag. Supports full version history per ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2 and 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2A

attributes.name: causality_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of the causal relationship between the suspect drug and the adverse event, using WHO-UMC causality categories. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i. Drives listedness and SUSAR determination. Assessed by the company's medical reviewer.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment System; GVP Module VI B.3

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the ICSR record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system (Argus Safety / Oracle AERS). Supports 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail and GDPR data processing records.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); GDPR Article 30

attributes.name: dechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome of dechallenge — whether the adverse event resolved or improved upon discontinuation of the suspect drug. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.3a. Key input for causality assessment and benefit-risk evaluation.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.3a; ICH E2A; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment

attributes.name: duplicate_assessment_outcome
attributes.description: Result of the duplicate case detection assessment performed during intake triage. Duplicate cases are linked to the master case and suppressed from regulatory submission counts. Critical for accurate signal detection and aggregate reporting.
attributes.references: GVP Module VI B.5; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Duplicate Detection

attributes.name: edc_reconciliation_status
attributes.description: Status of SAE reconciliation between the pharmacovigilance database (Argus Safety) and the clinical trial EDC system (Medidata Rave). Applicable when report_type = 'clinical_trial'. Ensures consistency between safety database and clinical database per ICH E6(R2) GCP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.17; 21 CFR Part 312.62; GVP Module VI

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the ICSR record in the source system. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail compliance and Silver layer incremental data loading.

attributes.name: listedness_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the adverse drug reaction is listed (expected) in the current Reference Safety Information (RSI) — Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS) or approved product labeling. Unlisted + serious = SUSAR (Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction), triggering expedited reporting. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2D; ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i; GVP Module VI B.3; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: literature_reference
attributes.description: PubMed Identifier (PMID) or Digital Object Identifier (DOI) for literature-sourced ICSRs. Populated when report_type = 'literature'. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.4.r.1. Supports systematic literature review (SLR) traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.4.r.1; GVP Module VI B.2; ICH E2D

attributes.name: minimum_criteria_met_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the ICSR meets the four ICH E2B minimum criteria for a valid case: (1) identifiable reporter, (2) identifiable patient, (3) suspect drug, (4) adverse event. Cases not meeting minimum criteria are tracked but not submitted. Corresponds to ICH E2D minimum information requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; ICH E2B(R3); GVP Module VI B.1

attributes.name: most_recent_info_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent follow-up information received for this case, resetting the regulatory clock for follow-up submissions. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.5.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.5; GVP Module VI B.4

attributes.name: patient_age_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for patient_age_value. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) D.2.2b. Supports neonatal and pediatric cases where age is expressed in days, weeks, or months.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) D.2.2b; ICH E11 (Pediatric Studies)

attributes.name: patient_age_value
attributes.description: De-identified patient age at the time of the adverse event onset, expressed as a numeric value. Must be used in conjunction with patient_age_unit. Stored per GDPR/HIPAA de-identification standards. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) D.2.2a.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) D.2.2a; GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; GVP Module VI

attributes.name: patient_sex
attributes.description: Biological sex of the patient as reported. De-identified demographic field per GDPR/HIPAA. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) D.5. Used in signal detection and benefit-risk assessment stratification.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) D.5; GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164

attributes.name: patient_weight_kg
attributes.description: Patient body weight in kilograms at the time of the adverse event, as reported. De-identified per GDPR/HIPAA. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) D.3. Used for dose-weight relationship analysis in signal detection.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) D.3; GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164

attributes.name: primary_ae_meddra_pt
attributes.business_glossary_term: Primary Adverse Event MedDRA Preferred Term (PT)
attributes.description: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) Preferred Term (PT) coding for the primary adverse event/reaction reported. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) E.i.2.1b. Standardized coding enables cross-case signal detection and regulatory submission.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) E.i.2.1b; MedDRA; ICH M1; GVP Module VI

attributes.name: primary_ae_meddra_soc
attributes.business_glossary_term: Primary Adverse Event MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC)
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) for the primary adverse event, derived from the MedDRA PT hierarchy. Supports aggregate signal detection by organ system and PSUR/PBRER tabulation requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) E.i.2.1a; MedDRA; ICH E2C(R2) PBRER; GVP Module VII

attributes.name: receipt_date
attributes.description: Date the ICSR was first received by the company (MAH/sponsor), establishing the regulatory clock start date (Day 0) for 7-day expedited and 15-day expedited reporting obligations. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.4.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.4; 21 CFR Part 314.81(b)(1); GVP Module VI B.4

attributes.name: rechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome of rechallenge — whether the adverse event recurred upon re-administration of the suspect drug after dechallenge. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.3b. Strengthens causality evidence and is critical for SUSAR assessment in clinical trials.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.3b; ICH E2A; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_deadline
attributes.description: Calculated deadline date by which the ICSR must be submitted to the relevant health authority (FDA, EMA, PMDA, NMPA, TGA). Derived from receipt_date plus applicable reporting window (7 or 15 calendar days for expedited reports; 90 days for non-expedited). SLA-critical field for compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81(b)(1); GVP Module VI B.4; ICH E2A; PMDA Pharmacovigilance Regulations

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_status
attributes.description: Current submission status of the ICSR to the applicable health authority. Tracks compliance against 7-day and 15-day expedited reporting deadlines. Overdue status triggers escalation per PV SLA management procedures.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81(b)(1); GVP Module VI B.4; ICH E2A; PMDA Pharmacovigilance Regulations

attributes.name: report_type
attributes.description: Classification of the ICSR source channel per ICH E2B(R3) C.1.3. Drives regulatory reporting obligations and processing workflows. Spontaneous reports from HCPs/patients, literature-sourced cases (PMID/DOI), clinical trial SAEs, solicited reports from patient support programs, and other sources.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.3; 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module VI

attributes.name: sender_case_number
attributes.description: Internal case number assigned by the company (MAH/sponsor) in the source system (Argus Safety / Oracle AERS). Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.8.1. Used for internal tracking and reconciliation with the worldwide unique case ID.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.8.1; Argus Safety Case Number

attributes.name: serious_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse event meets ICH E2A seriousness criteria (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, or medically significant). True = Serious Adverse Event (SAE). Drives expedited 7-day or 15-day regulatory reporting obligation. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) E.i.3.2.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) E.i.3.2; 21 CFR Part 312.32; GVP Module VI B.3

attributes.name: seriousness_criteria
attributes.description: Specific ICH E2A seriousness criterion or criteria met by the adverse event. Multiple criteria may apply. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) E.i.3.2a-f. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) E.i.3.2a-f; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: source_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the adverse event occurred. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.17.1. Determines applicable regulatory authority for submission routing (FDA, EMA, PMDA, NMPA, TGA, MHRA).
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.17.1; ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; GVP Module VI

attributes.name: susar_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the case qualifies as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) — i.e., serious, unexpected (unlisted), and with a reasonable causal relationship to the investigational medicinal product. True = SUSAR requiring 7-day (fatal/life-threatening) or 15-day expedited reporting to health authorities and ethics committees.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; GVP Module VI

attributes.name: suspect_product_indication
attributes.description: Medical indication (disease/condition) for which the suspect drug was prescribed or used, coded using MedDRA terminology. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) G.k.7.r.2b. Supports benefit-risk assessment and signal contextualization.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.7.r.2b; MedDRA; GVP Module VI

attributes.name: target_health_authority
attributes.description: Primary health authority to which this ICSR must be submitted. Determined by source_country_code and product registration status. Drives submission format selection (MedWatch 3500A, EudraVigilance E2B, J-ICSR, NMPA XML). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|NMPA|MHRA|TGA|WHO|ANVISA|Health_Canada|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance; PMDA E2B(R3) Implementation Guide; NMPA ADR Reporting Regulations

attributes.name: worldwide_unique_case_number
attributes.description: Globally unique case identifier assigned at intake, conforming to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.1 format (sender identifier + case number). Used for cross-regional deduplication and regulatory submission tracking across FDA MedWatch, EudraVigilance, J-ICSR, and NMPA.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.1; 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance Technical Specification

products.name: pv_adverse_reaction
products.description: Granular adverse event record linked to an ICSR. Captures the specific event term (MedDRA coded at PT, HLT, HLGT, SOC levels with version tracking), verbatim reporter term, onset date, resolution date, outcome (recovered, not recovered, fatal, unknown), seriousness criteria, severity grade (CTCAE where applicable), and listedness determination against reference safety information. Includes coding metadata: auto-coded vs manual review, coding date. One ICSR may contain multiple adverse events. Supports signal detection aggregation by MedDRA term and regulatory line listing generation.
products.reference: MedDRA Adverse Event Term / ICH E2A

attributes.name: pv_adverse_reaction_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each adverse reaction record within the pharmacovigilance system. Primary key for the pv_adverse_reaction data product in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 314; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: atc_classification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Linking adverse reactions to ATC therapeutic class enables signal detection by drug category, benefit-risk analysis, and PSUR aggregate reporting. Medical coding teams perform MedDRA-to-ATC cross-tabu

attributes.name: brand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: Adverse reactions aggregated by brand for safety surveillance, label update decisions, and competitive safety positioning. Essential for brand risk management committees and periodic benefit-risk eval

attributes.name: icsr_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) to which this adverse reaction belongs. One ICSR may contain multiple adverse reaction records. Supports header-detail navigation for case processing.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the suspect medicinal product (drug product) associated with this adverse reaction. Links to the master product record for the drug under pharmacovigilance surveillance.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) B.4; FDA NDA/BLA; EMA EudraVigilance product dictionary; Argus Safety product field

attributes.name: rsi_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.rsi. Business justification: Listedness determination for adverse reactions uses RSI (Reference Safety Information) as the authoritative source. Add rsi_id FK to link to the specific RSI version used for assessment. Remove rsi_do

attributes.name: action_taken
attributes.description: Action taken with the suspect medicinal product in response to the adverse reaction: dose reduced, drug withdrawn, dose not changed, not applicable, unknown, or dose increased. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.4.k.8 and is required for regulatory ICSR submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) B.4.k.8; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety action taken

attributes.name: case_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text medical narrative describing the clinical course of this adverse reaction, including relevant medical history, concomitant medications, treatment, and outcome. Required for regulatory ICSR submissions and medical review. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field H.1.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) H.1; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety narrative field

attributes.name: causality_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of the causal relationship between the suspect drug and the adverse reaction, using WHO-UMC or company standard causality categories. Drives listedness determination, SUSAR classification, and signal detection weighting.
attributes.references: WHO-UMC Causality Assessment System; ICH E2B(R3) B.4.k.18; FDA MedWatch; Argus Safety causality

attributes.name: causality_method
attributes.description: The methodology or algorithm used to perform the causality assessment (e.g., WHO-UMC scale, Naranjo algorithm, company-specific algorithm). Supports audit trail and methodological consistency across cases.
attributes.references: WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; Naranjo Algorithm; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety

attributes.name: coded_by
attributes.description: User identifier of the medical coder or system process that performed or confirmed the MedDRA coding. Required for audit trail under 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance. Stores the user login or system account name.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Argus Safety audit trail; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: coding_date
attributes.description: Date on which the MedDRA coding was completed for this adverse reaction. Used for coding turnaround time metrics, audit trail, and compliance with regulatory submission timelines.
attributes.references: MedDRA Term Selection: Points to Consider; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: coding_method
attributes.description: Indicates whether the MedDRA coding was performed automatically by the safety system (auto-coded), manually by a medical coder (manual review), or auto-coded and subsequently confirmed by manual review. Supports coding quality metrics and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: MedDRA Term Selection: Points to Consider; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety coding workflow; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this adverse reaction record was first created in the pharmacovigilance safety database. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VI. Supports case processing timeline metrics.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety audit trail

attributes.name: ctcae_grade
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade
attributes.description: Severity grade assigned per the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE), ranging from 1 (mild) to 5 (death). Applicable primarily for oncology clinical trial adverse events. Null for non-oncology or post-market cases where CTCAE grading is not applicable.
attributes.references: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Oncology guidance; Medidata Rave CTCAE grading

attributes.name: dechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome of dechallenge (withdrawal of the suspect drug) on the adverse reaction. Positive dechallenge (reaction improved or resolved after withdrawal) supports causality. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.4.k.18.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) B.4.k.18; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; Argus Safety dechallenge field

attributes.name: is_serious
attributes.description: Indicates whether this adverse reaction meets the regulatory definition of a Serious Adverse Event (SAE) per ICH E2A criteria. True if any seriousness criterion is met. Drives expedited reporting timelines (7-day or 15-day) to health authorities.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.3; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: is_susar
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this adverse reaction has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR). True when the reaction is serious, unexpected (unlisted), and there is a reasonable causal relationship to the investigational medicinal product. Triggers mandatory expedited reporting to health authorities and ethics committees.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA SUSAR reporting guideline

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this adverse reaction record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11. Used to track follow-up updates and case amendments in the safety database.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety audit trail

attributes.name: listedness_determination
attributes.description: Determination of whether this adverse reaction is listed (expected) or unlisted (unexpected) in the current Reference Safety Information (RSI), such as the Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS) or Investigator Brochure (IB). Unlisted serious reactions in clinical trials constitute Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) requiring expedited reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2D; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA SUSAR reporting guideline; Argus Safety listedness

attributes.name: meddra_hlgt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) High Level Group Term (HLGT) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA High Level Group Term (HLGT) code, one level above HLT in the MedDRA hierarchy. Supports broader therapeutic area grouping for signal detection and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: meddra_hlt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) High Level Term (HLT) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA High Level Term (HLT) code representing the grouping level above the Preferred Term. Used for aggregate signal detection and periodic safety update report (PSUR) tabulations.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2C(R2) PSUR

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) numeric code assigned to this adverse reaction after coding. The PT is the primary level used for regulatory reporting, signal detection, and line listing generation. Mandatory for ICSR submissions to FDA and EMA.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.2a; EMA EudraVigilance; FDA MedWatch

attributes.name: meddra_pt_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Name
attributes.description: Human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) label corresponding to the meddra_pt_code. Stored denormalized for reporting and line listing generation without requiring a join to the MedDRA reference table.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.2b

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code representing the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy. Used for regulatory line listings, PSUR summary tabulations, and risk management plan (RMP) categorization.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.2c; ICH E2C(R2); EMA RMP guideline

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Version
attributes.description: Version of the MedDRA dictionary used to code this adverse reaction (e.g., 26.0, 26.1). Critical for regulatory submissions and recoding exercises when MedDRA versions are updated. Required for reproducibility of signal detection analyses.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3); EMA EudraVigilance technical specification

attributes.name: medical_confirmation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse reaction has been medically confirmed by a healthcare professional (HCP). Medically confirmed cases carry greater weight in signal detection and regulatory reporting. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field A.1.7.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.7; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety

attributes.name: onset_date
attributes.description: Date on which the adverse reaction first began. Used to calculate time-to-onset from drug exposure, supports causality assessment, and is required for ICSR regulatory submissions. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.2.i.4.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.4; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety

attributes.name: outcome_code
attributes.description: Standardized outcome of the adverse reaction at the time of reporting. Values align with ICH E2B(R3) outcome codes: recovered/resolved, recovering/resolving, not recovered/not resolved, fatal, unknown, recovered with sequelae. Mandatory for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.7; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety outcome field

attributes.name: reaction_duration_days
attributes.description: Duration of the adverse reaction in days, calculated from onset to resolution. Stored as a business attribute when explicitly reported by the reporter or calculated during case processing. Supports time-to-resolution analytics and benefit-risk assessments.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.5; Argus Safety duration field; ICH E2C(R2) PSUR

attributes.name: reaction_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential line number of this adverse reaction within the parent ICSR, enabling ordering and identification of multiple events within a single case. Corresponds to the reaction/event sequence in ICH E2B(R3) message structure.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section B.2; Argus Safety reaction sequence

attributes.name: reaction_status
attributes.description: Current workflow processing status of this adverse reaction record within the pharmacovigilance case management system: new (received, not yet processed), under review, coded (MedDRA coding complete), medically reviewed, closed (finalized), or deleted (voided). Drives case management workflow in Argus Safety.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; Argus Safety case workflow; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: rechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome of rechallenge (re-administration of the suspect drug after withdrawal) if performed. Positive rechallenge (reaction recurred) strengthens causality. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.4.k.19.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) B.4.k.19; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; Argus Safety rechallenge field

attributes.name: regulatory_report_type
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory reporting obligation triggered by this adverse reaction: 7-day expedited (unexpected fatal/life-threatening SUSAR), 15-day expedited (other serious unexpected), periodic (PSUR/PBRER), non-expedited, or not reportable. Drives submission workflow and deadline tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: reporting_source_type
attributes.description: Classification of the original source from which this adverse reaction was reported: spontaneous (unsolicited), clinical trial, published literature, regulatory authority, or other. Determines applicable reporting timelines and regulatory obligations. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field A.1.4.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.4; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance; ICH E2D

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the adverse reaction resolved or ended. Null if the event is ongoing, fatal, or outcome is unknown. Used to calculate event duration and supports outcome determination. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.2.i.6.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.6; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; Argus Safety

attributes.name: seriousness_criteria
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of applicable seriousness criteria met by this adverse reaction per ICH E2A: death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability/incapacity, congenital anomaly, medically significant. Supports regulatory reporting classification and expedited reporting decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|prolonged_hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) B.1.i.3; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: severity_description
attributes.description: Narrative severity classification of the adverse reaction using standard WHO/ICH terminology: mild, moderate, severe, life-threatening, or fatal. Complements CTCAE grade for non-oncology cases and post-market surveillance where CTCAE grading is not used.
attributes.references: WHO Adverse Reaction Terminology; ICH E2B(R3); FDA MedWatch; Argus Safety severity field

attributes.name: signal_detection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this adverse reaction record has been flagged as contributing to a potential pharmacovigilance signal under review. Set by the signal detection process in the safety database. Supports signal management workflow and regulatory signal reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module IX; FDA Pharmacovigilance guidance

attributes.name: time_to_onset_days
attributes.description: Number of days from the first dose of the suspect drug to the onset of the adverse reaction. A key pharmacovigilance metric used in signal detection, causality assessment, and benefit-risk evaluation. Derived from drug start date and reaction onset date during case processing.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); WHO-UMC Signal Detection; FDA Pharmacovigilance guidance; Argus Safety

attributes.name: verbatim_term
attributes.description: The exact adverse event term as reported by the original reporter (patient, healthcare professional, or literature source) before MedDRA coding. Preserved verbatim for coding audit trail and signal detection. Required per ICH E2B(R3) field B.2.i.1.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.1; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; Argus Safety verbatim term

products.name: susar
products.description: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction record for clinical trial expedited reporting. Captures SUSARs identified from clinical trial ICSRs meeting expedited criteria: unexpected (not in IB/RSI), serious, and at least possibly causally related. Stores parent ICSR reference, trial phase, investigational product, expectedness determination against current IB, causality assessment by sponsor and investigator, 7-day (fatal/life-threatening) or 15-day reporting clock, and submission status to authorities (FDA IND safety report, EMA SUSAR, MHRA, PMDA). SLA-critical: 7-day and 15-day expedited reporting deadlines with criminal liability for non-compliance.

attributes.name: susar_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) ID
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the SUSAR record in the pharmacovigilance data product. Primary key for the silver-layer lakehouse entity.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on SUSAR Reporting

attributes.name: brand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: SUSARs tracked by brand for expedited regulatory reporting (FDA, EMA) and brand-specific safety monitoring during clinical development. Critical for development safety update reports (DSURs) and inves

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the qualified medical reviewer (physician) responsible for the medical assessment and causality determination of this SUSAR. Required for regulatory compliance and audit trail.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline; GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: icsr_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) from which this SUSAR was identified. Links the SUSAR to its originating safety case in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: SUSAR investigations in clinical trials generate specific costs for expedited assessments, unblinding procedures, and regulatory submissions. Finance tracks these via internal orders linked to trial b

attributes.name: patient_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to patient.patient. Business justification: SUSARs (Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions) in clinical trials must be traceable to the specific trial subject for expedited regulatory reporting to FDA (IND safety reports), EMA (EudraVig

attributes.name: rsi_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.rsi. Business justification: SUSAR expectedness determination uses RSI/Investigator Brochure as reference. Add rsi_id FK to link to the specific RSI version used for expectedness assessment. Remove ib_version_used as it normalize

attributes.name: trial_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical trial in which the SUSAR occurred. Used to associate the SUSAR with the relevant Investigational New Drug (IND) application and trial protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

attributes.name: argus_case_number
attributes.description: The unique case number assigned by the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system for this SUSAR. Serves as the system-of-record identifier for cross-system traceability.
attributes.references: Argus Safety System; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: assigned_treatment_arm
attributes.description: The treatment arm to which the subject was assigned (e.g., investigational product, comparator, placebo), populated after unblinding. Required for causality assessment and regulatory reporting when unblinding has occurred.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: blinding_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Trial Blinding Status at Time of SUSAR
attributes.description: Indicates whether the clinical trial was blinded at the time the SUSAR was identified, and if so, whether unblinding occurred for this case. Unblinding for SUSAR reporting is a critical regulatory and trial integrity decision.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.6; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this SUSAR record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system (Argus Safety / Oracle AERS). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GCP Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: ema_eudravigilance_submission_date
attributes.description: The date on which the SUSAR was submitted to the EMA via the EudraVigilance Clinical Trial Module (EVCTM). Null if not yet submitted or not applicable.
attributes.references: EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline; EU Clinical Trial Regulation No 536/2014; EudraVigilance EVCTM

attributes.name: expectedness_determination
attributes.description: The sponsor's determination of whether the adverse reaction is expected or unexpected based on comparison against the current Investigator's Brochure (IB) or Reference Safety Information (RSI). An 'unexpected' determination is a prerequisite for SUSAR classification.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section I; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: fda_ind_submission_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: FDA Investigational New Drug (IND) Safety Report Submission Date
attributes.description: The date on which the SUSAR was submitted to the FDA as an IND safety report under 21 CFR Part 312.32. Null if not yet submitted or not applicable. Used for SLA compliance tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); FDA Guidance on IND Safety Reporting

attributes.name: follow_up_number
attributes.description: Sequential number of the follow-up report for this SUSAR (e.g., 1 for first follow-up, 2 for second). Zero or null for initial reports. Used to track the version history of regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section A.1.12; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: initial_receipt_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sponsor first received valid minimum information about the adverse reaction, triggering the start of the expedited reporting clock. Day 0 for 7-day and 15-day SLA calculations per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section III; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c)(1); EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: investigational_product_dose
attributes.description: The dose of the investigational product administered to the subject at the time of the adverse reaction, including amount and unit (e.g., '100 mg', '5 mg/kg'). Stored as a string to accommodate varied dose expressions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section G.k.4.4; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: investigational_product_name
attributes.description: The International Nonproprietary Name (INN) or code name of the investigational medicinal product (IMP) suspected to have caused the adverse reaction. Captured at the time of SUSAR assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section G.k.2; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline; WHO INN Programme

attributes.name: investigational_product_route
attributes.description: The route of administration of the investigational product (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous). Coded per EDQM standard terminology as required for ICH E2B(R3) submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section G.k.4.2; EDQM Standard Terms; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: investigator_causality
attributes.description: The treating investigator's assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the adverse reaction, as reported on the Case Report Form (CRF). Captured separately from sponsor causality per ICH E2A requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section I; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: is_fatal
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse reaction resulted in the death of the subject. A fatal outcome triggers the 7-day expedited reporting clock and is a primary driver of reporting urgency.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section II; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c)(1)(i); EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: is_life_threatening
attributes.description: Indicates whether the adverse reaction was life-threatening at the time of occurrence (i.e., the subject was at immediate risk of death). Together with is_fatal, determines applicability of the 7-day reporting clock.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section II; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c)(1)(i); EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this SUSAR record was most recently modified in the pharmacovigilance system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and change tracking for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GCP Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: medical_review_date
attributes.description: The date on which the qualified medical reviewer completed the medical assessment of this SUSAR. Part of the audit trail for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: mhra_submission_date
attributes.description: The date on which the SUSAR was submitted to the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA). Null if not applicable.
attributes.references: MHRA Guidance on SUSAR Reporting; UK Clinical Trials Regulations 2004 (SI 2004/1031)

attributes.name: narrative_text
attributes.description: The free-text clinical narrative describing the SUSAR, including the sequence of events, medical history, treatment, and outcome. Required for all regulatory submissions per ICH E2B(R3). Classified as confidential due to sensitive clinical content.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section H.1; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: pmda_submission_date
attributes.description: The date on which the SUSAR was submitted to the Japan Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA). Null if not applicable.
attributes.references: PMDA Pharmacovigilance Regulations; Japanese Pharmaceutical Affairs Law

attributes.name: reaction_meddra_pt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Adverse Reaction MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) Code
attributes.description: The MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) Preferred Term code representing the primary adverse reaction. Mandatory for regulatory submissions to FDA, EMA, MHRA, and PMDA.
attributes.references: MedDRA Version Current; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: reaction_meddra_pt_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Adverse Reaction MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) Name
attributes.description: The human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term name corresponding to the reaction_meddra_pt_code. Stored for reporting clarity and to avoid repeated lookups against the MedDRA dictionary.
attributes.references: MedDRA Version Current; ICH E2B(R3); EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: reaction_meddra_soc_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Adverse Reaction MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) Name
attributes.description: The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) under which the primary adverse reaction is classified. Used for signal detection, aggregate analysis, and PSUR/PBRER reporting by therapeutic area.
attributes.references: MedDRA Version Current; ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2C(R2) PBRER

attributes.name: reaction_onset_date
attributes.description: The date on which the suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction first manifested in the subject. Used for temporal causality assessment and time-to-onset analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section G.k.4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: reaction_outcome
attributes.description: The outcome of the adverse reaction at the time of reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: recovered|recovering|not_recovered|recovered_with_sequelae|fatal|unknown — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section G.i.8; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the SUSAR record within the pharmacovigilance workflow. Drives workflow routing in Argus Safety and regulatory submission tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|under_review|submitted|follow_up_pending|closed|invalidated — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; Argus Safety Workflow; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: reporting_clock_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SUSAR is subject to a 7-day expedited reporting clock (fatal or life-threatening) or a 15-day reporting clock (all other serious unexpected reactions). Drives SLA enforcement and regulatory deadline calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline; MHRA Guidance on SUSAR Reporting

attributes.name: reporting_deadline_date
attributes.description: The calculated calendar date by which the SUSAR must be submitted to all applicable health authorities, derived from initial_receipt_date plus the applicable reporting clock (7 or 15 calendar days). SLA-critical field with criminal liability for non-compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline; MHRA Guidance

attributes.name: seriousness_criteria
attributes.description: The ICH E2A seriousness criterion or criteria met by this adverse reaction, which qualifies it as serious. Multiple criteria may apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fatal|life_threatening|hospitalization_required|prolonged_hospitalization|persistent_disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section II; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: sponsor_causality
attributes.description: The sponsor's assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the adverse reaction. A causality of 'related' or 'not assessable' (where benefit of doubt applies) is required for SUSAR classification.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section I; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: subject_age
attributes.business_glossary_term: Subject Age at Time of Reaction
attributes.description: The age of the clinical trial subject in years at the time the adverse reaction occurred. Required for regulatory submissions and demographic analysis. Classified as restricted PHI.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section D.2.2; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: subject_sex
attributes.description: The biological sex of the clinical trial subject as recorded in the case report. Required for ICH E2B(R3) regulatory submissions and demographic safety analysis. Classified as restricted PHI.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section D.5; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: submission_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SUSAR record represents an initial report, a follow-up report with additional information, or a final report. Tracks the reporting lifecycle across multiple submissions to health authorities.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: trial_phase
attributes.description: The phase of the clinical trial in which the SUSAR occurred (Phase I through Phase IV). Influences regulatory reporting obligations and signal assessment context.
attributes.value_regex: Phase I|Phase II|Phase III|Phase IV|Not Applicable
attributes.references: ICH E8(R1); 21 CFR Part 312.21; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

attributes.name: unblinding_date
attributes.description: The date on which the treatment assignment was unblinded for this SUSAR case, if applicable. Null for open-label trials or cases where unblinding was not performed. Critical for audit trail and trial integrity documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.6; ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA SUSAR Reporting Guideline

attributes.name: worldwide_unique_case_number
attributes.description: The globally unique case identifier assigned per ICH E2B(R3) standards, formatted as country code + organisation identifier + local case number. Used for regulatory submissions and cross-authority deduplication.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Section A.1.0.1; EudraVigilance; FDA FAERS

products.name: sae_report
products.description: Serious Adverse Event report record capturing SAEs from clinical trials, post-market surveillance, and spontaneous sources. Stores SAE classification criteria (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, medically important), time to onset, treatment given, dechallenge/rechallenge results, reporter information, site/investigator details, and reconciliation status with clinical trial EDC systems. Tracks the SAE from initial receipt through medical review, causality assessment, and regulatory submission. Supports reconciliation workflows between clinical database and PV safety database per ICH E2D guidance. SLA-critical: initial SAE notification within 24 hours of site awareness.

attributes.name: sae_report_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the SAE report record in the pharmacovigilance safety database. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: brand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: SAEs in clinical trials linked to investigational brand for development safety database, regulatory submission packages (NDA/BLA), and brand-level safety profile characterization. Required for integra

attributes.name: causality_assessor_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Causality assessment is a regulatory-critical determination requiring named accountability. Tracking the assessor employee enables audit trail compliance, workload management, and qualification verifi

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: SAE investigations require budget allocation for additional medical reviews, site follow-up visits, and causality assessments. Internal orders capture these incremental costs, enabling trial financial

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.hcp_master. Business justification: SAE reports in clinical trials identify the site investigator who reported the event. Essential for query resolution, site communication, medical review, and regulatory inspection readiness per GCP re

attributes.name: patient_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patient or clinical trial subject associated with this SAE. Links to the master patient/subject record for demographic and medical history context.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); ICH E6(R2) GCP; HIPAA; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the suspect medicinal product (drug substance or drug product) associated with the SAE. Links to the product master for INN, ATC code, formulation, and regulatory approval details.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element B.4; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81

attributes.name: reporter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the healthcare professional, patient, or other reporter who submitted the SAE. Links to the reporter master record for qualification, contact, and reporter type details.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element A.2; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: trial_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical trial or study in which the SAE occurred. Links to the clinical trial master record for protocol, phase, and IND/CTA details. Null for spontaneous post-market reports.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: case_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric case identifier assigned by the pharmacovigilance system (Argus Safety/Oracle AERS) upon initial receipt of the SAE. Used for cross-system tracking, regulatory submissions, and reconciliation with EDC systems such as Medidata Rave.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; Argus Safety Case Number; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: causality_assessment
attributes.description: Medical assessment of the causal relationship between the suspect medicinal product and the SAE, based on WHO-UMC or investigator assessment criteria. Drives SUSAR classification and regulatory reporting obligations.
attributes.references: WHO-UMC Causality Categories; ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the SAE report record was first entered into the pharmacovigilance safety database (Argus Safety/Oracle AERS). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: dechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome observed when the suspect drug was withdrawn or dose reduced (dechallenge). A positive dechallenge (event resolved on withdrawal) supports a causal relationship. Required field in ICH E2B(R3) ICSR submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element B.4.k.18.1; ICH E2A; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: edc_case_reference
attributes.description: Case or subject reference number from the clinical trial EDC system (e.g., Medidata Rave subject ID or AE sequence number) used to reconcile the SAE record between the safety database and the clinical database.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave

attributes.name: edc_reconciliation_status
attributes.description: Status of reconciliation between this SAE record in the pharmacovigilance safety database (Argus Safety) and the corresponding record in the clinical trial EDC system (Medidata Rave). Required per ICH E2D guidance to ensure consistency between clinical and safety databases.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave-Argus Safety reconciliation SOP

attributes.name: is_fatal
attributes.description: Indicates whether the SAE resulted in the death of the patient. Triggers mandatory expedited 7-day reporting to health authorities and escalation to senior medical review.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2D; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: is_susar
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SAE has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), requiring expedited 7-day (fatal/life-threatening) or 15-day reporting to health authorities and notification to investigators.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CT Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: listedness
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the adverse reaction is listed (expected) in the current Reference Safety Information (RSI) such as the Investigator Brochure or SmPC. Determines whether the event qualifies as unexpected for SUSAR classification.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.description: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term code assigned to the primary SAE event term. Standard coding used for regulatory submissions, signal detection, and aggregate safety analysis.
attributes.references: MedDRA v26+; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; FDA FAERS

attributes.name: meddra_pt_name
attributes.description: Human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term label corresponding to the meddra_pt_code. Displayed in safety reports, regulatory submissions, and signal detection outputs.
attributes.references: MedDRA v26+; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class code representing the highest-level anatomical or physiological classification of the SAE. Used for aggregate safety reporting and PSUR tabulations.
attributes.references: MedDRA v26+; ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2C(R2) PSUR

attributes.name: medical_review_status
attributes.description: Current status of the medical officer review of the SAE case. Tracks progression from initial triage through physician causality assessment and case narrative approval.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety workflow

attributes.name: narrative
attributes.description: Free-text medical narrative summarizing the SAE case including patient history, event description, clinical course, treatment, and outcome. Contains protected health information (PHI). Submitted as part of the ICSR to health authorities.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element H.1; ICH E2D; HIPAA; GDPR Article 9; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: onset_date
attributes.description: Date on which the serious adverse event first began or was first observed by the patient or healthcare professional. Used to calculate time-to-onset from first drug exposure.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element A.1.7; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: outcome
attributes.description: Clinical outcome of the SAE at the time of reporting or case closure. Drives case narrative, aggregate safety reporting, and benefit-risk assessment in PSUR/PBRER.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element B.2.i.7.2; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: patient_age_at_onset
attributes.business_glossary_term: Patient Age at Adverse Event Onset
attributes.description: Age of the patient in years at the time the serious adverse event began. Used for demographic analysis, signal detection, and population-specific risk assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element B.1.2.2; HIPAA; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: patient_sex
attributes.description: Biological sex of the patient as recorded at the time of the SAE. Used for demographic stratification in signal detection and aggregate safety reporting (PSUR/PBRER).
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element B.1.2.1; HIPAA; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: receipt_date
attributes.description: Date on which the company first received valid minimum information about the SAE (Day 0 for regulatory reporting clock). SLA-critical: initial SAE notification must be processed within 24 hours of site awareness per ICH E2D.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: rechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome observed when the suspect drug was re-administered after the initial adverse event (rechallenge). A positive rechallenge (event recurred) strongly supports causality. Required field in ICH E2B(R3) ICSR submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element B.4.k.18.2; ICH E2A; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the ICSR/SUSAR was submitted to the health authority. Compared against regulatory_submission_due_date to assess compliance with reporting timelines.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EudraVigilance

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the SAE/SUSAR must be submitted to the relevant health authority (FDA, EMA, etc.). Calculated from receipt_date based on applicable reporting timeline (7-day for fatal/life-threatening SUSAR; 15-day for other SUSARs; 30-day for non-expedited).
attributes.references: ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CT Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the SAE report from initial receipt through medical review, causality assessment, and regulatory submission. Drives SLA monitoring and submission queue management.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety workflow states

attributes.name: report_type
attributes.description: Classification of the SAE report by its originating source. Determines applicable regulatory reporting timelines and submission pathways (e.g., 7-day vs 15-day expedited reporting).
attributes.references: ICH E2D; ICH E2A; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: seriousness_criteria
attributes.description: One or more ICH E2A seriousness criteria met by this event: death, life-threatening, hospitalization (initial or prolonged), disability/incapacity, congenital anomaly/birth defect, or medically important event. Multiple criteria may apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|prolonged_hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_important — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2D; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: site_awareness_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investigational site or sponsor first became aware of the SAE. Used to calculate the 24-hour initial notification SLA and the 7/15-day regulatory reporting clock per ICH E2A and GCP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: submission_authority
attributes.description: Health authority to which the SAE/ICSR was submitted (e.g., FDA via FAERS, EMA via EudraVigilance). A single SAE may require submission to multiple authorities; this field captures the primary authority for this record. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2D; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; PMDA E2B guidelines

attributes.name: suspect_drug_dose
attributes.description: Dose of the suspect medicinal product administered at the time of the SAE, including numeric value and unit (e.g., '100 mg', '5 mg/kg'). Stored as string to accommodate varied unit formats from source systems.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element B.4.k.5a/b; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: suspect_drug_route
attributes.description: Route by which the suspect medicinal product was administered (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous). Coded using EDQM standard terms per ICH E2B(R3) requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element B.4.k.8; EDQM Standard Terms; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: time_to_onset_days
attributes.description: Number of days between the first dose of the suspect medicinal product and the onset of the SAE. Key pharmacovigilance metric used in signal detection, aggregate analysis, and benefit-risk evaluation.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; FDA FAERS

attributes.name: treatment_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the treatment(s) administered to manage the SAE, including concomitant medications, procedures, or interventions. Captured in the case narrative.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: treatment_given
attributes.description: Indicates whether specific treatment was administered to the patient in response to the SAE. Relevant for case narrative, medical review, and aggregate safety reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) element B.2.i.8; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the SAE report record. Supports audit trail, version control, and reconciliation workflows per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: worldwide_unique_case_number
attributes.description: Globally unique case identifier formatted per ICH E2B(R3) standard (country code + organisation identifier + local case number). Required for electronic ICSR submissions to FDA, EMA, and other health authorities.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI

products.name: pv_submission
products.description: Regulatory submission record for all pharmacovigilance reports submitted to health authorities worldwide. Covers expedited individual case reports (7-day fatal/life-threatening, 15-day serious), periodic aggregate reports (PSUR, PBRER, PADER, DSUR), and ad-hoc safety communications. Stores submission type, target authority, submission date, acknowledgement status, error handling, submission format (E2B R2/R3 XML, eCTD), gateway/portal details, submission reference number, resubmission history, and compliance status. Supports all major regulatory gateways including EudraVigilance (EVWEB/gateway), FAERS (FDA), MHRA Sentinel, PMDA gateway, and NMPA. Tracks authority-specific technical requirements (E2B R3 for EMA, E2B R2 for some national authorities). SLA-critical: regulatory deadline compliance with automatic escalation.
products.reference: ICH E2B / FDA MedWatch / EMA EudraVigilance

attributes.name: pv_submission_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each pharmacovigilance regulatory submission record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 314; EMA EudraVigilance Technical Specifications

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory application (NDA, BLA, MAA, IND) under which this pharmacovigilance submission is filed. Links to the regulatory.application product. Enables traceability between safety submissions and the marketing authorisation or investigational application.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.81; 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: brand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: Regulatory safety submissions (ICSRs, PSURs, SUSARs) must reference commercial brand for health authority tracking, compliance audit trails, and brand-level submission history. Essential for regulator

attributes.name: icsr_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) that is the subject of this submission, when submission_type is an ICSR variant. Links to the source safety case record in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS. Null for aggregate report submissions (PSUR, PBRER, DSUR).
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Data Model

attributes.name: original_submission_pv_submission_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the original pv_submission_id when this record represents a resubmission, follow-up, or amendment. Null for original submissions. Enables reconstruction of the full resubmission history chain.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.7; EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the medicinal product (Drug Product / Drug Substance) that is the subject of the safety report or aggregate submission. Links to the master product record.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k; EMA Product Dictionary; FDA NDC Directory

attributes.name: psur_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.psur. Business justification: Some PV submissions are for PSUR reports (submission_type indicates report type). Add psur_id FK (nullable - only populated for PSUR submission types). This links the submission transaction to the PSU

attributes.name: regulatory_inspection_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_inspection. Business justification: PV submissions often respond to inspection findings requiring expedited reporting or corrective submissions. Inspection-driven submission requirements are core regulatory process in pharmacovigilance

attributes.name: rmp_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.rmp. Business justification: Some PV submissions are for RMP reports. Add rmp_id FK (nullable - only populated for RMP submission types). Remove rmp_version as it normalizes to rmp.version_number.

attributes.name: sae_report_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.sae_report. Business justification: SAE reports generate regulatory submissions. Add sae_report_id FK (nullable - only populated for SAE submission types). This links the submission transaction to the SAE master record.

attributes.name: safety_report_icsr_id
attributes.description: The unique safety report identifier assigned within the source pharmacovigilance system (Argus Safety / Oracle AERS case number), used for cross-referencing between the submission record and the originating safety case. Distinct from the submission_number assigned by the health authority.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.0.1; Argus Safety Case Number Convention; Oracle AERS

attributes.name: safety_signal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pharmacovigilance safety signal record that prompted or is associated with this submission, where applicable. Links to the signal detection and management record. Null for routine ICSR submissions not linked to a formal signal.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: submission_country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Submission target country determines format (E2B R2/R3, CIOMS), gateway (EudraVigilance, FDA ESG, MHRA Yellow Card), and timelines. Operational requirement for submission routing and compliance tracki

attributes.name: susar_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.susar. Business justification: SUSAR records generate regulatory submissions (expedited reporting). Add susar_id FK (nullable - only populated for SUSAR submission types). One SUSAR can have multiple submissions (initial + follow-u

attributes.name: acknowledgement_code
attributes.description: Technical acknowledgement code returned by the health authority gateway per HL7 v2 / E2B messaging standards. AA = Application Accept; AE = Application Error; CA = Commit Accept; CE = Commit Error; TA = Technical Accept; TE = Technical Error. Drives automated error handling and resubmission workflows.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide; HL7 v2 Acknowledgement Codes; EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules

attributes.name: acknowledgement_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when the technical acknowledgement (ACK) message was received from the health authority gateway confirming successful receipt of the submission. Distinct from substantive acceptance. Used for SLA compliance evidence.
attributes.references: EMA EudraVigilance Gateway Technical Specifications; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide

attributes.name: argus_case_number
attributes.description: The case number from the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system that is the source of record for this submission. Enables direct traceability from the submission record back to the full safety case in the operational PV system.
attributes.references: Argus Safety / Oracle AERS; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: authority_case_number
attributes.description: The case or report reference number assigned by the receiving health authority upon acceptance of the submission (e.g., EudraVigilance case number, FDA FAERS case ID). Used for follow-up queries and regulatory correspondence. Populated after authority acceptance.
attributes.references: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; PMDA E2B Transmission Guide

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pharmacovigilance submission record was first created in the data platform. Audit trail field for data lineage and 21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11 electronic records compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11; GDPR Article 5(1)(f); ICH Q10

attributes.name: date_of_first_receipt
attributes.description: The date the company first received the minimum valid safety information constituting a reportable case (Day 0 for regulatory clock purposes). This is the anchor date from which the 7-day or 15-day expedited reporting deadline is calculated for ICSRs. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.4.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.4; ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1)

attributes.name: days_to_deadline
attributes.description: Number of calendar days remaining between the current date and the regulatory_deadline at the time of last record update. Negative values indicate overdue submissions. Used for SLA monitoring dashboards and automatic escalation triggers. Note: this is a snapshot value captured at record update time, not a live calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81

attributes.name: error_code
attributes.description: Structured error code returned by the health authority gateway or E2B validation engine upon rejection or technical failure (e.g., EudraVigilance business rule error code, FAERS conformance error code). Enables automated error categorisation and routing to the appropriate remediation team.
attributes.references: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Validation Rules

attributes.name: gateway_portal
attributes.description: The specific electronic gateway or web portal used to transmit this submission to the health authority. Determines technical format and protocol requirements. EudraVigilance Gateway and EVWEB are EMA channels; FAERS Gateway is the FDA channel for ICSRs; MHRA Sentinel is the UK post-Brexit channel. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EUDRAVIGILANCE_GATEWAY|EUDRAVIGILANCE_EVWEB|FAERS_GATEWAY|MHRA_SENTINEL|PMDA_GATEWAY|NMPA_GATEWAY|VIGIBASE_WHO|DIRECT_EMAIL|PAPER — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EMA EudraVigilance Technical Specifications; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; MHRA Sentinel System Guidance; PMDA E2B Transmission Guide

attributes.name: health_authority_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the target regulatory health authority to which this submission is directed. FDA = U.S. Food and Drug Administration; EMA = European Medicines Agency; MHRA = Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (UK); PMDA = Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (Japan); NMPA = National Medical Products Administration (China). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|ANVISA|TGA|HEALTH_CANADA|SWISSMEDIC|COFEPRIS|KFDA|MEDSAFE — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA; EMA; MHRA; PMDA; NMPA; ICH M8; WHO Prequalification Programme

attributes.name: is_expedited
attributes.description: Indicates whether this submission is subject to expedited regulatory reporting requirements (7-day or 15-day clock). True = expedited; False = periodic/non-expedited. Drives SLA escalation logic and compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: is_on_time
attributes.description: Indicates whether the submission was transmitted on or before the regulatory_deadline. True = submitted on time; False = submitted late. Key compliance KPI field populated at time of submission. Used for regulatory compliance reporting and CAPA tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81; PIC/S GVP Guidelines

attributes.name: is_susar
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this submission relates to a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) from a clinical trial, which carries specific expedited reporting obligations to both health authorities and investigators under ICH E2A and GCP regulations.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E6(R2) GCP; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 312.32; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: message_format
attributes.description: The technical format standard used for the submission message. E2B_R2_XML = ICH E2B(R2) XML format (used by some national authorities); E2B_R3_XML = ICH E2B(R3) XML format (required by EMA EudraVigilance and FDA from 2022); ECTD = Electronic Common Technical Document format (for aggregate reports); PDF = portable document format for ad-hoc communications; PAPER = legacy paper submission.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R2); ICH E2B(R3); ICH M8 eCTD; EMA EudraVigilance Technical Specifications; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: regulatory_deadline
attributes.description: The mandatory regulatory deadline date by which this submission must be transmitted to the health authority, calculated from the date of first receipt (Day 0) of the safety information. For expedited ICSRs: Day 7 (fatal/life-threatening) or Day 15 (serious). For PSURs/PBRERs: per approved data lock point schedule. SLA-critical field used for automatic escalation.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1); EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: rejection_reason
