attributes.description: Free-text or structured description of the reason(s) for rejection returned by the health authority gateway or authority reviewer when submission_status is REJECTED. Includes E2B validation error codes and human-readable explanations. Used for root cause analysis and CAPA.
attributes.references: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide

attributes.name: report_period_end
attributes.business_glossary_term: Report Period End Date (Data Lock Point)
attributes.description: End date of the data collection period (Data Lock Point, DLP) for aggregate reports (PSUR, PBRER, PADER, DSUR). Defines the cut-off date for safety data included in the report. Null for individual case (ICSR) submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); ICH E2F; EMA GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)

attributes.name: report_period_start
attributes.description: Start date of the data collection period covered by this submission. Applicable primarily to aggregate reports (PSUR, PBRER, PADER, DSUR) defining the International Birth Date (IBD) or period start. Null for individual case (ICSR) submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); ICH E2F; EMA GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)

attributes.name: report_type_qualifier
attributes.description: Qualifier indicating whether this is an initial report, a follow-up update to a previously submitted case, or a nullification (withdrawal) of a previously submitted report. Corresponds directly to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2 field.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2; EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: responsible_qppv
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) responsible for this submission under EU GVP regulations. The QPPV bears legal accountability for the completeness and accuracy of pharmacovigilance submissions to the EMA and EU member states.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module I; EU Directive 2001/83/EC Article 104; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: resubmission_count
attributes.description: Number of times this submission has been resubmitted to the health authority following a rejection or technical error. Zero indicates the original submission was accepted without resubmission. Used to track submission quality and identify systemic data quality issues.
attributes.references: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide

attributes.name: sender_identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the sending organisation as registered with the health authority gateway (e.g., EudraVigilance sender ID, FDA FAERS sender code). Required for gateway authentication and message routing.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.3.1; EMA EudraVigilance Registration; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: sender_organisation
attributes.description: Name of the pharmaceutical company or Marketing Authorisation Holder (MAH) submitting the report, as declared in the E2B message header (ICH E2B(R3) C.1.3.1). Required field in all E2B transmissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.3.1; EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: The principal real-world timestamp when the pharmacovigilance report was transmitted to the health authority gateway or portal. This is the legally significant submission event time used for regulatory deadline compliance calculations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2D; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: submission_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this submission, either generated internally or assigned by the receiving health authority gateway (e.g., EudraVigilance transmission ID, FAERS acknowledgement number). Used for tracking and cross-referencing with authority systems.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA EudraVigilance Gateway Technical Specifications; FDA FAERS Submission Guidance

attributes.name: submission_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the pharmacovigilance submission workflow. DRAFT = in preparation; PENDING = queued for transmission; SUBMITTED = transmitted to health authority gateway; ACKNOWLEDGED = technical acknowledgement received from gateway; ACCEPTED = substantively accepted by authority; REJECTED = rejected with errors requiring correction; RESUBMITTED = corrected and resubmitted after rejection; WITHDRAWN = voluntarily withdrawn by the company. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DRAFT|PENDING|SUBMITTED|ACKNOWLEDGED|ACCEPTED|REJECTED|RESUBMITTED|WITHDRAWN — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) Implementation Guide

attributes.name: submission_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pharmacovigilance submission by regulatory report type. ICSR_EXPEDITED_7DAY = fatal/life-threatening Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) requiring 7-calendar-day reporting; ICSR_EXPEDITED_15DAY = serious ICSR requiring 15-calendar-day reporting; ICSR_NON_EXPEDITED = non-expedited periodic ICSR; PSUR = Periodic Safety Update Report; PBRER = Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report; PADER = Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Report; DSUR = Development Safety Update Report. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ICSR_EXPEDITED_7DAY|ICSR_EXPEDITED_15DAY|ICSR_NON_EXPEDITED|PSUR|PBRER|PADER|DSUR|AD_HOC_SAFETY_COMM|REMS_ASSESSMENT|SUSAR — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2D; ICH E2C(R2); ICH E2F; 21 CFR 314.81; EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module VI

attributes.name: submission_version
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this submission for a given safety case or aggregate report. Version 1 = initial submission; Version 2+ = follow-up or amendment submissions. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2 (report type: initial/follow-up/nullification).
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2; EMA EudraVigilance Business Rules; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: transmission_reference
attributes.description: Unique message transmission identifier assigned by the health authority gateway at the point of receipt (e.g., EudraVigilance message ID, FAERS transmission reference). Distinct from the authority_case_number; this is the technical envelope identifier used for gateway-level tracing and acknowledgement matching.
attributes.references: EMA EudraVigilance Gateway Technical Specifications; FDA FAERS Technical Conformance Guide; ICH E2B(R3) A.1.0.1

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pharmacovigilance submission record was most recently modified in the data platform. Audit trail field for data lineage and 21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11 electronic records compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11; GDPR Article 5(1)(f); ICH Q10

products.name: psur
products.description: Periodic aggregate safety report master record covering PSUR, PBRER (ICH E2C R2), PADER (FDA), and DSUR (development phase) for each product-indication combination. Captures data lock point, reporting interval, international birth date (IBD), cumulative exposure data, interval and cumulative case summaries, signal summary, benefit-risk evaluation conclusion, and submission status per applicable authority. Tracks preparation milestones, author assignments, medical review, QC, and approval workflow. Supports EU PSUR single assessment (PSUSA) process, FDA PADER requirements, and ICH DSUR for investigational products. Includes structured benefit-risk assessment sections. SLA-critical: fixed regulatory submission deadlines based on IBD.
products.reference: ICH E2C(R2) PBRER / EU PSUR Single Assessment

attributes.name: psur_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the PSUR/PBRER/PADER/DSUR master record in the pharmacovigilance data lakehouse.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA Guideline on PSUR

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the marketing authorisation application (NDA/BLA/MAA) or investigational application (IND) under which this periodic safety report is submitted.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: brand_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand_plan. Business justification: PSURs inform brand planning as safety profile outcomes impact positioning, target population, and promotional strategy. Brand teams review PSUR benefit-risk conclusions quarterly to adjust market acce

attributes.name: health_authority_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA) to which this PSUR is submitted. Determines applicable regulatory requirements and submission format.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: mah_legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: PSUR is submitted by specific MAH legal entity. Determines signatory authority, regulatory obligations, and submission routing. Critical for regulatory compliance and multi-entity portfolio management

attributes.name: medical_publication_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.medical_publication. Business justification: PSURs cite key medical publications as evidence sources for benefit-risk assessment and safety specification updates. Critical for regulatory submission and scientific justification of safety profile.

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: PSURs reference patent status for benefit-risk assessment context, especially when evaluating whether formulation changes covered by new patents affect safety profile. Patent expiry impacts market dyn

attributes.name: psur_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pharmacovigilance scientist or medical writer assigned as lead author responsible for drafting this PSUR. Supports preparation milestone tracking and accountability.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module VII; FDA PADER Guidance; SOPs

attributes.name: psur_medical_reviewer_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the qualified physician or clinical pharmacologist responsible for the medical review and benefit-risk evaluation section of this PSUR. Required for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 17; EMA GVP Module VII; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; SOPs

attributes.name: psur_qppv_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the EU Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) who is responsible for oversight and approval of this PSUR prior to submission to EMA. Mandatory for EU-authorised products.
attributes.references: EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 23; EMA GVP Module I; Directive 2001/83/EC Article 104

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the medicinal product (drug substance or drug product) that is the subject of this periodic safety report.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 2; EMA PSUSA Procedure

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the QPPV (or designated signatory) formally approved the PSUR for regulatory submission. Represents the final internal milestone before submission and is an auditable event per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module I; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 23; 21 CFR Part 11; SOPs

attributes.name: benefit_risk_conclusion
attributes.description: Overall benefit-risk evaluation conclusion for the product as determined by the medical reviewer for this PSUR period. A finding of unfavourable or inconclusive may trigger regulatory action, label update, or risk management plan revision.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 17; EMA PSUSA Guideline; FDA PADER Guidance; ICH E2F

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this PSUR record was first created in the pharmacovigilance data lakehouse, providing the audit trail creation event per 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR data governance requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5; SOX; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: cumulative_case_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) Count
attributes.description: Total number of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) received from the IBD through the data lock point across all reporting intervals, providing the full post-marketing safety case history for the product.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 9; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA PSUSA Guideline

attributes.name: cumulative_exposure_patient_years
attributes.description: Total cumulative patient-years of exposure to the product from IBD through data lock point, calculated from treatment duration data. Used as the primary denominator for incidence rate calculations in benefit-risk assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 6.2; EMA PSUSA Guideline; ICH E2E Pharmacovigilance Planning

attributes.name: cumulative_exposure_patients
attributes.description: Estimated cumulative number of patients exposed to the product from the IBD through the data lock point, derived from post-marketing surveillance, clinical trials, and sales data. Used as denominator for cumulative incidence rate calculations.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 6; FDA PADER Guidance; EMA PSUSA Guideline

attributes.name: data_lock_point
attributes.description: The cut-off date up to which all safety data (adverse events, literature, clinical studies) are included in this PSUR. No new data arising after this date is incorporated into the current report period.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 2.3; FDA 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2); EMA PSUSA Guideline

attributes.name: draft_completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which the initial draft of the PSUR was completed by the lead author and made available for internal review. Used to track preparation milestones against the submission deadline.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module VII; SOPs; Veeva Vault RIM Workflow

attributes.name: ha_assessment_outcome
attributes.description: Outcome of the health authority's assessment of this PSUR, indicating any regulatory action required. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|no_action|label_update|rmp_update|referral|suspension|withdrawal — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
attributes.references: EMA PSUSA Procedure; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; ICH E2C(R2) Section 17; EMA GVP Module VII

attributes.name: international_birth_date
attributes.description: The date of first marketing authorisation for the product in any country worldwide, used as the anchor date for calculating PSUR submission deadlines and reporting intervals per ICH E2C(R2). SLA-critical field.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 2.2; EMA PSUSA Guideline; WHO IBD Definition

attributes.name: interval_case_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Interval Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) Count
attributes.description: Total number of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) received during the current reporting interval (between interval_start_date and data_lock_point), including both spontaneous and solicited reports.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 9; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA PSUSA Guideline; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: interval_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the current PSUR reporting interval, which is typically equal to the data lock point. Defines the close of the reporting window for interval case counts and exposure data.

attributes.name: interval_sae_count
attributes.description: Number of Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) reported during the current reporting interval. SAEs include fatal, life-threatening, hospitalisation-requiring, or permanently disabling events per ICH E2A criteria.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2C(R2) Section 9; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: interval_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the current PSUR reporting interval (the period covered by this report). Together with interval_end_date defines the reporting window for interval case counts and exposure data.

attributes.name: interval_susar_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Interval Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Count
attributes.description: Number of Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) identified during the current reporting interval. SUSARs require expedited reporting and are tracked separately for signal detection purposes.
attributes.references: ICH E2A; ICH E2C(R2); FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 17

attributes.name: label_update_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the safety findings in this PSUR require an update to the product label (SmPC, Package Insert, or Patient Information Leaflet). A True value initiates a label change management workflow.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 17; FDA 21 CFR 314.70; EMA SmPC Guideline; MHRA Guidance on Labelling

attributes.name: medical_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the medical reviewer completed the clinical and benefit-risk review of the PSUR draft. Milestone in the PSUR preparation workflow tracked against the submission deadline.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 17; EMA GVP Module VII; SOPs

attributes.name: new_safety_signals_count
attributes.description: Number of new safety signals identified during the reporting interval through signal detection activities (disproportionality analysis, literature review, spontaneous reports). Drives benefit-risk re-evaluation.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 16; EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module IX; FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: psusa_procedure_number
attributes.description: EMA-assigned procedure number for the PSUR Single Assessment (PSUSA) process applicable to centrally authorised products in the EU. Used to track the PSUSA workflow and outcome in Veeva Vault RIM and RIMS.
attributes.references: EMA PSUSA Procedure; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 107e; EMA GVP Module VII

attributes.name: qc_completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which quality control review of the PSUR was completed, verifying accuracy of case counts, exposure data, and regulatory formatting prior to QPPV approval and submission.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module VII; MasterControl/TrackWise QMS; SOPs; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: report_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to this PSUR/PBRER/PADER/DSUR submission, used in regulatory correspondence and tracking systems such as Argus Safety and Veeva Vault RIM.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA PSUR Single Assessment (PSUSA); FDA 21 CFR 314.81

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle workflow state of the PSUR record, tracking progression from initial drafting through medical review, QC, approval, and regulatory submission. Drives SLA monitoring and escalation workflows. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|in_review|qc_review|approved|submitted|accepted|withdrawn — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA PSUSA Procedure; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; Veeva Vault RIM Workflow

attributes.name: report_type
attributes.description: Classification of the periodic aggregate safety report: PSUR (Periodic Safety Update Report), PBRER (Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report per ICH E2C R2), PADER (Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Report per FDA), DSUR (Development Safety Update Report for investigational products), or PSUSA (PSUR Single Assessment for EU centralised procedure).
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); ICH E2F; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA PSUSA Guideline

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Regulatory-mandated submission frequency for this PSUR, which varies by product age, risk profile, and authority requirements. Drives automated SLA deadline calculation from the IBD.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 2.4; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 107b; FDA 21 CFR 314.81

attributes.name: reporting_period_number
attributes.description: Sequential ordinal number of this PSUR reporting period for the product (e.g., 1st, 2nd, 3rd PSUR), enabling chronological tracking of the full PSUR history for a product.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 2.3; EMA PSUSA Procedure

attributes.name: rmp_update_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Management Plan (RMP) Update Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the benefit-risk findings in this PSUR necessitate an update to the product's Risk Management Plan (RMP). A True value triggers a formal RMP revision workflow in the pharmacovigilance system.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 17; EMA GVP Module V (Risk Management Systems); EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: Native record identifier from the originating pharmacovigilance system (Argus Safety, Oracle AERS, or Veeva Vault RIM) for this PSUR record, enabling traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational system of record.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module II (Pharmacovigilance System Master File); SOX

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the PSUR was submitted to the health authority. Compared against submission_deadline to determine on-time or late submission for regulatory compliance tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA PSUSA Procedure; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: submission_deadline
attributes.description: Mandatory regulatory deadline by which this PSUR must be submitted to the applicable health authority, calculated from the IBD and reporting frequency. SLA-critical field monitored for compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 107b; FDA 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)

attributes.name: submission_format
attributes.description: Electronic or paper format used for regulatory submission of this PSUR. eCTD (Electronic Common Technical Document) is the standard for FDA and EMA submissions; NeeS is a non-eCTD electronic submission format.
attributes.references: FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eCTD Guideline; ICH M8 eCTD Specification; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this PSUR record in the data lakehouse, supporting audit trail requirements and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5; SOX; ICH E2C(R2)

products.name: rmp
products.description: Risk Management Plan master record. Captures RMP version, scope (product, indication, population), safety specification (important identified risks, important potential risks, missing information), pharmacovigilance plan activities (routine and additional), risk minimization measures (routine and additional including REMS for US), effectiveness evaluation plan, and PASS commitments. Tracks RMP approval status per authority (EMA, MHRA) and version history. Supports EU GVP Module V template, FDA REMS requirements, and PMDA RMP format. Links to resulting PV actions and PASS study commitments.
products.reference: EU GVP Module V Risk Management Plan

attributes.name: rmp_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Risk Management Plan record in the pharmacovigilance data lakehouse.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; ICH E2E

attributes.name: application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory application (NDA, BLA, MAA) to which this RMP is attached or submitted as a condition of approval.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: approval_id
attributes.description: Reference to the marketing authorization or approval record that mandated or is associated with this RMP.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

attributes.name: brand_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.brand_plan. Business justification: RMPs define risk minimization measures (REMS, restricted distribution) that constrain promotional strategy, market access, and channel strategy. Brand plans must reference RMP commitments to ensure co

attributes.name: mah_legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Risk Management Plan ownership by legal entity determines regulatory accountability, update obligations, and PRAC submission responsibility. Essential for lifecycle safety management and regulatory co

attributes.name: medical_heor_study_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.medical_heor_study. Business justification: Risk Management Plans explicitly commit to HEOR/PASS studies as regulatory obligations for risk characterization and minimization. RMPs reference specific committed studies for tracking and reporting

attributes.name: medical_publication_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.medical_publication. Business justification: RMPs reference key publications supporting safety specification, risk characterization, and epidemiology sections. Essential for regulatory review and scientific credibility of risk management strateg

attributes.name: patient_support_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.patient_support_program. Business justification: REMS programs (subset of RMPs requiring restricted distribution, prescriber certification, patient registries) are operationalized as patient support programs. PSP infrastructure implements RMP-mandat

attributes.name: previous_version_rmp_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding version of this RMP, enabling full version chain reconstruction and audit trail for regulatory inspections.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA version control guidance; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: promo_material_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.promo_material. Business justification: RMP-mandated risk minimization messaging (e.g., REMS communication plan, prescriber education) must appear in promotional materials. Regulatory requirement for products with approved RMPs; MLR reviews

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the medicinal product (drug substance or drug product) that this RMP covers, linking to the master product record.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; FDA 21 CFR 314; EMA EPAR

attributes.name: regulatory_inspection_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_inspection. Business justification: RMPs are updated following inspections identifying new safety concerns or pharmacovigilance system deficiencies. Inspection-driven RMP revisions are required by GVP Module V for safety specification u

attributes.name: additional_pv_activity_count
attributes.description: Number of additional pharmacovigilance activities (beyond routine) specified in the PV plan of this RMP, such as Post-Authorization Safety Studies (PASS), drug utilization studies, or enhanced pharmacovigilance programs.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V Part III; EU GVP Module VIII (PASS)

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the RMP document with the relevant health authority: draft (in preparation), submitted (filed with authority), approved (accepted by authority), rejected (not accepted), superseded (replaced by newer version), or withdrawn.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA/838713/2011 Rev 2; FDA REMS guidance

attributes.name: argus_rmp_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Argus Safety RMP Source System ID
attributes.description: Source system identifier for this RMP record as stored in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS, used for data lineage, reconciliation, and integration with the pharmacovigilance safety database.
attributes.references: Argus Safety / Oracle AERS; 21 CFR Part 11; EU GVP Module I

attributes.name: authority_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the health authority formally approved or accepted this version of the RMP. Null if not yet approved.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; FDA REMS guidance

attributes.name: benefit_risk_conclusion
attributes.description: Overall benefit-risk conclusion documented in this RMP version, reflecting the current assessment of the product's benefit-risk balance as evaluated by the marketing authorization holder and/or health authority.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V Part II; ICH E2E; EMA benefit-risk methodology

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this RMP record was first created in the pharmacovigilance data system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GVP Module I.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EU GVP Module I; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this version of the RMP becomes operationally effective and binding for pharmacovigilance activities and risk minimization measures.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; ICH E2E; FDA REMS guidance

attributes.name: effectiveness_evaluation_plan
attributes.description: Description of the plan to evaluate the effectiveness of risk minimization measures, including key performance indicators, data sources, and evaluation timelines as required by EU GVP Module XVI.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module XVI; EMA/204715/2012; FDA REMS assessment guidance

attributes.name: health_authority_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the primary health authority to which this RMP is submitted and by which it is governed (e.g., EMA for EU, FDA for US, MHRA for UK, PMDA for Japan). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EMA|FDA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|ANVISA|TGA|COFEPRIS|SAHPRA — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; FDA 21 CFR 505-1; PMDA RMP Guidance; ICH E2E

attributes.name: identified_risk_count
attributes.description: Number of important identified risks documented in the safety specification of this RMP version. An identified risk is one for which there is adequate evidence of an association with the medicinal product.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V Part II Safety Specification; ICH E2E Section 2.2

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this RMP record in the data system, used for change tracking, data lineage, and regulatory audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EU GVP Module I; GDPR Article 5(1)(e)

attributes.name: missing_information_count
attributes.description: Number of missing information items documented in the safety specification, representing gaps in knowledge about the safety of the medicinal product (e.g., use in pregnancy, pediatric use).
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V Part II Safety Specification; ICH E2E Section 2.4

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the next periodic review and potential update of the RMP, as agreed with the health authority or per internal PV schedule.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA/838713/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: pass_commitment_count
attributes.description: Number of Post-Authorization Safety Study (PASS) commitments included in this RMP version, representing studies imposed as conditions of marketing authorization or undertaken voluntarily.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module VIII; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Article 9(4)(cb); EU GVP Module V Part III

attributes.name: potential_risk_count
attributes.description: Number of important potential risks documented in the safety specification of this RMP version. A potential risk is one for which there is some basis for suspicion but insufficient evidence to confirm.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V Part II Safety Specification; ICH E2E Section 2.3

attributes.name: psur_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) or Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) that was submitted concurrently with or triggered this RMP version update.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module VII (PSUR); ICH E2C(R2); FDA 21 CFR 314.81

attributes.name: pv_plan_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the pharmacovigilance plan for this RMP includes only routine PV activities (spontaneous reporting, PSUR/PBRER) or also includes additional PV activities such as PASS studies, registries, or enhanced surveillance.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V Part III; ICH E2E Section 3

attributes.name: rems_program_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program Name
attributes.description: Official name of the FDA-approved REMS program associated with this RMP, if applicable (e.g., iPLEDGE for isotretinoin, TIRF REMS Access Program).
attributes.references: FDA REMS 21 CFR 505-1; FDA REMS database

attributes.name: rems_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is required by the FDA as part of the US risk management plan for this product. Applicable only for FDA submissions.
attributes.references: FDA REMS 21 CFR 505-1; FDA Guidance on REMS

attributes.name: risk_minimization_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether risk minimization measures in this RMP are limited to routine measures (product labeling, SmPC, PIL) or also include additional risk minimization measures (educational materials, controlled access programs, REMS for US).
attributes.references: EU GVP Module XVI; FDA REMS 21 CFR 505-1; ICH E2E Section 4

attributes.name: rmp_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to the RMP document, used in regulatory submissions and authority correspondence (e.g., RMP-2024-001).
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA/838713/2011 Rev 2; FDA REMS guidance

attributes.name: rmp_type
attributes.description: Classification of the RMP format based on the regulatory authority template: EU GVP Module V (EMA/MHRA), FDA Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS), PMDA RMP (Japan), or WHO RMP. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EU_RMP|FDA_REMS|PMDA_RMP|MHRA_RMP|WHO_RMP — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; FDA REMS 21 CFR 505-1; PMDA RMP Guidance; ICH E2E

attributes.name: safety_specification_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the safety specification section of the RMP, covering the epidemiology of the indication, non-clinical safety findings, clinical trial safety data, and post-marketing experience.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V Part II; ICH E2E Section 2

attributes.name: scope_indication
attributes.description: The approved or proposed therapeutic indication(s) covered by this RMP, as defined in the marketing authorization or clinical development program (e.g., treatment of relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma).
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V Part II; ICH E2E Section 2

attributes.name: scope_population
attributes.description: Description of the target patient population covered by this RMP, including age groups, special populations (pediatric, geriatric, renal/hepatic impairment), and any population restrictions.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V Part II; ICH E2E Section 2; EMA Pediatric Regulation

attributes.name: signal_detection_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier(s) to pharmacovigilance signal detection records or PRAC signal assessments that triggered or informed this RMP version update.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module IX (Signal Management); EMA PRAC signal assessment; Argus Safety

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which this version of the RMP was formally submitted to the health authority as part of a regulatory dossier or standalone submission.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA submission guidelines

attributes.name: superseded_date
attributes.description: Date on which this RMP version was superseded by a newer version. Null for the currently active version.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA version control guidance

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Full descriptive title of the Risk Management Plan document, typically including the product name, indication, and version.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; ICH E2E

attributes.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management) where the RMP document is stored and managed as part of the regulatory dossier.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; eCTD Module 1.8.2; EU GVP Module V

attributes.name: version_change_rationale
attributes.description: Documented rationale for updating this RMP version, including the trigger (e.g., new safety signal, PSUR outcome, authority request, new indication, PASS completion) and summary of changes from the previous version.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA/838713/2011 Rev 2; ICH E2E

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier of the RMP document (e.g., 1.0, 2.3), incremented with each regulatory submission or significant update. Supports version history tracking.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA/838713/2011 Rev 2

products.name: safety_signal
products.description: Safety signal record representing a new or evolving safety concern identified through signal detection activities. Captures signal source (spontaneous database, literature, clinical trial, real-world data), detection method (disproportionality analysis, clinical review, machine learning), MedDRA-coded term, signal strength metrics (PRR, ROR, EBGM, IC), and signal status lifecycle (new, under evaluation, validated, refuted, closed). Includes formal assessment records: methodology, data sources reviewed, benefit-risk impact evaluation, proposed label change recommendation, regulatory action required, PRAC/PSUR referral status, and final disposition. Each signal supports multiple assessment iterations. Tracks the full signal management workflow from detection through triage, validation, prioritization, assessment, and closure or regulatory action per GVP Module IX. SLA-critical: PRAC rapporteur notification timelines.
products.reference: ICH E2C / GVP Module IX Signal Management

attributes.name: safety_signal_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the safety signal record in the pharmacovigilance system. Primary key for the safety_signal data product.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report; GVP Module IX Signal Management

attributes.name: affairs_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.medical_affairs_plan. Business justification: Safety signals trigger medical affairs response plans for evidence gap closure, KOL communication strategy, and publication planning to address emerging safety concerns with scientific evidence.

attributes.name: assigned_assessor_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Signal assessment requires named ownership for regulatory accountability and workload distribution. Tracking assessor employee enables signal triage management, qualification verification, and audit t

attributes.name: atc_classification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Signal detection and prioritization by therapeutic class enables risk-benefit assessment, class-effect evaluation, and regulatory communication strategy. Supports signal management workflows and PRAC

attributes.name: incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_incident. Business justification: Safety signals can trigger compliance incidents when detection/reporting failures occur (e.g., missed signal, delayed PRAC notification). Signal management failures are reportable GVP non-compliance e

attributes.name: molecular_target_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: Safety signal validation requires molecular target review. Signal assessment committees evaluate target biology, pathway, tissue expression, and known class effects to determine if the signal is mecha

attributes.name: psur_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.psur. Business justification: Safety signals can be referred to PSUR reports for aggregate safety assessment (psur_referral_flag). Add psur_id FK (nullable - only when signal is referred to PSUR). This links the signal to the spec

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the medicinal product (drug substance or drug product) associated with this safety signal. Links to the master product entity for the implicated compound.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: analysis_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the data analysis period used for signal detection. Together with analysis_period_start_date, defines the cumulative or interval data window reviewed.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: analysis_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the data analysis period used for signal detection. Defines the temporal window of adverse event data reviewed to identify the signal.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: assessment_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the formal signal assessment findings, including methodology applied, data sources reviewed, clinical interpretation, and conclusions. Supports regulatory dossier preparation and PRAC submissions.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: benefit_risk_impact
attributes.description: Overall benefit-risk impact determination resulting from the signal assessment. Indicates whether the signal changes the benefit-risk balance of the product as favorable, unfavorable, uncertain, or neutral.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX; ICH E2C(R2) PBRER; EMA Benefit-Risk Methodology; GVP Module I

attributes.name: case_count
attributes.description: Total number of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) or adverse event cases contributing to this safety signal at the time of detection or most recent assessment. Used as a threshold criterion alongside disproportionality metrics.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: Date on which the safety signal was formally closed following completion of all assessment activities and regulatory actions. Represents the end of the signal management lifecycle.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the safety signal record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system (Argus Safety / Oracle AERS). Used for audit trail and data lineage compliance per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GVP Module IX; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: data_source_database
attributes.description: Name of the specific pharmacovigilance database or data source from which the signal was detected (e.g., FDA FAERS, WHO VigiBase, EudraVigilance, company spontaneous database, published literature). Supports traceability of signal origin.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; FDA FAERS

attributes.name: detection_method
attributes.description: Methodology used to identify the safety signal. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: disproportionality_analysis|clinical_review|machine_learning|literature_review|spontaneous_report|regulatory_authority — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: detection_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the safety signal was first detected or identified, representing the principal real-world event time. Critical for SLA tracking of PRAC rapporteur notification timelines and regulatory reporting deadlines.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; 21 CFR 314.81; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: ebgm_value
attributes.description: Empirical Bayes Geometric Mean (EBGM) — a Bayesian disproportionality metric used in the FDA FAERS database analysis. EBGM ≥2 is a commonly applied threshold for signal detection.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX; FDA FAERS Signal Detection; DuMouchel EBGM Method

attributes.name: fatal_case_count
attributes.description: Number of fatal outcome cases among the cases contributing to this safety signal. Fatal cases receive highest priority in signal triage and may trigger expedited regulatory notification.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management; GVP Module IX; 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: ic_value
attributes.description: Information Component (IC) — a Bayesian disproportionality metric used by the WHO Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) VigiBase. Positive IC values indicate a drug-event association stronger than expected by chance.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX; WHO UMC VigiBase IC Method; Bate et al. IC Algorithm

attributes.name: label_change_recommended
attributes.description: Indicates whether the signal assessment has resulted in a formal recommendation to update the product label (SmPC, USPI, or equivalent). Triggers regulatory submission activities.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX; 21 CFR 314.70; EMA SmPC Guideline; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term Code
attributes.description: MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code representing the primary adverse event or medical concept associated with this safety signal. Standardized coding per MedDRA hierarchy for regulatory submissions and signal tracking.
attributes.references: MedDRA Version Current; ICH M1 MedDRA Guideline; GVP Module IX; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: meddra_pt_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term Name
attributes.description: Human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term name corresponding to the meddra_pt_code. Provides the standardized medical terminology label for the safety signal event.
attributes.references: MedDRA Version Current; ICH M1 MedDRA Guideline; GVP Module IX

attributes.name: meddra_soc_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code for the primary adverse event, providing the highest-level classification in the MedDRA hierarchy. Used for signal clustering and therapeutic area analysis.
attributes.references: MedDRA Version Current; ICH M1 MedDRA Guideline; GVP Module IX

attributes.name: prac_notification_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee (PRAC) Rapporteur Notification Date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the PRAC rapporteur was notified of the safety signal. Compared against prac_notification_due_date to assess SLA compliance.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010

attributes.name: prac_notification_due_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee (PRAC) Rapporteur Notification Due Date
attributes.description: SLA-critical deadline by which the PRAC rapporteur must be notified of the validated safety signal per EMA regulatory requirements. Drives escalation workflows and compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Triage priority assigned to the safety signal based on clinical seriousness, signal strength, and public health impact. Drives SLA timelines for assessment completion and regulatory notification.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; FDA PDUFA VI Commitments

attributes.name: prr_value
attributes.description: Proportional Reporting Ratio (PRR) — a disproportionality analysis metric quantifying the ratio of the proportion of reports for a drug-event combination versus all other drugs. Values >2 with chi-squared >4 and ≥3 cases typically indicate a signal.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; Evans et al. PRR Method; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: psur_referral_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) Referral Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this safety signal has been referred for inclusion and evaluation in the next Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER).
attributes.references: GVP Module VII PSUR; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: regulatory_action_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the safety signal assessment has determined that a regulatory action is required (e.g., label update, DHPC, REMS modification, product withdrawal). Drives downstream regulatory affairs workflows.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; 21 CFR 314.81; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: regulatory_action_type
attributes.description: Type of regulatory action determined to be required based on the signal assessment outcome. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: label_update|rems_modification|dhpc|psur_referral|product_withdrawal|contraindication_addition|none — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GVP Module IX; 21 CFR 314.70; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; FDA REMS Guidance

attributes.name: rmp_update_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Management Plan (RMP) Update Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the signal assessment outcome requires an update to the product's Risk Management Plan (RMP). Triggers regulatory affairs and pharmacovigilance team coordination.
attributes.references: GVP Module V Risk Management Systems; EMA/838713/2011 Rev 2; Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010

attributes.name: ror_value
attributes.description: Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) — a disproportionality analysis metric representing the odds of a specific adverse event being reported for a drug versus all other drugs. Complements PRR in signal detection.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; van Puijenbroek ROR Method; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: serious_case_count
attributes.description: Number of Serious Adverse Event (SAE) cases among the total cases contributing to this signal. Serious cases include fatal, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, or congenital anomaly outcomes per ICH E2A.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management; GVP Module IX; 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: signal_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the safety signal including the nature of the concern, clinical context, patient population affected, and initial evidence summary. Supports signal triage and assessment documentation.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2); EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: signal_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier assigned to the safety signal upon creation in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS. Used for cross-system referencing, regulatory correspondence, and PRAC rapporteur notifications.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: signal_source_type
attributes.description: Classification of the data source from which the safety signal was detected. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spontaneous_database|literature|clinical_trial|real_world_data|social_media|health_authority — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; ICH E2C(R2); FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

attributes.name: signal_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the safety signal per GVP Module IX workflow: new (detected, not yet triaged), under_evaluation (active assessment in progress), validated (confirmed as a genuine safety concern), refuted (assessed and dismissed), closed (final disposition reached and documented).
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: signal_title
attributes.description: Concise, human-readable title describing the safety signal, typically formatted as [Drug Name] and [Adverse Event Term]. Used in regulatory correspondence, PRAC submissions, and internal safety committee communications.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: signal_type
attributes.description: Classification of the signal as new (not previously known), strengthened (existing signal with increased evidence), weakened (existing signal with decreased evidence), or refuted (previously identified signal now dismissed).
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: source_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier from the originating data source (e.g., FAERS case number, EudraVigilance report ID, literature PubMed ID, clinical trial NCT number) that triggered or contributed to the signal detection.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; FDA FAERS; EudraVigilance; WHO VigiBase

attributes.name: triage_date
attributes.description: Date on which the safety signal was formally triaged by the pharmacovigilance team to determine priority and assign for full assessment. Marks the transition from detection to active evaluation.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the safety signal record. Supports audit trail requirements and tracks signal assessment progression through the lifecycle.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GVP Module IX; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: validation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the safety signal was formally validated as a genuine safety concern following initial assessment. Triggers downstream regulatory notification and benefit-risk evaluation activities.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX Signal Management; EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2; ICH E2C(R2)

products.name: pv_product
products.description: Pharmacovigilance product master — the authoritative PV-domain view of medicinal products under safety surveillance. Captures product name, INN, ATC code, MAH (Marketing Authorization Holder), authorization numbers per country/region, formulation, route of administration, reference safety information document reference, international birth date (IBD), PSMF reference, QPPV assignment, and PV system governance metadata. Distinct from the commercial product catalog — this is the PV-specific product registration used for case processing, signal detection, PSUR scheduling, and regulatory reporting. Includes PSMF-level metadata: PV system description, organizational structure for pharmacovigilance, contracted party references, and compliance status per EU GVP Module II.
products.reference: EMA XEVMPD / FDA SPL Product Listing

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Marketing Authorization Holder (MAH) is the legal entity responsible for pharmacovigilance obligations. Required for regulatory submissions, liability determination, and safety reporting accountabilit

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.ndc_code. Business justification: US market products require NDC linkage for FDA FAERS submissions, product identification in US ICSRs, and recall coordination. Essential for US pharmacovigilance operations and regulatory compliance.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Core bridge between PV product master and commercial product master. Required for regulatory identifier reconciliation (NDC, EMA product number), lifecycle status alignment, product discontinuation im

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.mlr_review. Business justification: MLR reviews verify promotional materials comply with product safety profile (current label, RMP commitments, recent safety updates). Medical reviewers reference PV product master data to ensure fair b

When serious safety issues arise, teams review original project rationale, target sele

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.supplier_quality_agreement. Business justification: PV products must reference their supplier quality agreements which define pharmacovigilance responsibilities, ICSR exchange timelines, and deviation notification requirements. Essential for PV agreeme

attributes.name: argus_product_code
attributes.description: Native product identifier from the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system. Used for cross-system reconciliation and traceability between the Silver Layer PV product master and the operational PV case processing system.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety Product Configuration; ICH E2B(R3) integration

attributes.name: authorization_number
attributes.description: Official marketing authorisation or approval number issued by the health authority for the product in a specific country or region (e.g., NDA number, BLA number, EU MA number). Used to link PV records to regulatory approvals.
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314.81; EU GVP Module VI; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: authorization_type
attributes.description: Type of regulatory marketing authorisation application under which the product is approved (e.g., NDA — New Drug Application, BLA — Biologics License Application, MAA — Marketing Authorisation Application). Determines submission pathway and reporting requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NDA|BLA|MAA|ANDA|NDS|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR 314; 21 CFR 601; EU Directive 2001/83/EC; ICH M4

attributes.name: controlled_substance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the product contains a controlled substance subject to DEA scheduling requirements. True = controlled substance; False = not a controlled substance. Impacts PV reporting and distribution controls.
attributes.references: DEA Controlled Substances Act; 21 CFR 1308; EU Directive 2011/62/EU

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the PV product master record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GVP Module II.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EU GVP Module II; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: ema_product_number
attributes.description: EMA-assigned product number for centrally authorised products in the EU. Used for EudraVigilance submissions, PSUR repository submissions, and EU regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module VI; EudraVigilance Access Policy; EMA/816573/2011

attributes.name: eudravigilance_mp_code
attributes.description: EudraVigilance Medicinal Product Dictionary (EVMPD) identifier assigned by EMA for the product. Required for electronic ICSR submissions to EudraVigilance and EU regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module VI; EudraVigilance Data Analysis System; Regulation (EC) 726/2004

attributes.name: expedited_reporting_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this product is subject to expedited (7-day or 15-day) Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) reporting obligations to health authorities. Drives case processing timelines in Argus Safety.
attributes.references: ICH E2D; EU GVP Module VI Section 6.3; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1); 21 CFR 312.32

attributes.name: international_birth_date
attributes.description: International Birth Date (IBD) — the date of first marketing authorisation granted worldwide for the active substance. Serves as the reference date for PSUR/PBRER data lock point scheduling per ICH E2C(R2).
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 2.1; EU GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)

attributes.name: orphan_designation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the product holds an orphan drug designation for a rare disease indication. True = orphan designation granted; False = no orphan designation. Affects PV reporting thresholds and PSUR requirements.
attributes.references: EU Regulation 141/2000; 21 CFR 316; FDA Orphan Drug Act

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: Classification of the medicinal product by its scientific/regulatory category (e.g., small molecule, biologic, vaccine, gene therapy, cell therapy, combination product). Drives applicable regulatory framework and PV requirements.
attributes.references: ICH S6(R1); EU GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 3.2(e)

attributes.name: psmf_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this product to the applicable Pharmacovigilance System Master File (PSMF) that describes the PV system governing this product. Mandatory for EU GVP Module II compliance.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module II; Directive 2001/83/EC Article 104; EMA/816573/2011

attributes.name: psur_due_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) Next Due Date
attributes.description: Next scheduled due date for submission of the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) or Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) to the relevant health authority. Calculated from IBD and submission frequency.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2) Section 2.1; EU GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(ii)

attributes.name: psur_frequency
attributes.business_glossary_term: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) Submission Frequency
attributes.description: Regulatory-mandated frequency for Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) submission for this product. Drives the PSUR scheduling calendar.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EU GVP Module VII; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(ii)

attributes.name: pv_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the product within the pharmacovigilance system. Drives case processing eligibility, signal detection inclusion, and PSUR scheduling. Active = currently under PV surveillance; Suspended = temporarily halted; Withdrawn = marketing authorisation withdrawn; Under_review = under regulatory review; Archived = historical record only.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module VI; 21 CFR 314.81; Argus Safety product configuration

attributes.name: rems_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is required by the FDA for this product. True = REMS is mandated; False = REMS not required. Applicable to US-authorised products only.

attributes.name: rmp_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Risk Management Plan (RMP) is required for this product by the applicable health authority. True = RMP is mandated; False = RMP not required. Drives risk minimisation activity tracking.
attributes.references: EU GVP Module V; EMA/838713/2011; 21 CFR 505-1 (REMS)

attributes.name: signal_detection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this product is currently included in the active signal detection and management programme. True = included in signal detection runs; False = excluded (e.g., archived or withdrawn products).
attributes.references: EU GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the PV product master record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GVP Module II.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EU GVP Module II; SOX

products.name: suspect_drug
products.description: Suspect and concomitant drug record within an ICSR. Captures drug name (verbatim and WHO Drug Dictionary coded), drug role (suspect, concomitant, interacting), dose, frequency, route, indication, start/stop dates, action taken (drug withdrawn, dose reduced, dose not changed, unknown), dechallenge result, rechallenge result, and batch/lot number. One ICSR may have multiple suspect and concomitant drugs. Enables product-level case aggregation for signal detection, line listing generation, and exposure-based analyses.

attributes.name: suspect_drug_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the suspect or concomitant drug record within an Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR). Primary key of this entity.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module VI

attributes.name: icsr_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) to which this suspect or concomitant drug record belongs. One ICSR may contain multiple drug records.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: master_id

attributes.name: masterdata_ndc_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.ndc_code. Business justification: US ICSRs require NDC-level product identification for FDA submissions. Enables precise product matching, regulatory compliance, and integration with FDA Structured Product Labeling (SPL) for listednes

attributes.name: material_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: Suspect drugs must link to material master for batch traceability, quality investigations, and manufacturing deviation correlation. Enables root cause analysis when batch_lot_number indicates potentia

attributes.name: procurement_goods_receipt_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.goods_receipt. Business justification: Links suspect drug batches to receiving records enabling verification of receiving conditions (temperature excursions, packaging damage, storage) that may contribute to adverse events. Essential for c

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: When a suspect drug is identified in a safety case, linking to the vendor enables batch-level investigation, quality complaint initiation, and potential recall actions. Critical for product quality co

attributes.name: action_taken
attributes.description: Action taken with the suspect or concomitant drug in response to the adverse event (e.g., drug withdrawn, dose reduced, dose not changed, unknown). Critical for dechallenge assessment and causality evaluation. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.8.
attributes.value_regex: drug withdrawn|dose reduced|dose increased|dose not changed|unknown|not applicable
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: additional_dosing_text
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing any additional dosing information not captured in structured fields, such as dose titration schedules, special administration instructions, or deviations from prescribed dosing. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.6.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.6; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: batch_lot_number
attributes.description: Manufacturing batch or lot number of the drug product administered to the patient. Critical for product quality investigations, batch recalls, and manufacturing defect signal detection. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.7.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.7; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; EMA GVP Module VI; cGMP

attributes.name: coding_status
attributes.description: Status of the WHO Drug Dictionary coding process for this drug record: coded (coding complete), pending (awaiting coding), not coded (unable to code), auto-coded (coded by automated system), or manually coded (coded by a pharmacovigilance specialist).
attributes.references: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); Argus Safety; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: country_of_administration
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the drug was administered to the patient. Used for regional signal detection and regulatory reporting stratification.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: cumulative_dose_amount
attributes.description: Total cumulative dose of the drug received by the patient from start to stop date (or to the date of the adverse event). Used in dose-response analyses and exposure-based signal detection. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.5a.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.5a; EMA GVP Module IX

attributes.name: cumulative_dose_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the cumulative dose amount (e.g., mg, g, IU). Must be interpreted in conjunction with cumulative_dose_amount. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.5b.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.5b; UCUM; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: dechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome observed after the drug was withdrawn or dose reduced (dechallenge): whether the adverse event improved or resolved. A positive dechallenge supports causality. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.9.i.3.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.3; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: Physical form of the drug product administered to the patient (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, patch, solution). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.9.2. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|injection|solution|patch|cream|powder|suspension|inhaler|suppository — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.9.2; EDQM Standard Terms; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: dose_amount
attributes.description: Numeric quantity of the drug administered per dose as reported. Must be interpreted in conjunction with dose_unit. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.1a.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.1a; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: dose_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the dose amount (e.g., mg, mcg, g, mg/kg, IU, mL). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.1b. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg|mcg|g|mg/kg|IU|mL|mg/mL|% — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.1b; UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: dosing_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which the drug was administered (e.g., once daily, twice daily, weekly). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.3. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: once daily|twice daily|three times daily|four times daily|weekly|biweekly|monthly|as needed|continuous|every 8 hours — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.3; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: drug_authorization_number
attributes.description: Marketing authorization or approval number (e.g., NDA number, BLA number, MAA number) of the drug product. Links the drug record to the regulatory approval and supports regulatory reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.3.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module VI; NDA/BLA/MAA

attributes.name: drug_role
attributes.description: Role of the drug in the adverse event case: suspect (primary drug under investigation), concomitant (taken alongside but not suspected), interacting (suspected drug-drug interaction), or treatment (used to treat the adverse event). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.1.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: drug_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential number identifying the position of this drug record within the parent ICSR, used for ordering and referencing multiple drugs in a single case (e.g., drug 1, drug 2). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.1.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.1; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Expiry date of the drug product batch administered to the patient. Used in product quality investigations to assess whether an expired product may have contributed to the adverse event. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.8.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; cGMP

attributes.name: indication
attributes.description: Medical condition or disease for which the drug was prescribed or taken, coded using MedDRA terminology. Supports indication-stratified signal detection and benefit-risk assessment. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.7.r.2b.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.7.r.2b; MedDRA; EMA GVP Module IX

attributes.name: indication_verbatim
attributes.description: Indication for drug use as reported verbatim by the reporter, prior to MedDRA coding. Preserved for traceability and coding audit. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.7.r.2a.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.7.r.2a; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: is_blinded
attributes.description: Indicates whether the drug identity is blinded (True) in the context of a clinical trial (e.g., randomized controlled trial where the patient or investigator does not know the assigned treatment). Affects SUSAR reporting and unblinding procedures.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.2.5; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: is_company_product
attributes.description: Indicates whether the drug is a product owned or marketed by the reporting company (True) or a competitor/third-party product (False). Determines regulatory reporting obligations and case ownership.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: parent_drug_code
attributes.description: WHO Drug Dictionary parent drug code representing the active moiety or parent compound, used to group drug products sharing the same active substance for aggregate signal detection and PSUR analyses.
attributes.references: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module IX

attributes.name: rechallenge_result
attributes.description: Outcome observed after the drug was reintroduced following dechallenge (rechallenge): whether the adverse event recurred. A positive rechallenge is strong evidence of causality. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.9.i.4.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.4; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this suspect or concomitant drug record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VI.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this suspect or concomitant drug record was last modified in the pharmacovigilance system. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VI.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Route by which the drug was administered to the patient (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.10.2. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|transdermal|intrathecal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.10.2; EDQM Standard Terms; FDA 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: source_system_drug_code
attributes.description: Identifier of this drug record in the originating pharmacovigilance source system (e.g., Argus Safety case drug ID or Oracle AERS drug sequence identifier). Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the system of record.
attributes.references: Argus Safety / Oracle AERS; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the patient started taking the drug. Used to calculate drug exposure duration and temporal relationship to adverse event onset. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.4.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.4; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: stop_date
attributes.description: Date on which the patient stopped taking the drug. Nullable if the drug was ongoing at the time of the report. Used to calculate exposure duration and assess dechallenge timing. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.5.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.4.r.5; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: time_to_onset_days
attributes.description: Number of days between the drug start date and the onset of the adverse event. A key temporal metric for causality assessment and signal detection algorithms (e.g., disproportionality analysis).
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; EMA GVP Module IX

attributes.name: verbatim_drug_name
attributes.description: Drug name exactly as reported by the reporter (patient, healthcare professional, or other source) before any coding or standardization. Preserved for traceability and audit. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.2.2.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.2.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: who_drug_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code assigned by the WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) to the coded medicinal product. Used for product-level case aggregation, line listing, and signal detection analytics.
attributes.references: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2B(R3) G.k.2.3.r.1

attributes.name: who_drug_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) Coded Drug Name
attributes.description: Standardized drug name as coded against the WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD), representing the preferred term for the medicinal product. Enables cross-case aggregation and signal detection.
attributes.references: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2B(R3) G.k.2.3; EMA GVP Module IX

products.name: reporter
products.description: Reporter master data — the individual or organization who submitted an adverse event report. Captures reporter type (healthcare professional, patient/consumer, lawyer, regulatory authority, literature), qualification (physician, pharmacist, nurse, dentist, consumer), country, institution, anonymized reporter identifier (per GDPR/HIPAA), contact preference for follow-up, and reporter reliability assessment.
