Enables reporter-level case aggregation, duplicate detection, follow-up management, and compliance with ICH E2B reporter data requirements. Distinct from HCP master — this is the PV-specific reporter identity used solely for case processing.

attributes.name: reporter_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the pharmacovigilance reporter record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for the reporter master data entity.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Entity

attributes.name: country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Reporter country determines follow-up feasibility, data privacy regulations (GDPR vs others), contact protocols, and language requirements. Operational necessity for case management and regulatory com

attributes.name: debarment_check_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.debarment_check. Business justification: Reporters (especially clinical investigators) must be screened against FDA debarment and OIG exclusion lists per GCP requirements. Debarment screening is mandatory for investigator qualification and o

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.hcp_master. Business justification: When reporter is HCP (is_hcp flag), linking to hcp_master enables license verification, specialty validation for causality assessment, NPI matching for regulatory submissions, and structured follow-up

attributes.name: master_reporter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the canonical/master reporter record when this record has been identified as a duplicate. Null if this record is itself the master. Supports deduplication and case re-linking workflows in the PV system.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Duplicate Management

attributes.name: masterdata_address_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.address. Business justification: Structured address linkage enables standardized contact management, duplicate reporter detection, and GDPR compliance (right to erasure). Replaces fragmented address fields with master data reference

attributes.name: anonymized_reporter_code
attributes.description: Privacy-compliant pseudonymous identifier assigned to the reporter in lieu of personal identifiers, enabling case aggregation and follow-up management without exposing PII. Mandatory under GDPR and HIPAA for PV processing.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4 & Article 25; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E2B(R3) A.1.7

attributes.name: argus_reporter_code
attributes.description: Source system identifier for the reporter as assigned by Argus Safety / Oracle AERS. Used for lineage tracing and deduplication against the operational PV system.
attributes.references: Argus Safety / Oracle AERS Reporter Master; ICH E2B(R3) A.1.7

attributes.name: consent_date
attributes.description: Date on which the reporter provided or withdrew consent to be contacted for follow-up. Required for GDPR audit trail demonstrating lawful basis for processing personal data.

attributes.name: consent_to_contact
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reporter has provided explicit consent to be contacted for follow-up queries regarding the adverse event report. Mandatory consent gate under GDPR Article 7 before any follow-up communication is initiated.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.508; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: contact_preference
attributes.description: Preferred channel for follow-up communication as indicated by the reporter. Drives the follow-up workflow in Argus Safety. 'no_contact' indicates the reporter has declined further contact, which must be respected per GDPR consent obligations.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Follow-up Workflow

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the reporter record was first created in the PV system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records in regulated pharmaceutical environments.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; GDPR Article 30

attributes.name: department
attributes.description: Department or unit within the reporter's organization (e.g., Oncology Ward, Clinical Pharmacology, Drug Safety). Supports routing of follow-up queries to the correct organizational unit.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.4; Argus Safety Reporter Master

attributes.name: duplicate_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reporter record has been identified as a potential or confirmed duplicate of another reporter record. Duplicate reporters must be resolved before case processing to prevent double-counting in aggregate safety analyses.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; Argus Safety Duplicate Detection

attributes.name: email
attributes.description: Primary email address of the reporter for electronic follow-up correspondence. Classified as restricted PII. Used only for PV case follow-up; not shared with commercial systems. Consent-gated per GDPR.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.6; GDPR Article 4 & Article 6; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: family_name
attributes.description: Last/family name of the individual reporter. Stored in restricted classification per GDPR and HIPAA. Used for follow-up correspondence and duplicate detection. May be withheld or anonymized per reporter consent.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.3b; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: fax
attributes.description: Fax number of the reporter or their institution, used for formal follow-up correspondence in jurisdictions where fax remains a regulatory-accepted communication channel (e.g., Japan PMDA submissions).
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.6; PMDA Pharmacovigilance Guidelines

attributes.name: first_report_date
attributes.description: Date on which the reporter submitted their first adverse event report to the company. Used for longitudinal reporter relationship analysis and tenure-based reliability assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Master; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: follow_up_deadline
attributes.description: Target date by which a follow-up response from the reporter is required to meet regulatory submission timelines (e.g., 15-day expedited reporting for SUSARs and SAEs). Calculated based on initial receipt date and applicable regulatory clock.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR §312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: follow_up_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether outstanding follow-up queries have been sent to this reporter and a response is pending. Drives the follow-up management workflow in Argus Safety to ensure timely case completion within regulatory timeframes.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §312.32; Argus Safety Follow-up Workflow

attributes.name: gdpr_erasure_date
attributes.description: Date on which the GDPR Right to Erasure request was processed and PII fields were anonymized. Null if no erasure request has been received. Required for GDPR compliance audit trail.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 17 & Article 30; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: gdpr_erasure_requested
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reporter has submitted a Right to Erasure (Right to be Forgotten) request under GDPR Article 17. When true, PII fields must be anonymized while retaining the anonymized case record for pharmacovigilance regulatory obligations under GDPR Article 17(3)(c).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 17; EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: given_name
attributes.description: First/given name of the individual reporter. Stored in restricted classification per GDPR and HIPAA. Used for follow-up correspondence and duplicate detection. May be withheld or anonymized per reporter consent.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.3a; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: is_hcp
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reporter is a qualified Healthcare Professional (HCP). HCP-reported cases carry higher regulatory weight and may trigger expedited 15-day reporting obligations to FDA, EMA, and other health authorities.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.2; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 or ISO 639-2 language code representing the reporter's preferred communication language. Used to route follow-up correspondence to appropriately qualified multilingual PV staff and to select translated follow-up letter templates.
attributes.references: ISO 639-1; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: last_report_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent adverse event report submitted by this reporter. Used to identify active versus dormant reporters and to support follow-up prioritization.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Master; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: license_number
attributes.description: Professional license or registration number of the HCP reporter (e.g., medical license, pharmacy registration). Used to verify reporter qualification and credibility. Stored as confidential business data.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.2; FDA MedWatch 3500A; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for PV case processor notes regarding the reporter, such as communication history, special handling instructions, or context about the reporter's relationship to the case. Not transmitted in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: Argus Safety Reporter Master; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: organization_name
attributes.description: Name of the institution, hospital, clinic, regulatory authority, or company from which the reporter submitted the adverse event report. Relevant for institutional reporters and regulatory authority submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.4; EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §314.81

attributes.name: phone
attributes.description: Primary telephone number of the reporter for follow-up contact. Classified as restricted PII. Stored in E.164 international format where possible. Used exclusively for PV case follow-up activities.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.6; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

attributes.name: qualification
attributes.description: Professional qualification of the reporter, particularly relevant for Healthcare Professional (HCP) reporters. Determines the clinical credibility weighting of the report and regulatory classification. ICH E2B(R3) field A.2.1.2. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: physician|pharmacist|nurse|dentist|other_health_professional|consumer|unknown — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.2; EMA GVP Module VI; FDA MedWatch 3500A

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA) when the reporter is a regulatory body. Used to route mandatory ICSR submissions and track authority-initiated follow-up requests.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.4; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; EMA GVP Module VI; MHRA Yellow Card; PMDA Guidelines

attributes.name: reliability_score
attributes.description: Internal PV team assessment of the reporter's historical reliability based on completeness and accuracy of prior submissions. Used to weight signal detection analysis and prioritize follow-up resources. Assigned by the PV case processor.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Assessment

attributes.name: reporter_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the reporter record within the PV system. Inactive or blocked reporters are excluded from new case assignments. Supports duplicate detection and data quality management.
attributes.references: Argus Safety Reporter Master; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: reporter_type
attributes.description: Classification of the reporter by their relationship to the adverse event. Drives regulatory reporting obligations and follow-up workflows. ICH E2B(R3) field A.2.1.1. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: healthcare_professional|patient_consumer|lawyer|regulatory_authority|literature|other — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.1; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: source_type
attributes.description: Classification of the original source through which the adverse event report was received. Determines regulatory handling requirements; e.g., literature-sourced reports require medical literature monitoring per GVP Module VI. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spontaneous|literature|clinical_trial|regulatory_authority|solicited|other — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.4; EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §314.81

attributes.name: specialty
attributes.description: Medical or clinical specialty of the HCP reporter (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology). Supports signal detection analysis by therapeutic area and enables targeted follow-up by medically qualified personnel.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Reporter Master

attributes.name: total_reports_submitted
attributes.description: Cumulative count of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) submitted by this reporter. Used for duplicate detection, reporter profiling, and reliability assessment. Updated upon each new case linkage.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Reporter Aggregation

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the reporter record. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR Article 30 record-keeping obligations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; GDPR Article 30

products.name: pv_action
products.description: Pharmacovigilance action record capturing regulatory and safety actions taken in response to validated signals, PSUR findings, RMP updates, or authority requests. Action types include: labeling updates (CCDS, SmPC, USPI changes), DHPC (Dear Healthcare Professional Communication), restricted indication, market suspension/withdrawal, REMS modification, RMP update trigger, and PASS study initiation. Tracks action type, triggering event, responsible party, target completion date, authority notification requirement, implementation evidence, and effectiveness assessment. Links signals, PSURs, and RMPs to their downstream regulatory consequences.
products.reference: GVP Module XVI / FDA REMS / EMA RMP Action

attributes.name: pv_action_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the pharmacovigilance action record. Primary key for this entity. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — represents a discrete regulatory/safety action with a defined lifecycle triggered by a validated signal, PSUR finding, RMP update, or health authority request.
attributes.references: ICH E2E Pharmacovigilance Planning; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA GVP Module V

attributes.name: compliance_capa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_capa. Business justification: PV actions (label changes, DHPCs, REMS modifications) require compliance CAPA tracking for implementation, effectiveness verification, and regulatory commitment closure. Standard pharmaceutical qualit

attributes.name: content_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.medical_content. Business justification: PV actions (label updates, DHPCs, risk communications) trigger creation or revision of medical content for MSL field teams, ensuring consistent scientific messaging following safety updates.

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Safety actions (label updates, REMS implementation, DHPC distribution, risk communication campaigns) generate implementation costs tracked via internal orders. Finance captures costs for regulatory su

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hcp.hcp_master. Business justification: Safety actions (DHPC, REMS communications, prescriber notifications) target specific HCPs. Linking enables tracking of communication delivery, acknowledgment receipt, and effectiveness assessment per

attributes.name: pass_study_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.pass_study. Business justification: PV actions can mandate PASS studies as risk minimization measures. Add pass_study_id FK (nullable - only when action mandates a PASS study). Remove pass_study_title and pass_study_protocol_number as t

attributes.name: psur_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) or Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) finding that triggered this action. Nullable when the action is not PSUR-driven.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module VII; 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the medicinal product (drug substance or drug product) subject to this pharmacovigilance action. Links to the master product record for the affected compound or finished dosage form.
attributes.references: EMA XEVMPD; FDA NDC Directory; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: regulatory_inspection_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_inspection. Business justification: PV actions are frequently commitments made in inspection responses (e.g., labeling updates, process improvements). Tracking inspection-driven actions is core to inspection response management and clos

attributes.name: responsible_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: PV actions (label changes, DHPC, REMS) require named accountability for regulatory compliance and action tracking. Linking to employee enables workload management, escalation routing, and audit trail

attributes.name: rmp_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Risk Management Plan (RMP) associated with or updated by this pharmacovigilance action. Nullable when the action is not RMP-driven.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2E; FDA REMS Guidance

attributes.name: sae_report_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.sae_report. Business justification: SAE events can trigger PV actions (regulatory notifications, safety measures). Add sae_report_id FK (nullable - only when action is triggered by SAE). The triggering_event_type field indicates the tri

attributes.name: safety_signal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the validated safety signal that triggered this pharmacovigilance action. Links the action to its upstream signal detection record for traceability and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

attributes.name: susar_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.susar. Business justification: SUSAR events can trigger PV actions (label changes, regulatory notifications). Add susar_id FK (nullable - only when action is triggered by SUSAR). The triggering_event_type field indicates the trigge

attributes.name: action_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the pharmacovigilance action, including the specific risk minimization measures to be implemented, rationale, and expected patient safety impact. Captured from Argus Safety case narrative or Veeva Vault RIM action record.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: action_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the PV action, formatted as PVA-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}. Used in regulatory correspondence, authority notifications, and cross-system tracking within Argus Safety/Oracle AERS and Veeva Vault RIM.
attributes.references: ICH E2E; EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: action_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the pharmacovigilance action, tracking progression from initiation through completion or cancellation. Drives workflow routing in safety management systems.
attributes.references: ICH E2E; EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory or safety action being taken. Includes labeling updates (CCDS/SmPC/USPI changes), Dear Healthcare Professional Communication (DHPC), restricted indication, market suspension/withdrawal, Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) modification, Risk Management Plan (RMP) update trigger, and Post-Authorization Safety Study (PASS) initiation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: labeling_update|dhpc|restricted_indication|market_suspension|market_withdrawal|rems_modification|rmp_update|pass_initiation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V; FDA REMS Guidance; ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: actual_completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which the pharmacovigilance action was fully implemented and closed. Compared against target_completion_date to assess timeliness and regulatory compliance. Nullable until action is completed.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH E2E

attributes.name: argus_case_number
attributes.description: Source system case or action number from Argus Safety/Oracle AERS, the operational system of record for pharmacovigilance. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the source PV system.
attributes.references: Argus Safety/Oracle AERS; 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GVP Module I

attributes.name: authority_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the relevant health authority (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA, etc.) was formally notified of this pharmacovigilance action. Nullable when notification is not required or not yet submitted.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module V; MHRA Guidance on PV

attributes.name: authority_notification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pharmacovigilance action requires formal notification to one or more health authorities (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, etc.) prior to or upon implementation. Drives regulatory submission workflows.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: benefit_risk_impact
attributes.description: Assessment of how this pharmacovigilance action affects the overall benefit-risk balance of the medicinal product. Informs PSUR/PBRER benefit-risk conclusions and regulatory authority communications.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module VII; FDA Benefit-Risk Framework

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this PV action record was first captured in the system (Argus Safety/Oracle AERS or Veeva Vault). Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); EMA GVP Module I

attributes.name: dhpc_distribution_scope
attributes.business_glossary_term: Dear Healthcare Professional Communication (DHPC) Distribution Scope
attributes.description: Geographic scope of the Dear Healthcare Professional Communication (DHPC) distribution when action_type is dhpc. Indicates whether the communication is national, regional, or global. Not applicable for non-DHPC actions.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module XV; 21 CFR Part 200.5; MHRA DHCP Guidance

attributes.name: effectiveness_assessment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the effectiveness assessment of this pharmacovigilance action was completed or is scheduled. Supports periodic benefit-risk evaluation and regulatory reporting cycles.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module XVI; FDA REMS Assessment Guidance; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: effectiveness_assessment_outcome
attributes.description: Outcome of the post-implementation effectiveness assessment, indicating whether the pharmacovigilance action successfully minimized the identified risk. Informs subsequent signal management and RMP update decisions.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module XVI; FDA REMS Assessment Guidance; ICH E2E

attributes.name: effectiveness_assessment_status
attributes.description: Status of the post-implementation effectiveness assessment for this pharmacovigilance action. Tracks whether the action achieved its intended risk minimization objective, as required by EMA GVP Module XVI and FDA REMS assessment requirements.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module XVI; FDA REMS Assessment Guidance; ICH E2E

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: Date on which this pharmacovigilance action was escalated to senior management or the QPPV. Nullable when escalation_flag is false. Supports governance and oversight reporting.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module I; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: escalation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pharmacovigilance action has been escalated due to missed deadlines, critical safety findings, or authority pressure. Triggers executive and QPPV notification workflows.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module I; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: implementation_evidence_ref
attributes.description: Document reference number or Veeva Vault document ID for the evidence package demonstrating that the pharmacovigilance action has been implemented (e.g., updated label version, DHPC distribution confirmation, REMS modification approval letter).
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: initiated_date
attributes.description: The date on which the pharmacovigilance action was formally initiated or triggered. Represents the principal real-world business event timestamp (day-level precision) for regulatory timeline tracking and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH E2E

attributes.name: labeling_document_type
attributes.description: Type of labeling document affected when action_type is labeling_update. Identifies whether the Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS), Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC), US Prescribing Information (USPI), Patient Information Leaflet (PIL), or package insert is being updated. Null or not_applicable for non-labeling actions.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA SmPC Guideline; 21 CFR Part 201; Directive 2001/83/EC

attributes.name: labeling_section_affected
attributes.description: Specific section(s) of the labeling document being updated (e.g., Section 4.4 Special Warnings, Section 4.8 Undesirable Effects, Boxed Warning, Contraindications). Applicable only for labeling_update action type.
attributes.references: EMA SmPC Guideline; 21 CFR Part 201.57; ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: market_scope
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes identifying the markets affected by this pharmacovigilance action. Supports multi-jurisdictional impact assessment and country-level regulatory tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: notified_authorities
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of health authority codes (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA) that have been or must be notified of this action. Supports multi-jurisdictional regulatory tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; PMDA Pharmacovigilance Regulations

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Risk-based priority classification of the pharmacovigilance action, determining escalation urgency and resource allocation. Critical actions typically involve immediate patient safety risks requiring expedited regulatory response.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2E; FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

attributes.name: regulatory_deadline_date
attributes.description: Mandatory deadline imposed by a health authority (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA) for completion or notification of this pharmacovigilance action. Distinct from the internally-set target_completion_date. Non-compliance may result in regulatory sanctions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA GVP Module V; MHRA Guidance on PV; PMDA Regulations

attributes.name: rems_program_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program Name
attributes.description: Name of the FDA-approved Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program being modified when action_type is rems_modification. Nullable for non-REMS actions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.520; FDA REMS Guidance; FDAAA Section 505-1

attributes.name: responsible_party
attributes.description: Organizational unit or party accountable for implementing and completing this pharmacovigilance action. Determines workflow ownership and escalation paths within the safety management system. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pv_team|regulatory_affairs|medical_affairs|manufacturing|commercial|external_cro|external_cmo — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module I; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: target_completion_date
attributes.description: Planned date by which the pharmacovigilance action must be fully implemented. Drives SLA monitoring, regulatory deadline tracking, and escalation workflows. Distinct from actual completion date.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH E2E

attributes.name: triggering_event_reference
attributes.description: Free-text or structured reference number identifying the specific triggering event (e.g., signal case number, PSUR submission number, authority correspondence reference). Provides cross-system traceability.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V; ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: triggering_event_type
attributes.description: Classification of the upstream event or finding that necessitated this PV action. Distinguishes between signal validation outcomes, PSUR/PBRER findings, RMP periodic reviews, health authority requests, SUSAR clusters, out-of-specification (OOS) trends, and literature review findings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: signal_validation|psur_finding|rmp_review|authority_request|susar_cluster|oos_trend|literature_review — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this PV action record. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module I.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GVP Module I; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM or QualityDocs for the regulatory submission package, labeling document, or DHPC associated with this action. Supports document management and regulatory submission traceability.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GVP Module V

products.name: rsi
products.description: Reference Safety Information record — the authoritative document defining the expected adverse reaction profile for listedness/expectedness assessment. Captures RSI document type (Investigator's Brochure for trials, SmPC for EU, USPI for US, CCDS as company core), version, effective date, product scope, and the enumerated list of expected adverse reactions by MedDRA preferred term. Used in every ICSR to determine whether a reaction is listed (expected) or unlisted (unexpected), directly driving expedited reporting obligations and SUSAR determination. Version-controlled with effective dating to support point-in-time listedness assessment.
products.reference: ICH E2A RSI / Investigator Brochure / SmPC

attributes.name: rsi_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Reference Safety Information record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, ICH E2C, 21 CFR Part 312, EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: previous_version_rsi_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding version of this RSI document for the same product and document type. Enables version chain traversal for historical listedness assessment and change impact analysis.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, ICH E2C(R2), EMA GVP Module VI B.4.2

attributes.name: applicable_region
attributes.description: Geographic region or regulatory jurisdiction for which this RSI document is authoritative (e.g., 'USA', 'EU', 'JPN', 'GLOBAL'). Determines which RSI version is used for listedness assessment in region-specific expedited reporting. Use ISO 3-letter country codes or 'GLOBAL' for CCDS.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, EMA GVP Module VI, 21 CFR Part 312.32, PMDA Safety Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this RSI version received internal company approval (e.g., sign-off by the Global Safety Officer or Medical Affairs). Distinct from effective_date; the document may be approved before it becomes effective for listedness assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2F, EMA GVP Module VI, 21 CFR Part 11 (electronic approval records)

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the individual (typically Global Safety Officer, Medical Director, or Regulatory Affairs Lead) who provided final internal approval for this RSI version. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11, EMA GVP Module VI, ICH E2F

attributes.name: argus_rsi_code
attributes.description: Native identifier of this RSI record in the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system. Enables bidirectional traceability between the Databricks Silver Layer and the operational PV system for reconciliation and audit purposes.
attributes.references: Argus Safety RSI Configuration, Oracle AERS, 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: atc_code
attributes.description: WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for the active substance, used to categorize the drug by therapeutic area and mechanism. Supports signal detection and aggregate safety analysis across product classes.
attributes.references: WHO ATC/DDD Index, ICH E2B(R3), EMA GVP Module IX

attributes.name: change_reason
attributes.description: Categorized reason for issuing this new RSI version. Supports root cause analysis and regulatory inspection readiness. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new_safety_signal|regulatory_request|periodic_review|label_update|clinical_data|spontaneous_reports|post_market_study|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2F, EMA GVP Module VI, ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: change_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the key changes introduced in this RSI version compared to the previous version (e.g., 'Added hepatotoxicity as listed reaction; updated frequency of nausea from common to very common'). Supports impact assessment for ongoing ICSRs and SUSAR re-evaluation.
attributes.references: ICH E2F Section 3.1, EMA GVP Module VI B.4.2, ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this RSI record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR Article 5(2) accountability principle.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11, GDPR Article 5(2), ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: development_phase
attributes.description: Stage of the product's development lifecycle at the time this RSI version was issued. Determines which document type is applicable (IB for clinical phases, SmPC/USPI for marketed). Relevant for SUSAR reporting obligations under IND/CTA.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, 21 CFR Part 312, EMA GVP Module VI B.4

attributes.name: document_language
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 language code of the RSI document (e.g., 'en', 'de', 'fr', 'ja'). The English version is typically the master; translations may exist for regional submissions. Listedness assessment is performed against the language-appropriate version.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3), EMA GVP Module VI, ISO 639-1

attributes.name: document_title
attributes.description: Full official title of the reference safety document (e.g., 'Investigator's Brochure for Compound XYZ Edition 5' or 'Summary of Product Characteristics for DrugName 10mg Tablets'). Human-readable identity label for the document.
attributes.references: ICH E2F, EMA SmPC Guideline, 21 CFR Part 201

attributes.name: document_type
attributes.description: Type of the reference safety document that defines the expected adverse reaction profile. IB = Investigator's Brochure (used in clinical trials), SmPC = Summary of Product Characteristics (EU marketed products), USPI = United States Prescribing Information (US marketed products), CCDS = Company Core Data Sheet (global company reference), PIL = Patient Information Leaflet. Drives which document is consulted for listedness assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2, ICH E2F, EMA GVP Module VI, 21 CFR Part 312.23, 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: Pharmaceutical dosage form of the drug product covered by this RSI (e.g., 'tablet', 'injection', 'capsule', 'infusion'). Relevant when a product has multiple formulations with different safety profiles requiring separate RSI documents.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.2.r.4, EMA SmPC Guideline, 21 CFR Part 201

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this version of the RSI document becomes the authoritative reference for listedness/expectedness assessment. Used in point-in-time queries to determine which RSI version was active at the time of an adverse event report.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2, EMA GVP Module VI B.4.2, 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: emea_product_number
attributes.description: EMA centralized procedure product number (EMEA/H/C/XXXXXX) associated with this RSI when document_type is 'SmPC'. Links the RSI to the EU marketing authorization for EudraVigilance reporting and PSUR obligations.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VI, EMA GVP Module VII, EU Regulation 726/2004

attributes.name: ind_number
attributes.description: FDA Investigational New Drug (IND) application number associated with this RSI, applicable when document_type is 'IB'. Links the RSI to the specific IND under which clinical trials are conducted and SUSAR reporting obligations arise.

attributes.name: indication
attributes.description: Primary approved or investigated clinical indication for which the product is used, as stated in this RSI version (e.g., 'Non-small cell lung cancer', 'Rheumatoid arthritis'). Contextualizes the expected safety profile for the intended patient population.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2), EMA SmPC Guideline Section 4.1, 21 CFR Part 201.57

attributes.name: inn
attributes.description: WHO-assigned International Nonproprietary Name (INN) for the active substance covered by this RSI. Provides a globally standardized, non-proprietary identifier for the drug substance, enabling cross-product and cross-company safety comparisons.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme, ICH E2B(R3) C.2.r.1, EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: is_current_version
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this record represents the currently active version of the RSI for the given product, document type, and region. True = this is the version used for all new ICSR listedness assessments. Supports efficient querying without date-range filtering.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, EMA GVP Module VI B.4.2, Argus Safety RSI Configuration

attributes.name: listed_reaction_count
attributes.description: Total number of distinct adverse reactions enumerated as listed/expected in this RSI version, expressed as MedDRA Preferred Terms. Provides a quick summary metric for version comparison and completeness validation without querying the reaction detail table.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, MedDRA Terminology, EMA GVP Module VI B.4

attributes.name: meddra_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Version
attributes.description: Version of the MedDRA terminology used to encode the listed adverse reactions in this RSI (e.g., '26.0', '26.1'). Critical for consistent listedness assessment — MedDRA term changes between versions can affect whether a reaction is considered listed.
attributes.references: MedDRA Introductory Guide, ICH E2B(R3), EMA GVP Module VI, FDA MedDRA Guidance

attributes.name: nda_bla_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: New Drug Application (NDA) / Biologics License Application (BLA) Number
attributes.description: FDA NDA or BLA application number associated with this RSI, applicable when document_type is 'USPI' for approved marketed products. Links the RSI to the approved marketing authorization for expedited and periodic safety reporting.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314, 21 CFR Part 601, FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting

attributes.name: product_name
attributes.description: Proprietary or brand name of the medicinal product to which this RSI applies. May be a compound name (INN) for investigational products or a trade name for marketed products. Supports product-level filtering in ICSR listedness assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3), EMA GVP Module VI, 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: psur_data_lock_point
attributes.business_glossary_term: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) Data Lock Point
attributes.description: Data lock point date for the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) cycle in which this RSI version was first used. Supports traceability of RSI changes across PSUR reporting periods.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2), EMA GVP Module VII, 21 CFR Part 314.81(b)(2)(vii)

attributes.name: regulatory_authority
attributes.description: Primary regulatory authority to which this RSI document is submitted or under whose jurisdiction it is maintained. Drives authority-specific reporting obligations and listedness determination rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|HEALTH_CANADA|TGA|ANVISA|CDSCO — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E2A, EMA GVP Module VI, 21 CFR Part 312, PMDA Safety Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: rmp_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or version of the Risk Management Plan (RMP) that was current when this RSI version was issued. The RMP's safety specification informs the listed reactions in the RSI and must be consistent with it.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V, ICH E2E, 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Route by which the drug product is administered (e.g., 'oral', 'intravenous', 'subcutaneous', 'intramuscular', 'topical'). Relevant for products with multiple administration routes that may have distinct safety profiles and separate RSI sections.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3) C.2.r.5, EMA SmPC Guideline Section 4.2, 21 CFR Part 201

attributes.name: rsi_code
attributes.description: Business-assigned unique code identifying this RSI document record, typically encoding product abbreviation, year, and sequence number. Used as the externally-known identifier across pharmacovigilance systems including Argus Safety.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, EMA GVP Module VI, 21 CFR Part 312.32

attributes.name: rsi_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the RSI document version. 'draft' = under preparation; 'approved' = internally approved but not yet effective; 'active' = currently in force for listedness assessment; 'superseded' = replaced by a newer version; 'retired' = no longer applicable; 'withdrawn' = removed from use. Only one version per product/document type should be 'active' at any time.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, EMA GVP Module VI, Veeva Vault RIM lifecycle states

attributes.name: source_document_reference
attributes.description: Document management system identifier (e.g., Veeva Vault document ID) for the source RSI document. Enables traceability from the RSI data record back to the controlled document in the eTMF or QualityDocs vault.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM/eTMF, 21 CFR Part 11, EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: superseded_date
attributes.description: Date on which this RSI version was superseded by a newer version and ceased to be the active reference. Null if this is the current active version. Together with effective_date, defines the validity interval for point-in-time listedness assessment.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, EMA GVP Module VI B.4.2, ICH E2C(R2)

attributes.name: susar_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Applicable Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this RSI is used for SUSAR determination in clinical trials. True when document_type is 'IB' or 'CCDS' and the product is under active clinical investigation. Drives the 7/15-day expedited reporting clock for unexpected serious reactions.
attributes.references: ICH E2A Section 2, EMA GVP Module VI B.4, 21 CFR Part 312.32(c)

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic area or disease indication for which the product is developed or approved (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Used for domain-level safety reporting and signal management.
attributes.references: ICH E2C(R2), EMA GVP Module VII, 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this RSI record in the data platform. Together with created_timestamp, provides a complete audit trail for data governance and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11, GDPR Article 5(2), EMA GVP Module VI

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version or edition number of the RSI document (e.g., '5.0', '2.1', '12'). Critical for point-in-time listedness assessment — the version in effect at the time of an adverse event determines whether a reaction is listed or unlisted. Corresponds to the edition field in Argus Safety RSI configuration.
attributes.references: ICH E2A, ICH E2F Section 3.1, EMA GVP Module VI B.4, 21 CFR Part 312.32(c)

products.name: pv_agreement
products.description: Pharmacovigilance agreement record governing safety data exchange obligations between the MAH and partners. Covers SDEAs (Safety Data Exchange Agreements), PVAs (Pharmacovigilance Agreements), and co-vigilance arrangements with licensees, CROs, CMOs, co-promotion partners, and local affiliates. Captures agreement type, counterparty, effective/expiry dates, reporting timelines (days to exchange), product scope, responsible party designations (PSUR authorship, signal management, regulatory submission), and compliance monitoring status. Required under GVP Module I and ICH E2E for all outsourced PV activities.
products.reference: EU GVP Module I SDEA / Safety Data Exchange Agreement

attributes.name: pv_agreement_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the pharmacovigilance agreement record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity. Role: MASTER_AGREEMENT.

attributes.name: mah_legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Pharmacovigilance agreements are contracts between legal entities defining safety data exchange obligations. MAH legal entity linkage foundational for contract management, audit trail, and regulatory

attributes.name: royalty_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.royalty_agreement. Business justification: Pharmacovigilance agreements with licensors/licensees for in-licensed or out-licensed products often reference the same commercial relationship as royalty agreements. Linking enables tracking of safet

attributes.name: third_party_due_diligence_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Third Party Due Diligence Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.third_party_due_diligence. Business justification: Pharmacovigilance agreements require due diligence on counterparties per GVP Module VI (management and reporting of adverse reactions). Vendor qualification for PV services mandates compliance screeni

attributes.name: agreement_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique reference number assigned to the pharmacovigilance agreement (e.g., SDEA-2024-0042). Used in regulatory correspondence, audit trails, and partner communications. Maps to the document number in Veeva Vault RIM or Argus Safety agreement registry.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the pharmacovigilance agreement. DRAFT = under negotiation; ACTIVE = in force and binding; SUSPENDED = temporarily paused by mutual consent or regulatory action; TERMINATED = permanently ended before expiry; EXPIRED = reached end date without renewal; UNDER_REVIEW = undergoing periodic review or amendment.

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pharmacovigilance agreement by its legal and operational nature. SDEA = Safety Data Exchange Agreement; PVA = Pharmacovigilance Agreement; CO_VIGILANCE = co-vigilance arrangement; CO_PROMOTION = co-promotion partner PV agreement; AFFILIATE = local affiliate PV agreement. Determines the regulatory obligations and reporting obligations applicable to each party.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; ICH E2E; EMA/873138/2011

attributes.name: amendment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent amendment to the pharmacovigilance agreement. Nullable if no amendments have been made since original execution. Used to track agreement evolution and trigger re-review workflows.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2E

attributes.name: argus_agreement_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier used in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS to link this pharmacovigilance agreement to the partner configuration for automated ICSR routing and exchange. Enables traceability between the agreement record and the operational safety system configuration.
attributes.references: Argus Safety; Oracle AERS; GVP Module VI; ICH E2B(R3)

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Current compliance monitoring status of the pharmacovigilance agreement based on periodic reviews, audits, and KPI tracking. COMPLIANT = all obligations met; NON_COMPLIANT = one or more obligations breached; UNDER_REVIEW = compliance assessment in progress; PENDING_AUDIT = scheduled for compliance audit. Supports GVP Module I oversight requirements.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; GVP Module II; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: counterparty_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the counterparty's principal place of business. Determines applicable national competent authority reporting requirements and data privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA).
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; GVP Module I; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: counterparty_name
attributes.description: Full legal name of the external organisation that is party to this pharmacovigilance agreement. May be a CRO, CMO, CDMO, licensee, co-promotion partner, or local affiliate. Used in regulatory submissions and audit documentation.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; GDPR Article 28; ICH E2E

attributes.name: counterparty_pv_contact_email
attributes.description: Email address of the designated pharmacovigilance contact at the counterparty organisation. Used for operational safety data exchange communications and escalation notifications.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; GDPR Article 4; ICH E2E

attributes.name: counterparty_pv_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the designated pharmacovigilance contact person at the counterparty organisation responsible for safety data exchange under this agreement. Required for operational communication and escalation.

attributes.name: counterparty_type
attributes.description: Classification of the counterparty by their operational role in the pharmaceutical value chain. CRO = Contract Research Organization; CMO = Contract Manufacturing Organization; CDMO = Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization; LICENSEE = product licensee; CO_PROMOTER = co-promotion partner; AFFILIATE = local affiliate entity; DISTRIBUTOR = distribution partner. Drives applicable GVP obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CRO|CMO|CDMO|LICENSEE|CO_PROMOTER|AFFILIATE|DISTRIBUTOR — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GVP Module I; GVP Module VI; ICH E2E

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pharmacovigilance agreement record was first created in the system. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per model conventions. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module I.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GVP Module I; ICH E2E

attributes.name: data_exchange_format
attributes.description: Specifies the technical format used for exchanging Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) between parties. E2B_R2 = ICH E2B(R2) XML format; E2B_R3 = ICH E2B(R3) FHIR-based format; PAPER = paper-based exchange; PROPRIETARY = system-specific format; NOT_SPECIFIED = format not yet defined. Drives technical integration requirements with Argus Safety/Oracle AERS.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA/EMEA/H/20665/04; FDA 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: data_exchange_method
attributes.description: Technical transmission method used for exchanging safety data between parties. EVWEB = EMA EudraVigilance Web Trader; GATEWAY = automated gateway-to-gateway; SFTP = secure file transfer; EMAIL = encrypted email; MANUAL = manual entry; API = direct API integration. Determines system configuration in Argus Safety.
attributes.references: ICH E2B(R3); EMA EudraVigilance; FDA FAERS; GVP Module VI

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the pharmacovigilance agreement becomes legally binding and operational obligations commence. Determines the start of mandatory safety data exchange timelines. Formatted as yyyy-MM-dd per model conventions.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; 21 CFR Part 314.81; ICH E2E

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the pharmacovigilance agreement ceases to be in force unless renewed or extended. Nullable for open-ended agreements. Used to trigger renewal workflows and compliance alerts. Formatted as yyyy-MM-dd per model conventions.

attributes.name: governing_law_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction whose laws govern the interpretation and enforcement of this pharmacovigilance agreement. Determines applicable legal framework for dispute resolution.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; GVP Module I; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: icsr_exchange_days
attributes.business_glossary_term: Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) Exchange Timeline (Days)
attributes.description: Number of calendar days within which Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) must be exchanged between the MAH and the counterparty following initial receipt. Typically 7 days for fatal/life-threatening SUSARs and 15 days for other serious cases per GVP Module VI. Drives compliance monitoring and SLA tracking.
attributes.references: GVP Module VI; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA/873138/2011

attributes.name: is_gdpr_dpa_in_place
attributes.business_glossary_term: GDPR Data Processing Agreement (DPA) In Place Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a GDPR-compliant Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is in place with the counterparty covering the personal data exchanged as part of pharmacovigilance activities. Mandatory for EU-based safety data exchange under GDPR Article 28.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 28; GVP Module I; EMA/873138/2011

attributes.name: language
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 or ISO 639-2 language code of the governing language of the pharmacovigilance agreement document (e.g., EN for English, DE for German, FR for French). Relevant for legal interpretation and translation obligations.

attributes.name: last_compliance_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent periodic compliance review conducted for this pharmacovigilance agreement. Used to track review frequency and identify overdue reviews per GVP Module I requirements for oversight of outsourced PV activities.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; GVP Module II; ICH E2E

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this pharmacovigilance agreement record. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per model conventions. Supports change tracking and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GVP Module I; ICH E2E

attributes.name: next_compliance_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the next periodic compliance review of this pharmacovigilance agreement is scheduled. Drives workflow scheduling and resource planning for the PV compliance team.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; GVP Module II; ICH E2E

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, special conditions, derogations, or operational notes relevant to this pharmacovigilance agreement that are not captured in structured fields. Used by PV operations and regulatory affairs teams.

attributes.name: psur_responsible_party
attributes.business_glossary_term: Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) Responsible Party
attributes.description: Designates which party bears primary responsibility for authoring and submitting Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRERs) to regulatory authorities. MAH = Marketing Authorisation Holder; COUNTERPARTY = partner organisation; JOINT = shared responsibility; NOT_APPLICABLE = PSURs not in scope of this agreement.
attributes.references: GVP Module VII; ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR Part 314.81

attributes.name: qppv_contact_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) Contact Name
attributes.description: Name of the Qualified Person Responsible for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) designated by the MAH under this agreement. The QPPV is a mandatory regulatory role under EU GVP legislation responsible for the PV system. Captured for regulatory compliance and audit purposes.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; Directive 2001/83/EC Article 8(3)(ia); EMA/873138/2011

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_responsible_party
attributes.description: Designates which party is responsible for submitting safety reports (ICSRs, SUSARs, PSURs, RMPs) to national competent authorities (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, etc.) for products in scope. Determines accountability in regulatory inspections and audits.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA/873138/2011

attributes.name: renewal_notification_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days before the agreement expiry date that a renewal notification must be issued to the counterparty. Drives automated alerting in the PV agreement management system to prevent lapses in safety data exchange coverage.

attributes.name: rmp_responsible_party
attributes.description: Designates which party is responsible for maintaining and updating the Risk Management Plan (RMP) for products covered under this agreement. Relevant for EU-authorised products where RMP is mandatory per GVP Module V.
attributes.references: GVP Module V; EMA/838713/2011; ICH E2E

attributes.name: signal_management_responsible_party
attributes.description: Designates which party is responsible for signal detection, assessment, and management activities for products covered under this agreement. MAH = Marketing Authorisation Holder; COUNTERPARTY = partner; JOINT = shared; NOT_APPLICABLE = signal management not in scope. Aligns with GVP Module IX obligations.
attributes.references: GVP Module IX; ICH E2E; EMA/873138/2011

attributes.name: susar_exchange_days
attributes.business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Exchange Timeline (Days)
attributes.description: Number of calendar days within which Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) must be exchanged between parties. Typically 7 days for fatal/life-threatening and 15 days for non-fatal/non-life-threatening SUSARs per GVP Module VI and ICH E2D. Separate from general ICSR exchange timelines.
attributes.references: GVP Module VI; ICH E2D; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA/873138/2011

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which the pharmacovigilance agreement was formally terminated prior to its scheduled expiry date. Nullable if the agreement has not been terminated. Triggers wind-down procedures for safety data exchange and regulatory notification obligations.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason for early termination of the pharmacovigilance agreement (e.g., product withdrawal, partnership dissolution, regulatory action, mutual agreement). Required for regulatory audit trail and compliance documentation.

attributes.name: territory_scope
attributes.description: Description of the geographic territories or regulatory jurisdictions covered by this agreement (e.g., specific countries, regions, or global). Determines which national competent authorities are in scope for regulatory reporting obligations under this agreement.
attributes.references: GVP Module I; ICH E2E; EMA/873138/2011

attributes.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier of the executed pharmacovigilance agreement document stored in Veeva Vault (RIM or QualityDocs module). Enables direct navigation to the source document for audit and review purposes. Aligns with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault RIM; GVP Module I

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier of the pharmacovigilance agreement document (e.g., 1.0, 2.1). Incremented upon each amendment or renewal. Supports document lifecycle management in Veeva Vault and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GVP Module I; Veeva Vault RIM

products.name: pass_study
products.description: Post-Authorization Safety Study record tracking PASS commitments and execution. Captures study protocol reference, study type (non-interventional, registry-based, database study, active surveillance), regulatory category (imposed as condition of MA, or voluntary), ENCePP/EU PAS Register number, study objectives, primary safety endpoints, study population, data sources, key milestones (protocol submission, interim reports, final report), and authority approval/assessment status. Tracks PASS commitments arising from RMPs, PSUR recommendations, Article 20/31 referrals, and marketing authorization conditions. Supports both EU (EMA) and US (FDA PMR/PMC) post-marketing study requirements.
products.reference: EU GVP Module VIII PASS / ENCePP

attributes.name: pass_study_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Post-Authorization Safety Study (PASS) record in the pharmacovigilance data lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: EMA Guideline on good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP) Module VIII; 21 CFR Part 505(o)(3)

attributes.name: approval_id
attributes.description: Reference to the marketing authorization under which this PASS commitment was imposed or voluntarily undertaken. Links to the regulatory marketing authorization record.

attributes.name: budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget. Business justification: PASS studies require multi-year budget planning for study execution, interim/final reporting, and potential protocol amendments. Finance allocates dedicated budgets to track planned vs. actual costs,

attributes.name: cro_cmo_engagement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.cro_cmo_engagement. Business justification: Post-authorization safety studies are often conducted by CROs; linking tracks study execution responsibility, governance meeting cadence, and technical agreement compliance. Essential for PASS study v

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pass Study Internal Order Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Post-authorization safety studies are regulatory commitments requiring dedicated budget tracking. Each PASS study is assigned an internal order for cost collection (CRO fees, data analysis, reporting)

attributes.name: medical_heor_study_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to medical.medical_heor_study. Business justification: PASS studies are operationally executed as HEOR studies with real-world evidence collection. Links regulatory commitment tracking (PV) to actual study execution and data collection (Medical Affairs).

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the medicinal product (drug product or biological) that is the subject of this PASS commitment. Links to the master product entity.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E2E Pharmacovigilance Planning

attributes.name: rmp_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Risk Management Plan (RMP) from which this PASS commitment originates, if applicable. Null if the PASS arises from a PSUR recommendation or Article 20/31 referral rather than an RMP.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V (Risk Management Systems); EMA GVP Module VIII

attributes.name: safety_signal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.safety_signal. Business justification: PASS studies are often initiated to address specific safety signals (safety_concern_addressed field). Add safety_signal_id FK (nullable - only when study addresses a specific signal). This links the s

attributes.name: sponsor_legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Post-authorization safety studies are regulatory commitments by specific legal entities to health authorities. Determines study ownership, reporting obligations, and ENCePP registration requirements.

attributes.name: actual_sample_size
attributes.description: Actual number of study subjects or patient records enrolled or included in the final analysis. Compared against planned sample size to assess study feasibility and statistical validity.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

attributes.name: argus_study_code
attributes.description: Study identifier as recorded in the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system. Used for cross-system traceability between the PASS commitment record and safety case data associated with the study.
attributes.references: Oracle Argus Safety; EMA GVP Module VIII; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: authority_approval_status
attributes.description: Status of the regulatory authority's review and approval of the PASS protocol or study design. Reflects the PRAC/CHMP assessment outcome for EU studies or FDA review status for US PMR/PMC studies.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; PRAC assessment procedures; 21 CFR 505(o)(3)

attributes.name: commitment_source
attributes.description: Identifies the regulatory or scientific trigger that originated the PASS commitment. Supports traceability from commitment to regulatory action. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rmp|psur_recommendation|article_20_referral|article_31_referral|ma_condition|fda_pmr|fda_pmc|dsmb_recommendation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; Directive 2010/84/EU; 21 CFR 505(o)(3)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the PASS study record was first created in the pharmacovigilance data product. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VIII.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: data_sources
attributes.description: Description of the data sources to be used in the PASS study, such as electronic health records (EHR), claims databases, disease registries, spontaneous reporting databases, or prospective cohort data. Multiple sources may be listed.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ENCePP Guide on Methodological Standards in Pharmacoepidemiology

attributes.name: encep_register_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: European Network of Centres for Pharmacoepidemiology and Pharmacovigilance (ENCePP) / EU Post-Authorisation Study (EU PAS) Register Number
attributes.description: Official registration number assigned by the ENCePP EU PAS Register upon study registration. Mandatory for non-interventional PASS studies conducted in the EU per GVP Module VIII. Format typically EUPAS followed by numeric digits.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ENCePP Code of Conduct; Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010

attributes.name: final_report_due_date
attributes.description: Regulatory deadline by which the final study report must be submitted to the relevant health authority. Defined in the MA condition, PMR/PMC commitment, or RMP.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; 21 CFR 505(o)(3); RMP commitment schedule

attributes.name: final_report_submission_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the final study report was submitted to the regulatory authority. Null if the final report has not yet been submitted. Used for compliance tracking.

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Countries or regions in which the PASS study is conducted. Comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes (e.g., GBR, DEU, FRA, USA). Determines applicable national competent authority reporting requirements.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ISO 3166-1; ICH E2E

attributes.name: interim_report_due_date
attributes.description: Regulatory deadline by which the interim progress report must be submitted to the relevant health authority. Derived from the MA condition or PMR/PMC commitment schedule.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; 21 CFR 505(o)(3); MA condition schedule

attributes.name: interim_report_submission_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the interim study report was submitted to the regulatory authority. Used to assess compliance with commitment timelines and identify potential delays.

attributes.name: is_interventional
attributes.description: Indicates whether the PASS study involves any intervention in the standard of care (True) or is purely observational/non-interventional (False). Non-interventional studies are subject to GVP Module VIII; interventional studies are subject to GCP and clinical trial regulations.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; Directive 2001/20/EC; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

attributes.name: is_paediatric_study
attributes.description: Indicates whether the PASS study includes or is specifically designed for a paediatric population (True). Triggers additional regulatory requirements under the EU Paediatric Regulation and FDA PREA/BPCA.
attributes.references: EU Paediatric Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006; FDA PREA; FDA BPCA; ICH E11

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the PASS study record. Used for change tracking, audit trail compliance, and data synchronization with source systems such as Veeva Vault RIM and Argus Safety.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; EMA GVP Module VIII; GDPR Article 5 (data accuracy)

attributes.name: lead_authority
attributes.description: Primary regulatory authority responsible for oversight and assessment of this PASS study. Uses standard authority abbreviations. For EU studies, typically EMA/PRAC; for US studies, FDA. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EMA|FDA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|ANSM|BfArM|AIFA|SWISSMEDIC — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E2E; 21 CFR 505(o)(3)

attributes.name: meddra_pt_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
attributes.description: MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code representing the primary safety outcome or adverse event of interest being studied in the PASS. Enables standardized cross-study and cross-authority safety signal comparison.
attributes.references: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; EMA GVP Module VIII

attributes.name: planned_sample_size
attributes.description: Target number of study subjects or patient records to be included in the PASS study as specified in the approved protocol. Used for feasibility assessment and statistical power calculations.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ENCePP Guide on Methodological Standards; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

attributes.name: primary_safety_endpoint
attributes.description: Description of the primary safety outcome measure(s) to be evaluated in the PASS study, such as incidence rate of a specific adverse event, risk of a serious adverse reaction, or mortality endpoint.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E2E; ISPE Guidelines for Pharmacoepidemiology

attributes.name: principal_investigator_name
attributes.description: Full name of the lead scientific investigator responsible for the conduct of the PASS study. Classified as confidential as it identifies a named professional associated with a regulatory commitment.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ENCePP Code of Conduct

attributes.name: protocol_approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the regulatory authority formally approved the PASS study protocol. For EU studies, this is the PRAC/CHMP opinion date. Null if not yet approved.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; PRAC assessment procedures

attributes.name: protocol_reference_number
attributes.description: Document control number or version identifier of the approved study protocol as maintained in the eTMF or Veeva Vault RIM system. Used for traceability between the PASS record and the protocol document.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; Veeva Vault RIM; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: protocol_submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the PASS study protocol was formally submitted to the relevant regulatory authority (e.g., PRAC for EU studies, FDA for US PMR/PMC) for review and approval.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; 21 CFR 505(o)(3); PRAC procedural guidance

attributes.name: protocol_version
attributes.description: Version number of the current approved study protocol (e.g., 1.0, 2.1). Tracks protocol amendments submitted to and approved by the regulatory authority.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: psur_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or submission identifier of the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) or Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) that recommended or triggered this PASS commitment, if applicable.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VII (PSUR); ICH E2C(R2); 21 CFR 314.81

attributes.name: regulatory_category
attributes.description: Indicates whether the PASS is imposed as a condition of the Marketing Authorization (MA) by the regulatory authority or is undertaken voluntarily by the Marketing Authorization Holder (MAH). Distinguishes EU imposed conditions from US FDA Post-Marketing Requirements (PMR) and Post-Marketing Commitments (PMC).
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; 21 CFR 505(o)(3) PMR/PMC; Regulation (EU) No 1235/2010 Article 10a

attributes.name: safety_concern_addressed
attributes.description: Description of the specific identified risk, potential risk, or missing information from the RMP or safety profile that this PASS study is designed to characterize or quantify. Directly links the study to the pharmacovigilance safety concern.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module V (RMP); EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E2E

attributes.name: study_end_date
attributes.description: Actual or planned date on which data collection for the PASS study is completed. Null if the study is ongoing. Used to calculate study duration and track commitment deadlines.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; EU PAS Register; 21 CFR 505(o)(3)

attributes.name: study_number
attributes.description: Sponsor-assigned unique alphanumeric study number used to identify the PASS across internal systems, regulatory submissions, and correspondence with health authorities.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E2E

attributes.name: study_objectives
attributes.description: Narrative description of the primary and secondary scientific objectives of the PASS study, including the specific safety questions to be addressed as defined in the approved study protocol.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E2E Pharmacovigilance Planning

attributes.name: study_population_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the target study population including inclusion/exclusion criteria, therapeutic indication, age groups, and any special populations (e.g., paediatric, elderly, renally impaired) as defined in the study protocol.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E11 (Paediatric Studies); EMA Guideline on studies in special populations

attributes.name: study_start_date
attributes.description: Actual or planned date on which data collection or patient enrolment for the PASS study commenced. Key milestone for regulatory reporting and commitment tracking.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; EU PAS Register; 21 CFR 505(o)(3)

attributes.name: study_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the PASS study. Tracks progression from planning through protocol submission, execution, reporting, and completion or early termination. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planned|protocol_submitted|ongoing|interim_report_submitted|final_report_submitted|completed|terminated|suspended — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; 21 CFR 314.81; EU PAS Register status taxonomy

attributes.name: study_title
attributes.description: Full descriptive title of the Post-Authorization Safety Study as registered in the study protocol and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; EU PAS Register

attributes.name: study_type
attributes.description: Methodological classification of the PASS study design. Determines applicable regulatory requirements and reporting obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: non_interventional|registry_based|database_study|active_surveillance|cohort|case_control|cross_sectional — promote to reference product]
