attributes.references: EMA GVP Module VIII; ICH E2E; ISPE Guidelines for Pharmacoepidemiology Studies

products.name: pv_agreement_product_scope
products.description: This association product represents the Coverage relationship between pv_agreement and pv_product. It captures the specific safety data exchange obligations, reporting timelines, and responsible party designations that apply when a particular product falls under a particular pharmacovigilance agreement. Each record links one pv_agreement to one pv_product with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship - the same agreement may have different exchange timelines or responsible parties for different products, and the same product may be governed by multiple agreements with different counterparties across different territories.. Existence Justification: In pharmacovigilance operations, a single PV agreement routinely covers multiple products (e.g., a CRO agreement covering an entire therapeutic portfolio), and a single product is frequently governed by multiple agreements simultaneously (e.g., different co-promotion agreements in different territories, or a manufacturing agreement plus a licensing agreement). The business actively manages this relationship through agreement negotiation, product scope amendments, and compliance monitoring - tracking which products are covered under which agreements, with what reporting timelines, and which party is responsible for what activities.

attributes.name: pv_agreement_product_scope_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this agreement-product coverage record. Primary key.

attributes.name: pv_agreement_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pv Agreement Product Scope - Pv Agreement Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the pharmacovigilance agreement that governs safety data exchange obligations for this product

attributes.name: pv_product_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pv Agreement Product Scope - Pv Product Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the PV product master record that is covered under this agreement

attributes.name: amendment_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific agreement amendment that added, modified, or removed this product from scope. Supports audit trail and compliance verification.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this product-agreement scope record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and compliance monitoring.

attributes.name: data_exchange_format
attributes.description: Technical format used for exchanging Individual Case Safety Reports for this product under this agreement. May vary by product based on system capabilities or regulatory requirements in different territories.

attributes.name: data_exchange_method
attributes.description: Technical transmission method used for exchanging safety data for this product between parties. May differ by product based on data volume or system integration maturity.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this product came into scope under this specific agreement. May differ from the agreement's overall effective date if products are added via amendment.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this product exits scope under this agreement. May differ from the agreement's overall expiry date if products are removed via amendment or transferred to another agreement.

attributes.name: icsr_exchange_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days within which Individual Case Safety Reports for this product must be exchanged between parties under this agreement. May vary by product based on risk profile or regulatory requirements.

attributes.name: product_inclusion_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this product's inclusion in the agreement scope. ACTIVE = currently covered, PENDING = negotiated but not yet effective, SUSPENDED = temporarily out of scope, TERMINATED = permanently removed from scope.

attributes.name: product_scope
attributes.description: Free-text or structured description of the medicinal products (by INN, brand name, or development code) covered under this pharmacovigilance agreement. Defines the boundary of safety data exchange obligations. May reference specific NDC codes, ATC classifications, or internal product identifiers. [Moved from pv_agreement: This free-text field in pv_agreement describes which products are covered, but the structured representation of product coverage belongs in the association. The agreement-level attribute becomes redundant once the association is properly modeled with explicit product links.]
attributes.references: GVP Module I; ICH E2E; 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: psur_responsible_party
attributes.description: Designates which party bears primary responsibility for authoring and submitting Periodic Safety Update Reports for this product under this agreement. May differ by product based on marketing authorization holder status.

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_responsible_party
attributes.description: Designates which party is responsible for submitting safety reports (ICSRs, SUSARs, PSURs) to regulatory authorities for this product under this agreement. Depends on marketing authorization holder status per territory.

attributes.name: rmp_responsible_party
attributes.description: Designates which party is responsible for maintaining and updating the Risk Management Plan for this product under this agreement. Particularly important for products with REMS or additional risk minimization measures.

attributes.name: signal_management_responsible_party
attributes.description: Designates which party is responsible for signal detection, assessment, and management activities for this product under this agreement. Critical for high-risk products or those with complex safety profiles.

attributes.name: susar_exchange_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days within which Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions for this product must be exchanged under this agreement. Typically more stringent than ICSR timelines due to regulatory urgency.

attributes.name: territory_scope
attributes.description: Geographic territories or regulatory jurisdictions covered for this specific product under this agreement. May be a subset of the agreement's overall territory scope - e.g., an agreement may cover multiple territories but this product may only be marketed in certain regions.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this product-agreement scope record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking and compliance verification.

products.name: product_listedness
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory listedness determination between a PV product and its approved therapeutic indications. It captures jurisdiction-specific approval metadata, label claim text, and listedness status used for SUSAR classification and causality assessment in pharmacovigilance case processing. Each record links one pv_product to one product_indication with regulatory approval attributes that exist only in the context of this specific product-indication pairing per jurisdiction.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical pharmacovigilance operations, a single PV product (e.g., ibuprofen 200mg tablet) has multiple approved therapeutic indications across different jurisdictions (pain relief, fever reduction, inflammation), and each indication can apply to multiple PV products (same API in different formulations or strengths). The business actively manages listedness determination records per product-indication-jurisdiction combination for SUSAR classification during adverse event case processing, with each record carrying jurisdiction-specific approval dates, label claim text, and regulatory metadata that belong to neither the product nor the indication alone.

attributes.name: product_listedness_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the product-indication listedness record. Primary key.

attributes.name: indication_id

products.name: rmp_review
products.description: This association product represents the expert review relationship between Risk Management Plans (RMPs) and Healthcare Professionals (HCPs). It captures the formal review process where qualified HCPs (medical reviewers, therapeutic area specialists, external consultants) evaluate RMP documents for regulatory compliance, scientific accuracy, and clinical appropriateness. Each record links one RMP version to one reviewing HCP with attributes documenting the review scope, findings, and approval status required for regulatory audit trails and quality assurance.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical regulatory operations, Risk Management Plans (RMPs) undergo formal expert review by multiple qualified healthcare professionals serving in different roles (medical reviewers, therapeutic area specialists, external consultants). Each RMP version requires review by multiple HCPs with relevant expertise, and each HCP reviews multiple RMPs throughout their engagement with the organization. The review process generates relationship-specific data (review dates, reviewer roles, sections reviewed, comments, approval status) that belongs to neither the RMP nor the HCP alone, but to the specific review event.

products.name: signal_indication_assessment
products.description: This association product represents the indication-specific safety signal assessment between safety_signal and product_indication. It captures the stratified analysis of how a particular safety signal manifests differently across approved or investigational indications for the same medicinal product. Each record links one safety signal to one product indication with indication-specific signal strength metrics, case distribution, causality assessment, and regulatory action recommendations (label changes, restrictions, contraindications) required for GVP Module IX signal validation and PRAC reporting. Supports the pharmacovigilance requirement that signal validation must be performed with indication-level stratification, as the same adverse event may have different risk profiles, causality, and benefit-risk balance across different therapeutic uses of the product.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical pharmacovigilance operations, a single safety signal (e.g., hepatotoxicity) must be assessed separately for each approved or investigational indication of a medicinal product, because the same adverse event may have different risk profiles, causality, case distributions, and benefit-risk implications across different therapeutic uses. Conversely, each product indication accumulates multiple concurrent safety signals over its lifecycle that require ongoing monitoring and indication-specific regulatory action decisions. This is an operational M:N relationship mandated by GVP Module IX signal validation requirements.

attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this indication-specific signal assessment requires notification to the PRAC rapporteur per EMA pharmacovigilance requirements.

attributes.name: regulatory_action_required
attributes.description: Type of regulatory action recommended for this signal-indication combination. Values: none, label_update, indication_restriction, indication_withdrawal, prac_referral, urgent_safety_restriction.

attributes.description: Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) calculated specifically for this signal-indication combination using indication-stratified case data.

products.name: signal_expert_consultation
products.description: This association product represents the expert consultation engagement between safety signals and healthcare professional subject matter experts. It captures the formal involvement of HCP experts (KOLs, advisory board members, external consultants) in safety signal evaluation and validation activities. Each record links one safety signal to one HCP expert with consultation-specific attributes including expert opinion, causality assessment, risk evaluation contribution, meeting participation details, and compensation tracking required for regulatory documentation per GVP Module IX and transparency reporting requirements.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical safety signal management, a single safety signal is routinely evaluated by multiple HCP experts (KOLs, advisory board members, therapeutic area specialists) to obtain diverse clinical perspectives for regulatory validation per GVP Module IX requirements. Conversely, each HCP expert consultant evaluates multiple safety signals across different therapeutic areas and products throughout their engagement with the pharmaceutical company. The business actively manages these consultation engagements as discrete operational records with consultation dates, expert opinions, causality assessments, meeting types, and honorarium tracking required for regulatory submissions and transparency reporting.

attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records and Electronic Signatures

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current stage in the drug substance development and commercial lifecycle, from discovery through discontinuation.

attributes.name: moa_summary
attributes.description: High-level summary of the drug substance's mechanism of action, describing how it produces its pharmacological effect at the molecular or cellular level.

attributes.name: molecular_formula
attributes.description: Chemical formula representing the number and type of atoms in one molecule of the drug substance (e.g., C8H9NO2).
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: molecular_weight
attributes.description: Molecular weight of the drug substance expressed in grams per mole (g/mol), calculated from the molecular formula.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: nce_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the drug substance has been designated as a New Chemical Entity by regulatory authorities, qualifying for extended data exclusivity periods.

attributes.name: orphan_drug_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the drug substance has received orphan drug designation for treatment of rare diseases affecting fewer than 200,000 patients.

attributes.name: particle_size_specification
attributes.description: Defined particle size distribution range or specification for the drug substance, critical for dissolution and bioavailability (e.g., D50 < 10 microns).
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: pharmacopoeial_monograph
attributes.description: Reference to the official pharmacopoeial monograph (USP, EP, JP, or other) that defines quality standards for the drug substance.

attributes.name: physical_form
attributes.description: Physical state or form of the drug substance at standard conditions (e.g., crystalline solid, liquid, lyophilized powder).
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: polymorphic_form
attributes.description: Specific crystalline or amorphous form of the drug substance, identifying the polymorph used in manufacturing (e.g., Form I, Form II, anhydrous, hydrate).
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: regulatory_status
attributes.description: Summary of regulatory approval status across major markets (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.), indicating where the drug substance has received marketing authorization.

attributes.name: retest_period_months
attributes.description: Time period in months after which the drug substance should be re-examined to ensure it still meets specifications before use in manufacturing.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2) Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products

attributes.name: salt_form
attributes.description: Chemical salt form of the drug substance if applicable (e.g., hydrochloride, sodium, sulfate), or 'free base' or 'free acid' if not a salt.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: solubility_profile
attributes.description: Aqueous solubility characteristics of the drug substance across physiologically relevant pH ranges, critical for formulation development and bioavailability.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: specification_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the current quality specification document defining acceptance criteria for the drug substance.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: stability_profile
attributes.description: Summary of the drug substance's stability characteristics under various storage conditions, including temperature and humidity sensitivity.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2) Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products

attributes.name: stereochemistry
attributes.description: Three-dimensional spatial arrangement of atoms in the drug substance molecule, including chirality and isomeric configuration (e.g., R/S designation, E/Z configuration).
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: storage_conditions
attributes.description: Recommended storage conditions for the drug substance to maintain quality and stability (e.g., store at 2-8°C, protect from light, store under inert atmosphere).
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2) Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products

attributes.name: synthesis_route_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the chemical synthesis route or manufacturing process used to produce the drug substance, enabling change control and traceability.
attributes.references: ICH Q7 Good Manufacturing Practice Guide for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients

attributes.name: therapeutic_class
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic classification of the drug substance based on its clinical use and pharmacological properties.
attributes.references: WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) Classification System

attributes.name: usan_name
attributes.description: United States Adopted Name assigned by the USAN Council, representing the official generic name used in the United States for the drug substance.

products.name: drug_product
products.description: Master record for the finished drug product (DP) or finished dosage form (FDF) derived from one or more drug substances. Captures dosage form (tablet, capsule, injection, etc.), route of administration, strength, formulation type, reference listed drug (RLD) linkage, shelf life, storage conditions, and CMC summary. Bridges the DS/DP hierarchy and is referenced by manufacturing batch records, regulatory submissions, and commercial SKUs.
products.reference: ICH Q8 Drug Product Definition / CMC

attributes.name: drug_product_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the finished drug product record. Primary key for the drug product entity.
attributes.references: ICH M4 Quality - Common Technical Document

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Product development lead for formulation design, process development, scale-up, and tech transfer. Core R&D accountability for CMC sections of regulatory submissions and manufacturing readiness. Essen

Essential for regulatory completeness, supplier qualification, and CMC documentation cross-referencing.

attributes.name: drug_substance_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) or drug substance used in this drug product formulation.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.ndc_code. Business justification: Drug products assigned NDC codes for US regulatory compliance (FDA establishment registration), supply chain tracking (serialization), reimbursement (billing). Replaces denormalized ndc_code string wi

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Drug products require patent coverage tracking for lifecycle management, LOE planning, Orange Book listings, and generic defense strategy. Essential for regulatory submissions and commercial planning.

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.plant. Business justification: Drug product manufacturing plant assignment for production planning, batch genealogy, GMP site compliance, regulatory site registration. Complements existing manufacturing_site_id (manufacturing domai

attributes.name: rld_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the RLD drug product if this product is a generic or biosimilar requiring bioequivalence demonstration.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book, FDA Generic Drug Approval Process

attributes.name: therapeutic_area_id

attributes.name: unit_of_measure_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.unit_of_measure. Replaces denormalized strength_unit with FK to UOM master for s

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the drug product received initial regulatory approval from the primary health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA).
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book, EMA Product Register

attributes.name: black_box_warning_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the drug product labeling includes a black box warning (boxed warning) for serious or life-threatening risks.

attributes.name: cmc_summary
attributes.description: High-level summary of the chemistry, manufacturing, and controls information for the drug product, including formulation composition and manufacturing process overview.
attributes.references: ICH M4 Quality - CMC Section, FDA eCTD Module 3

attributes.name: controlled_substance_schedule
attributes.description: The DEA controlled substance schedule classification if the drug product contains a controlled substance (Schedule I through V), or non-controlled if not applicable.
attributes.references: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308, Controlled Substances Act

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this drug product record was first created in the system.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: discontinuation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the drug product was discontinued or withdrawn from the market, if applicable.
attributes.references: FDA Drug Shortages Database, EMA Product Discontinuation

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: The physical form in which the drug product is manufactured and administered (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, solution, suspension, cream, ointment, transdermal patch). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|injection|solution|suspension|cream|ointment|patch — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Dosage Form Terminology, ICH M4 Quality

attributes.name: excipients
attributes.description: List of inactive ingredients (excipients) used in the drug product formulation, such as binders, fillers, preservatives, and colorants.
attributes.references: FDA Inactive Ingredient Database, ICH Q3C Impurities

attributes.name: formulation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the drug product formulation based on release characteristics (e.g., immediate release, extended release, delayed release, modified release, controlled release).
attributes.references: FDA Dissolution Testing Guidance, ICH Q6A

attributes.name: launch_date
attributes.description: The date on which the drug product was first made commercially available in the market.
attributes.references: Commercial Operations Data, Product Launch Plan

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle stage of the drug product (e.g., development, approved, marketed, discontinued, withdrawn from market).
attributes.references: FDA Product Lifecycle Management, EMA Product Status

attributes.name: moa
attributes.description: Description of the biochemical or physiological mechanism by which the drug product exerts its therapeutic effect.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this drug product record was last modified or updated.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: package_size
attributes.description: The quantity of dosage units per package (e.g., 30 tablets, 100 mL, 10 vials).
attributes.references: FDA Labeling Requirements, SAP MM Packaging Data

attributes.name: packaging_type
attributes.description: The primary packaging configuration for the drug product (e.g., bottle, blister pack, vial, ampule, prefilled syringe, tube).
attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability, FDA Container Closure Systems

attributes.name: patent_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the primary patent protection for the drug product expires, opening the market to generic competition.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book Patent Information, Company IP Portfolio

attributes.name: prescription_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the drug product requires a prescription (Rx), is available over-the-counter (OTC), or is behind-the-counter.

attributes.name: product_code
attributes.description: Internal product code assigned to the drug product for identification across manufacturing, regulatory, and commercial systems. Typically alphanumeric and unique within the organization.

attributes.name: product_name
attributes.description: The commercial or proprietary name of the drug product as it appears on labeling and marketing materials.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book, EMA Product Information

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: Classification of the drug product by regulatory and commercial category (e.g., branded, generic, biosimilar, vaccine, over-the-counter, medical device combination product).
attributes.references: FDA Product Classification, EMA Product Categories

attributes.name: qbd_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the drug product was developed using Quality by Design principles as defined by ICH Q8.
attributes.references: ICH Q8 Pharmaceutical Development, FDA QbD Guidance

attributes.name: rems_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the drug product is subject to a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy program required by the FDA to ensure safe use.

attributes.name: rld_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this drug product is designated as a Reference Listed Drug by the FDA for bioequivalence studies.

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: The path by which the drug product is administered to the patient (e.g., oral, intravenous, intramuscular, subcutaneous, topical, transdermal).
attributes.references: FDA Route of Administration Terminology, ICH E2B

attributes.name: shelf_life_months
attributes.description: The approved shelf life of the drug product from date of manufacture, expressed in months, under specified storage conditions.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability Testing, FDA Stability Guidance

attributes.name: storage_conditions
attributes.description: The required storage conditions for the drug product to maintain stability and quality (e.g., store at 2-8°C, protect from light, store below 25°C).
attributes.references: ICH Q1A Stability Testing, FDA Labeling Requirements

attributes.name: strength
attributes.description: The amount of active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) per unit of dosage form, expressed with unit of measure (e.g., 500 mg, 10 mg/mL, 5%).
attributes.references: ICH Q6A Specifications, FDA Labeling Requirements

attributes.name: strength_value
attributes.description: Numeric value of the active pharmaceutical ingredient strength for computational and analytical purposes.

attributes.name: usan
attributes.description: The United States Adopted Name for the active pharmaceutical ingredient, assigned by the USAN Council.

products.name: formulation
products.description: Detailed formulation record specifying the qualitative and quantitative composition (Q1/Q2) of a drug product, including all active and inactive ingredients, their pharmacopoeial grades, functional roles, and quantities per unit dose and per batch. Tracks formulation version history, Quality by Design (QbD) design space parameters, critical process parameters (CPP), and critical quality attributes (CQA). Supports CMC Module 3 documentation, scale-up, and technology transfer.
products.reference: ICH Q8 Pharmaceutical Development / CMC Section 3.2.P.1

attributes.name: formulation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the formulation record. Primary key for the formulation entity.

attributes.name: development_plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.plant. Business justification: Formulation development site tracking for technology transfer documentation, scale-up studies, process validation, site-specific design space. Critical for CMC regulatory submissions (CTD Module 3), m

attributes.name: drug_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent drug product that this formulation defines. Links to the finished dosage form (FDF) in the product master catalog.
attributes.references: ICH M4 Quality (Module 3) - Drug Product Specification

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Formulation development projects are tracked via internal orders for cost accumulation, budget control, and capitalization eligibility determination. This link enables pharmaceutical companies to trac

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Formulations have distinct patent protection (composition, process). Essential for lifecycle management, line extension strategy, and generic defense through formulation patents.

attributes.name: scientist_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Formulation scientist responsible for QbD design space, CPP/CQA definition, stability strategy, and regulatory documentation. Direct accountability for formulation performance and regulatory defense.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Unit Dose Strength Uom Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.unit_of_measure. Business justification: Formulation unit dose strength UOM for manufacturing instructions (batch records), specifications (release criteria), regulatory filings. Replaces denormalized unit_dose_strength_uom with FK to UOM ma

attributes.name: api_count
attributes.description: Number of distinct active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) in the formulation. Most formulations have 1 API; combination products have 2 or more.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance - Fixed Combination Drug Products

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who approved this formulation. Typically a quality assurance manager or regulatory affairs lead.
attributes.references: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System - Management Responsibilities

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date when this formulation was formally approved for use in manufacturing or clinical trials. Represents a key lifecycle milestone.
attributes.references: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System - Change Control

attributes.name: batch_size_target
attributes.description: Planned or standard batch size for manufacturing this formulation, expressed in the unit specified by batch_size_uom. Used for scale-up calculations and manufacturing planning.
attributes.references: ICH Q8 Pharmaceutical Development - Scale-Up and Post-Approval Changes

attributes.name: batch_size_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the batch size (e.g., kg for bulk powder, L for liquid, units for finished dosage forms). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: kg|L|units|tablets|capsules|vials|syringes — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH Q7 Good Manufacturing Practice for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients

attributes.name: bioequivalence_reference
attributes.description: Reference to bioequivalence or bioavailability studies conducted for this formulation, particularly relevant for generic formulations or formulation changes requiring bridging studies.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance - Bioavailability and Bioequivalence Studies

attributes.name: composition_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the formulation composition, including all active and inactive ingredients, their roles, and quantities. Supports CMC Module 3 documentation and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH M4 Quality (Module 3.2.P.1) - Description and Composition of the Drug Product

attributes.name: cpp_summary
attributes.description: Summary of critical process parameters (CPPs) identified for this formulation. CPPs are process parameters whose variability has an impact on a critical quality attribute (CQA) and therefore should be monitored or controlled.
attributes.references: ICH Q8(R2) Pharmaceutical Development - Critical Process Parameters

attributes.name: cqa_summary
attributes.description: Summary of critical quality attributes (CQAs) for this formulation. CQAs are physical, chemical, biological, or microbiological properties that should be within an appropriate limit, range, or distribution to ensure the desired product quality.
attributes.references: ICH Q8(R2) Pharmaceutical Development - Critical Quality Attributes

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Date when this formulation record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for formulation lifecycle management.

attributes.name: design_space_description
attributes.description: Textual summary of the QbD design space, including key input variables, process parameters, and their acceptable ranges. References supporting studies and risk assessments.
attributes.references: ICH Q8(R2) Pharmaceutical Development - Design Space

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: Physical form in which the drug product is manufactured and administered (e.g., tablet, capsule, injectable solution). Aligns with FDA and EMA dosage form terminologies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|solution|suspension|emulsion|cream|ointment|gel|patch|injection|lyophilized_powder|suppository — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Data Standards Manual - Dosage Form Terminology

attributes.name: ectd_module_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD) Module Reference
attributes.description: Specific eCTD module and section reference where this formulation is documented (e.g., '3.2.P.1', '3.2.P.3.3'). Facilitates traceability to regulatory documentation.

attributes.name: excipient_count
attributes.description: Number of distinct inactive ingredients (excipients) in the formulation. Includes fillers, binders, disintegrants, lubricants, coatings, preservatives, and other functional excipients.

attributes.name: formulation_code
attributes.description: Business identifier for the formulation, used across manufacturing, regulatory, and quality systems. Typically follows internal coding conventions for Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) documentation.
attributes.references: ICH Q8 Pharmaceutical Development - QbD Principles

attributes.name: formulation_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or title of the formulation, often including the drug product name, strength, and dosage form (e.g., 'Compound XYZ 50mg Tablet Formulation').

attributes.name: formulation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the formulation. Tracks progression from early development through commercial manufacturing and potential discontinuation.
attributes.references: ICH Q8 Pharmaceutical Development - Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: formulation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the formulation based on its release mechanism and pharmacokinetic profile. Critical for regulatory submissions and manufacturing process design.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance for Industry - Modified Release Solid Oral Dosage Forms

attributes.name: gmp_grade_required
attributes.description: Indicates the GMP grade required for manufacturing this formulation: clinical (for investigational products), commercial (for marketed products), or both (for formulations used in both contexts).
attributes.references: ICH Q7 GMP for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who last modified this formulation record. Part of audit trail for compliance and quality management.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Date when this formulation record was last modified. Tracks changes to formulation specifications, status, or metadata.

attributes.name: manufacturing_process_type
attributes.description: Primary manufacturing process or technology used to produce this formulation (e.g., wet granulation for tablets, aseptic filling for injectables). Influences equipment selection and process validation strategy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: wet_granulation|dry_granulation|direct_compression|coating|lyophilization|aseptic_filling|emulsification|spray_drying — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH Q8 Pharmaceutical Development - Manufacturing Process

attributes.name: patent_protected
attributes.description: Indicates whether this formulation is covered by one or more patents, providing intellectual property protection. Links to patent records in the intellectual property domain.

attributes.name: pharmacopoeial_standard
attributes.description: Primary pharmacopoeial standard to which this formulation conforms (USP = United States Pharmacopeia, EP = European Pharmacopoeia, JP = Japanese Pharmacopoeia, BP = British Pharmacopoeia, IP = Indian Pharmacopoeia, ChP = Chinese Pharmacopoeia).

attributes.name: qbd_design_space_defined
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality by Design (QbD) Design Space Defined Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Quality by Design (QbD) design space has been established for this formulation, defining the multidimensional combination of input variables and process parameters that ensure quality.
attributes.references: ICH Q8(R2) Pharmaceutical Development - Design Space

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory submission (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA) in which this formulation was described or approved. Links formulation records to regulatory dossiers in RIMS.
attributes.references: ICH M4 Common Technical Document - Module 3 Quality

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Intended pathway by which the drug product is administered to the patient. Critical for formulation design and regulatory classification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|intramuscular|subcutaneous|topical|transdermal|inhalation|ophthalmic|otic|rectal|vaginal — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Data Standards Manual - Route of Administration

attributes.name: scale_up_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of commercial batch size to development batch size, indicating the degree of scale-up achieved. Used to assess scale-up risk and process robustness.

attributes.name: shelf_life_months
attributes.description: Approved or proposed shelf life for the formulation in months, based on stability data. Defines the period during which the product remains within specifications under defined storage conditions.

attributes.name: stability_profile_summary
attributes.description: Summary of stability characteristics for this formulation, including storage conditions, shelf life, and key degradation pathways. References formal stability studies conducted per ICH Q1A guidelines.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2) Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products

attributes.name: storage_conditions
attributes.description: Recommended storage conditions for the formulation (e.g., 'Store at 2-8°C', 'Store below 25°C', 'Protect from light'). Critical for maintaining product quality and stability.
attributes.references: ICH Q1A(R2) Stability Testing - Storage Conditions

attributes.name: technology_transfer_status
attributes.description: Status of technology transfer activities for this formulation, tracking the transfer of manufacturing knowledge and processes from development to commercial manufacturing sites or to CMOs/CDMOs.

attributes.name: unit_dose_strength
attributes.description: Quantity of active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) per unit dose (e.g., 50 mg per tablet, 100 mg/mL for solution). Expressed in the unit specified by unit_dose_strength_uom.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for the formulation, tracking iterative changes during development, scale-up, and optimization. Follows semantic versioning (e.g., 1.0, 1.1, 2.0).
attributes.references: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System - Change Management

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who created this formulation record. Part of audit trail for compliance and quality management.
