domains.name: intellectual
domains.description: SSOT for intellectual property portfolio including patents (NCE, NBE, formulations, processes), patent expiry timelines, exclusivity periods (orphan drug, data exclusivity, pediatric), trademark registrations, drug master files, freedom-to-operate analyses, and licensing agreements. Supports lifecycle management decisions, generic/biosimilar entry defense strategies, and coordination with legal counsel on patent litigation.
domains.references: USPTO / EPO / WIPO Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)

products.name: patent
products.description: Core master record for all pharmaceutical patents owned or licensed by the company. Captures patent number, title, filing/grant/expiry dates, patent family reference, jurisdiction, patent type (composition of matter, method of use, formulation, process, polymorph, salt form), covered compound (INN/USAN), therapeutic area, legal status, and assignee. Also serves as the anchor for trade secrets and know-how records via asset classification. SSOT for the IP portfolio — anchors lifecycle management, LOE planning, litigation defense, and generic/biosimilar entry strategy.

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each patent record in the IP portfolio. Primary key for the patent master data product.

attributes.name: country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Patents are jurisdiction-specific; essential for freedom-to-operate analysis, market entry planning, and regulatory strategy in global pharmaceutical operations.

attributes.name: lead_inventor_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical IP operations require tracking lead inventors as employees for invention assignment verification, inventor compensation calculations, and regulatory inspection readiness. Replaces denor

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Patents are owned by legal entities; critical for IP ownership tracking, portfolio valuation, M&A due diligence, and financial reporting of intangible assets.

attributes.name: masterdata_atc_classification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Patents are classified by therapeutic area; essential for portfolio analysis, competitive benchmarking, and therapeutic area-specific IP strategy.

attributes.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Patents incur maintenance costs allocated to cost centers; required for IP budget management, financial planning, and cost allocation in pharmaceutical R&D.

attributes.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: Patents claim specific INNs; essential for patent landscaping, FTO analysis, and molecule-patent linkage in pharmaceutical IP management.

attributes.name: masterdata_profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: Patents are assigned to therapeutic areas/product lines represented by profit centers; critical for portfolio valuation, segment reporting, and strategic IP management.

attributes.name: material_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.material. Business justification: Patents cover specific materials (APIs, formulations); essential for product development, supply chain planning, and patent-product linkage in pharmaceutical operations.

attributes.name: patent_family_id
attributes.description: Identifier grouping all related patent applications and grants that share a common priority filing across multiple jurisdictions. Used to manage global IP portfolio coherence and track international prosecution strategy.
attributes.references: WIPO PCT; EPO DOCDB Patent Family Definition

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.plant. Business justification: Manufacturing process patents are associated with specific plants; required for technology transfer, GMP compliance, and site-specific IP protection.

attributes.name: adjusted_expiry_date
attributes.description: Final effective expiry date after applying all patent term adjustments (PTA), patent term extensions (PTE) for regulatory review delays, and supplementary protection certificates (SPC). Represents the true end of patent exclusivity for commercial planning purposes.

attributes.name: annuity_paid_through_date
attributes.description: Date through which patent annuity (maintenance) fees have been paid, confirming the patent is in good standing. Used by IP operations to monitor fee payment compliance and prevent unintentional lapse.

attributes.name: asset_classification
attributes.description: Broader intellectual property asset classification for this record. Primarily 'patent' for this product, but also supports trade secrets and know-how records anchored to the patent master per the SSOT design. Enables unified IP portfolio reporting across asset types.
attributes.references: Internal IP Policy; TRIPS Agreement Article 39; 18 U.S.C. § 1839 (Defend Trade Secrets Act)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this patent record was first created in the IP portfolio system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.

attributes.name: data_exclusivity_expiry
attributes.description: Date on which regulatory data exclusivity (RDE) expires, preventing generic/biosimilar applicants from referencing the originator's clinical data. In the US, NCEs receive 5 years; biologics receive 12 years under BPCIA. In the EU, the 8+2+1 rule applies. Complements patent expiry in LOE planning.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Calculated or legally determined date on which patent protection lapses, typically 20 years from the filing date subject to patent term adjustments (PTA), patent term extensions (PTE), and supplementary protection certificates (SPC). The primary LOE (Loss of Exclusivity) planning anchor for lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry strategy.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 154(b); EPC Article 63; EU Regulation 469/2009 (SPC); FDA 21 CFR § 314.53

attributes.name: external_counsel_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier or name of the external law firm or patent attorney managing prosecution, maintenance, or litigation for this patent. Supports coordination between in-house IP team and outside counsel.
attributes.references: Internal IP Policy; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the patent application was formally submitted to the patent office. Establishes the priority date for novelty assessment and is the anchor for calculating patent term and exclusivity periods.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 111; EPC Article 80; WIPO PCT Rule 20

attributes.name: fto_clearance_status
attributes.description: Current freedom-to-operate (FTO) analysis status for this patent relative to the company's commercial activities. Cleared indicates no infringement risk identified; at_risk indicates potential third-party patent conflict; blocked indicates active infringement concern; under_review indicates ongoing FTO analysis. Critical for launch readiness and litigation risk management.

attributes.name: grant_date
attributes.description: Date on which the patent was officially granted by the patent office, conferring enforceable rights to the assignee. Null for applications still under examination. Used to calculate patent term adjustments (PTA) and supplementary protection certificate (SPC) eligibility.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 154; EPC Article 97; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: legal_status
attributes.description: Current legal standing of the patent in its jurisdiction lifecycle. Pending indicates application under examination; granted indicates active protection; abandoned/lapsed indicates failure to prosecute or maintain; opposed indicates third-party challenge; litigated indicates active court proceedings. Drives LOE planning and portfolio valuation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|granted|abandoned|expired|lapsed|opposed|litigated — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: USPTO PAIR; EPO Register; 35 U.S.C. § 154; EPC Article 63

attributes.name: litigation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this patent is currently subject to active litigation, including Paragraph IV ANDA challenges, inter partes review (IPR), post-grant review (PGR), or district court infringement proceedings. Triggers escalated monitoring and legal counsel coordination.

attributes.name: maintenance_fee_due_date
attributes.description: Next scheduled date by which maintenance (annuity) fees must be paid to the patent office to keep the patent in force. Failure to pay results in lapse of patent rights. Critical for IP portfolio maintenance operations.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPC Rule 51; USPTO Fee Schedule

attributes.name: orange_book_listed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this patent is listed in the FDA Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations (Orange Book). Orange Book listing triggers Paragraph IV certification obligations for ANDA filers and is central to Hatch-Waxman litigation strategy.
attributes.references: 21 CFR § 314.53; FDA Orange Book; Hatch-Waxman Act (21 U.S.C. § 355)

attributes.name: orphan_drug_exclusivity_expiry
attributes.description: Date on which orphan drug market exclusivity expires, granting 7 years (US) or 10 years (EU) of market protection for drugs treating rare diseases. Distinct from patent expiry and critical for rare disease portfolio lifecycle planning.
attributes.references: Orphan Drug Act (21 U.S.C. § 360bb); EU Regulation 141/2000; FDA ODE; EMA COMP

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Classification of the company's relationship to the patent. Owned indicates full proprietary ownership; licensed_in indicates rights acquired from a third party; licensed_out indicates rights granted to a third party; co_owned indicates joint ownership; assigned indicates transfer of ownership has occurred.

attributes.name: patent_number
attributes.description: Officially assigned patent number issued by the relevant patent office (e.g., USPTO, EPO, WIPO). Serves as the primary external business identifier for the patent. Format varies by jurisdiction (e.g., US10123456B2, EP3456789A1).

attributes.name: patent_type
attributes.description: Classification of the patent by the nature of the invention. Composition of matter covers the active molecule (NCE/NBE); method of use covers therapeutic indications; formulation covers drug product design; process covers manufacturing methods; polymorph and salt form cover physical-chemical variants. Critical for LOE (Loss of Exclusivity) strategy and generic/biosimilar entry defense.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 101; ICH Q6A; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: pediatric_exclusivity_expiry
attributes.description: Date on which the 6-month pediatric exclusivity extension expires, granted by the FDA under the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) for conducting pediatric studies. Attaches to and extends both patent and data exclusivity periods.
attributes.references: Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA); 21 U.S.C. § 355a; FDA

attributes.name: priority_date
attributes.description: Earliest claimed priority date, typically the date of the first-filed application in the patent family (provisional or national phase). Determines prior art cutoff and is critical for freedom-to-operate (FTO) analyses and validity challenges.
attributes.references: Paris Convention Article 4; WIPO PCT; 35 U.S.C. § 119

attributes.name: prosecution_status
attributes.description: Detailed status of the patent application within the prosecution workflow at the patent office. Provides granular tracking beyond legal_status for IP counsel and patent attorneys managing active applications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: filed|examination|office_action|response_pending|allowed|granted|abandoned — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: USPTO PAIR; EPO Online Filing; MPEP

attributes.name: purple_book_listed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this patent is listed in the FDA Purple Book (List of Licensed Biological Products). Relevant for biologics and biosimilar entry defense under the Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act (BPCIA).

attributes.name: spc_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) expires, representing the final end of patent-based market exclusivity in the relevant EU jurisdiction. Null if no SPC applies.

attributes.name: spc_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) granted in EU member states to extend patent protection beyond the standard 20-year term to compensate for regulatory review time. Null if no SPC has been granted.

attributes.name: term_adjustment_days
attributes.description: Number of days added to the patent term by the USPTO as Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) to compensate for delays in patent prosecution caused by the USPTO. Directly impacts the effective expiry date calculation.

attributes.name: term_extension_days
attributes.description: Number of days added to the patent term under 35 U.S.C. § 156 (US) to compensate for time lost during FDA regulatory review of the drug product. Maximum extension is 5 years; total remaining term cannot exceed 14 years post-approval.

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Primary therapeutic area or disease category addressed by the patented compound or method (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neuroscience). Aligns with the company's R&D portfolio structure and supports commercial lifecycle planning.
attributes.references: ICH E8; WHO ATC Classification; Internal Therapeutic Area Taxonomy

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Official title of the patent as filed and granted by the patent office. Describes the invention in human-readable form and is used for portfolio reporting and IP management.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this patent record. Used for change tracking, data synchronization, and audit compliance under 21 CFR Part 11.

attributes.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this patent record to the corresponding document stored in Veeva Vault (RIM or QualityDocs module), where the patent application, grant certificate, and related correspondence are archived. Supports traceability to the system of record for IP documents.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10

products.name: patent_claim
products.description: Individual claims within a granted or pending patent, capturing claim number, claim type (independent, dependent), claim text, claim scope classification (broad, narrow, genus, species), and validity status. Critical for freedom-to-operate analyses, infringement assessments, and generic/biosimilar entry defense strategies. Each claim has its own legal standing and may be challenged independently during inter partes review (IPR) or opposition proceedings.

attributes.name: patent_claim_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each individual patent claim record within the intellectual property portfolio management system.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 112; USPTO Patent Rules 37 CFR Part 1

attributes.name: country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Patent claims are jurisdiction-specific; critical for patent prosecution strategy, litigation planning, and claim scope analysis in pharmaceutical IP management.

attributes.name: drug_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_product. Business justification: Specific patent claims cover specific products. Essential for FTO analysis, claim construction in litigation, Orange Book listing accuracy, and claim-level infringement assessment. Removes denormalize

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent patent record to which this claim belongs. Each patent may contain multiple independent and dependent claims.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 101; USPTO Patent Rules 37 CFR Part 1

attributes.name: responsible_patent_counsel_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Responsible Patent Counsel Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical patent prosecution tracks which internal IP attorney manages each claim for office action responses, amendment strategy, and litigation support. Replaces text field responsible_patent_c

attributes.name: amendment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the most recent amendment to this claim was filed or entered. Null if the claim has never been amended. Used to track prosecution history and assess prosecution history estoppel in infringement proceedings.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 132; USPTO 37 CFR 1.111; EPC Rule 137; USPTO MPEP § 714

attributes.name: application_number
attributes.description: The official application number assigned by the patent office upon filing (e.g., US 16/123,456 or EP 19 123 456.7). Used to track prosecution history, office actions, and correspondence with patent counsel. Serves as the primary external identifier for the application.
attributes.references: USPTO 37 CFR 1.53; EPC Rule 41; PCT Rule 26bis

attributes.name: challenge_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the claim is subject to an active or completed post-grant challenge. IPR (Inter Partes Review) and opposition proceedings can invalidate individual claims independently. Critical for generic/biosimilar entry defense and Paragraph IV ANDA litigation strategy.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §§ 311-319 (IPR); EPC Articles 99-105 (Opposition); Hatch-Waxman Act 21 U.S.C. § 355(j)

attributes.name: claim_amendment_version
attributes.description: Version number tracking amendments made to the claim text during prosecution or post-grant proceedings (e.g., reexamination, IPR). Version 1 represents the originally filed claim; subsequent versions reflect amendments. Used to maintain prosecution history and support claim construction arguments.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 316(d); USPTO 37 CFR 42.121; EPC Rule 80; USPTO MPEP § 714

attributes.name: claim_category
attributes.description: Subject matter category of the claim defining what is being protected. Composition claims protect chemical or biological entities (NCE, NBE, API); method/use claims protect therapeutic uses or manufacturing processes; formulation claims protect drug product (DP) compositions; dosage form claims protect FDF configurations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: composition|method|process|apparatus|use|formulation|dosage_form|biological — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 101; USPTO MPEP § 2106; EPC Article 52; ICH Q11 Drug Substance

attributes.name: claim_number
attributes.description: Sequential number of the claim within the patent document as filed or granted (e.g., Claim 1, Claim 2). Claim numbering follows USPTO and EPO conventions and is used in legal proceedings, IPR petitions, and freedom-to-operate analyses.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 112(b); USPTO 37 CFR 1.75; EPO Rule 43 EPC

attributes.name: claim_priority_date
attributes.description: The earliest effective filing date from which this claim's priority is established, including priority claims under Paris Convention or PCT. The priority date determines prior art cutoff and is critical for validity assessments and patent term calculations.
attributes.references: Paris Convention Article 4; PCT Article 8; 35 U.S.C. § 119; EPC Article 87

attributes.name: claim_scope_classification
attributes.description: Business classification of the claim's legal breadth and coverage. Broad claims cover wide ranges of embodiments; narrow claims are limited to specific embodiments. Genus claims cover a class of compounds or methods; species claims cover a specific member. Used in lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry defense strategy.
attributes.references: USPTO MPEP § 2173; EPO Guidelines for Examination; ICH Q8 Quality by Design

attributes.name: claim_text
attributes.description: Full verbatim text of the claim as it appears in the granted patent or pending application. This is the legally operative language used in infringement assessments, IPR petitions, inter partes review proceedings, and freedom-to-operate (FTO) analyses. Classified confidential due to strategic IP sensitivity.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 112; USPTO 37 CFR 1.75; EPC Article 84; ICH M4 eCTD

attributes.name: claim_type
attributes.description: Structural classification of the claim indicating whether it stands alone (independent) or references and narrows a prior claim (dependent or multiple dependent). Independent claims define the broadest scope; dependent claims add limitations. Critical for infringement analysis and claim charting.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 112(d); USPTO 37 CFR 1.75(c); EPO Rule 43(4) EPC

attributes.name: cpc_classification_code
attributes.description: The Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) code assigned by USPTO or EPO, providing more granular technical classification than IPC. Used in patent landscape analyses, freedom-to-operate searches, and competitive intelligence for drug discovery and CMC domains.
attributes.references: USPTO/EPO CPC Scheme; WIPO IPC; USPTO MPEP § 902

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this patent claim record was first created in the IP management system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this patent claim record originated. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail requirements. Veeva Vault RIM is the primary system of record for IP and regulatory data in the pharmaceutical enterprise.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10; Veeva Vault RIM; ISPE GAMP 5 (Computer System Validation)

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The calculated expiration date of the patent claim, accounting for standard 20-year patent term from filing date, patent term adjustments (PTA), and patent term extensions (PTE) granted for regulatory review delays under Hatch-Waxman or SPC in Europe. Critical for lifecycle management and loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) planning.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 154(b) (PTA); 35 U.S.C. § 156 (PTE); EU Regulation 469/2009 (SPC); Hatch-Waxman Act

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the patent application containing this claim was filed with the relevant patent office. Used to calculate patent term and determine prior art under AIA first-inventor-to-file rules.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 111; USPTO 37 CFR 1.53; EPC Article 80; PCT Article 11

attributes.name: fto_relevance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this claim has been identified as relevant in one or more freedom-to-operate (FTO) analyses. FTO-relevant claims require monitoring for potential infringement by third-party products or by the company's own pipeline compounds.
attributes.references: USPTO Patent Rules; ICH Q11; EMA Guideline on Similar Biological Medicinal Products

attributes.name: grant_date
attributes.description: The date on which the patent containing this claim was officially granted by the patent office. Marks the start of the enforceable patent term. Null for pending applications.

attributes.name: ipc_classification_code
attributes.description: The International Patent Classification (IPC) code assigned to this claim, indicating the technical field of the invention (e.g., A61K for pharmaceutical preparations, A61P for therapeutic activity). Used for patent landscape analyses, competitive intelligence, and prior art searches.
attributes.references: WIPO IPC (Strasbourg Agreement 1971); USPTO Classification; EPO CPC

attributes.name: ipr_petition_number
attributes.description: The official PTAB (Patent Trial and Appeal Board) or EPO Opposition Division case number for any active or completed inter partes review (IPR) or opposition proceeding challenging this claim. Null if no IPR or opposition has been filed. Critical for litigation tracking and generic/biosimilar defense strategy.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §§ 311-319; USPTO 37 CFR Part 42; EPC Articles 99-105; AIA § 6

attributes.name: is_orange_book_listed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this claim is associated with a patent listed in the FDA Orange Book (Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations). Orange Book listing triggers 30-month stay provisions under Hatch-Waxman upon ANDA Paragraph IV certification, directly impacting generic entry timelines.
attributes.references: 21 U.S.C. § 355(b)(1); FDA 21 CFR Part 314.53; Hatch-Waxman Act

attributes.name: is_purple_book_listed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this claim is associated with a patent listed in the FDA Purple Book (Lists of Licensed Biological Products). Purple Book listing is relevant for biosimilar entry defense under the Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act (BPCIA) patent dance provisions.
attributes.references: 42 U.S.C. § 262(k); BPCIA; FDA Purple Book; 21 U.S.C. § 355(j)

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this patent claim record was most recently modified in the IP management system. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and data synchronization with Veeva Vault RIM and external patent docketing systems.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); ICH Q10; Veeva Vault RIM; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: litigation_case_reference
attributes.description: Court case number or docket reference for any active or completed patent infringement litigation involving this claim (e.g., Paragraph IV ANDA litigation, biosimilar patent dance disputes). Classified confidential due to legal privilege sensitivity. Null if no litigation is associated.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 271; Hatch-Waxman Act 21 U.S.C. § 355(j)(5)(B); BPCIA 42 U.S.C. § 262(l); Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

attributes.name: molecule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the molecule or biological entity protected by this claim. NCE (New Chemical Entity) for small molecules; NBE (New Biological Entity) for large molecule biologics; biosimilar for follow-on biologics; vaccine, gene therapy, or cell therapy for advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs). Determines applicable regulatory pathway and exclusivity provisions.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314 (NCE); 21 CFR Part 601 (NBE/BLA); EMA ATMP Regulation EC 1394/2007; ICH Q11

attributes.name: outside_counsel_firm
attributes.description: Name of the external law firm engaged to prosecute or defend this claim. Classified confidential due to legal privilege and commercial sensitivity. Used for matter management, billing reconciliation, and legal spend tracking.
attributes.references: USPTO 37 CFR 1.32; ABA Model Rules; SOX Section 302 (legal matter disclosure)

attributes.name: parent_claim_number
attributes.description: For dependent claims, the claim number of the parent claim from which this claim depends. Null for independent claims. Used to reconstruct claim dependency trees for infringement and validity analyses.

attributes.name: patent_office_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the patent office where this claim was filed or is being prosecuted. USPTO (US), EPO (European), UKIPO (UK post-Brexit), JPO (Japan), CNIPA (China), WIPO (PCT international). Determines applicable procedural rules and examination standards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USPTO|EPO|UKIPO|JPO|CNIPA|WIPO|PMDA — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Paris Convention; PCT; EPC; USPTO 37 CFR; JPO Patent Act; CNIPA Regulations

attributes.name: patent_term_extension_months
attributes.description: Number of months of patent term extension granted to compensate for regulatory review delays during NDA/BLA/MAA approval processes. In the US, PTE is granted under 35 U.S.C. § 156 (Hatch-Waxman); in Europe, via Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC). Directly impacts loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) date calculations.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 156; EU Regulation 469/2009 (SPC); Hatch-Waxman Act; EMA SPC Guidance

attributes.name: prosecution_status
attributes.description: Current status of the claim within the patent prosecution lifecycle at the relevant patent office. Pending claims are under examination; allowed claims have been approved but not yet granted; granted claims are part of an issued patent; rejected claims received a final office action; abandoned claims were not pursued further.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 131; USPTO 37 CFR 1.101; EPC Article 97; PCT Rule 69

attributes.name: spc_number
attributes.description: The official reference number of the Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) granted in EU member states for this claim. SPCs extend effective patent protection for up to 5 years post-patent expiry for medicinal products that required regulatory approval. Null if no SPC has been granted.
attributes.references: EU Regulation 469/2009; EMA SPC Guidance; MHRA SPC Guidance (UK)

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The therapeutic area or disease indication covered by this claim (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Aligns with the company's portfolio therapeutic areas and is used for lifecycle management, LOE planning, and commercial strategy coordination.
attributes.references: ATC Classification (WHO); ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Studies; FDA Therapeutic Area Guidance

attributes.name: validity_status
attributes.description: Current legal standing of the claim. Valid claims are enforceable; invalid claims have been found unpatentable; cancelled claims were withdrawn during prosecution or post-grant proceedings; amended claims were modified during IPR or reexamination; under_review indicates active challenge proceedings; stayed indicates enforcement is paused pending litigation outcome.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 316; USPTO 37 CFR Part 42; EPO Rule 80 EPC; MHRA IP Guidance

products.name: patent_family
products.description: Groups related patents and patent applications filed across multiple jurisdictions that share a common priority application. Tracks the priority application number, priority date, PCT application number, family type (simple, extended, INPADOC), and member count. Enables portfolio-level analysis of global IP coverage for a given invention and supports lifecycle management across jurisdictions.

attributes.name: patent_family_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the patent family record in the Pharmaceuticals IP portfolio system. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: lead_inventor_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Patent families in pharmaceuticals require tracking lead inventors as employees for invention disclosure workflows, assignment execution, and inventor compensation. Replaces denormalized lead_inventor

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Patent families are owned by legal entities; essential for portfolio valuation, corporate structure reporting, and strategic IP management across business units.

attributes.name: masterdata_atc_classification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Patent families are organized by therapeutic area; required for strategic portfolio management, competitive intelligence, and therapeutic area investment decisions.

attributes.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Patent families are managed by business units with cost center allocation; essential for portfolio budgeting, cost tracking, and financial accountability.

attributes.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: Patent families cover specific INNs; required for competitive intelligence, portfolio strategy, and molecule-specific IP protection planning.

attributes.name: masterdata_profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: Patent families align with business segments; essential for strategic portfolio management, segment P&L, and therapeutic area performance tracking.

attributes.name: priority_country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Priority country is fundamental to patent family strategy and filing decisions; required for PCT strategy and global patent portfolio management.

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Patent families are managed under IP compliance programs governing portfolio governance, data integrity in filings, and inventor compensation. Program scope includes IP lifecycle management and regula

attributes.name: annual_maintenance_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total annualized cost in US dollars for maintaining all active member patents in this family, including renewal fees, annuities, and agent fees across all jurisdictions. Used for IP budget planning and portfolio rationalization decisions.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; GAAP ASC 350; IFRS IAS 38

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the patent family record was first created in the IP data system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5; ICH Q10

attributes.name: data_exclusivity_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which regulatory data exclusivity (RDE) protection expires for the drug covered by this patent family. Data exclusivity prevents generic/biosimilar applicants from referencing the originator's clinical data for a defined period (e.g., 5 years NCE in US, 8+2+1 years in EU).
attributes.references: 21 CFR §314.108; EU Directive 2001/83/EC Article 10; FDA CDER

attributes.name: dmf_reference_number
attributes.description: The FDA Drug Master File (DMF) number or equivalent regulatory dossier reference associated with the API or formulation covered by this patent family. Links IP protection to the regulatory submission record.
attributes.references: 21 CFR §314.420; FDA DMF Guidance; ICH CTD Module 3

attributes.name: earliest_expiry_date
attributes.description: The earliest expiration date among all granted member patents in the family, before any patent term extensions or supplementary protection certificates. Critical for generic/biosimilar entry defense strategy planning.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §154; EPC Article 63; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: family_code
attributes.description: Internally assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the patent family within the IP management system. Used for cross-referencing across Veeva Vault RIM and SAP IP modules.

attributes.name: family_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name assigned to the patent family, typically reflecting the invention title or the compound/technology it covers (e.g., 'Compound X Formulation Family').
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; WIPO PCT Rules

attributes.name: family_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the patent family. 'Active' indicates at least one member patent is in force; 'Pending' indicates applications under examination; 'Expired' indicates all members have lapsed; 'Abandoned' indicates prosecution was discontinued. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|pending|expired|abandoned|licensed_out|litigated — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: family_type
attributes.description: Classification of the patent family grouping methodology. 'Simple' groups patents sharing the same priority; 'Extended' includes equivalents; 'INPADOC' follows the European Patent Office INPADOC definition. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: simple|extended|INPADOC|domestic|international — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the patent family record was formally established in the IP management system, typically corresponding to the priority application filing date. Used for portfolio age analysis and lifecycle tracking.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §111; EPC Article 80; WIPO PCT Article 11

attributes.name: freedom_to_operate_status
attributes.description: Current status of the Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis for this patent family. 'Cleared' indicates no blocking third-party patents identified; 'At Risk' indicates potential infringement risk; 'Blocked' indicates a blocking patent exists; 'Under Review' indicates analysis in progress.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §271; EPC Article 64; ICH Q10 IP Management

attributes.name: granted_member_count
attributes.description: Number of patent applications within the family that have been granted (issued) patents across all jurisdictions. Distinguishes granted protection from pending applications for portfolio strength assessment.

attributes.name: invention_category
attributes.description: Classification of the type of invention covered by the patent family. New Chemical Entity (NCE) covers novel small molecules; New Biological Entity (NBE) covers biologics; formulation covers drug product compositions; process covers manufacturing methods; method_of_use covers therapeutic indications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NCE|NBE|formulation|process|combination|device|method_of_use — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR §314; ICH Q6A; ICH Q6B; EPC Article 52

attributes.name: invention_title
attributes.description: The official title of the invention as stated in the priority or PCT application. Reflects the technical scope of the patent family and is used for portfolio reporting and IP strategy communications.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §112; EPC Rule 42; WIPO PCT Rule 4.3

attributes.name: jurisdiction_count
attributes.description: Number of distinct national or regional jurisdictions in which the patent family has at least one active member application or granted patent. Measures geographic breadth of IP protection.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the patent family record. Supports change tracking, audit compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5; ICH Q10

attributes.name: latest_expiry_date
attributes.description: The latest expiration date among all granted member patents in the family, including any patent term extensions (PTE) or supplementary protection certificates (SPC). Defines the outer boundary of IP exclusivity for lifecycle management.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §156; EU Regulation 469/2009 (SPC); FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: licensing_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the patent family is subject to a licensing arrangement. 'Licensed In' means the company holds a license from a third party; 'Licensed Out' means the company has granted a license to a third party; 'Cross Licensed' indicates a bilateral arrangement.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §261; EPC Article 73; ICH Q10; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: litigation_status
attributes.description: Current litigation status associated with this patent family. Tracks whether the family is subject to active patent infringement suits, inter partes review (IPR), or post-grant review (PGR) proceedings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: none|threatened|filed|settled|judgment_for_patentee|judgment_against — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §282; AIA §316; EPC Article 138; GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: member_count
attributes.description: Total number of individual patent applications and granted patents that are members of this family across all jurisdictions. Indicates the breadth of global IP coverage for the invention.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for IP counsel to record strategic observations, prosecution history highlights, licensing negotiation context, or lifecycle management decisions relevant to the patent family. Not intended for structured data.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: orange_book_listed
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more patents in this family are listed in the FDA Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations (Orange Book). Orange Book listing triggers 30-month stay provisions against ANDA filers under Hatch-Waxman.

attributes.name: orphan_drug_exclusivity_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the invention covered by this patent family has been granted orphan drug designation and associated market exclusivity (7 years in the US, 10 years in the EU). Relevant for rare disease portfolio strategy.
attributes.references: 21 CFR §316; EU Regulation 141/2000; FDA ODE; EMA COMP

attributes.name: patent_register_listed
attributes.description: Indicates whether patents in this family are listed on the EMA European Patent Register or national patent registers linked to marketing authorisations, triggering data exclusivity and market protection provisions.
attributes.references: EU Directive 2001/83/EC; EMA Patent Register; EU Regulation 726/2004

attributes.name: patent_term_extension_granted
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Patent Term Extension (PTE) or Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) has been granted for any member of this family, compensating for regulatory review time under FDA or EMA processes.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §156; EU Regulation 469/2009; FDA CDER PTE Guidance

attributes.name: pct_application_number
attributes.description: The international application number filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) administered by WIPO, if applicable. Format: PCT/[country code][year]/[serial number]. Enables simultaneous patent protection in multiple jurisdictions.

attributes.name: pct_filing_date
attributes.description: The international filing date of the PCT application, if applicable. Determines the 30/31-month national phase entry deadline for member jurisdictions.

attributes.name: pct_publication_number
attributes.description: The WIPO publication number assigned to the PCT international application upon publication (e.g., WO2023/123456). Used for public disclosure tracking and prior art searches.

attributes.name: pediatric_exclusivity_expiry_date
attributes.description: The expiry date of pediatric exclusivity granted under the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) in the US or the Paediatric Regulation in the EU, adding 6 months of additional exclusivity to qualifying patents.

attributes.name: portfolio_segment
attributes.description: Strategic classification of the patent family within the IP portfolio. 'Core' patents protect primary commercial products; 'Defensive' patents block competitor freedom to operate; 'Licensing' patents are monetized through out-licensing; 'Acquired' patents came through M&A.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; SOX Section 302; ISPE GAMP 5

attributes.name: priority_application_number
attributes.description: The application number of the earliest-filed patent application that establishes the priority date for the family. Typically a national or regional application number (e.g., US provisional or EP application).
attributes.references: Paris Convention Article 4; 35 U.S.C. §119; EPC Rule 52

attributes.name: priority_date
attributes.description: The filing date of the earliest priority application in the family. Establishes the effective date of invention disclosure for novelty and prior art assessments under Paris Convention.
attributes.references: Paris Convention Article 4; 35 U.S.C. §119; EPC Rule 52

attributes.name: responsible_ip_counsel
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the internal IP attorney or external patent counsel responsible for managing prosecution and maintenance of this patent family. Used for accountability and workload management in the IP department.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; SOX Section 302; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The primary therapeutic area or disease indication covered by the invention (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Aligns with the company's portfolio therapeutic area taxonomy for lifecycle management reporting.
attributes.references: ATC Classification (WHO); ICH E6; FDA Therapeutic Area Guidance

products.name: exclusivity_period
products.description: Tracks all regulatory exclusivity periods granted to pharmaceutical products, distinct from patent protection. Covers orphan drug exclusivity (7 years US / 10 years EU), data exclusivity (5 years NCE / 3 years new indication), pediatric exclusivity extension (6 months), new chemical entity exclusivity, biologics exclusivity (12 years US), and REMS exclusivity. Captures exclusivity type, granting authority (FDA, EMA, PMDA), start date, expiry date, product reference, and associated NDA/BLA/MAA number. Critical for lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry defense.
products.reference: FDA Orange Book / Purple Book Exclusivity

attributes.name: exclusivity_period_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each regulatory exclusivity period record in the pharmaceutical intellectual property portfolio.

attributes.name: country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Exclusivity is jurisdiction-specific; essential for lifecycle management, LOE planning, and market-specific revenue forecasting in pharmaceutical commercialization.

attributes.name: masterdata_atc_classification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Exclusivity is granted for specific therapeutic indications; required for competitive intelligence, market analysis, and therapeutic area-specific LOE planning.

attributes.name: masterdata_inn_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.inn_registry. Business justification: Exclusivity is granted for specific INNs; critical for lifecycle management, molecule-specific LOE planning, and regulatory exclusivity tracking.

attributes.name: masterdata_ndc_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.ndc_code. Business justification: Exclusivity protects specific NDC-coded products; critical for LOE forecasting, generic entry planning, and product-specific revenue protection.

attributes.name: masterdata_profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: Exclusivity periods protect product revenues in specific segments; critical for forecasting, investor relations, and segment-level LOE impact analysis.

attributes.name: medicinal_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pharmaceutical product (Drug Product or Drug Substance) to which this exclusivity period applies.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; EMA Product Register

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: FK to intellectual.patent.patent_id — Exclusivity periods are often tied to specific patents — linking enables IP lifecycle management and loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) planning critical for commercial strategy.

attributes.name: responsible_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical regulatory affairs assigns specific employees to monitor exclusivity periods for LOE risk management, generic entry forecasting, and commercial planning coordination. Critical for lifec

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the NDA, BLA, or MAA was approved by the granting authority, which typically triggers the start of the exclusivity period. Serves as the anchor date for exclusivity calculations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314; FDA Orange Book; EMA EPAR; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: brand_name
attributes.description: The proprietary/trade name of the drug product under which the exclusivity was granted and the product is marketed. Used for commercial lifecycle management and trademark coordination.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; EMA EPAR; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: challenge_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exclusivity period is subject to a legal or regulatory challenge. Paragraph IV = ANDA Paragraph IV certification challenge under Hatch-Waxman; Inter Partes = IPR/PGR challenge at USPTO; Court Order = court-ordered modification; Under Review = authority-initiated review. Critical for generic entry defense strategy.
attributes.references: Hatch-Waxman Act 21 USC 355(j); 35 USC 315 (IPR); FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this exclusivity period record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX; GDPR Article 5; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: data_package_type
attributes.description: Type of regulatory data package submitted with the application. Full = complete standalone dossier (NCE/NBE); 505(b)(2) = hybrid relying on published literature or prior approvals; Hybrid = EU hybrid application; Bibliographic = based on published scientific literature. Determines applicable exclusivity type and duration.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.54 (505(b)(2)); EMA Directive 2001/83/EC Article 10; ICH M4

attributes.name: dmf_number
attributes.description: FDA Drug Master File (DMF) number associated with the drug substance or drug product covered by this exclusivity, where applicable. Supports CMC (Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls) linkage and regulatory audit.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.420; FDA DMF Guidance; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: The pharmaceutical dosage form of the product covered by this exclusivity (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, solution, patch). Relevant because exclusivity may be dosage-form specific.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; ICH Q6A; EMA Guideline on Pharmaceutical Development

attributes.name: exclusivity_category
attributes.description: Broad category of the exclusivity period indicating whether it applies to a small molecule (NCE/NME), biologic (NBE), orphan drug designation, pediatric extension, or combination product.
attributes.references: FDA CDER/CBER Guidance; ICH Q6A; EMA Guideline on Orphan Medicinal Products

attributes.name: exclusivity_code
attributes.description: Internally assigned unique alphanumeric code identifying this exclusivity period record, used for cross-system referencing and lifecycle management tracking.
attributes.references: Internal IP Management Standard; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: exclusivity_duration_months
attributes.description: Total duration of the exclusivity period expressed in months as granted by the regulatory authority (e.g., 84 months for US orphan drug, 120 months for EU orphan drug, 144 months for US biologics). Supports duration validation and comparison across jurisdictions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA 42 USC 262; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

attributes.name: exclusivity_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory exclusivity period expires, after which generic or biosimilar applicants may reference the innovator data. Critical for lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry defense planning.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA 42 USC 262; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

attributes.name: exclusivity_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory exclusivity period commences, typically aligned with the date of first approval (NDA/BLA/MAA approval date) or orphan designation date depending on exclusivity type.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108; FDA Orange Book; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

attributes.name: exclusivity_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the exclusivity period. Active = currently in force; Expired = past expiry date; Withdrawn = voluntarily or involuntarily revoked by authority; Challenged = subject to legal or regulatory challenge; Pending = granted but not yet effective; Suspended = temporarily halted pending review.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; EMA Orphan Register; 21 CFR Part 314; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: exclusivity_type
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory exclusivity type granted. NCE = New Chemical Entity (5 years US); ODE = Orphan Drug Exclusivity (7 years US / 10 years EU); PED = Pediatric Exclusivity Extension (6 months); DATA = Data Exclusivity for new indication (3 years US); BIOL = Biologics Exclusivity (12 years US); REMS = Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy exclusivity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NCE|ODE|PED|DATA|BIOL|REMS|NME|PATENT_LINKAGE — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA 42 USC 262; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

attributes.name: first_generic_entry_date
attributes.description: The projected or actual date on which the first generic (ANDA) or biosimilar (351(k) BLA) product may enter the market following expiry or challenge of this exclusivity. Used for lifecycle management, revenue forecasting, and LOE (Loss of Exclusivity) planning.
attributes.references: Hatch-Waxman Act; BPCIA 42 USC 262; FDA Orange Book; EMA Biosimilar Guidelines

attributes.name: granting_authority
attributes.description: Regulatory authority that granted this exclusivity period (e.g., FDA for US market, EMA for EU market, PMDA for Japan, MHRA for UK post-Brexit). Determines jurisdiction and applicable exclusivity rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|MHRA|NMPA|WHO|DEA — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; EMA Orphan Register; ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: indication
attributes.description: The specific disease or condition for which the product is approved and for which this exclusivity was granted. Particularly important for new indication (3-year data exclusivity) and orphan drug exclusivity where exclusivity is indication-specific.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; EMA EPAR; ICH E8; 21 CFR Part 314.108

attributes.name: is_orphan_designated
attributes.description: Indicates whether the product holds an orphan drug designation from FDA (Orphan Drug Act) or EMA (Regulation EC 141/2000), which is a prerequisite for orphan drug exclusivity (ODE). Distinct from exclusivity_type as designation may exist without exclusivity being granted.
attributes.references: FDA Orphan Drug Act 21 CFR Part 316; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this exclusivity period record, supporting change tracking and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records regulations.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX; GDPR Article 5; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: legal_counsel_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes from legal counsel regarding this exclusivity period, including litigation strategy, challenge responses, and coordination with patent attorneys. Classified as confidential due to potential attorney-client privilege content.
attributes.references: Internal IP Legal Policy; SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: lifecycle_stage
attributes.description: Current lifecycle management stage of the product relative to this exclusivity period. Pre-Approval = exclusivity anticipated but not yet granted; Active Protection = exclusivity in force; LOE Watch = within 24 months of expiry requiring active monitoring; Post-Expiry = exclusivity has lapsed.
attributes.references: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; Internal Lifecycle Management Policy

attributes.name: loe_risk_level
attributes.description: Assessed risk level for Loss of Exclusivity (LOE) based on proximity to expiry, challenge status, and competitive pipeline. Critical for commercial lifecycle management and strategic planning.
attributes.references: Internal IP Lifecycle Management Policy; ICH Q10

attributes.name: orphan_designation_number
attributes.description: Official orphan drug designation number assigned by FDA (ODA) or EMA (EC Regulation 141/2000) when exclusivity_type is ODE. Required for orphan drug exclusivity validation and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: FDA Orphan Drug Act 21 CFR Part 316; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: patent_linkage_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exclusivity period is linked to a listed patent in the FDA Orange Book or equivalent patent register, enabling coordination between patent protection and regulatory exclusivity for lifecycle management.
attributes.references: Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Orange Book; 21 CFR Part 314.53

attributes.name: pediatric_extension_expiry_date
attributes.description: The adjusted expiry date reflecting the 6-month pediatric exclusivity extension, if granted. Null if pediatric_extension_granted is False.
attributes.references: Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA); EU Paediatric Regulation EC 1901/2006

attributes.name: pediatric_extension_granted
attributes.description: Indicates whether a 6-month pediatric exclusivity extension (PED) has been granted under the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) or EU Paediatric Regulation, extending the base exclusivity or patent term by 6 months.
attributes.references: Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA); EU Paediatric Regulation EC 1901/2006; 21 CFR Part 314.108

attributes.name: regulatory_basis
attributes.description: The specific statutory or regulatory provision under which this exclusivity was granted (e.g., 21 CFR 314.108(b)(2) for NCE, Orphan Drug Act Section 527, BPCIA Section 7002, EU Regulation 141/2000 Article 8). Supports legal and regulatory audit trails.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108; Orphan Drug Act; BPCIA; EMA Regulation EC 141/2000; Hatch-Waxman Act

attributes.name: rems_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is required as a condition of approval for this product, which may confer additional exclusivity protections or market access restrictions relevant to generic entry.
attributes.references: FDA REMS Guidance; 21 USC 355-1; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: The route by which the drug product is administered (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, topical). Exclusivity may be route-specific, particularly for new indication or new formulation exclusivity.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; ICH M4; EMA SmPC Guideline

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this exclusivity period data was sourced (e.g., Veeva Vault RIM, FDA Orange Book feed, EMA EPAR, SAP S/4HANA). Supports data lineage and Silver layer provenance tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; Internal Data Governance Policy; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The therapeutic area or disease category associated with the approved indication (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neurology, Cardiovascular). Used for portfolio segmentation and LOE impact analysis by therapeutic area.
attributes.references: ICH E8; ATC Classification; FDA CDER Therapeutic Area Classification

products.name: trademark
products.description: Master record for all pharmaceutical trademark registrations including brand names, logos, trade dress, and slogans. Captures trademark name, registration number, filing date, registration date, expiry/renewal date, jurisdiction, Nice classification, goods and services description, trademark type (word mark, figurative, combined), owner entity, and current status (pending, registered, opposed, cancelled). Supports brand protection strategy and commercial launch activities.

attributes.name: trademark_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each trademark registration record in the pharmaceutical intellectual property portfolio.
attributes.references: ISO 15836 (Dublin Core Metadata); Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Trademarks are registered by jurisdiction; required for brand protection strategy, market entry planning, and global brand portfolio management.

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Trademarks are registered to legal entities; required for brand ownership tracking, legal compliance, and M&A due diligence in pharmaceutical branding.

attributes.name: masterdata_atc_classification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Trademarks are associated with therapeutic categories; required for brand strategy, market positioning, and therapeutic area-specific brand portfolio management.

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Trademarks are managed under compliance programs (brand integrity, anti-counterfeiting, promotional compliance, trademark watch). Program scope includes trademark governance and regulatory adherence f

attributes.name: responsible_counsel_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical trademark portfolios require internal IP counsel assignment for renewal deadline management, opposition response coordination, and brand protection strategy. Essential for workload bala

attributes.name: application_number
attributes.description: The official application number assigned by the trademark office at the time of filing, prior to registration. Used to track the application through examination and opposition proceedings.
attributes.references: USPTO TEAS; EUIPO eSearch; WIPO Madrid System

attributes.name: associated_brand_name
attributes.description: The commercial brand name of the pharmaceutical drug product associated with this trademark, if applicable. Links the trademark record to the commercial product portfolio for launch planning and brand protection strategy.
attributes.references: FDA Approved Drug Products (Orange Book); EMA Product Database; INN (International Nonproprietary Name) Guidelines

attributes.name: colour_claim
attributes.description: Description of any specific colour or colour combination claimed as a feature of the trademark (e.g., Pantone codes, RGB values, or textual colour descriptions). Relevant for figurative and combined marks where colour is a distinctive element.
attributes.references: WIPO Nice Agreement; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 4; USPTO TEAS

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the trademark record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); GDPR Article 5(2); SOX; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: disclaimer_text
attributes.description: Any disclaimer of exclusive rights to specific elements of the trademark (e.g., generic or descriptive terms within a combined mark) as required or accepted by the trademark office during examination.
attributes.references: 15 U.S.C. § 1056; USPTO TEAS; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the current trademark registration term expires and renewal must be filed to maintain protection. Critical for lifecycle management and brand protection continuity.
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid System; 15 U.S.C. § 1058; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 53

attributes.name: external_counsel_firm
attributes.description: Name of the external law firm or IP agent responsible for managing the trademark prosecution and maintenance in the relevant jurisdiction. Supports coordination with legal counsel on prosecution strategy and renewal deadlines.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; Pharmaceutical IP management best practices; SOX compliance

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the trademark application was officially filed with the relevant trademark office. Establishes priority date for the mark in the jurisdiction.
attributes.references: WIPO Paris Convention Art. 4; 15 U.S.C. § 1051; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 32

attributes.name: goods_services_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the goods and/or services covered by the trademark registration, as specified in the application. For pharmaceutical trademarks, typically describes the therapeutic area, dosage form, and indication of the drug product covered.
attributes.references: WIPO Nice Agreement; 15 U.S.C. § 1051(a)(2); EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 33

attributes.name: inn_name
attributes.description: The WHO-assigned International Nonproprietary Name (INN) of the active pharmaceutical ingredient associated with the trademarked drug product. Used to distinguish the brand trademark from the generic molecule name and to assess potential INN-based conflicts.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; ICH Q6A; FDA USAN Council

attributes.name: internal_reference_code
attributes.description: Internal company reference code or docket number assigned to the trademark record in the company's IP management system (e.g., Veeva Vault RIM or internal IP docketing system). Enables cross-referencing with internal IP portfolio management tools.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; SAP S/4HANA IP Module; Internal IP Docketing Standards

attributes.name: licensing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the trademark is subject to one or more active licensing agreements (True) or is exclusively used by the owner entity (False). Supports coordination with the licensing agreements portfolio in the IP domain.
attributes.references: 15 U.S.C. § 1055; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 25; WIPO Licensing Guide

attributes.name: litigation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the trademark is currently involved in active litigation or legal proceedings (True), such as infringement actions, cancellation proceedings, or inter partes disputes. Triggers coordination with legal counsel.
attributes.references: 15 U.S.C. § 1114; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 130; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: madrid_international_number
attributes.description: The WIPO-assigned international registration number for trademarks filed under the Madrid Protocol. Populated only when madrid_protocol_flag is True.
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid System; WIPO Madrid Protocol Art. 3

attributes.name: madrid_protocol_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this trademark registration was obtained through the WIPO Madrid Protocol international registration system (True) or through a direct national/regional filing (False). Affects renewal procedures and management workflows.
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid Protocol (1989); WIPO Madrid System

attributes.name: mark_type
attributes.description: Classification of the trademark by its nature: word mark (text only), figurative mark (logo/image only), combined mark (text and image), three-dimensional mark (shape), sound mark, or colour mark. Drives brand protection strategy and enforcement scope. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: word_mark|figurative_mark|combined_mark|three_dimensional_mark|sound_mark|colour_mark — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WIPO Nice Agreement; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 4; 15 U.S.C. § 1127

attributes.name: nice_class_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of Nice Classification class numbers (1–45) under which the trademark is registered. For pharmaceutical trademarks, typically includes Class 5 (pharmaceutical preparations) and potentially Class 10 (medical devices) or Class 44 (medical services). Defines the scope of goods and services covered by the mark.
attributes.references: WIPO Nice Agreement (11th Edition); 15 U.S.C. § 1112; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 33

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional remarks, prosecution history notes, strategic comments, or legal observations relevant to the trademark record that are not captured in structured fields.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; Internal IP Management Best Practices

attributes.name: office_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the trademark office or registry where the application was filed or registration is held (e.g., USPTO for United States, EUIPO for European Union, UKIPO for United Kingdom, JPO for Japan, CNIPA for China, WIPO for international registrations). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USPTO|EUIPO|UKIPO|JPO|CNIPA|WIPO|CIPO|IP_AUSTRALIA — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid System; USPTO; EUIPO; UKIPO; JPO; NMPA/CNIPA; PMDA

attributes.name: opposition_deadline_date
attributes.description: The date by which third parties may file an opposition to the trademark application in the relevant jurisdiction. Critical for monitoring the application's progress toward registration and for assessing third-party challenge risk.
attributes.references: 15 U.S.C. § 1063; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 46; WIPO Madrid System

attributes.name: opposition_status
attributes.description: Current status of any opposition proceedings against the trademark application: not_opposed (no opposition filed), opposition_filed (third-party opposition pending), opposition_withdrawn (opponent withdrew), or opposition_decided (proceeding concluded by the trademark office).
attributes.references: 15 U.S.C. § 1063; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 46–47; WIPO Madrid System

attributes.name: owner_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the trademark owner's country of domicile or incorporation, as recorded in the trademark register.

attributes.name: priority_claim_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction in which the priority application was originally filed, as claimed under the Paris Convention.

attributes.name: priority_claim_date
attributes.description: The date of the earliest priority application claimed under the Paris Convention, if the trademark application claims priority from a prior filing in another jurisdiction. Establishes the effective priority date for multi-jurisdictional filings.
attributes.references: WIPO Paris Convention Art. 4; 15 U.S.C. § 1126; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 34

attributes.name: product_launch_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the primary market where the associated pharmaceutical drug product is commercially launched or planned for launch under this trademark. Links trademark protection to commercial launch activities.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; FDA; EMA; PMDA; NMPA; Commercial Launch Best Practices

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the trademark was officially registered by the trademark office. Marks the start of the initial registration term and triggers renewal obligation tracking.
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid System; 15 U.S.C. § 1057; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 45

attributes.name: registration_number
attributes.description: The official registration number assigned by the trademark office upon successful registration of the mark. Serves as the externally-known unique identifier for the trademark in the relevant jurisdiction.
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid System; USPTO TEAS; EUIPO eSearch; 15 U.S.C. § 1057

attributes.name: registration_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the trademark registration: pending (application filed, under examination), registered (officially granted), opposed (subject to third-party opposition proceedings), cancelled (registration revoked), expired (lapsed due to non-renewal), or abandoned (application withdrawn or lapsed). Critical for brand protection and commercial launch readiness.
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid System; 15 U.S.C. § 1058; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 47

attributes.name: renewal_date
attributes.description: The date by which the renewal application must be submitted to the trademark office to avoid lapse of the registration. May differ from expiry_date due to grace period provisions.
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid System Rule 30; 15 U.S.C. § 1059; EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001 Art. 53

attributes.name: renewal_reminder_date
attributes.description: The internal reminder date set for initiating the trademark renewal process, typically set a defined number of months before the official renewal_date. Supports proactive renewal management and avoidance of unintentional lapse.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; Internal IP Docketing Standards; WIPO Madrid System

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The therapeutic area or disease category for which the associated drug product is indicated (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Supports portfolio segmentation and brand strategy analytics.
attributes.references: ATC (Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical) Classification System; WHO ATC Index; ICH E8

attributes.name: trademark_name
attributes.description: The brand name, word mark, or slogan that is the subject of the trademark registration (e.g., a proprietary drug brand name). Serves as the primary human-readable identity label for the trademark record.
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid System; 15 U.S.C. § 1051 (Lanham Act); EU Trade Mark Regulation 2017/1001

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the trademark record was last modified in the system. Supports audit trail requirements, change tracking, and incremental data processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); GDPR Article 5(2); SOX; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: use_anywhere_date
attributes.description: The date on which the trademark was first used anywhere (not necessarily in commerce) in connection with the identified goods/services. Relevant for establishing priority in use-based trademark systems.

attributes.name: use_in_commerce_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Trademark First Use in Commerce Date
attributes.description: The date on which the trademark was first used in commerce in connection with the goods/services identified in the registration. Required for use-based trademark systems (e.g., USPTO) and relevant for establishing priority and defending against cancellation for non-use.

attributes.name: watch_service_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a trademark watch service is active for this mark (True), monitoring for conflicting third-party applications in the relevant jurisdictions. Supports proactive brand protection strategy.
attributes.references: WIPO Madrid System; USPTO; EUIPO; Pharmaceutical IP best practices

products.name: drug_master_file

Covers Type I-V DMFs (manufacturing site, drug substance/API, packaging, excipient, reference information). Captures DMF number, type, holder, submission/amendment dates, regulatory authority, active status, and associated substance. Supports CMC submissions and third-party API/excipient qualification for regulatory filings.
products.reference: FDA DMF / EDMF (European Drug Master File)

attributes.name: plant_id
