attributes.name: incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_incident. Business justification: Patent litigation should link to compliance incidents for IP disputes that constitute compliance or legal risk events. This enables integrated risk management across IP and compliance domains.

attributes.name: internal_counsel_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical patent litigation requires internal counsel ownership for case strategy, budget management, and outside counsel coordination. Replaces text field internal_counsel_name with employee FK

attributes.name: ip_watch_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.ip_watch. Business justification: IP watch records track competitive threats (e.g., Paragraph IV ANDA filings, competitor patent applications). When a watch escalates to actual litigation, the patent_litigation record should link back

attributes.name: masterdata_cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Litigation costs are allocated to business units; essential for legal spend tracking, forecasting, and financial impact assessment of patent disputes.

attributes.name: medicinal_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Patent litigation targets specific products (Paragraph IV, biosimilar challenges). Essential for commercial risk assessment, legal spend tracking, revenue-at-risk forecasting. Removes denormalized pro

attributes.name: orange_book_listing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.orange_book_listing. Business justification: Patent litigation in pharmaceuticals is often triggered by Paragraph IV certifications challenging Orange Book-listed patents. Linking patent_litigation to orange_book_listing tracks which Orange Book

attributes.name: regulatory_inspection_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_inspection. Business justification: Patent litigation (Paragraph IV ANDA challenges, biosimilar disputes) can trigger regulatory inspections. Inspection outcomes affect litigation strategy and settlement negotiations. Essential for coor

attributes.name: warning_letter_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.warning_letter. Business justification: Patent litigation related to data integrity violations or GXP non-compliance can result in warning letters. Litigation discovery may reveal compliance failures requiring coordinated legal and quality

attributes.name: actual_legal_spend_usd
attributes.description: Cumulative actual legal fees and costs incurred to date for this litigation matter, expressed in US dollars. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA FI/CO module legal spend tracking. Used for legal budget management and P&L reporting.
attributes.references: ASC 450; SOX Section 302; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

attributes.name: appeal_court
attributes.description: Name of the appellate court or tribunal hearing the appeal (e.g., U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, U.S. Supreme Court, EPO Board of Appeal). Null if no appeal has been filed.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 141; Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure

attributes.name: appeal_filed
attributes.description: Indicates whether an appeal has been filed following the trial court or PTAB judgment. True if an appeal is pending or has been decided; False if no appeal was filed.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 141; Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure

attributes.name: asserted_patent_numbers
attributes.description: Semicolon-delimited list of patent numbers (e.g., US9,123,456; US10,234,567) asserted or challenged in this litigation. These are the Orange Book-listed or Blue Book-listed patents at issue. Links to the patent portfolio for expiry and claim analysis.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.53; 35 U.S.C. § 271(e)(2); Orange Book (FDA Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations)

attributes.name: case_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for internal legal team notes, strategic observations, and case-specific commentary. May include attorney work product summaries, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations. Classified as confidential due to potential attorney-client privilege content.
attributes.references: Attorney-Client Privilege; Federal Rules of Evidence Rule 502; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: case_number
attributes.description: Official court-assigned or tribunal-assigned docket number uniquely identifying the litigation case (e.g., civil action number, IPR petition number, PGR petition number). Serves as the primary external business identifier for cross-referencing with legal counsel and court records.
attributes.references: USPTO Rules of Practice; 35 U.S.C. § 311 (IPR); 35 U.S.C. § 321 (PGR); 21 CFR Part 314.53

attributes.name: case_priority
attributes.description: Internal priority classification assigned to the litigation case based on revenue at risk, strategic importance, and likelihood of adverse outcome. Critical cases receive executive-level oversight; high cases are monitored by senior IP counsel; medium and low cases follow standard legal management processes.

attributes.name: case_type
attributes.description: Classification of the litigation case by legal mechanism. Paragraph IV ANDA challenges arise under Hatch-Waxman; IPR and PGR are USPTO trial proceedings; patent infringement suits are district court actions; declaratory judgment actions are filed by generic/biosimilar challengers; biosimilar patent dance refers to BPCIA exchange proceedings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: paragraph_iv_anda|inter_partes_review|post_grant_review|patent_infringement|declaratory_judgment|biosimilar_patent_dance — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §§ 271, 311, 321; 21 CFR Part 314.53; Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act (BPCIA)

attributes.name: court_or_tribunal
attributes.description: Name of the judicial or administrative body presiding over the case (e.g., U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, European Patent Office Opposition Division).
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §§ 141, 311; USPTO Trial Practice Guide; EPC Article 99

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this patent litigation record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: estimated_liability_usd
attributes.description: Management's best estimate of the potential financial exposure or liability associated with this litigation case, expressed in US dollars. Used for legal reserve provisioning, financial disclosure under ASC 450 (contingencies), and SOX compliance. Includes potential damages, lost profits, and legal costs.
attributes.references: ASC 450 (Contingencies); SOX Section 302; IAS 37 (Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets)

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the complaint, petition, or challenge was formally filed with the court or tribunal. For Paragraph IV ANDA challenges, this is the date the ANDA filer notified the NDA holder. Critical for calculating the 30-month stay period and litigation timelines.

attributes.name: first_filer_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the ANDA challenger is the first filer entitled to 180-day generic exclusivity under the Hatch-Waxman Act. True if the defendant holds first-filer status; False otherwise. Relevant for assessing the competitive landscape and timing of generic entry.
attributes.references: 21 U.S.C. § 355(j)(5)(B)(iv); Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: institution_decision_date
attributes.description: Date on which the PTAB issued its decision on whether to institute the IPR or PGR trial. A decision to institute means the petition met the threshold for review. Null for non-PTAB proceedings.

attributes.name: ipr_petition_number
attributes.description: USPTO-assigned petition number for Inter Partes Review proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB). Format follows USPTO convention (e.g., IPR2023-01234). Null for non-IPR case types.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 311; 37 CFR Part 42; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

attributes.name: judgment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the court or tribunal issued its final judgment, final written decision (for PTAB proceedings), or order. Null if the case has not yet reached judgment.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §§ 318, 328; Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 58

attributes.name: lead_outside_counsel
attributes.description: Full name of the lead attorney at the outside counsel firm responsible for managing this litigation matter. Used for escalation, communication, and legal budget accountability.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: legal_budget_usd
attributes.description: Approved annual or total budget allocated for legal fees and costs associated with this litigation matter, expressed in US dollars. Used for variance analysis against actual legal spend and budget reforecasting.
attributes.references: ASC 450; SOX Section 302; SAP S/4HANA CO Module

attributes.name: litigation_status
attributes.description: Current procedural status of the litigation case reflecting its lifecycle stage. Active cases are ongoing; settled cases have reached agreement; dismissed cases were terminated without judgment; judgment_entered reflects a court ruling; appealed cases are under appellate review; stayed cases are paused pending other proceedings; closed cases are fully resolved. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|settled|dismissed|judgment_entered|appealed|stayed|closed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

attributes.name: next_key_milestone
attributes.description: Description of the next significant procedural or substantive milestone in the litigation (e.g., claim construction hearing, expert discovery deadline, summary judgment motion, PTAB oral argument, appellate briefing deadline). Used for litigation calendar management.
attributes.references: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

attributes.name: next_milestone_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next key procedural or substantive milestone in the litigation. Used for proactive legal calendar management and escalation triggers.
attributes.references: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

attributes.name: outcome
attributes.description: Final outcome or resolution of the litigation case. Patent upheld means the challenged patent survived; patent invalidated means the patent was found invalid or unenforceable; infringement found or non-infringement found reflects district court rulings; settled indicates out-of-court resolution; dismissed indicates termination without merits ruling; consent judgment reflects agreed court order. Null for active cases. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: patent_upheld|patent_invalidated|infringement_found|non_infringement_found|settled|dismissed|consent_judgment — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §§ 282, 318, 328; Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

attributes.name: outside_counsel_firm
attributes.description: Name of the external law firm engaged to represent the company in this litigation matter. Used for legal spend tracking, conflict-of-interest management, and outside counsel performance evaluation.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302 (legal contingency disclosure); GDPR Article 28 (data processor agreements with counsel)

attributes.name: paragraph_iv_notice_date
attributes.description: Date on which the company received the formal Paragraph IV certification notice from the ANDA filer, as required under the Hatch-Waxman Act. Triggers the 45-day window to file suit and the 30-month stay. Null for non-Paragraph IV case types.

attributes.name: plaintiff_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the party initiating the litigation (typically the innovator/NDA holder asserting patent rights, or the generic/biosimilar applicant filing a declaratory judgment action). May be the company itself or a subsidiary.
attributes.references: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 10; 21 CFR Part 314.53

attributes.name: revenue_at_risk_usd
attributes.description: Estimated annual revenue at risk if the litigation outcome is unfavorable and generic or biosimilar entry occurs earlier than the patent expiry date. Expressed in US dollars. Critical input for lifecycle management decisions and commercial strategy.
attributes.references: ASC 450; SOX Section 302; ICH Q10 (lifecycle management)

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which a settlement agreement was executed between the parties, if the case was resolved through settlement rather than judgment. Null for cases resolved by judgment or still active.
attributes.references: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 41; FTC Act (reverse payment settlement scrutiny); 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: settlement_entry_date
attributes.description: Agreed date on which the generic or biosimilar entrant is permitted to launch its product under the terms of the settlement agreement. Critical for lifecycle management and revenue forecasting. Null for non-settlement outcomes.
attributes.references: Hatch-Waxman Act; FTC Act; 21 CFR Part 314.53

attributes.name: suit_filed_date
attributes.description: Date on which the NDA holder filed the patent infringement suit in response to the Paragraph IV notice, within the 45-day statutory window. Null for case types where the company is the defendant or for non-Hatch-Waxman proceedings.

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Therapeutic area or disease category associated with the drug product at the center of the litigation (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neuroscience). Enables portfolio-level analysis of litigation exposure by therapeutic area.
attributes.references: ATC Classification System (WHO); ICH E6 (GCP); FDA Therapeutic Area Guidance

attributes.name: thirty_month_stay_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the automatic 30-month stay of FDA approval of the ANDA expires under the Hatch-Waxman Act. Calculated from the date the NDA holder received the Paragraph IV certification notice. Null for non-Hatch-Waxman case types. Critical for generic entry defense strategy.

attributes.name: trial_date
attributes.description: Scheduled or actual date of the trial or oral hearing before the court or tribunal. For PTAB proceedings, this is the oral argument date. Null if trial has not been scheduled or the case settled prior to trial.
attributes.references: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this patent litigation record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking for compliance purposes.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5

products.name: patent_prosecution
products.description: Tracks patent application prosecution workflow from filing through grant or abandonment, including all annuity and maintenance fee payment obligations across all jurisdictions. Captures application number, prosecution stage, patent office, examiner, office actions received, response deadlines, prosecution attorney, prosecution strategy, and complete annuity/maintenance fee history (fee year, due dates, amounts, currencies, payment status, paying agents, confirmation receipts, grace periods, surcharge amounts). Failure to pay annuities results in patent lapse. Supports docketing, deadline management, fee compliance, cost tracking, portfolio maintenance operations, and annuity budget forecasting.

attributes.name: patent_prosecution_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each patent prosecution record in the portfolio management system. Primary key for the patent_prosecution data product.

attributes.name: patent_family_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_family. Business justification: Patent prosecution records track individual patent applications. Patent families group related applications filed across multiple jurisdictions that share a common priority. Each prosecution record sh

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: Patent prosecution tracks the application process from filing through grant. When a patent is granted, the prosecution record should link to the resulting patent master record. The grant_number in pat

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Patent prosecution activities are governed by compliance programs (inventor compensation, conflict of interest, data integrity in patent filings, confidentiality). Program controls ensure regulatory a

attributes.name: prosecution_attorney_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical IP operations assign internal attorneys to prosecution matters for docket management, office action response coordination, and quality metrics. Replaces text field prosecution_attorney

attributes.name: abandonment_date
attributes.description: Date the application was formally abandoned, either expressly by the applicant or by operation of law (e.g., failure to respond to office action within statutory period or failure to pay issue fee). Null unless prosecution_stage = 'abandoned'.

attributes.name: annuity_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which the annuity or maintenance fee for the current fee year must be paid to maintain the patent in force. Failure to pay by this date (or within the grace period) results in patent lapse. Critical docketing field.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPC Article 86; 37 CFR 1.362; PCT Rule 57

attributes.name: annuity_fee_amount
attributes.description: Base annuity or maintenance fee amount due for the current fee year, in the currency specified by annuity_fee_currency. Used for IP budget forecasting and cost tracking across the patent portfolio.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPC Article 86; USPTO Fee Schedule; EPO Fee Schedule

attributes.name: annuity_fee_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the annuity fee amount (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, CNY). Required for multi-currency portfolio cost consolidation and budget reporting.

attributes.name: annuity_fee_year
attributes.description: The renewal/annuity year number for which the most recent maintenance fee obligation applies (e.g., year 3, year 7, year 12). Annuity years are counted from the filing date in most jurisdictions. Used for fee schedule management and budget forecasting.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 41 (USPTO Maintenance Fees); EPC Article 86 (Renewal Fees); PCT Rule 57

attributes.name: annuity_grace_period_end_date
attributes.description: Last date on which the annuity fee can be paid with a surcharge before the patent lapses. Typically 6 months after annuity_due_date in most jurisdictions. After this date, the patent is irrevocably lapsed unless restoration procedures are available.

attributes.name: annuity_payment_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the annuity or maintenance fee was paid to the patent office or paying agent. Used to confirm timely payment and to calculate any applicable surcharges.

attributes.name: annuity_payment_status
attributes.description: Current payment status of the annuity/maintenance fee obligation for the current fee year. Pending = not yet due or awaiting payment; Paid = confirmed payment received; Overdue = past due date, within grace period; Lapsed = grace period expired without payment; Waived = fee waived per applicable rules.

attributes.name: annuity_surcharge_amount
attributes.description: Late payment surcharge amount applied when the annuity fee is paid after the due date but within the grace period. Tracked separately from the base fee for cost analysis and to identify patterns of late payment.

attributes.name: application_number
attributes.description: Official application number assigned by the patent office upon filing (e.g., US16/123456, EP21700001.2, PCT/US2023/012345). Serves as the primary external identifier for tracking prosecution status across jurisdictions.
attributes.references: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1; EPO Rule 41 EPC; PCT Rule 26bis

attributes.name: application_type
attributes.description: Classification of the patent application by filing type. Utility = standard non-provisional; Provisional = 12-month placeholder; PCT = Patent Cooperation Treaty international; Continuation/Divisional/CIP = derived from parent application. Determines prosecution rules and term calculations. CIP = Continuation-In-Part.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. §§ 111, 119, 120, 121; PCT Article 11; EPO Rule 36 EPC

attributes.name: claim_count
attributes.description: Total number of claims in the current version of the patent application or granted patent, including independent and dependent claims. Affects official filing fees in many jurisdictions and indicates the breadth of IP protection sought.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 112; 37 CFR 1.75; EPC Rule 43; PCT Rule 6

attributes.name: cpc_classification
attributes.description: Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) code assigned by USPTO or EPO (e.g., A61K 31/4745). More granular than IPC; used for patent analytics, freedom-to-operate (FTO) searches, and competitive landscape mapping.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this patent prosecution record was first created in the IP docketing system. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5(2)

attributes.name: examiner_art_unit
attributes.description: Patent office art unit or examination division to which the application is assigned (e.g., USPTO Art Unit 1627 for pharmaceutical compositions). Informs prosecution strategy based on art unit allowance rates and examiner tendencies.
attributes.references: USPTO MPEP § 903; EPO Technical Board of Appeal classification

attributes.name: examiner_name
attributes.description: Name of the patent examiner assigned to the application at the patent office. Used for prosecution strategy planning, examiner history analysis, and interview request management.
attributes.references: USPTO MPEP § 408; EPO Guidelines for Examination Part C

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Calculated date on which the patent expires, typically 20 years from the filing date subject to any patent term extensions (PTE), supplementary protection certificates (SPC), or pediatric exclusivity extensions. Critical for lifecycle management, generic entry forecasting, and LOE (loss of exclusivity) planning.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 154; EPC Article 63; TRIPS Agreement Article 33; 21 CFR Part 60 (PTE)

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Date the patent application was officially filed with the patent office. Establishes the priority date for prior art purposes and is the anchor for calculating the 20-year patent term under most jurisdictions. Critical for patent term extension (PTE) and supplementary protection certificate (SPC) calculations.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 111; PCT Article 11; EPC Article 80; TRIPS Agreement Article 33

attributes.name: grant_date
attributes.description: Date the patent was officially granted by the patent office. Marks the start of enforceable patent rights and triggers the annuity/maintenance fee schedule in most jurisdictions. Null until prosecution_stage = 'granted'.

attributes.name: independent_claim_count
attributes.description: Number of independent claims in the application or granted patent. Independent claims define the broadest scope of protection and are the primary focus of validity and infringement analyses.

attributes.name: invention_type
attributes.description: Pharmaceutical classification of the invention being patented. NCE (New Chemical Entity) = novel small molecule; NBE (New Biological Entity) = biologic/biosimilar; formulation = drug product composition; process = manufacturing/synthesis method; method_of_use = therapeutic indication; combination = multi-component therapy. Critical for lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry defense strategy.
attributes.references: ICH Q6A/Q6B; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Summary of Product Characteristics

attributes.name: ipc_classification
attributes.description: International Patent Classification (IPC) code assigned to the application (e.g., A61K 31/00 for pharmaceutical preparations). Used for patent landscape analysis, prior art searches, and competitive intelligence. Multiple codes may be stored as a comma-separated string.
attributes.references: WIPO IPC (International Patent Classification) 8th Edition; Strasbourg Agreement 1971

attributes.name: last_office_action_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent office action received from the patent office. Used to calculate the statutory response deadline and to trigger docketing alerts for prosecution attorneys.

attributes.name: law_firm_name
attributes.description: Name of the external patent law firm engaged for prosecution of this application, if applicable. Used for vendor management, cost tracking, and conflict-of-interest monitoring across the IP portfolio.

attributes.name: office_action_count
attributes.description: Total number of office actions (rejections, objections, or requirements) received from the patent office during prosecution of this application. Indicates prosecution complexity and is used for cost estimation and strategy assessment.
attributes.references: USPTO MPEP Chapter 700; EPO Guidelines for Examination Part C Chapter IV

attributes.name: office_action_type
attributes.description: Classification of the most recent office action received. Restriction = requirement to elect claims; Non-final = first substantive rejection; Final = final rejection after response; Advisory = after final response; Allowance/Notice of Allowance = claims approved for grant.
attributes.references: USPTO MPEP §§ 706, 821; EPO Guidelines for Examination Part C

attributes.name: parent_application_number
attributes.description: Application number of the parent patent application from which this application claims priority (applicable for continuation, divisional, or CIP applications). Used to reconstruct the patent family hierarchy and assess claim scope relative to the parent.

attributes.name: patent_office_code
attributes.description: Two- or three-letter code identifying the national or regional patent office handling the application (e.g., US = USPTO, EP = EPO, JP = JPO/PMDA, CN = CNIPA, WO = WIPO PCT). Drives jurisdiction-specific deadline rules and annuity schedules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: US|EP|JP|CN|WO|GB|DE|FR|CA|AU|IN|KR|BR|MX|RU — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WIPO ST.3 (Two-letter codes for countries); PCT Rule 4.9

attributes.name: paying_agent_name
