attributes.name: opposition_filed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a third party (e.g., generic manufacturer, biosimilar applicant) has filed an opposition, invalidity action, or equivalent challenge against this patent term extension or SPC. True triggers escalation to the legal team for litigation management and LOE date reassessment.
attributes.references: EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 15; 35 U.S.C. § 156; EPC Art. 105; CJEU SPC litigation precedents

attributes.name: orphan_drug_exclusivity
attributes.description: Indicates whether the product covered by this extension also benefits from orphan drug exclusivity (7 years in the US under the Orphan Drug Act, 10 years in the EU under Regulation (EC) No 141/2000). Used in conjunction with PTE/SPC to determine the effective exclusivity cliff date.
attributes.references: 21 U.S.C. § 360cc (Orphan Drug Act); EU Regulation (EC) No 141/2000; FDA Office of Orphan Products Development

attributes.name: pediatric_extension_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this patent term extension or SPC is eligible for an additional 6-month pediatric extension under the US Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) or EU Paediatric Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006. True if a Written Request (US) or Paediatric Investigation Plan (EU) has been completed and accepted.
attributes.references: 21 U.S.C. § 505A (BPCA); EU Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006 Art. 36; FDA Pediatric Exclusivity Guidance

attributes.name: pediatric_extension_granted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the additional 6-month pediatric extension has been formally granted on top of the base PTE or SPC. Distinct from eligibility — this flag confirms the authority has approved the pediatric supplement. When True, the adjusted_expiry_date should reflect the additional 6 months.
attributes.references: 21 U.S.C. § 505A; EU Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006 Art. 36; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: regulatory_review_period_days
attributes.description: The total number of days of the regulatory review period as determined by the granting authority. For US PTE, this is the period from IND filing to NDA/BLA approval, reduced by any applicant-caused delays. Directly determines the maximum permissible extension duration under 35 U.S.C. § 156.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 156(g); FDA 21 CFR Part 60; EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 13

attributes.name: spc_product_definition
attributes.description: For EU/UK SPC applications only: the definition of the 'product' as per Article 1(b) of EU Regulation 469/2009, specifying the active ingredient or combination of active ingredients of a medicinal product. This definition determines the scope of SPC protection and is critical for freedom-to-operate analyses and generic entry defense.
attributes.references: EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 Art. 1(b); CJEU Case C-322/10 (Medeva); CJEU Case C-493/12 (Eli Lilly)

attributes.name: testing_phase_start_date
attributes.description: For US PTE calculations: the date on which the regulatory review testing phase began, typically the date of IND (Investigational New Drug) application submission. Used to calculate the testing phase component of the regulatory review period under 35 U.S.C. § 156(g)(1).
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 156(g)(1); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; FDA 21 CFR Part 60

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The therapeutic area or disease indication for which the drug product covered by the extension is approved (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neurology). Used for portfolio analytics, lifecycle management planning, and commercial strategy alignment.
attributes.references: ATC Classification (WHO); ICH E8; FDA Therapeutic Area Guidance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this patent term extension record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking for IP portfolio management and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX; Veeva Vault RIM

attributes.name: veeva_vault_document_reference
attributes.description: The document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management) where the official extension application documents, correspondence with the granting authority, and supporting regulatory dossier are stored. Enables direct navigation from this record to the source regulatory documents.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11 (Electronic Records)

products.name: ip_watch
products.description: Competitive intelligence records tracking third-party IP activities that may threaten the company's portfolio. Monitors competitor patent filings, ANDA/505(b)(2) submissions, biosimilar applications (aBLA), and patent challenges. Captures watch type, competitor, filing date, reference number, technology area, affected products, risk assessment, and recommended response. Supports proactive IP defense and early warning for generic/biosimilar entry.
products.reference: Competitive IP Intelligence / ANDA Paragraph IV Watch

attributes.name: ip_watch_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each IP watch record tracking a third-party IP activity that may threaten the company's portfolio.

attributes.name: country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Competitive intelligence is jurisdiction-specific; required for paragraph IV response planning, biosimilar monitoring, and market-specific threat assessment.

attributes.name: lead_patent_counsel_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Lead Patent Counsel Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical competitive intelligence assigns internal IP counsel to watch items for threat assessment, paragraph IV response coordination, and litigation decision-making. Replaces text field lead_p

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: IP watch records track competitive intelligence on third-party patents that may threaten the company's freedom to operate. The patent_number (STRING) should be replaced with a FK to patent.patent_id t

attributes.name: risk_register_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_risk_register. Business justification: IP watch activities (competitor filings, Paragraph IV notices, biosimilar applications) identify compliance risks (exclusivity loss, revenue at risk, litigation exposure) that populate risk registers

attributes.name: affected_ndc
attributes.description: The National Drug Code (NDC) of the specific drug product formulation or SKU threatened by the competitor's filing. Enables precise linkage to the commercial product portfolio and Orange Book listings.

attributes.name: affected_product_name
attributes.description: The proprietary or International Nonproprietary Name (INN) of the company's drug product that is potentially threatened by the competitor's IP activity. Supports linkage to commercial and lifecycle management decisions.
attributes.references: WHO INN Programme; FDA Orange Book; Internal Product Master

attributes.name: authority_name
attributes.description: The name of the regulatory or intellectual property authority with which the competitor's filing was made, such as FDA, EMA, USPTO, EPO, PMDA, or NMPA. Provides context for applicable rules and timelines.
attributes.references: FDA; EMA; USPTO; EPO; PMDA; NMPA; ICH

attributes.name: biosimilar_interchangeability
attributes.description: Indicates whether the competitor's aBLA biosimilar application seeks an interchangeability designation with the company's reference biologic product. Interchangeable biosimilars may be substituted at the pharmacy level without prescriber intervention, representing a higher commercial threat.
attributes.references: 42 U.S.C. § 262(k)(4); FDA Biosimilar Interchangeability Guidance; BPCIA (Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act)

attributes.name: closed_date
attributes.description: The date on which the IP watch record was formally closed, indicating that the threat has been resolved, the litigation concluded, the competitor's application was withdrawn or rejected, or the matter is no longer actively monitored.

attributes.name: commercial_revenue_at_risk
attributes.description: Estimated annual revenue (in USD) of the affected product that is at risk of erosion if the competitor's generic or biosimilar entry is successful. Used to prioritize IP defense investment and inform lifecycle management decisions.
attributes.references: Internal Commercial Finance Policy; SOX Financial Reporting Compliance

attributes.name: competitor_country
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country of incorporation or principal operations of the competitor entity filing the IP activity.

attributes.name: competitor_name
attributes.description: Name of the third-party company or entity that filed the competing patent, ANDA, aBLA, or patent challenge being monitored. Critical for competitive intelligence and IP defense strategy.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this IP watch record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: detected_date
attributes.description: The date on which the company's IP watch function first identified or was notified of the competitor's filing or IP activity. Used to measure response time and early warning effectiveness.

attributes.name: estimated_generic_entry_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Generic or Biosimilar Market Entry Date
attributes.description: The estimated date on which the competitor's generic drug or biosimilar product could enter the market, based on patent expiry, exclusivity expiry, regulatory approval timelines, and litigation outcomes. Critical for lifecycle management and revenue forecasting.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; FDA Biosimilar Product Information; Internal Lifecycle Management Framework

attributes.name: exclusivity_at_risk
attributes.description: The type of regulatory exclusivity period that may be threatened or circumvented by the competitor's filing, such as orphan drug exclusivity, data exclusivity, pediatric exclusivity, New Chemical Entity (NCE) exclusivity, New Biological Entity (NBE) exclusivity, or Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) protection.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.108 (NCE Exclusivity); Orphan Drug Act; BPCIA; Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Exclusivity Database

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the competitor filed the patent application, ANDA, aBLA, or patent challenge with the relevant regulatory or IP authority. This is the principal real-world event date for the watch record.
attributes.references: USPTO Filing Rules; 21 CFR Part 314.94; EMA Biosimilar Guidelines

attributes.name: filing_reference_number
attributes.description: The official reference number assigned by the regulatory or IP authority to the competitor's filing, such as an ANDA application number, aBLA application number, USPTO patent application number, or IPR petition number. Enables direct cross-referencing with public databases.
attributes.references: FDA ANDA Database; USPTO Patent Center; EMA Biosimilar Register

attributes.name: fto_analysis_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis is required in response to the competitor's patent filing or IP activity, to assess whether the company's products or processes may infringe the competitor's claims.
attributes.references: Internal IP Due Diligence SOP; USPTO Patent Examination Guidelines

attributes.name: fto_analysis_status
attributes.description: Current status of the Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis associated with this IP watch record, tracking whether the analysis has been initiated, is in progress, or has been completed.

attributes.name: lawsuit_filed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the company has filed a patent infringement lawsuit in response to the competitor's Paragraph IV certification or other IP challenge. Triggers the 30-month stay of FDA approval under Hatch-Waxman.

attributes.name: lawsuit_filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the company filed the patent infringement lawsuit in response to the IP threat. Must be within 45 days of receiving the Paragraph IV notice letter to trigger the 30-month stay.

attributes.name: outside_counsel_firm
attributes.description: Name of the external law firm engaged to represent the company in litigation or IP proceedings related to this watch record. Classified as confidential due to legal strategy sensitivity.
attributes.references: Internal Legal Engagement Policy; Attorney-Client Privilege Guidelines

attributes.name: paragraph_iv_certification
attributes.description: Indicates whether the competitor's ANDA or 505(b)(2) submission includes a Paragraph IV certification asserting that the company's listed patent is invalid or will not be infringed. Triggers the 30-month stay provision under the Hatch-Waxman Act.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.94(a)(12)(i)(A)(4); Hatch-Waxman Act (Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act)

attributes.name: paragraph_iv_notice_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Paragraph IV Notice Letter Receipt Date
attributes.description: The date on which the company received the formal Paragraph IV notice letter from the ANDA or 505(b)(2) applicant, as required under the Hatch-Waxman Act. The 45-day window to file suit and trigger the 30-month stay begins from this date.

attributes.name: recommended_response
attributes.description: The recommended strategic or legal response to the identified IP threat, such as filing a patent infringement lawsuit, filing an IPR petition, seeking a preliminary injunction, entering licensing negotiations, or monitoring without action. Classified as confidential due to legal strategy sensitivity.
attributes.references: Internal IP Defense Strategy SOP; USPTO IPR Rules (37 CFR Part 42)

attributes.name: resolution_outcome
attributes.description: The final outcome of the IP dispute or watch activity upon closure, indicating whether the matter was settled (e.g., licensing agreement), won by the company, lost (competitor entry permitted), withdrawn by the competitor, dismissed by the authority, or remains ongoing.
attributes.references: Internal IP Litigation Tracking SOP; USPTO Trial and Appeal Board Rules

attributes.name: response_deadline
attributes.description: The statutory or internally-set deadline by which the company must initiate a legal or regulatory response to the IP threat (e.g., 45-day deadline to file suit following Paragraph IV notice, IPR petition deadline of 1 year from service of infringement complaint).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.107; 35 U.S.C. § 315(b) (IPR Petition Deadline); Hatch-Waxman Act

attributes.name: risk_assessment_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the risk assessment conducted by the IP and legal team, describing the basis for the risk level assignment, key vulnerabilities, and potential commercial exposure. Classified as confidential due to legal strategy sensitivity.
attributes.references: Internal IP Risk Assessment SOP; Attorney-Client Privilege Guidelines

attributes.name: risk_level
attributes.description: Assessed risk level of the IP threat to the company's portfolio, reflecting the likelihood of successful generic or biosimilar entry and the commercial impact. Drives prioritization of legal and IP defense resources.
attributes.references: Internal IP Risk Assessment Framework; ICH Q9 (Quality Risk Management)

attributes.name: technology_area
attributes.description: The scientific or technical domain of the IP activity, such as small molecule chemistry, biologics, formulation technology, manufacturing process, delivery device, or specific therapeutic mechanism. Aligns with internal R&D and IP portfolio taxonomy.
attributes.references: ICH Q8 (Pharmaceutical Development); ICH Q11 (Development and Manufacture of Drug Substances)

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: The disease or clinical indication area relevant to the IP activity, such as oncology, immunology, rare diseases, cardiovascular, or neurology. Used to prioritize IP defense resources by commercial importance.
attributes.references: WHO ATC Classification; Internal Therapeutic Area Taxonomy

attributes.name: thirty_month_stay_expiry
attributes.description: The date on which the 30-month stay of FDA approval expires following a Paragraph IV certification and timely patent infringement lawsuit. Null if no Paragraph IV certification was filed. Critical for generic entry timeline planning.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this IP watch record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: watch_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, observations, or legal strategy notes related to the IP watch record, entered by the IP analyst or legal counsel. Classified as confidential due to potential legal strategy content.

attributes.name: watch_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier assigned to this IP watch record, used for cross-referencing with legal counsel, RIMS, and Veeva Vault RIM module. Typically follows a structured format such as IPW-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; Internal IP Management SOP

attributes.name: watch_source
attributes.description: The source or monitoring service through which the IP activity was identified, such as FDA Orange Book, FDA ANDA database, USPTO patent database, EPO database, EMA biosimilar register, Derwent Innovation, Clarivate IP watch service, or internal monitoring. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fda_orange_book|fda_anda_database|uspto_database|epo_database|ema_register|derwent_innovation|clarivate_watch|internal_monitoring|third_party_service — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; USPTO Patent Center; EPO Espacenet; EMA Biosimilar Register

attributes.name: watch_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the IP watch record, indicating whether the threat is newly identified (open), being assessed (under_review), escalated to legal or senior management, actively monitored (monitoring), or resolved (closed).

attributes.name: watch_type
attributes.description: Classification of the third-party IP activity being monitored. Covers competitor patent filings, Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) submissions, 505(b)(2) submissions, abbreviated Biologics License Application (aBLA) biosimilar filings, patent challenges (e.g., IPR, PGR, inter partes review), and trademark oppositions.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314 (ANDA); 21 CFR Part 351 (aBLA); USPTO Inter Partes Review Rules; FDA Orange Book

products.name: ip_valuation
products.description: Financial valuation records for IP assets including patents, trademarks, trade secrets, and know-how portfolios. Used for balance sheet reporting (IAS 38 intangible asset recognition), M&A due diligence, licensing negotiations, tax transfer pricing, and impairment testing. Captures valuation date, valuation method (income approach/DCF, market approach, cost approach, relief-from-royalty), IP asset reference, valuation currency, fair market value, useful economic life, amortization method, carrying value, discount rate, and valuation firm. Supports R&D capitalization decisions and SOX-compliant financial reporting.

attributes.name: ip_valuation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each IP valuation record in the pharmaceutical IP portfolio. Primary key for the ip_valuation data product.

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: IP valuations determine carrying value of capitalized patents/trademarks in fixed asset register. Finance links valuation reports to asset records for purchase price allocation (M&A), impairment testi

attributes.name: lead_valuator_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical finance requires tracking which employee conducted IP valuations for SOX compliance, transfer pricing documentation, and impairment testing. Replaces text field lead_valuator_name with

attributes.name: medicinal_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: IP valuations driven by product commercial forecasts. Essential for M&A, impairment testing, transfer pricing, and portfolio prioritization. Removes denormalized inn and nda_bla_number.

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patent record in the intellectual.patent product that is the subject of this valuation. Enables linkage to patent expiry, exclusivity periods, and prosecution status for lifecycle management decisions.

attributes.name: rd_capitalization_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.rd_capitalization. Business justification: IP valuations determine fair value of capitalized R&D for purchase price allocation, impairment testing, and transfer pricing studies. Finance links valuation reports to capitalized R&D records for ca

attributes.name: amortization_method
attributes.description: Accounting method used to systematically allocate the cost of the intangible IP asset over its useful economic life. Straight-line is most common for pharmaceutical patents; units-of-production may be used for process IP tied to manufacturing volume; not_amortized applies to indefinite-life intangibles such as certain trademarks.

attributes.name: annual_amortization_charge
attributes.description: Annual amortization expense amount for the IP asset in the valuation currency, calculated based on the carrying value and amortization method. Used for P&L reporting, R&D capitalization decisions, and COGS allocation in pharmaceutical financial statements.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the valuation was formally approved by the authorized internal reviewer. Marks the transition of valuation_status from in_review to approved and establishes the effective date for financial reporting use.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the internal finance or legal authority who approved the valuation for use in financial reporting or business decisions. Required for SOX-compliant internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR).
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; IAS 38; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records)

attributes.name: carrying_value
attributes.description: Net book value of the IP asset on the balance sheet as of the valuation date, after accumulated amortization and any impairment charges. Compared against fair market value to determine whether an impairment loss must be recognized under IAS 36.
attributes.references: IAS 38 para 74; IAS 36 Impairment of Assets; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this IP valuation record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the audit trail creation marker required for SOX-compliant internal controls and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

attributes.name: development_stage
attributes.description: Current clinical or regulatory development stage of the drug or biologic associated with the IP asset at the time of valuation. Determines applicable probability of success benchmarks and valuation methodology. Aligns with IND/NDA/BLA lifecycle stages as defined by FDA and ICH guidelines. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: discovery|preclinical|phase_1|phase_2|phase_3|nda_bla_filed|approved|post_market — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312 (IND); FDA 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); ICH E8; IAS 38

attributes.name: discount_rate_pct
attributes.description: Risk-adjusted discount rate (expressed as a percentage, e.g., 12.50 for 12.5%) applied in the income approach or DCF valuation to convert projected future cash flows to present value. Reflects the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) or IP-specific risk premium. Critical input for sensitivity analysis and impairment testing.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 210; IAS 36 para 55; OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines Chapter VI

attributes.name: exclusivity_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most commercially significant regulatory exclusivity period (data exclusivity, orphan drug exclusivity, or pediatric exclusivity) expires for the IP asset. Represents the effective end of market protection and is a critical input to the DCF projection horizon and generic/biosimilar entry defense strategy.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; Hatch-Waxman Act; Orphan Drug Act; IAS 38

attributes.name: fair_market_value
attributes.description: Estimated fair market value of the IP asset as of the valuation date, expressed in the valuation currency. Represents the price at which the asset would change hands between a willing buyer and willing seller, neither being under compulsion. Used for IAS 38 intangible asset recognition and balance sheet reporting.
attributes.references: IAS 38 para 74; IVSC IVS 104 Bases of Value; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: impairment_indicator_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more impairment indicators (as defined under IAS 36) were identified for this IP asset at the valuation date. Triggers a formal impairment test when True. Indicators include clinical trial failure, regulatory rejection, loss of market exclusivity, or significant decline in projected revenues.
attributes.references: IAS 36 Impairment of Assets para 12; IAS 38; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: impairment_loss_amount
attributes.description: Amount by which the carrying value exceeds the recoverable amount of the IP asset, recognized as an impairment loss in the income statement. Populated only when impairment_indicator_flag is True and a formal impairment test confirms the loss. Expressed in valuation currency.

attributes.name: ip_asset_type
attributes.description: Classification of the IP asset being valued. Determines applicable valuation methodology and accounting treatment under IAS 38. Patents cover NCE/NBE/formulation/process IP; trademarks cover brand assets; trade secrets and know-how cover undisclosed proprietary information; exclusivity types cover regulatory-granted market protections. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: patent|trademark|trade_secret|know_how|data_exclusivity|orphan_drug_exclusivity|dmf|rems — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
attributes.references: IAS 38 Intangible Assets; IVSC IVS 210 Intangible Assets

attributes.name: litigation_support_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this valuation was prepared in connection with patent infringement litigation, inter partes review (IPR), or other IP dispute proceedings. When True, the valuation is subject to legal privilege considerations and must be coordinated with external patent litigation counsel.
attributes.references: 35 USC 284 (Patent Damages); IVSC IVS 101; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Date by which this valuation must be reviewed or refreshed. Typically set annually for balance sheet reporting or triggered by material changes in the IP asset's commercial prospects (e.g., clinical trial readout, regulatory decision, competitive entry). Supports proactive impairment monitoring.

attributes.name: peak_sales_forecast
attributes.description: Projected peak annual net sales attributable to the IP asset, expressed in valuation currency. Key input to income approach and relief-from-royalty DCF models. Derived from commercial forecasting models and used in licensing negotiation and M&A due diligence.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 210; OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines Chapter VI; IAS 38

attributes.name: probability_of_success_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Probability of Technical and Regulatory Success Percentage
attributes.description: Risk-adjusted probability (expressed as a percentage, e.g., 65.00 for 65%) that the IP asset will achieve full commercial realization, accounting for clinical development risk, regulatory approval probability, and market access uncertainty. Applied as a risk adjustment factor in rNPV (risk-adjusted Net Present Value) income approach valuations.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 210; ICH E8; FDA Guidance on Clinical Development; IAS 38

attributes.name: rd_capitalization_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the IP asset meets the IAS 38 criteria for capitalization of development costs (technical feasibility, intention to complete, ability to use/sell, probable future economic benefits, adequate resources, ability to measure expenditure). When True, associated development costs are capitalized rather than expensed.

attributes.name: report_issue_date
attributes.description: Date on which the formal valuation report was issued by the valuation firm or internal team. May differ from valuation_date when retrospective valuations are performed for M&A due diligence or tax transfer pricing purposes.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 103 Reporting; IAS 38; OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines

attributes.name: risk_adjusted_npv
attributes.description: Risk-adjusted net present value of the IP asset, calculated by applying the probability_of_success_pct to the DCF-derived NPV. Standard valuation metric in pharmaceutical IP for assets still in clinical development. Expressed in valuation currency.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 210; IAS 38; ICH E8; FDA Guidance on Clinical Development

attributes.name: royalty_rate_pct
attributes.description: Notional or actual royalty rate (expressed as a percentage of net sales) used in the relief-from-royalty valuation method or as the basis for intercompany licensing transfer pricing. Derived from comparable uncontrolled transactions or industry benchmarks for the relevant therapeutic area and IP type.
attributes.references: OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines Chapter VI; IVSC IVS 210; IAS 38

attributes.name: sap_asset_number
attributes.description: SAP S/4HANA Fixed Asset (FI-AA module) asset number assigned to the intangible IP asset on the balance sheet. Enables reconciliation between the IP valuation record and the SAP general ledger intangible asset register for IAS 38 balance sheet reporting and amortization posting.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; IAS 38; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Therapeutic area classification of the drug or biologic associated with the IP asset (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Used for portfolio segmentation, royalty rate benchmarking, and comparable transaction analysis in market approach valuations.

attributes.name: transfer_pricing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this valuation was prepared specifically to support intercompany IP licensing transfer pricing documentation under OECD guidelines. When True, the valuation must comply with OECD BEPS Action 8-10 arm's length principle requirements and be included in the transfer pricing master file.
attributes.references: OECD BEPS Action 8-10; OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines Chapter VI; IAS 38

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this IP valuation record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for SOX audit trail, data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer, and change detection in downstream financial reporting pipelines.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

attributes.name: useful_economic_life_years
attributes.description: Estimated remaining useful economic life of the IP asset in years as of the valuation date. For patents, typically aligned with remaining patent term or commercial exclusivity period. Drives amortization schedule and DCF projection horizon under IAS 38.
attributes.references: IAS 38 para 88-96; IVSC IVS 210; ICH Q10

attributes.name: valuation_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the valuation amounts (fair market value, carrying value, royalty rate base) are expressed. Enables multi-currency consolidation for global pharmaceutical IP portfolios.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IAS 21 Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates; IAS 38

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The reference date as of which the IP asset fair market value is determined. This is the principal business event date for the valuation — distinct from the date the report was issued or approved. Required for IAS 38 impairment testing and balance sheet reporting.
attributes.references: IAS 38 para 74; IVSC IVS 103 Reporting; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: valuation_firm_name
attributes.description: Name of the external valuation firm or internal team that performed the IP valuation. Required for SOX audit trail and independence assessment. For external valuations, this is the registered firm name (e.g., Big Four accounting firm, specialist IP valuation boutique).
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; IVSC IVS 103 Reporting; IAS 38

attributes.name: valuation_method
attributes.description: Primary valuation methodology applied to determine the IP asset value. Income DCF (Discounted Cash Flow) projects future cash flows attributable to the IP; Relief-from-Royalty estimates value as avoided royalty payments; Market Comparable benchmarks against observable transactions; Cost Approach estimates reproduction/replacement cost; Multi-Period Excess Earnings (MPEEM) isolates IP contribution from total business earnings.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 210 Intangible Assets; IAS 38; OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines Chapter VI

attributes.name: valuation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for material assumptions, key value drivers, sensitivity analysis commentary, or qualifications noted by the valuator. Captures context that cannot be expressed in structured fields, such as market access assumptions, competitive landscape considerations, or regulatory risk factors specific to the IP asset.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 103 Reporting; IAS 38; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: valuation_purpose
attributes.description: Business purpose for which this valuation was commissioned. Determines applicable standard of value and reporting requirements. Balance sheet and impairment test valuations must comply with IAS 38/IAS 36; M&A due diligence supports deal pricing; transfer pricing supports OECD-compliant intercompany IP licensing; litigation support valuations are prepared for patent infringement proceedings.
attributes.references: IAS 38; IAS 36 Impairment of Assets; OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines; IVSC IVS 101

attributes.name: valuation_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric reference number assigned to this valuation engagement, typically issued by the valuation firm or internal finance team. Used for cross-referencing with audit files, board papers, and external valuation reports.
attributes.references: IAS 38; SOX Section 302/404; IVSC International Valuation Standards

attributes.name: valuation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the valuation record. Draft indicates work-in-progress; in_review indicates submission to finance/legal for approval; approved indicates SOX-compliant sign-off; superseded indicates replaced by a newer valuation; withdrawn indicates cancelled prior to approval.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; IAS 38; IVSC International Valuation Standards

attributes.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault (RIM or QualityDocs module) for the formal valuation report and supporting documentation. Enables direct retrieval of the source valuation report for audit, due diligence, and regulatory inspection purposes.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX Section 302/404; Veeva Vault RIM

products.name: invention_disclosure
products.description: Internal invention disclosure records submitted by R&D scientists and engineers as the first step in the patent filing process. Captures disclosure number, title, inventors, submission date, business unit, technology area, compound or process described, novelty assessment, commercial relevance assessment, IP committee review status, recommended action (file patent, maintain as trade secret, publish defensively, abandon), and decision date. Bridges R&D innovation with IP prosecution workflow.

attributes.name: invention_disclosure_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the invention disclosure record. Primary key for the invention_disclosure data product.

attributes.name: drug_substance_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_substance. Business justification: Early-stage invention disclosures for NCEs reference specific drug substances. Essential for patent prosecution strategy, portfolio planning, and R&D-IP alignment. Removes denormalized compound identi

attributes.name: lead_inventor_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical R&D requires tracking lead inventors as employees for invention assignment execution, inventor compensation, and patent prosecution initiation. Replaces text field lead_inventor_name wi

attributes.name: patent_family_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_family. Business justification: Invention disclosures may be filed as part of a broader patent family strategy (e.g., filing in multiple jurisdictions, continuation applications). Linking invention_disclosure to patent_family enable

attributes.name: patent_prosecution_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_prosecution. Business justification: Invention disclosure is the first step in the IP lifecycle, submitted by R&D scientists. When a disclosure is approved for patent filing, it should link to the resulting patent_prosecution record. The

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Invention disclosures are governed by compliance programs (inventor rights, conflict of interest, confidentiality, assignment agreements). Program controls ensure regulatory compliance and ethical con

attributes.name: business_unit
attributes.description: Organizational business unit or division within the company that originated the invention (e.g., Oncology R&D, Biologics Research, Process Development, CMC). Determines IP ownership allocation and budget accountability.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; ICH Q10

attributes.name: co_inventor_names
attributes.description: Semicolon-delimited list of full names of all co-inventors contributing to the disclosed invention. Required for complete inventorship declaration on patent applications per USPTO and EPC requirements.
attributes.references: USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 115; GDPR Article 4; EPC Article 81

attributes.name: commercial_relevance_score
attributes.description: IP committee or business development assessment of the commercial value and strategic importance of the invention to the company's pipeline and market position. Influences prioritization of patent prosecution resources.
attributes.references: WIPO IP Valuation Guidelines; HEOR Framework

attributes.name: confidentiality_level
attributes.description: Data classification level assigned to this invention disclosure record, governing access controls and information handling. Restricted disclosures contain highly sensitive IP; confidential disclosures are for internal use only.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5; 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 27001; Defend Trade Secrets Act

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: SAP cost center code associated with the business unit that originated the invention disclosure. Used for IP prosecution cost allocation and financial reporting.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when the invention disclosure record was first created in the IP management system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver layer.

attributes.name: decision_date
attributes.description: Date on which the final disposition decision (file patent, trade secret, defensive publication, or abandon) was formally approved and recorded. Marks the closure of the IP committee review cycle for this disclosure.
attributes.references: WIPO IP Management Guidelines; USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 111

attributes.name: defensive_publication_date
attributes.description: Date on which the invention was published defensively (e.g., via Research Disclosure or IP.com) to create prior art and prevent third parties from patenting the same invention. Null if defensive publication was not the chosen disposition.

attributes.name: disclosure_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally-known reference number assigned to the invention disclosure upon submission (e.g., ID-2024-00123). Used by R&D, IP counsel, and IP committee to track the disclosure through the prosecution workflow.
attributes.references: USPTO Best Practices; WIPO IP Management Guidelines

attributes.name: disclosure_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the invention disclosure record within the IP prosecution workflow. Tracks progression from initial draft through IP committee decision.

attributes.name: disclosure_type
attributes.description: Classification of the invention disclosure by the nature of the intellectual property: New Chemical Entity (NCE), New Biological Entity (NBE), formulation, manufacturing process, combination product, platform technology, or other. Drives patent strategy and prosecution approach. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: nce|nbe|formulation|process|combination|platform|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: USPTO Classification; ICH Q6A; ICH Q6B; WIPO IPC

attributes.name: elb_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this invention disclosure to the corresponding experiment records in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides the evidentiary basis for the invention and supports conception and reduction-to-practice documentation.
attributes.references: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; 21 CFR Part 11; USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 102

attributes.name: external_counsel_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier or matter number assigned by external patent counsel (law firm) handling the prosecution of the patent application derived from this disclosure. Enables coordination between internal IP team and outside counsel.

attributes.name: fto_assessment_status
attributes.description: Status of the Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis conducted to determine whether commercializing the invention would infringe third-party patents. FTO clearance is a prerequisite for commercial development decisions.
attributes.references: USPTO; EPC; WIPO IP Management Guidelines; ICH Q10

attributes.name: fto_clearance_opinion
attributes.description: Legal opinion outcome of the FTO analysis: clear (no blocking third-party patents identified), risk identified (potential infringement risk), conditional clear (clear subject to design-around or licensing), or not assessed. Informs go/no-go decisions for development.
attributes.references: USPTO; EPC; WIPO IP Management Guidelines

attributes.name: inventive_step_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the disclosed invention satisfies the non-obviousness (US) or inventive step (EP/PCT) requirement for patentability. Evaluated by IP counsel in conjunction with prior art search findings.
attributes.references: USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 103; EPC Article 56; ICH Q10

attributes.name: inventor_assignment_signed
attributes.description: Indicates whether all inventors have signed the invention assignment agreement transferring IP ownership to the company. A signed assignment is a legal prerequisite for the company to file and own the resulting patent.
attributes.references: USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 261; WIPO IP Management Guidelines; Employment IP Assignment Agreements

attributes.name: inventor_employee_ids
attributes.description: Semicolon-delimited list of internal employee identifiers for all inventors (lead and co-inventors). Used to link inventors to HR records for assignment agreements and inventorship verification.

attributes.name: ip_committee_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the IP committee formally reviewed the invention disclosure and reached a recommendation. Null if review has not yet occurred.

attributes.name: ip_committee_review_status
attributes.description: Current status of the invention disclosure within the IP committee review process. Tracks whether the disclosure has been submitted to the committee, is under active review, has been reviewed, or has been deferred for additional information.
attributes.references: WIPO IP Management Guidelines; ISO 9001; ICH Q10

attributes.name: novelty_assessment
attributes.description: IP counsel or IP committee assessment of whether the disclosed invention meets the novelty requirement for patentability based on prior art search results. Informs the recommended action decision.
attributes.references: USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 102; EPC Article 54; PCT Rule 33

attributes.name: pipeline_compound_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the invention is directly associated with an active pipeline compound or program. Pipeline-linked disclosures receive elevated IP prosecution priority and are tracked in lifecycle management reviews.
attributes.references: ICH Q10; WIPO IP Management Guidelines

attributes.name: prior_art_search_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal prior art search has been conducted for this invention disclosure. A completed prior art search is a prerequisite for the IP committee's patentability recommendation.
attributes.references: USPTO MPEP § 704; EPC Rule 61; PCT Rule 33

attributes.name: prior_art_search_date
attributes.description: Date on which the prior art search was completed by IP counsel or a designated patent search firm. Used to assess the currency of the search relative to the filing decision.

attributes.name: provisional_filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which a provisional patent application was filed with the USPTO based on this invention disclosure. Establishes the priority date for the subsequent non-provisional application. Null if no provisional was filed.

attributes.name: recommended_action
attributes.description: IP committee's recommended disposition for the invention disclosure: file a patent application, maintain as a trade secret, publish defensively to create prior art, or abandon. Drives the downstream IP prosecution workflow.
attributes.references: USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 111; WIPO IP Management Guidelines; EPC Article 75

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the invention disclosure was formally submitted by the inventor(s) to the IP department. Establishes the internal priority date for IP prosecution planning.

attributes.name: target_filing_date
attributes.description: Planned date by which the patent application derived from this disclosure should be filed, as determined by IP counsel and the IP committee. Used for prosecution timeline management and resource planning.
attributes.references: USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 102; WIPO IP Management Guidelines

attributes.name: technology_area
attributes.description: Scientific or technical domain to which the invention belongs (e.g., small molecule synthesis, biologics, formulation, process chemistry, drug delivery, diagnostics, digital health). Used for IP portfolio segmentation and committee routing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologics|formulation|process_chemistry|drug_delivery|diagnostics|digital_health|medical_device|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ATC Classification; ICH Q8; ISPE GAMP

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Clinical or disease area that the invention is intended to address (e.g., oncology, immunology, rare diseases, neurology, cardiovascular). Aligns with the company's pipeline and commercial strategy for IP portfolio prioritization.
attributes.references: ATC Classification; WHO ICD-11; ICH E6

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Descriptive title of the invention as provided by the submitting inventor(s). Summarizes the subject matter of the disclosure for IP committee review and patent prosecution purposes.
attributes.references: USPTO 37 CFR 1.72; WIPO IP Management Guidelines

attributes.name: trade_secret_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the invention has been designated as a trade secret rather than being filed as a patent application. Trade secret designation triggers specific confidentiality controls and access restrictions under the Defend Trade Secrets Act (DTSA) and applicable law.
attributes.references: Defend Trade Secrets Act (DTSA) 18 U.S.C. § 1836; EU Trade Secrets Directive 2016/943; GDPR

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording the most recent modification to the invention disclosure record. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking for IP governance and 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.

attributes.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault (RIM or QualityDocs module) where the signed invention disclosure form and supporting documentation are stored. Ensures traceability between the data record and the controlled document.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10

products.name: orange_book_listing
products.description: Records of patents and exclusivities listed in the FDA Orange Book (Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations) for each NDA/ANDA product. Captures NDA number, product name, active ingredient, dosage form, strength, listed patent number, patent expiry date, exclusivity code, exclusivity expiry date, and listing status. Directly governs generic entry timelines and Paragraph IV challenge eligibility. Analogous listings for EU (Article 10 reference) and other markets are also captured.

attributes.name: orange_book_listing_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each Orange Book listing record in the intellectual property portfolio system. Primary key for this data product.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.53 (FDA Orange Book Patent Listing Requirements)

attributes.name: drug_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.drug_product. Business justification: Orange Book listings reference specific drug products (NDC-level). Essential for generic competition monitoring, Paragraph IV strategy, and patent-product linkage accuracy. Removes denormalized identi

attributes.name: exclusivity_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.exclusivity_period. Business justification: FDA Orange Book listings include both patent and exclusivity information. The exclusivity_code and exclusivity_expiry_date (STRING, DATE) should be replaced with a FK to exclusivity_period.exclusivity

attributes.name: masterdata_ndc_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.ndc_code. Business justification: Orange Book listings reference specific NDC codes; required for regulatory compliance, paragraph IV defense, and product-patent linkage tracking.

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: FDA Orange Book listings reference specific patents that protect approved drug products. The patent_number (STRING) should be replaced with a FK to patent.patent_id to link the regulatory listing to t

attributes.name: responsible_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical regulatory affairs assigns employees to monitor Orange Book listings for paragraph IV certification tracking, litigation response coordination, and generic entry forecasting. Critical f

attributes.name: anda_first_filer_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a first-filer ANDA applicant has been identified for this patent listing, triggering the 180-day generic exclusivity period under Hatch-Waxman. True if a first filer has been designated; False otherwise. Affects the timing of subsequent generic approvals.
attributes.references: 21 U.S.C. § 355(j)(5)(B)(iv); Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: applicant_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: NDA Applicant / Marketing Authorization Holder Name
attributes.description: Name of the NDA/BLA holder (marketing authorization holder) who submitted the patent or exclusivity listing to the FDA Orange Book. Identifies the company responsible for maintaining the listing.

attributes.name: atc_code
attributes.description: WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for the active ingredient. Enables therapeutic area grouping, competitive landscape analysis, and cross-market IP portfolio analytics.
attributes.references: WHO ATC/DDD Index; ICH E3; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this Orange Book listing record was first created in the data product. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH Q10 (Pharmaceutical Quality System)

attributes.name: delisting_date
attributes.description: Date on which the patent or exclusivity was removed from the FDA Orange Book, either voluntarily by the NDA holder or by FDA order. Null if the listing remains active. Relevant for tracking generic entry eligibility changes.

attributes.name: dosage_form
attributes.description: Physical form of the finished dosage form (FDF) as listed in the Orange Book (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, solution, patch). Determines therapeutic equivalence evaluation and generic substitutability. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|injection|solution|patch|cream|suspension|powder|gel|suppository — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; 21 CFR Part 314.3; USP Dosage Form Nomenclature

attributes.name: first_generic_eligibility_date
attributes.description: Earliest date on which a generic drug product may receive final FDA approval, accounting for both patent expiry and exclusivity expiry dates. Derived from the later of patent expiry, exclusivity expiry, and 30-month stay expiry. Critical for lifecycle management and loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) planning.
attributes.references: Hatch-Waxman Act; 21 CFR Part 314.107; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: listing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the patent or exclusivity was first listed in the FDA Orange Book by the NDA holder. Establishes the effective date of the listing for Paragraph IV certification and 30-month stay calculations.

attributes.name: listing_status
attributes.description: Current status of the Orange Book listing record. 'Active' indicates the patent or exclusivity is currently listed and enforceable. 'Delisted' indicates the NDA holder has removed the listing. 'Withdrawn' indicates FDA-initiated removal. 'Pending' indicates submission under review. 'Corrected' indicates an amendment was filed.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.53(f); FDA Orange Book; Hatch-Waxman Act

attributes.name: litigation_status
attributes.description: Current status of patent infringement litigation associated with this Orange Book listing, typically arising from a Paragraph IV certification. Tracks whether litigation is active, settled, or resolved by court judgment. Informs LOE risk assessment and legal strategy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: none|active|settled|judgment_for_patentee|judgment_for_challenger|appeal_pending|dismissed — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: market
attributes.description: Regulatory market or jurisdiction for which this listing record applies. 'US' for FDA Orange Book; 'EU' for EMA Article 10 reference product listing; 'UK' for MHRA; 'JP' for PMDA; 'CN' for NMPA. Enables multi-market IP portfolio management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: US|EU|UK|JP|CN|CA|AU|BR|IN|KR — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; EMA Article 10 (Directive 2001/83/EC); MHRA; PMDA; NMPA; ICH Q10

attributes.name: nda_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: New Drug Application (NDA) / Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) Number
attributes.description: FDA-assigned application number (NDA, ANDA, or BLA) under which the drug product is approved and listed in the Orange Book. Governs which patents and exclusivities are associated with the approved product.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.53; FDA Orange Book (Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations)

attributes.name: orphan_drug_designation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the listed drug product holds an FDA Orphan Drug Designation (ODD), conferring 7-year market exclusivity upon approval. True if ODD is active; False otherwise. Relevant for rare disease portfolio strategy and generic entry defense.
attributes.references: Orphan Drug Act (21 U.S.C. § 360bb); 21 CFR Part 316; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: paragraph_iv_date
attributes.description: Date on which the first Paragraph IV certification was received by the NDA holder for this listed patent. Initiates the 45-day window to file patent infringement suit and triggers the 30-month stay clock if suit is filed.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.95; Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: paragraph_iv_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Paragraph IV certification has been filed by an ANDA applicant challenging this listed patent as invalid, unenforceable, or not infringed. True triggers the 45-day notice period and potential 30-month stay of ANDA approval.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.95; Hatch-Waxman Act Section 505(j)(2)(A)(vii)(IV); FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: patent_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the listed patent expires as published in the FDA Orange Book. This date directly governs the earliest date a generic applicant may receive final approval absent a Paragraph IV challenge or court ruling.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.53; Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: patent_term_extension_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the listed patent has been granted a Patent Term Extension (PTE) under 35 U.S.C. § 156 to compensate for regulatory review time. True if a PTE has been granted; False otherwise. Affects the effective patent expiry date used for generic entry calculations.
attributes.references: 35 U.S.C. § 156 (Patent Term Extension); Hatch-Waxman Act; USPTO Patent Term Extension

attributes.name: patent_type
attributes.description: Classification of the listed patent as covering the drug substance (active ingredient), drug product (formulation/composition), or method of use. Determines the nature of Paragraph IV challenges and carve-out labeling strategies.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.53(b); FDA Orange Book; Hatch-Waxman Act

attributes.name: patent_use_code
attributes.description: FDA-assigned use code (e.g., U-001) that identifies the specific approved method of use covered by the listed patent. Required for method-of-use patents; determines the scope of Paragraph IV certifications and carve-out labeling eligibility.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.53(b)(1); FDA Orange Book Use Code Registry

attributes.name: pediatric_exclusivity_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a 6-month pediatric exclusivity extension has been granted under the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA), attaching to all existing patents and exclusivities for the listed product. True if pediatric exclusivity is in effect.
attributes.references: Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA); 21 U.S.C. § 355a; FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: reference_listed_drug_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this NDA product is designated as the Reference Listed Drug (RLD) against which ANDA applicants must demonstrate bioequivalence. True if the product is the RLD; False if it is a non-RLD listed product.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.3; FDA Orange Book RLD Designation; Hatch-Waxman Act

attributes.name: rems_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the listed drug product is subject to an FDA-approved Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). REMS requirements may affect generic applicant ability to demonstrate shared REMS compliance, impacting generic entry timelines.
attributes.references: 21 U.S.C. § 355-1 (REMS); FDA REMS Database; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: route_of_administration
attributes.description: Route by which the drug product is administered (e.g., oral, intravenous, topical, subcutaneous). Used in therapeutic equivalence evaluations and generic entry assessments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|transdermal|ophthalmic — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book; ICH M4 (CTD); 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: spc_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) expires in the relevant EU/UK jurisdiction. Represents the effective end of patent-based market protection for the listed product in that market.
attributes.references: EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009; MHRA SPC Guidance

attributes.name: spc_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) granted in EU/UK jurisdictions to extend patent protection beyond the standard 20-year term for medicinal products. Applicable for EU and UK market listings; null for US Orange Book entries.
attributes.references: EU Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 (SPC for Medicinal Products); MHRA SPC Guidance

attributes.name: strength
attributes.description: Labeled strength of the drug product as listed in the Orange Book (e.g., '10 mg', '500 mg/5 mL'). Strength is a key differentiator for therapeutic equivalence and generic substitution eligibility.

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the NDA holder submitted the patent or exclusivity information to the FDA for Orange Book listing. Must occur within 30 days of NDA approval or patent grant per 21 CFR Part 314.53(d).

attributes.name: therapeutic_equivalence_code
attributes.description: FDA therapeutic equivalence evaluation code assigned to the drug product in the Orange Book (e.g., AB, AA, BC, BX). 'A' codes indicate therapeutically equivalent to the RLD; 'B' codes indicate not therapeutically equivalent. Drives pharmacy substitution decisions and formulary management.
attributes.references: FDA Orange Book Preface — Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: thirty_month_stay_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the 30-month stay of ANDA approval expires following a timely-filed patent infringement suit in response to a Paragraph IV certification. After this date, FDA may grant final ANDA approval regardless of ongoing litigation outcome.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 314.107(b)(3); Hatch-Waxman Act Section 505(j)(5)(B)(iii); FDA Orange Book

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this Orange Book listing record was last modified in the data product. Supports change tracking, audit compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and Silver Layer data freshness monitoring.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH Q10

attributes.name: veeva_vault_doc_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the corresponding Orange Book listing submission document stored in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management). Enables traceability between the data record and the source regulatory document.
attributes.references: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures)

products.name: annuity_fee
products.description: Tracks patent annuity (maintenance fee) payment obligations and payment history across all jurisdictions for the patent portfolio. Captures patent reference, jurisdiction, fee year, due date, fee amount, currency, payment date, payment status (paid, overdue, waived, lapsed), paying agent, and confirmation receipt number. Failure to pay annuities results in patent lapse, making this a critical operational record for portfolio maintenance.

attributes.name: annuity_fee_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each patent annuity (maintenance fee) payment obligation or payment record in the portfolio.

attributes.name: accounts_payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: Patent annuity fees are paid to patent offices via accounts payable. Finance links annuity fee records to AP invoices for payment tracking, accrual reconciliation, cost center allocation, and annual I

attributes.name: authorized_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical IP operations require employee authorization for annuity payments for budget control, lapse prevention, and SOX compliance. Replaces text field authorized_by with employee FK for audit

attributes.name: patent_id
attributes.description: Reference to the patent record in the intellectual property portfolio for which this annuity fee obligation applies.

attributes.name: bank_reference_number
attributes.description: The bank transaction reference number or wire transfer confirmation number associated with the annuity fee payment, used for financial reconciliation against the company's bank statements and SAP FI records.
attributes.references: SOX; IFRS IAS 21; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

attributes.name: confirmation_receipt_number
attributes.description: Official receipt or acknowledgement number issued by the patent office or paying agent confirming successful payment of the annuity fee. Serves as proof of payment for audit and compliance purposes.
attributes.references: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.8; EPO Rule 51 EPC; 21 CFR Part 11; SOX

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: The SAP S/4HANA cost center code to which the annuity fee expense is allocated, enabling departmental cost tracking and IP portfolio cost management reporting.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; SOX; Internal Finance Policy

attributes.name: covered_product_name
attributes.description: The commercial or INN (International Nonproprietary Name) of the pharmaceutical product covered by the patent for which this annuity fee is being maintained. Supports commercial impact analysis and lifecycle management decisions.
attributes.references: INN (International Nonproprietary Name); WHO INN Programme; ICH Q10

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this annuity fee record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Used for audit trail and data lineage compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX; GDPR Article 5; ISO 8601

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the jurisdiction in which the annuity fee is payable (e.g., USD for US dollars, EUR for euros, JPY for Japanese yen, GBP for British pounds).

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: The statutory deadline by which the annuity fee must be paid to maintain the patent in force in the relevant jurisdiction. Missing this date without a grace period payment results in patent lapse.
attributes.references: USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPO Rule 51 EPC; PCT Rule 22bis; MHRA; PMDA

attributes.name: entity_size_category
attributes.description: The entity size classification applicable to this annuity fee payment, which determines the applicable fee discount at the USPTO and certain other patent offices. Large entities pay full fees; small entities (fewer than 500 employees) pay 60% of large entity fees; micro entities pay 40% of large entity fees.

attributes.name: exchange_rate
attributes.description: The foreign exchange rate applied to convert the local jurisdiction currency amount to the company's functional reporting currency at the time of payment. Used for financial consolidation and cost tracking.

attributes.name: fee_amount
attributes.description: The official annuity fee amount due to the patent office in the local jurisdiction currency, as prescribed by the applicable fee schedule for the relevant fee year and entity size category.
attributes.references: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.20; EPO Rule 51 EPC; ISO 4217

attributes.name: fee_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this annuity fee obligation, typically generated by the paying agent or internal IP management system for tracking and reconciliation purposes.
attributes.references: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.20; EPO Rule 51 EPC; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: fee_schedule_version
attributes.description: The version or effective date of the patent office fee schedule used to determine the annuity fee amount for this payment obligation. Fee schedules are periodically updated by patent offices and the applicable version must be documented for audit purposes.
attributes.references: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.20; EPO Rule 51 EPC; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: fee_year
attributes.description: The renewal year number for which the annuity fee is due, counting from the patent filing or grant date depending on jurisdiction rules (e.g., year 3, year 10, year 20). Critical for determining the applicable fee schedule.
attributes.references: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.20; EPO Rule 51 EPC; PCT Rule 22bis

attributes.name: functional_currency_amount

attributes.name: gl_account_code

attributes.name: grace_period_end_date
attributes.description: The final date by which a late annuity fee payment can be made with a surcharge to avoid patent lapse, as permitted by the relevant patent office. Varies by jurisdiction (e.g., 6 months in the US, typically with surcharge).

attributes.name: instruction_date

attributes.name: jurisdiction

attributes.name: lapse_date

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: paying_agent_name

attributes.name: paying_agent_reference

attributes.name: payment_date
